The Good, The Bad, And The Ugly: Cardinals Shock Rams in Week 6 Upset
full_text:
If the Arizona Cardinals could play every game at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, they might be undefeated.
Former Los Angeles Rams offensive coordinator and current Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur got the better of his former head coach, capturing his second win in Los Angeles.
Arizona, behind kicker Chad Ryland booting home six field goals, powered the Cardinals’ scoring attack by capping an 18-16 road win over the once-Super Bowl favorite Rams.
The Cardinals finally ended their four-game skid and captured their first NFC West win of the season after starting 0-2 in division.
Here is the good, the bad, and the ugly from Arizona’s stunning victory in California.
After allowing over 30 points in their past four games and feeling almost lifeless at times, the Cardinals defense had its best performance since week one.
Arizona bounced back, holding Los Angeles to just 16 points, with a trio of three-and-outs, a fumble, and a big fourth-down stop in plus territory. It was the season's most complete defensive performance, holding a Rams offense below its scoring average.
Cardinals pressure kept Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford under constant duress, forcing him to rely on checkdowns for most of the afternoon. The longest play of the afternoon came on the final Rams offensive drive, when Los Angeles receiver Puka Nacua caught a 43-yard pass to set up their second and final touchdown.
Arizona’s defense came up big, preventing Los Angeles from converting a two-point attempt and forcing a fumble on the same play in the second quarter.
The defense also forced two more fumbles on back-to-back plays in the final quarter, stripping Rams receiver Tyler Higbee and recovering the second fumble.
So far this season, the Cardinals offense hasn't been great on third-down conversions. Nothing changed against the Rams, as they limped in that department again. Arizona went 5-for-15 on third down, missing two critical conversions that could’ve iced the game.
Up by one possession, Arizona had a chance to eat up the clock, but a quick third-and-out gave Los Angeles plenty of time to drive downfield. Fortunately for the Cardinals, defense held on fourth down, giving quarterback Jacoby Brissett another chance to close out the game with under three minutes.
Again, the Cardinals receivers couldn’t reel in the critical third-down conversion to officially put the game in doubt. Arizona escaped today, but with two late-game opportunities, a better team will not give them a chance to hold on.
If bad luck stuck Arizona’s kicking game as it did for Los Angeles, who knows if the Cardinals score a single point. Ryland accounted for all 18 points for Arizona, and the offense couldn’t dial up a proper red-zone play to score.
On five red-zone trips, Arizona scored zero touchdowns, its worst mark this season. It was the first time since the 2017 season that the Cardinals won a game by field goals alone.
While Arizona did a fine job driving the field and picking apart a good Los Angeles defense. The Rams' red zone scheme was kryptonite for whatever LaFluer was scripting. Makes sense for the team that knows his play calling better than anyone.
The Cardinals left a lot of points on the board, and, echoing the sentiment from the previous section, better teams will take advantage of it.
Arizona will face the Denver Broncos at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Arizona, on Sunday at 1:05 pm Arizona time for Larry Fitzgerald’s Ring of Honor induction.

title: 4 Big Instant Reactions After Cardinals' Stunning Win vs Rams
full_text:
The classic football saying "any given Sunday" couldn't be any truer this week, as the Arizona Cardinals defeated their divisional foes the Los Angeles Rams in Week 6 action.
The Cardinals down their NFC West rivals 16-15 on the final play of regulation and improved to 2-4 on the regular season in what was by far the biggest upset of the Sunday slate.
Four big takeaways after Arizona's second victory of the season:
Before the season, a Cardinals win over the Rams would be considered the upset of the decade, as the Rams looked primed for a Super Bowl appearance and, by many, the likely winner. However, the Rams' season has not gone according to plan. Superstar and future first-ballot Hall of Famer Myles Garrett has missed a couple of weeks due to injury, including this game against Arizona.
In this game, the Rams got zero sacks. If Garrett were in, he would have had a highly productive day. Quarterback Matthew Stafford has also taken a step back from his MVP campaign last season. While Stafford is still a good, very smart quarterback, this offense isn't as electric as it once was.
Yes, the Cardinals did great things in this game. However, the team still has a ton of issues to fix before it can win games like this regularly.
A huge part of the Cardinals' win was that many players who had to step up due to injury or trade did. Last week, the Cardinals traded Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans, which gave wide receiver Kendirck Bourne more targets.
The 10-year veteran had a productive game, catching five passes for 47 yards. Before joining the Cardinals, Bourne spent time with the San Francisco 49ers, who run a similar offensive scheme. So, Bourne could be a nice piece in the passing game going forward.
In the run game, Bam Knight had a great showing with Jeremiyah Love sidelined due to injury. Knight ran for 80 yards and averaged 5.3 yards per carry.
In a shocking result, the Cardinals' defense was the biggest surprise. Opposing offenses, especially quarterbacks, have dissected this unit week after week. However, defensive coordinator Nick Rallis' defense held the Rams in check. Stafford posted his second-lowest QBR of the season; the Rams offense went 4-for-10 on third-down conversions and 0-for-2 on fourth down.
A huge reason Arizona's defense played well was its ability to tackle the Rams after the catch. The Rams offense is very effective after the catch, and the Cardinals did their best to contain that. Leading the Cardinals in tackles was linebacker Mack Wilson Sr.
This will go down as one of the best Cardinals defensive performances in recent memory. It's up to Rallis to build off of this momentum. Next week the Cardinals face the Denver Broncos. The Broncos' offense has looked sluggish at the start of the season. So, if the Cardinals' defense performs well against the Broncos, it could be a sign they're turning the corner.
While players stepped up on offense and the defense was great, the Cardinals' special teams were the reason they won this game. Kicker Chad Ryland deserves a lot of credit and respect, as he went 6-for-6 on field goals.
Ryland's field goals were 34, 30, 22, 38, 2,7 and 43 yards. Many of these were shorter because the Cardinals had red-zone offensive woes. Arizona didn't score a single touchdown, even though they got into the red zone five times. Ryland's reliability was huge for Arizona, especially his 43-yard game-winning kick as time expired in SoFi Stadium.
Overall, time will tell how people view this game. Is it an outlier or actually a stepping stone? Next week's home game against the Broncos will tell us a lot about this team.

title: 13 Winners, Losers From Cardinals' Shocking Win vs Rams
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals earned a massive upset victory over the Los Angeles Rams in Week 6, making waves through the NFL landscape and giving Mike LaFleur's side their second win of the regular season.
The dust is still settling on Sunday's action at SoFi Stadium — here's our winners and losers:
Talk about a job-saving performance.
Rallis' unit entered this week as one of the worst in the league and faced a matchup against a highly potent Rams offense. If things had gone south for Arizona's defense yet again after giving up four straight of 30+ points, the Cardinals very well could have fired Rallis after this week and it would have been justified.
Yet that wasn't the case. Rallis called an incredible game, dialing up pressure and limiting the Rams to just 16 points at SoFi Stadium. Arizona stopped Los Angeles on fourth down twice and forced a turnover on Sunday.
The Cardinals got the upset win, though Arizona almost more importantly showed signs of life on Sunday.
If they can perform like this on a more consistent basis, Arizona will be the sneaky team many had hoped for.
The Cardinals continue to do the tough things consistently with piecing together sustainable drives between the 20-yard lines. However, Arizona's red zone struggles have been well documented this season, and their trip to SoFi Stadium didn't produce any better results.
LaFleur ultimately settled for all field goals on the afternoon, marking the first time since 2017 where the Cardinals won a game without scoring a touchdown. Arizona went into the red zone a whopping five times with no touchdowns.
That was good enough this week, though there's clearly larger issues at hand. The Cardinals nearly lost as a result of their inability to punch it in for six if not for a game-saving drive at the end of action.
It's better to learn from wins as opposed to losses, though Arizona's biggest problem on the offensive side of the ball nearly cost them.
Ryland's job security has been quietly discussed this season, especially after missing two kicks earlier in the team's schedule to compound chatter from training camp/preseason.
However, when the game was on the line and the Cardinals' field goal unit being rushed to the field with no timeouts, Ryland buried home a 43-yard game-winning field goal to seal the biggest upset of Week 6.
Knocking home game-winning kicks is something Ryland's done on multiple occasions previously, though the overall consistency of the Cardinals' kicker has been questioned over the last calendar year.
It was good to see Ryland come through when the Cardinals needed him most — not only on the final drive, but also scoring every single point for Arizona on six different field goals.
There's plenty of Cardinals fans who are itching to see Beck take the field, and after spending a third-round pick on the quarterback, perhaps rightfully so. With that said, Beck has an uphill climb to reaching the field with two veterans in Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew ahead of him.
Beck was inactive yet again, only serving as an emergency third quarterback while the FOX broadcast mentioned a conversation with LaFleur where the head coach said the Cardinals wanted to see Beck "at the right time."
That time, especially after an upset win over Los Angeles, now feels delayed.
Our previous prediction of Week 12 for Beck's first action looks more and more realistic, as the Cardinals' rookie needed losses to pile — quickly — to make starting sooner rather than later a realistic possibility.
Brissett by no means played incredible, but a win in LaFleur's eyes only stretches Brissett's wiggle room before change comes at quarterback.
Baker's been picked on by opposing offenses this year in coverage, though Baker probably had his best game to date in Los Angeles.
Baker notched his third sack of the season, filled in quickly on run stops numerous times and made an impressive pass break-up to prevent a Rams touchdown early in action.
There's been a lot of talk about Baker being on the downswing of his career and even emerging as a potential trade candidate, though the tenured leader of Arizona's defense and face of the franchise quickly put those talks to bed.
As long as Baker continues to roam near the front seven and can shoot into gaps to disrupt plays before they begin, he'll succeed.
Allgeier was expected to take a big step up with Jeremiyah Love out, though that was anything but the case.
Bam Knight outshined the heftier-paid Allgeier in nearly every way possible, gaining 80 yards on 15 carries (5.3 yards per carry) compared to Allgeier's 38 yards on 18 attempts (2.1 yards per carry). Knight looked the more explosive out of the backfield duo by a wide margin and if Love is to miss another week, it will be Knight who likely gets the lead role in carries.
Allgeier simply is better suited for short-yardage scenarios and pass protection duties whereas Knight is the more dynamic player with the ball in his hands.
Allgeier's not a massive loser, though it was a bit disappointing to see him overshadowed by another Cardinals backup running back.
Sweat just might be coming alive.
After an incredibly slow start to the season, Sweat's last few weeks have slowly but surely seen him work his way back to his old form. Tonight marked his second sack in three weeks while also pairing four tackles and two quarterback hits against the Rams.
Sweat's had plenty of noise surrounding his name to begin 2026, and rightfully so. However, today was a big step forward in getting the Cardinals' edge rusher back to the pass rush production fans were desperately hoping to see.

title: Cardinals Fans Sound Off After Thrilling Week 6 Upset Win vs Rams
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals turned the NFL world upside down with their Week 6 win over the division rival Los Angeles Rams.
The Cardinals now advance to 2-4 on the season with both wins coming at SoFi Stadium after previously defeating the Chargers in Week 1.
What did Cardinals fans on social media make of this improbable victory?
Defensive Coordinator Nick Rallis' unit was on the struggle bus last week. The Cardinals defense gave up 45 points to the Detroit Lions . However, much to fans' surprise, the Cardinals defense played well, especially in the first half.
As Rams on SI's Blaine Grisak pointed out, the Cardinals brought the heat on Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford:
Matthew Stafford has been under duress all afternoon. The Cardinals are just bringing the heat and Stafford is 1-for-3 when pressured and been sacked twice. Rams offense with another quick 3-and-out. Only 9 runs to 15 passes.
Budda Baker with the SACK! Cardinals defense BALLIN’ in LA today! pic.twitter.com/9fdPXEHh5j
The Arizona defense played extremely well, but it was a double-edged sword. In one way, it was great to see the Cardinals hold the Rams' high-octane offense in check. However, many fans were wondering where this great defense had been the past couple of weeks.
This is the Nick Ralls defense people want to see. Creative and aggressive.
Where has this been the last few weeks??
The Cardinals led 15-9 late in the game. However, despite the lead, a Los Angeles win seemed probable, as the Cardinals couldn't put the game away on offense. Sadly, many fans were not surprised by the Cardinals' lack of clutch play late.
As Kelly in Phoenix pointed out, the Cardinals' inability to close out games has been an issue for a while:
Ah. Yes. I almost forgot we were the Cardinals for a minute.
The cardinals are poverty 😂😂
NOOOOOOOOOO pic.twitter.com/MZ1bzQxH6R
The Arizona cardinals exist solely just give the whole division 2 free wins
Before Stafford connected with Rams tight end Colby Parkinson for the Rams touchdown and lead, another user predicted the Cardinals would blow the game.
Cardinals are gonna let the Rams off the hook aren’t they
With the Rams up 16-15, Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett and the offense had to win the game. However, many weren't confident in Brissett's ability to lead a game-winning drive, as he hadn't played well. Brissett threw one interception and finished with a passer rating of 73.3.
Two users on X pointed out that Brissett doesn't throw to the Cardinals' number-one wideouts, as Michael Wilson had a quiet day in Los Angeles.
Jacoby Brissett  to Michael Wilson now that he's found his new toy in Kendrick Bourne. pic.twitter.com/P1930Z1mdK
Jacoby Brissett refuses to throw to #1’s. Michael Wilson is cooked now
Many posted a GIF of former San Francisco 49ers Quarterback Jimmy Garoppolo running out to the field down 24 to 20 in Super Bowl 54. Later in the drive, Garoppolo overthrew an open 49ers receiver for a potential Super Bowl-winning touchdown. This GIF is commonly used when people think an athlete, especially the quarterback, won't deliver in a moment.
Jacoby Brissett pic.twitter.com/FS1NxH0XKn
Some had faith Brissett could deliver in the big moment. Their faith was rewarded as Brissett found wideout Jalen Brooks for 44 yards, setting up Cardinals kicker Chad Ryland for the game-winning kick.
Jacoby brissett bout to walk us down for a game winning FG
Jacoby Brissett 15 second drill for game pic.twitter.com/R4vLyWAVHZ
CHAD RYLAND FOR THE WIN AND THE CARDINALS STUN THE RAMS. #NFL #Cardinals #Rams #AZvsLAR https://t.co/aQi4eANgSN
The Arizona victory left some not-so-happy. Yes, a win is good, but the Cardinals most likely aren't going anywhere this season. So a win hurts their draft position in what seems like a very good draft class.
BAAAAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHA We are TANKING and we still somehow spoiled a game for the Rams Hurting our own draft position in the process since the Titans won This is so Cardinals pic.twitter.com/IjkQY88A1c
The Arizona Cardinals have two wins at SoFi this season. That is more wins than the Chargers and Rams combined who play their home games at that stadium. Arizona also only have two wins on the season. Crazy! 😂
Overall, though, this game had some positive takeaways for fans, which isn't something you can say about every Cardinals game this year.

title: The Controversial Call That Rescued Cardinals' Upset Win vs Rams
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals shocked the entire NFL world in Week 6 after upsetting the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium, though it didn't come without some chatter.
Down by one point with a minute left, the Cardinals received the ball and managed to get the Rams' defense to jump offsides on a hard count. Quarterback Jacoby Brissett found receiver Jalen Brooks downfield for a chunk play — and some extra yardage on top thanks to a personal foul penalty on Rams cornerback Josh Wallace.
Wallace was called for unnecessary roughness, which gave the Cardinals 15 more yards and placed Arizona in prime field goal territory at the LAR 29-yard line. Chad Ryland hit a game-winning kick as time expired, and seemingly in the snap of a finger the Rams walked out of SoFi Stadium as shocked victims of an upset.
However, when looking at replays, it's a tough 50/50 call at best. Wallace doesn't make contact with Brooks' helmet. The FOX broadcast mentioned it after reviewing the play, and many on social media reacted afterwards.
Brutal penalty call here. Between the TD replay review and this flag, Cardinals had some fortuitous moments in the final minute. pic.twitter.com/HT20WXjs6Q
"I can actually see where in real time you might throw it. But replay assist should jump in to fix it," SI.com's Albert Breer put on X.
WOW... Rams get called for a personal foul for hitting a defenseless receiver... he barely touched him but the refs added 15 yards to the end of this play for that pic.twitter.com/6xuLynSAiw
"Yeah you know it’s bad when the ref for the broadcast team says it was a bad call," Stephen said on X.
I'm sorry but how on Earth can the officials find a way to F**K THE RAMS every single week. Not a foul on Wallace. @NFLOfficiating you owe this guy an apology twice. Rams may have deserved to lose but not like this!!!
UNREAL PERSONAL FOUL WHAT DO YOU WANT HIM TO DO??? pic.twitter.com/L4XLXmZw0W
Wallace, when the replay is slowed down, does launch himself into contact with Brooks — though the wideout didn't strike Brooks' head.
In real time, like Breer suggested above, it's an understandable call. With that established, replay assistance may have been able to buzz down and correct the call.
In the event the Cardinals didn't get the additional yardage, they were still at the Rams' 44-yard line with over 40 seconds left. No wins are guaranteed, though it's reasonable to believe Arizona may have put themselves in position to win regardless.
Still, hypotheticals don't count for wins in the NFL. And adding to that, Arizona were nearly two touchdown underdogs to the Rams entering this week, and when the dust settles on Week 6, excuses won't count towards the win-loss column.
The Cardinals and Rams are now tied at 2-4 in the NFC West, though Arizona has the tiebreaker over Los Angeles and is technically third in the division.
Arizona will see Los Angeles travel to State Farm Stadium for Week 10 action in the desert.

title: Rare Injury Sparks Cardinals' Crazy Upset Win vs Rams
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals managed a stunning 18-16 upset victory over the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium with plenty of factors working in their favor.
Defensively, coordinator Nick Rallis was able to shut the Rams' offense down with a blend of pressure and creative fronts to keep Los Angeles' potent attack at bay. On the other side of the ball, Arizona managed to reestablish their ground game and sustained numerous long scoring drives.
Week 6 was truly a crazy one, from start to finish.
However, it all started early in the first quarter with a rare injury. Rams kicker Blake Grupe tried to tackle Cardinals return man Devin Duvernay during a kickoff on the first quarter, which ultimately hurt Grupe and put him out with a knee injury.
Blake Grupe - It looks like there’s concern for entire body but listed with a knee injury. Not sure which one. Maybe both. pic.twitter.com/vpJ8IiDxho
And whether the Rams realized it in the moment or not, it would change the entire complexion of the game.
The Rams scored a touchdown halfway through the second quarter but were forced to try for a two-point conversion instead of going up 10-6.
Los Angeles quarterback Matthew Stafford was sacked on the two-point attempt and fumbled, nearly seeing the Cardinals return it for a score before defensive lineman L.J. Collier was brought down on the fumble return.
LJ Collier wanted to take the two-point conversion return all the way 😅 AZvsLAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CCOkklUaau
This was massive, as it kept the Cardinals within a field goal's reach.
In the waning moments of the third quarter, the Rams again found themselves deep in Cardinals territory but needing to go for it rather than potentially tying to game at 12-12.
Los Angeles tried to run a fullback dive, which was stuffed by Arizona's defense.
Cardinals defense comes up with the stop on 4th and 1! AZvsLAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/kieCYIdECf
The Cardinals would march down the field and extend their lead by another three points, again changing the dynamic of the game.
Because of prior events in the game that forced the Rams in a deficit, the Cardinals were only down by one point on their final drive. Aided by a chunk play and debatable penalty from a Los Angeles defender, Arizona quickly found themselves in field goal position.
Not to tie the game and send it to overtime, but to win.
Chad Ryland banged home a 43-yard field goal as time expired to give the Cardinals the upset victory.
Cardinals win their second game of the season at SoFi Stadium 😮 pic.twitter.com/B3I5Q5Ttkt
The NFL is very much a week to week league, though nobody expected the Cardinals to upset the Rams in Week 6.
And while it was a complete team effort, Arizona was undoubtedly on the receiving end of a domino effect that all started when the Rams lost their kicker earlier in the game.

title: Marvin Harrison Jr.’s Texans Debut Already Has Cardinals Taking Heat
full_text:
Marvin Harrison Jr. has officially played his first snaps as a non-Arizona Cardinal, helping the Houston Texans emerge victorious over the Jacksonville Jaguars in London.
Harrison tallied three receptions for 34 yards on limited snaps, which stirred some conversations across the internet.
Marvin Harrison Jr. gets his first catch as a Texan HOUvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/79N9CysaG5
"We haven't seen Marvin Harrison Jr. this motivated in years. Arizona is really a place where football players go to die. MHJ has found his home in Houston ❤️" wrote Dov Kleiman on X.
PHNX's Bo Brack added , "The Texans win, pushing the Cardinals newly acquired second round pick down the draft board with a chance to plummet. Marvin Harrison Jr. got some easy looks in Houston despite a limited role. Not a great return on investment for Arizona so far 😬"
Welp, looks like HOU figured out Marv is better at winning over the middle than he is running clear outs all game. Go figure. Not like his tape coming out suggested that would be the case or anything. 🤦🏻‍♂️
"Oh look at that, the Texans are lining Marv up in the slot. Imagine that," said Locked On's Alex Clancy.
Harrison was traded for a second-round pick (among other minor moving parts from both sides) last Sunday after struggling through the first two years and change in Arizona.
“Definitely nervous, but I’m nervous before every game, because I care so much about this game of football,” Harrison said (h/t Houston Chronicle ). “After the first catch, I was pretty good to go.”
There's a belief this is only the start for Harrison's fresh start with the Texans.
"Marvin Harrison Jr. gets traded from Arizona to Houston, goes through three time zones in a week, stays up late learning a new offense, travels to London and catches 3 of 4 targets on just 12 offensive snaps," said Texans Commentator on X.
"All three catches came over the middle, two in-breakers, including a tough contested grab between two defenders. Yet we were supposed to believe he just sucked because of some out-of-context route cutups, raw separation stats and a few training camp drops?
"Maybe the quarterback, scheme, route assignments, coaching and overall environment matter too. Maybe there’s more to evaluating a receiver than declaring he forgot how to play football based on a few clips and numbers without context."
While it was indeed time for a change of scenery for Harrison, it would be unfortunate to see Arizona's former No. 4 overall pick realize the potential so many Cardinals fans were hoping he'd reach.

title: Cardinals vs Rams Final Inactives: Who's In, Who's Out for Week 6
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals and Los Angeles Rams have revealed their list of final inactives ahead of their Week 6 clash at SoFi Stadium.
The Cardinals had Budda Baker (groin), Zaven Collins (hip), Kitan Crawford (ankle) and Blake Gillikin (back) questionable entering the weekend. All four players are active for Arizona on Sunday.
For Los Angeles, Kam Curl (ankle) and Trent McDuffie (groin) were questionable entering today. McDuffie has been ruled out while Curl is active for the Rams.
Kickoff is at 1:05 PM MST in Inglewood.
The obvious talk of the town was Love, as the third overall pick is set to officially be sidelined for the first time in 2026 after dealing with a nagging ankle injury.
"He's doing good, but you guys see the way he cuts. Like just being candid, he cuts hard. That's a superpower of his, and when he's putting his left foot in the ground, it's just not right right now," Cardinals HC MIke LaFleur said.
"And to get him to be to his best ability, it's what's right so he can go out and perform the way that he wants. So he can go out and honestly run the routes that he wants, because to run routes and separate, you got to be able to put those feet in the ground, and it's got to be deliberate. We want to get him healed so he can do that in the pass game and in the run game."
The Cardinals ultimately did not need Reed as Baker was healthy.
“Everything-- from top to bottom. They are only getting better each week. They’re obviously ascending," said Jacoby Brissett this week on L.A.'s defense.
"and bringing (Rams DE) Aaron Donald back didn’t do us any justice, but we have to go out there and do our job. We look forward to this challenge coming into this week and I think we’ll be ready.”

title: Rams vs Cardinals Bold Predictions: Puka Nacua Erupts vs Arizona
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals and Los Angeles Rams, in just a few hours time, will clash at SoFi Stadium for Week 6 action.
The Cardinals desperately need a win to prevent their season from slipping out of their hands while the Rams are hoping to avoid a disaster 2-4 start. The NFC West tilt should be fun between Sean McVay and his protégé in Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur.
Three bold predictions for today:
Death. Taxes. Puka Nacua getting the pigskin.
The Cardinals have struggled to take away No. 1 receiving options all throughout the 2026 season, and with safety Budda Baker questionable entering Sunday, Arizona's secondary could be down both starters at safety alongside cornerback Will Johnson down for the season as well.
Nacua is no stranger to success against the Cardinals. His last two games (combined) against Arizona in 2025 saw him total 17 receptions for 243 yards and three touchdowns while he's fresh off a 17-reception performance on Monday Night Football.
The Rams use Nacua — plenty — and that will continue against an incredibly weak Cardinals defense that can't seem to figure out how to limit explosive weapons on a weekly basis.
Sean McVay always seems to have the answers to the test. To beat the Cardinals, using Nacua is like an open study guide.
Donald has played in three games for Los Angeles since his return to NFL football, totaling just six tackles and one fumble recovered. He hasn't successfully reached the quarterback yet for a sack, but that appears likely to change against Arizona.
More and more, Donald is finding his footing again along the Rams' defensive line. That's bad news for a Cardinals offensive line missing multiple starters.
"I never thought that Aaron over the last few years — even though he wasn’t playing whenever I’d see him, whether it be at SoFi (Stadium) or over at Sean’s or whatnot, he looked like he could play," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said this week of Donald.
"Have you ever seen a cheetah warm up? No, they don’t. They just go. Well, Aaron can just go, and there’s a reason he’s the best to ever do it.”
Jacoby Brissett's time to throw is one of the fastest in the NFL, though he's been sacked 12 times through five games. The Cardinals' lackluster run game will lead to more pass-rush opportunities for Donald, who might be close to knocking the dust completely off.
Time is now running out for Jacoby Brissett to justify the raise he held out for over the summer, and Week 6's task against the third-ranked Rams defense is going to be a tall one with Jeremiyah Love out due to injury and Marvin Harrison Jr. traded to Houston.
After Week 1's win against the Los Angeles Chargers, the Cardinals' offense has largely been hit or miss. The team's rushing attack has dwindled, and Arizona relying on Brissett's arm to win games clearly isn't a recipe for success.
Brissett hasn't been the team's worst problem, though it's very clear through five weeks of football he's not a solution.
If the Cardinals struggle as expected, Arizona may open Pandora's box by benching Brissett and bringing veteran backup quarterback Gardner Minshew into the mix, who should finish action at SoFi Stadium but will only begin conversations around the team's quarterback position.

title: Where Falcons Rookie Zachariah Branch Found Support after Costly Mistakes
full_text:
Zachariah Branch was one of the most talked-about Atlanta Falcons rookies during the offseason.
Coming out of USC and Georgia, his blazing speed and explosiveness as a wide receiver and return specialist had Atlanta fans excited for what’s to come out of the third-round NFL draft pick.
Through Branch’s first six NFL games, he’s primarily been the return man for the Falcons (2-4).
But in their Week 6 31-23 loss on Sunday to the Chicago Bears (4-2) , he faced his first adversity, fumbling two costly returns for the Falcons.
“Zachariah’s somebody that we’re going to be counting on. He’s a conscientious kid,” Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski told reporters postgame. “He has to take care of the football; he has done a good job up to date. He will learn from this.”
Down 14-7 with a little less than two minutes left in the second quarter, Atlanta was looking to turn the corner earlier in their failed fourth-quarter comeback effort.
Branch fielded a punt from Bears punter Tory Taylor, and muffed it as he was falling forward to the ground. Chicago’s Josh Blackwell recovered it, and running back D’Andre Swift scored on a two-yard rush to take a 21-7 halftime lead.
And then late in the third, after the Bears had taken a 28-7 lead, Branch had a chance to redeem himself on a kickoff.
After returning it for 26 yards, he fumbled it again, and the Bears recovered it, this time by Nick McCloud. Bears kicker Cairo Santos got a 50-yard field goal out of it.
As Branch walked sheepishly to the sideline, Stefanski spoke with him and tapped the rookie on his helmet.
Atlanta running back Bijan Robinson then pulled Branch aside.
“He’s a rookie,” Robinson said. “He needs a leader to be with him in that moment. And for me, it’s important to make sure that he’s alright because in this world that we live in, a lot of worldly things can get into his mind.”
Branch had slammed his helmet to the ground in frustration. But Robinson brought a calming presence to the frustrated first-year NFL player.
When the camera panned back over to the Falcons duo, they had their heads bowed.
“I just wanted to make sure that he was OK mentally and that his faith is high,” Robinson said of the exchange. “We prayed together, and I just wanted to make sure that he’s spiritually well. Because for a young guy, that’s the most important thing. Zach, he’s obviously a hell of a player, but I’ve always got to keep him in the game no matter what the situation is.”
Branch finished Sunday with one punt fielded and four kick returns for 86 yards. He also got involved with the offense during the late rally, making two catches for nine yards.
Quarterback Michael Penix Jr. completed a pass to Branch for a two-point conversion after Atlanta scored its first points in the fourth quarter after a scoreless third.
“He’ll be better for this,” Stefanski said of Branch.
Searching for their first home win of the season, the Falcons next host the unbeaten San Francisco 49ers (5-0) in Atlanta next Sunday, Oct. 25, at 1 p.m. San Francisco will put their undefeated streak on the line against the Washington Commanders on Oct. 19’s edition of Monday Night Football.
Falcons-49ers kick off at 1 p.m. on FOX.

title: Falcons Get Update on LB Kendal Daniels After Scary Injury
full_text:
Atlanta Falcons rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels was transported to Grady Hospital after suffering a frightening injury against the Chicago Bears on Sunday, but initial reports offered reason for optimism.
Daniels reportedly had movement in all his extremities and was seen walking under his own power in the locker room after the game, according to The Athletic 's Josh Kendall . The full extent of his injury remains unknown, but the Falcons later confirmed that he was alert and had movement in his extremities.
“Kendal’s a kid we all love, we all respect,” Stefanski said. “And then you have to play football, and that’s the hard part. It’s easy for me to say, ‘You got to play.’ Now, they take comfort in knowing he’s doing better, but those are moments. Those are hard.”
Stefanski reiterated that the initial reports were encouraging and added that the team hoped they would remain positive as Daniels underwent further evaluation.
All told, Daniels was down on the field and being tended to for nearly 15 minutes.
“The medical staff did an outstanding job of getting him safely off the field,” Stefanski said. “All reports so far are good. We’ll continue to pray they remain good.”
Daniels suffered the injury in the third quarter while tackling Bears tight end Colston Loveland. His facemask appeared to make contact with Loveland's knee, leaving the rookie on the ground as medical personnel rushed to his aid. Trainers eventually brought out a cart and stretcher to assist Daniels off the field as teammates gathered around him.
“He’s like, ‘Y’all go finish this off,’” quarterback Michael Penix Jr. said afterward.
Center Ryan Neuzil acknowledged how difficult it was to see a teammate go down while praising the Falcons for continuing to fight.
“That’s always tough. That’s the name of the game. Scary things happen. It’s really tough, and especially for the team to rally back after that. Made a couple key stops, and then we were able to gain some momentum after that. It was good to see just people keep fighting,” Neuzil said.
Daniels, a rookie from Oklahoma, is a key part of Atlanta's defense as the team looks to turn its season around. Sunday's injury gave the Falcons a scare, with players and coaches forced to watch as medical personnel attended to a teammate.
The Falcons are awaiting further evaluation to determine the full extent of Daniels' injury. For now, the initial reports have been encouraging.

title: Falcons Forced to Use Silent Count at Home Against Bears
full_text:
ATLANTA – Mercedes-Benz Stadium has not been kind to the Atlanta Falcons this season. After a 31-23 loss to the Chicago Bears, Kevin Stefanski’s team is now 0-3 at home, but Sunday brought another troubling development. Atlanta not only dropped the game, but the Falcons’ head coach also confirmed that the offense had to go to a silent count because of a large contingent of Bears fans.
“We love our fans. Our fans are so supportive,” Stefanski said after the game. “But we just felt like we knew we likely would need to be on a silent count.”
Additionally, in anticipation of this, the Falcons practiced with crowd noise this week, as they typically do for road games.
“We did the silent count all week, so we were good with the silent count stuff,” quarterback Michael Penix Jr. said. “The crowd noise thing is always tough whenever you play at home, and you hear during the week that you gotta work through a silent cadence. You always expect (Falcons) fans to overrule the opponent’s fans, but we were ready for it. I feel like we executed the silent cadence well.”
Although Penix said the Falcons executed the silent cadence well, the need to prepare for crowd noise at home underscored how little traditional home-field advantage Atlanta enjoyed on Sunday.
As a unit, the Falcons had just 100 net yards through the first three quarters and were outscored 31-7. They fell behind early, but rallied in the fourth quarter, totaling 157 net yards and nearly pulling off a remarkable comeback.
“It’s just the name of the game,” center Ryan Neuzil said. “Chicago is a really good team, and they just have a bunch of fans worldwide, so they travel really well. It’s always harder to be on a silent count.”
Overall, the Falcons have struggled to defend their home field. They are winless this season, surrendering a late lead to the Ravens and suffering lopsided scoring performances against the Bears (until their late rally) and the Panthers, but the issues run much deeper.
The Falcons have won only three home games with Penix as a starter over the last three years, and not since Oct. 13 of last season. Since Mercedes-Benz Stadium opened in 2017, the Falcons are just 34-42 at home.
“Shoot, you have to win your games at home,” Stefanski said. “It’s very, very disappointing. This is a place we love to play, and we love to play in front of our fans. And not to be able to win this one stings. We got to find ways to play better and coach better, starting this week.”
The Falcons will get the chance to flip that script on Sunday when the San Francisco 49ers come to Atlanta, but it will be another franchise with a large fan-base.
The silent count was an unusual wrinkle, but the bigger concern is a team that still struggles to turn its own stadium into an advantage. Right now, it doesn’t feel like home.

title: 4 Winners, 3 Losers after Atlanta Falcons Fall to Chicago Bears
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons had a frustrating afternoon against the Chicago Bears , losing 31-23, with several standout individual performances overshadowed by costly turnovers, offensive line struggles, and a growing list of injuries.
Atlanta found some positives in its team. However, special teams mistakes, an inconsistent running game and protection breakdowns made it difficult for the Falcons to put together a complete performance.
Here is a look at the biggest winners and losers from Atlanta's matchup against Chicago.
Atlanta's defensive line was one of the few bright spots of the afternoon. The unit managed to generate pressure on Bears quarterback Caleb Williams, recording six total quarterback hits and three sacks.
They held the league's No. 1 rushing attack to just 98 yards.
Brandon Dorlus, Gervon Dexter, and LaCale London each recorded a sack, providing Atlanta with several impactful plays in the trenches. Their ability to disrupt Williams gave the defense opportunities to get off the field and prevent the Bears quarterback from becoming too comfortable in the pocket.
Although the Falcons struggled in other areas, the defensive line showed encouraging signs of progress. Generating consistent pressure will be essential moving forward, especially against quarterbacks who can extend plays and create opportunities outside the pocket.
Atlanta needs more performances like this from its defensive front as it looks to become more consistent on that side of the ball.
Bates continues to prove why he is one of Atlanta's most valuable defensive players. The veteran safety has consistently found ways to make an impact, using his instincts and physicality to create opportunities for the Falcons.
His forced fumble against Chicago was another example of his ability to change the momentum of a game. Turnovers are particularly important for a defense that needs to give its offense additional possessions and opportunities to score. He was also tied for the team lead with seven tackles.
Bates' consistent playmaking remains a major asset for Atlanta. Even when the defense struggles collectively, he has the ability to deliver a momentum-changing play.
His leadership and production will remain important as the Falcons attempt to regroup following a disappointing performance.
Pitts provided a much-needed spark for Atlanta's offense, recording two touchdowns while finishing with five receptions for 60 yards. He scored both touchdowns in the 4th quarter to help Atlanta cut the lead to 8.

Penix finished the afternoon completing 19 of 33 passes for 225 yards and three touchdowns. Although the quarterback struggled during the first three quarters, he helped give Atlanta's offense a spark in the fourth quarter as the Falcons attempted to mount a comeback.
His late production demonstrated the potential of Atlanta's passing attack when the offense finds its rhythm. Penix was able to connect with his receivers for multiple touchdowns despite dealing with significant pressure throughout the game.

Branch had a costly afternoon on special teams, committing two turnovers that hurt Atlanta's chances of establishing momentum.
The rookie muffed a punt in the second quarter before fumbling a kickoff in the third quarter. Both mistakes disrupted the Falcons' efforts to gain favorable field position and placed additional pressure on the defense.
The first fumble was particularly damaging as the Falcons were getting the ball with just under two minutes to go in the first half, down 14-7, and with some momentum.
Instead, they went into the break down 21-7, and the game suddenly felt out of reach.
The Falcons need more reliable execution on special teams, and Branch will have to learn from the mistakes as he continues adjusting to the NFL.
Atlanta's offensive line had one of its most difficult performances of the season, struggling to protect Penix and surrendering five sacks. Michael Penix Jr. was pressured on 46% of his dropbacks after the Bears blitzed him on 56.4% of his pass attempts.
The protection breakdowns prevented the quarterback from consistently settling into the pocket and limited the offense's ability to develop plays downfield. Communication issues appeared to contribute to the problems, with Chicago's defenders finding opportunities to penetrate the protection and disrupt Atlanta's passing game.
Bears defensive back Kyler Gordon also forced two fumbles on Penix. One was overturned, while the other proved especially costly and effectively ended Atlanta's hopes of mounting a comeback.

After promising performances earlier in the season, Atlanta's rushing attack has struggled to maintain the same level of consistency.

While those numbers represent averages of 5.1 and 6.8 yards per carry, respectively, his limited workload in the latest game raises questions about Atlanta's ability to consistently establish its ground attack.
Robinson remains one of the Falcons' most dangerous offensive weapons, and his efficiency shows that he can produce when given opportunities. However, nine carries are not enough to consistently make him the centerpiece of an offense that has benefited from his explosiveness.

title: Gut Reaction: Too Little Too Late as Bears Dominate Falcons Despite Score
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons fell to the Chicago Bears 31-23 in a scoreline that probably flattered the Falcons; the final score made it look closer than it felt throughout the game.
The game couldn’t have started much worse for the Falcons. The Bears go on a long, time-consuming drive that results in a touchdown. The Falcons go three-and-out on their first drive and give up a 23-yard punt return by Kalif Raymond, putting Chicago in good field position to start their second drive.
The Bears converted a 3rd and 17 after a fumbled snap; six plays later it was 14-0, and Caleb Williams was 10/10 for 122 yards and a touchdown.
Meanwhile, Penix had gone into the medical tent, presumably to take a look at his injured ribs. Penix returned, but it was another three-and-out for the Falcons.
The Falcons' defense stood up to the Bears on consecutive possessions, giving the offense a chance to find itself. Penix missed a wide-open Drake London on a well-drawn-up play-action, but they found paydirt on the next drive when Penix threw a nice fade to Jahan Dotson to make the score 14-7.
The Falcons needed to show some life, because at this point in the game, they were in danger of being blown out in front of a pro Chicago-transplant crowd in Mercedes-Benz Stadium.
Atlanta’s defense held again with just under two minutes left in the first half. FOX’s play-by-play man Kevin Burkhardt rightly said it seemed as if the Falcons had weathered the storm.
Then Zachariah Branch muffed a punt at the 10-yard line. Branch lost the punt return duties to Olamide Zaccheaus earlier this year after he fielded a punt inside the five that took him into the endzone. I’ll be a little surprised if we don’t see Zaccheaus back there for the next several weeks.
To add insult to injury, cornerback Avieon Terrell left after the second-down play with a shoulder injury. On third down, the Bears pushed the ball into the end zone to make it 21-7.
Any momentum the Falcons had clawed back was sucked through the roof of the stadium going into the half.
21-7 at the half. Outgained 243 to 97, and the Bears held the ball for 22:13 of the 30 minutes. It was the least amount of time the Falcons had the ball in the first half of a game since 2012. How do you stop Bijan Robinson? Make him watch from the sidelines.
The Falcons looked like a team that had already made offseason plans. Getting beaten handily by the Panthers with Cooper Rush at quarterback was almost understandable, predictable even. But the first-half showing by the Falcons would lead even the staunchest of Falcons’ defenders to be ready for a roster reset at the end of the year.
It got worse in the second half, not better.
Atlanta knew they needed a spark in the second half, and they came out more aggressive. They got a pass interference call against Drake London for a big gain, and then they were bailed out on a roughing the punter penalty after Penix was sacked on a third-down blitz.
They weren’t able to take advantage of their good fortune. Penix got sacked again on a Bears blitz, and the drive ended on an incomplete pass to Drake London on fourth and three from the Bears' 28.
Atlanta came into the game banged up on defense, and then it got worse. There was Terrell’s shoulder injury. Divine Deablo left with an arm injury. The most serious of all looked to be Kendal Daniels, who injured his head/neck area on a tackle . He went off on a stretcher, which looked more precautionary. A concussion looked probable after both his hands went to the side of his head and he rolled over after the tackle.
FOX later reported that Daniels was fully conscious and had movement in all of his extremities.
Terrell returned in the second half. His brother A.J. is eligible to return to the team this week if his hamstring injury is deemed recovered.
Entering the fourth quarter, the Falcons trailed 28-7 and had fewer yards on offense (100) than the Bears had in penalty yards (133).
The book is out on Penix: Pressure him. The Bears put Penix under pressure, and he was 9/20 passing for 48 yards when the Bears were up 31-7.
Robinson was bottled up because the Bears kept him off the field. The defense couldn’t stop Caleb Williams.
The special teams had enough errors to lose the game on their own.
Even after all the bad through three-plus quarters, and ironically, Tom Brady doing color commentary, the Falcons made it interesting.
The Falcons showed some life after the game was seemingly out of hand. A pair of Kyle Pitts touchdowns were both encouraging and head-scratching. He looks amazing with the ball in his hands. Why is his first target in the fourth with the score 31-7?
Atlanta had the ball and was down 31-23 with just under four minutes to play.  But with the game in the balance again, the Bears turned up the pressure again and forced a turnover on downs.
We saw the good Falcons and the bad Falcons against the Bears. Unfortunately, the good Falcons didn't show up until it was 31-7. However, they showed they weren't ready to just mail-in the rest of the season.
They have a big opportunity coming up next Sunday.
Rekindle the season against the 49ers, or start looking towards 2027 when the Falcons have a ton of space under the salary cap and a full allotment of draft picks.

title: Falcons Lose Key Defenders to Injury In Week 6 Against Bears
full_text:
ATLANTA -- The Atlanta Falcons are trailing the Chicago Bears early, but the afternoon just got a good bit worse when linebacker Divine Deablo went down with an arm injury in the second quarter. Later, the Falcons lost rookie cornerback Avieon Terrell with a shoulder injury.
UPDATE: The Falcons announced that Deablo is OUT for the remainder of the game against the Chicago Bears. He ends his day with four tackles (two solo).

Deablo is the Falcons' second-leading tackler with 26, but his size and athleticism make him a valuable asset to Jeff Ulbrich's defense.
Rookie linebackers Kendal Daniels and Harold Perkins Jr. would be the next men up for the Falcons. Veterans Christian Harris and Josh Woods are also depth options who could see their playing time elevated, should Deablo miss time.
As for Terrell, the Falcons are already down several members of their secondary. His older brother, A.J. Terrell Jr., was placed on injured reserve on Sept. 22 with a groin injury. Second-stringer C.J. Henderson also suffered a groin injury and was unavailable for this game.
Terrell was filling in for both players Sunday, and the Falcons are down to Mike Hughes, Mike Ford Jr., Malcolm Dewalt IV, and Robert Longerbeam in the cornerback room.

title: Former Falcons DT Grady Jarrett Issues Warning to Chicago Bears Teammates
full_text:
Former Atlanta Falcons defensive tackle Grady Jarrett may have only spent one season as a teammate with running back Bijan Robinson in Atlanta, but it doesn't take long for the All-Pro to make an impression.
Jarrett returns to Atlanta for the first time as a Chicago Bears player on Sunday, and his unit is tasked with trying to stop one of the best players in the NFL. The Bears have the 23rd-ranked EPA against the run, according to Sumer Sports , and Robinson and the Falcons represent by far their biggest challenge of the season.
"It's going to take everybody doing what we need to do," Jarrett said this week about slowing down Robinson. "Attacking the line of scrimmage. Not playing passively. Not playing selfishly. It takes a whole unit to attempt to slow down a special play like Bijan.
"God-given ability to see, to burst, to separate, contact balance; this is a really special player, special person. He knows he's the bloodline of that organization. We've got a heck of a challenge ahead of us."
The Bears have only allowed one 100-yard rusher this season; the Vikings' Aaron Jones went for 105 in Week 2. What Chicago has been good at is getting early leads and forcing teams to abandon the run.
The Eagles' Saquon Barkley had 82 yards, but he only had 15 carries as the Bears built a 20-7 lead in the third quarter. Braelon Allen of the Jets had only 14 carries as the Jets fell behind by two scores early in the third.
The Falcons' defense will need to keep the Bears off the field and slow down their No. 1 rushing offense. The easiest way to slow down Robinson is to keep him on the sidelines.
One of the main players tasked with stopping the Bears' rushing attack is defensive tackle Gervon Dexter Sr. Dexter signed a lucrative contract extension with the Falcons after being traded to Atlanta from Chicago.
Jarrett spent last season with Dexter and the Bears and got to know the young lineman well.
"I talked to Gervon when he signed his extension," admitted Jarrett. "I was super happy for him, happy for his family, loved my time here with him, and excited for him. Another young player that's gonna continue to get better. Got a fresh start in Atlanta, so I couldn't be happier for him."
Jarrett will have a lot of familiar faces on the opposite sideline and in the stands on Sunday, but he's all business when it comes time to strap on the helmet.
"I know those people down there, great people, so I'm excited for him, but as far as talking every day, we're both getting ready for an opponent every week, so we ain't breaking bread, talking every day," Jarrett said with a grin.
With kickoff scheduled for 1 p.m. EST at Mercedes-Benz Stadium , there will be plenty of time for Jarrett to make the rounds when the game is over.
"Like I said, I love him as a man, as former teammate, and as for his future, I'm excited for him. He's doing what he's doing. He's looked like he's having fun doing his thing and, personally, I'm happy for him," Jarrett said.

title: FalconsSI Staff Unanimous in Chicago Bears vs. Atlanta Falcons Predictions
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are looking to bounce back from a tough overtime loss to the Baltimore Ravens when they host the Chicago Bears on Sunday.
Atlanta will look to earn its first home victory of the season against a Chicago team featuring quarterback Caleb Williams and the NFL’s No. 1 rushing offense. The Falcons On SI staff is unanimous in its prediction.
Falcons SI staff each enter the week with a 3-2 record on the season. Here is what each writer predicts for Sunday’s matchup.
Atlanta took a tough blow in its overtime loss to the Ravens last week. It was a reality check for sure, but also gave the Falcons direction of where to improve.
The Falcons win by stopping the Bears’ No. 1 rushing offense , led by D’Andre Swift. They will catch a break with the second head of the backfield monster, Kyle Monangai, being ruled out for his second straight game with turf toe and a thumb injury. Stop the run and get pressure on a returning-from-injury Caleb Williams, and Atlanta secures its first win at home for the year.
Prediction : Falcons 35, Bears 24
Michael Penix Jr. has been one of the best quarterbacks this season when he’s not pressured. The Bears haven’t been pressuring quarterbacks and are missing edge rusher Montez Sweat.
Penix keeps the defense honest with his arm, while Bijan Robinson does Bijan Robinson things. The defense contains the Bears No.1 rushing offense, but Caleb Williams has a big game on broken plays.
Falcons do enough to even their record.
Prediction : Falcons 27, Bears 22
Caleb Williams’  return adds another layer to Sunday’s matchup as the Falcons look to respond after a tough overtime loss to the Ravens. Atlanta’s biggest challenge will be slowing down Chicago’s No. 1 ranked rushing offense after struggling to contain Baltimore on the ground last week.
I expect the Falcons to deliver a stronger defensive performance while getting their offense back on track. Atlanta should do enough on both sides of the ball to secure a hard fought victory, earn its first home win of the season and improve to 3-3.
Prediction : Falcons 31, Bears 23
The health of the two quarterbacks, Michael Penix Jr. (ribs) and Caleb Williams (hamstring), will ultimately dictate how this game goes. Both are set to play, but how healthy will they be? The Bears have shown some outrageous scoring spurts (59 points in Week 1), but it's been a rocky road since then because of various injuries. Atlanta's defensive line will need another big performance on Sunday.
Both secondaries have shown they can be exploited this season, but Penix needs to stay clean. If he can, the Falcons quarterback has been one of the best quarterbacks when not under pressure. The Bears have some pass rushers who are set to miss this game , so that could be the formula for a Falcons win.
Prediction : Falcons 24, Bears 20
As long as Penix is healthy (and plays like it), the Falcons offense is going to be tough for the Bears to match up against. The Bears are without their best defensive lineman, Montez Sweat, and honestly, their d-line is pretty bad even when he's healthy. The Bears' top corner, Jaylon Johnson, is having a bad start to the year, so I look for Drake London to have yet another big game.
While Caleb Williams' return is the big headline, the biggest test for the Falcons' defense will be whether they can contain the Bears' rushing attack. The Falcons' run defense got gashed by an elite Ravens rushing attack, and now they'll face a Bears rushing attack that's just as good.
Ultimately though, I trust the Falcons defense and Jeff Ulbrich to get some stops when they need them.
Prediction : Falcons 27, Bears 23
The game kicks off at 1 p.m. at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on FOX .

title: Star-Crossed Falcons Draft Pick Comes Full Circle with Latest Roster Moves
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have made several defensive roster moves ahead of Sunday’s Week 6 matchup against the Chicago Bears, signing linebacker edge rusher Bralen Trice to the active roster and bringing safety Jammie Robinson back to the practice squad .
Atlanta also elevated Robinson and defensive end Drake Jackson as standard practice squad elevations, adding depth to the defense for Sunday’s contest.
Trice’s promotion comes after the third-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft made an impression during his opportunities with Atlanta this season. The former Washington standout spent the 2024 and 2025 seasons on injured reserve before returning to the field this year. He was out of practice squad elevations, and the Falcons had the choice of waiving him, hoping he'd pass through waivers and re-sign him to the practice squad, or signing him to the 53.
In three games this season, Trice has recorded one tackle and one pass defensed. He has also contributed to the defensive line rotation, playing approximately 26% of Atlanta’s defensive snaps during his three practice squad elevations.
His most notable performance came against the Green Bay Packers in Week 3, when he registered four quarterback hurries against Jordan Love. Those opportunities helped demonstrate his potential as a contributor to Atlanta’s pass rush.
Trice recorded 101 tackles, 28.5 tackles for loss, and 18 sacks during his three seasons at Washington, establishing himself as a productive defender before entering the NFL.
The Falcons also signed Robinson to the practice squad after releasing him from the active roster earlier in the week. Atlanta subsequently elevated the safety for Sunday’s game.
Robinson has appeared in two games for the Falcons this season, recording two solo tackles. He previously played six games for Atlanta in 2025 after spending his first two NFL seasons with the Carolina Panthers.
Across 29 career regular-season games, Robinson has recorded 19 tackles, including 15 solo stops. His experience in the secondary and contributions on special teams give Atlanta additional depth against Chicago.
Jackson will also be available Sunday after receiving his second consecutive standard practice squad elevation. The Falcons hope this is precautionary, as they continue to monitor the status of edge rusher Za'Darius Smith, who remains questionable with a neck injury .
The defensive end has appeared in one game for Atlanta this season. Across his NFL career, he has recorded 24 tackles, six sacks, nine passes defensed, and one interception.
Jackson previously played for the San Francisco 49ers and Washington Commanders before joining Atlanta.

title: 3 Biggest Problems With Ravens 4th Quarter Defense After Another Collapse
full_text:
The Ravens fourth-quarter defense remains as broken as it ever was.
Whatever you thought of it under Wink Martindale his final few years in charge, or in Mike Macdonald’s first year-and-a-half in charge and during both of Zach Orr’s years in charge, it’s just as bad under rookie head coach Jesse Minter.
And it’s only getting worse.
The parable that was pushed by Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta, who has been a vastly overhyped evaluator and pedestrian roster-builder going on a decade on the job, was that the former coaches were preventing this team from breaking through. And Minter, a former Ravens assistant, was supposed to arrive with the secret sauce, and DeCosta added a $30M pass rusher to a $20M defensive tackle and a $20M inside linebacker and a $19M corner and a $20M hybrid safety and all those first-round picks on the defense, and yet it’s same as it ever was.
Maybe, just maybe, the Ravens (4-2) defense simply includes some of the most bloated contracts and overpaid players in the NFL (linebacker Roquan Smith and corner Marlon Humphrey carrying the top cap charges at their positions), who continue to succumb to mostly bad quarterbacks when it matters most. And maybe, just maybe, DeCosta getting carte blanche to build a rookie coaching staff after John Harbaugh was fired after nearly 20 years on the job, came at a price too.
Because for all of the issues this defense has – lack of late-game pressure and lack of late-game interceptions and lack of late-game playmakers – the novice head coach trying to run a sideline and manage a game for the first time,  while also getting the best out of his defense in the clutch, is proving to be a massive issue, too. Sunday’s debacle to the Browns , allowing 130 yards and 8 first downs and getting outscored, 10-0, in the final quarter in a 13-10 loss, was all too familiar; Minter’s defense has already blown three double-digit leads and lost twice, and the disparity between his first half and second half defense is kind of sickening.
This team now has a record 16 losses with a double-digit lead since the start of 2019, Lamar Jackson's first full season at QB, his first MVP season and the start of a ridiculous run of dominant offensive football in which the Ravens were the second-most prolific teams in the NFL through three quarters but can't hold leads like everybody else.
“I'm not going to sound like a broken record,” said hybrid defender Kyle Hamilton, the voice of this team who played his tail off Sunday. “It's 'Groundhog Day' with this question. I don't know. I'm not going to give you an answer. I really don't know. So, sorry, that's the best I can give you, but we've had this conversation so many times. I don't even feel like addressing it again."
For the season, here are the Ravens defensive ranks in the first half and second half:
First Half          Second Half
Passing Yards: 462 (5th)          780 (28th)
Oppo Passer Rating: 71.8 (4th)         102.3 (22nd)
Points/Drive Allowed: 2.55 (24th)      1.44 (4th)
Points Differential: +52 (1st)          -35 (31st)
The nasty trends get most acute in the fourth quarter and Minter needs to get all of this turned around quickly:
You can’t manage to consistently suffocate teams in the first half like noted above, and then become a total sham in the fourth quarter and tell me coaching isn’t playing a role in this. Come on man. You can’t tell me that Minter has  far superior roster in his two years running the Chargers defense and those teams did get turnovers and key sacks to close out games and were above average in points per drive allowed in the fourth quarter and touchdowns/drive in the fourth quarter.
Is he spread too thin, too soon?
I’m not saying I think defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver would have all the answers, either, but this has become a deeply-entrenched, personality flaw of the Ravens. And while DeCosta is the common denominator, he ain’t fixing it and he won’t be taking any accountability for it and he hasn’t been able to fix it despite inheriting a two-time MVP quarterback. So Minter best consider any and all options to redistribute game-day responsibilities to try to keep his defense from falling apart late.
The Ravens fourth-quarter rankings:
Yards: 113/G (29th) Pass Yds: 94/G (31st) First Downs: 7/G (29th)
Pts/Drive: 3.5 (29th) TD/Drive: 37.5% (28th) Points Allowed : 56 (30th)
Watson picked them apart in the middle of the field – an issue for years – in mustering two scoring drives in the fourth quarter after virtually nothing in the first 45 minutes.
“The frustrating part is the fact that we lost,” defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike said. “That was a game that we believed that we should have won, and we didn't. We didn't make the plays that we were supposed to make. [We have to give] credit to the Browns, but that's on us, and we are going to get it fixed."
The Ravens corners and safeties still do not have an interception all season (Kyle Hamilton’s pick came when he was deployed as a linebacker). Free safety Malaki Starks at least broke a pass up. But when Browns head coach Todd Monken – one of the coaches the Ravens fired – opened up the pass game late when he had to, Baltimore suffered.
Deshaun Watson threw for 94 yards on them in the fourth quarter and rookie KC Concepcion, who works the slot where the Ravens really stink , finally got going. Minter benched struggling rookie nickelback Chandler Rivers on defense but the problems persisted. Hmm.
Minter doesn’t want to blitz or go with heavy fronts, but his nickel and dime defenses got exposed in the fourth quarter once more (again, I don’t see play makers). Seems he gets pretty predictable late in games and better change his spots some. Here are the season numbers in the fourth quarter:
Pass Yards: 583 (31st) Comp %: 70% (24th) Opp Pass Rating : 107.8 (23rd)
Third Down Conv : 37% (22nd)
Watson can still move some but he’s no Josh Allen or Trevor Lawrence (oh yeah, the Ravens will see them soon). Anyone a little slippery gives the Ravens fits with the game on the line. The Ravens got a push off the edge and were getting pressure at times even with a three-man rush … until the fourth quarter. They're lucky Michael Penix couldn't come back in the game in OT last week.
This Sunday the Ravens had five sacks in the first three quarters but none on 14 dropbacks in the fourth quarter and just a couple of pressures. On the season in the fourth quarter:
Pressure Rate : 30.1% (26th) Sack Rate: 3.9% (T-27th)
Hendrickson got his first sack, though the finger injury and bandage on his hand still seems to be impacting him. He’d better have a helluva second half. Again, Minter didn’t have this problem with the Chargers, but he also better figure out that trying to replicate what he did there, with this GM in charge who has repeatedly put coordinators in positions where they had to gamble more than they’d like, probably won’t work, either.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Ravens Choke Away Another 10-Point Lead To Browns In 13-10 Loss: Here's How They Did It
full_text:
The choke gene may have gone dormant for a couple of weeks, but it remains. The hiring of Jesse Minter as head coach certainly didn’t eliminate it, and all the hallmarks of all the collapses of the past played out again Sunday in Cleveland. Minter’s defense once again was far worse in the second half that it’s been in the first half, they got crushed on third down when it mattered most, young kicker Tyler Loop missed a critical field goal and running back Derrick Henry, who rarely fumbles but when he does it tends to come in these collapses, gave the ball away late, too.
And so, for the 16th time since 2019 the Baltimore Ravens lost a game in which they led by double digits, this time, 13-10, to the Browns and rookie head coach Todd Monken, Baltimore’s former offensive coordinator who was fired along with John Harbaugh, because of all those  blown leads and blown games. Minter now has blown three leads of 10 points or more himself, and he’s lost two of them, and his second-half adjustments remain quite questionable.
“In all three phases we had chances to gain separation,” Minter said after the game.  "It was our own self-inflicted things – we put ball on the ground and missing a kick, getting a penalty down in the low redzone allowing the game to get there.”
The Browns lead the AFC North, while the Ravens fell to 4-2. The Ravens hope to get two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson back from his ankle injury next week. Backup Snoop Huntley, who was great for two drives in Week 5 but is a very limited passer and a player the Ravens quit on after the 2024 season for myriad reasons, could generate almost nothing. The Ravens had 235 net yards (despite the Browns being down two top defensive tackles) and they will face more probing questions about their inability to manage leads and beat teams they should beat when getting up that big.
A week ago Minter opined how the overtime win at Atlanta could be the start of a new identity for the team. Welp. Baltimore scored on its first two drives, then not again and Minter's defense gets worse as games go on. They allowed 130 yards in the fourth quarter and eight first downs and it's the same as it's always been there. No more Harbaugh and Zach Orr to blame, but you could certainly wonder why the guy who puts together overprices choking defenses keeps his job (mediocre-at-best GM Eric DeCosta).
Here’s what you need to know about how it went down, in DeCosta's record 16th choke at the helm:
The Ravens had a great chance to make it a two-score game in the fourth quarter when young kicker Tyler Loop, who continues to struggle for consistency but did hit a game-winning kick in Brazil l ast month, pushed a 48-yard attempt that could have made it a 13-3 game, and the Ravens fell into a funk.
It’s a kick he has to make and looked like some key misses in the past. The next time the Ravens got the ball running back Derrick Henry, who was bottled up after a hot start, broke free for a strong first-down run but was stripped of the ball, setting up the Browns in Baltimore territory. And, after controversial pass interference call on third own, Cleveland capped the drive with a TD run to tie it at 10.
On the ensuing kickoff, Rasheen Ali muffed the ball, putting the Ravans back at their own 15 to start the drive, and the tenor of the game has shifted entirely from the point of the missed field goal on.
"I didn't hit the ball clean," Loop said after the game, while continuing his refrain about sticking to his process.
This was a rough day for Henry. The Ravens got the perimeter run game going, tearing off first-down runs off left tackle and right tackle. But the Browns started to run blitz more and crowd the line of scrimmage and dominated the final three quarters with their defensive line against the Ravens makeshift offensive line.
Henry had eight rushes for 41 yards in the first quarter .. and then nine for 17 the rest of the day. He repeatedly got bottled up and tackled in the in backfield in short yardage situations again and could not make an impact in the second half and his fumble was devastating and, while he does it rarely, when he it does happen it tends to be part of Baltimore’s overall collapse. It conjures too many images of past choke jobs.
"I need to be better," Henry said. "I have to take care of the ball."
The line could get no push, rookie guard-turned-center, Vega Ioane, had a few bad snaps in the second half as well, the A Gap became an issue again on sacks and pressures and it just wasn’t good enough up front.
Rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle called a great play for rookie Josh Cuevas early in the game where he was lined up at guard before catching a pass, but he did not get enough players involved in the run game, including Justice Hill.
The Ravens cannot push the ball downfield at all with this backup quarterback, which has always been my biggest issue with him. This was a tough assignment with him on the road in a divisional game with the Ravens compromised from a personnel standpoint, but he was shaky.
Huntley refused to use his legs as much as he should have against a defense that plays so much man coverage, especially when the Browns began selling out to eliminate running back Derrick Henry. His mobility provided no relief, his decision making suffered as the game went on and he was very lucky some lob passes in the middle of the field were not picked off, including a pass right at a Browns defender late in the fourth quarter.
Huntley averaged 5.3 yards per attempt, the Ravens screen game was highly lacking, $13M tight end Mark Andrews made absolutely no impact in the passing game whatsoever, and the combination of this quarterback and these targets was problematic.
Kyle Hamilton was a menacing figure around the line of scrimmage and seemed to have a great feel what former Monken was doing with the offense at all times.
Hamilton delivered a thumping tackle on running back Jaleel McLaughlin on a screen pass with the Browns backed up deep in the first half. He negated a Browns first down on an inside run with the game tight in the second half while engaged with a guard – yeah, a guard. And he blew up Browns talented rookie KC Concepcion on a designed screen in the third quarter for a loss at a time when the Browns were starting to gain a modicum of offensive momentum.
Hamilton was a factor stuffing the run and serving as a deterrent all day. On a second-and-short run blitz in the fourth quarter he had another stuff for a loss. It’s too bad more teammates could not come up with individual moments at critical times, but this defense has earned the chocking reputation in large part because of that.
Rookie receiver Ja’Kobi Lane has barely played this season, suffering a wrist injury in the first half of Week 1 that required a surgical procedure and landed him in Injured Reserve. Lane was an immediate sensation this summer at training camp and in the preseason, quickly establishing himself as a starter but it remained to be seen how quickly he could find his way in this offense after staccato start to his career.
No worries, as it turns out.
Lane caught his first four targets and all were critical plays; all produced first downs and he helped out Huntley on third-and-10 and was a problem working the middle of the field, where it became apparent in camp he was most comfortable. Lane came through on third-and-six on two occasions as well and also had an 11 yard gain on first down.
On a day in which the scope of the passing game was going to be limited and Andrews a shell of what he used to be and with starting receiver Rashod Bateman limited in practice all week and barely playing in this game before departing with injury, Lane being a chain mover was a big deal in an ugly, field position divisional ball game.
The Ravens have been one of the league’s premier defensive teams in the first half all season. The problems have come, consistently, after halftime.
Sunday was more of the same, and the most…

title: Four Ravens X-Factors For Clash vs. Browns
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens will continue the 2026 regular season with the second leg of a two-game road stint against the Cleveland Browns in Week 6 , and the difference in the game could come down to how an individual player performs when it matters most or over the course of the game by capitalizing on their opportunities when presented with them.
With a win, the Ravens improve to 5-1 and would further strengthen their hold on the top spot in the AFC North division standings. A loss would, at worst, tie them for second place with the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals if they both win on Sunday.
Here are four players who could wind up tilting the scales in favor of the Ravens and first-year head coach Jesse Minter.
The polarizing third-round rookie will be making his long-awaited return to the lineup after being activated from injured reserve on Saturday following a full week of practice. Lane was the unquestioned star of the Ravens' training camp and preseason, making highlight-reel catches on a daily basis by showing off his impressive hands and catch radius. His regular-season debut was cut short in Week 1 after he suffered a fractured wrist and had his first career touchdown negated by a penalty.
His size and length will make him a dangerous weapon in the red zone, a mismatch in one-on-one contested catch situations and an alluring target underneath when the Ravens need to pick up a first down and the opposing defense is too busy keying in on Zay Flowers, who is having a sensationally productive start to the season.
Even though the Browns rank in the bottom half of the league in rushing offense and top running back Quinshon Judkins is out with an ankle injury, they'll still look to establish some sort of ground game. The fifth-year veteran will be key in ensuring Todd Monken and Co. can't gash them between the tackles by taking on and defeating double teams. He did a great job helping lead that charge against one of the best rushing attacks last week and will need to do so again versus one of the worst.
The 11th-year journeyman veteran made his Ravens debut last week and played 19 offensive snaps in place of fellow blocking specialist Durham Smythe, who suffered a season-ending torn Achellies in Week 4. With fourth-round rookie Matthew Hibner out for this game due to a hand injury, Vannett will almost certainly see the field even more often in this game, especially as lead blocker on the edge or from the backfield, an area he shined in limited action against the Atlanta Falcons .
The second-year pro has been a tackling machine over the past two weeks for the Ravens defense after struggling mightily in that aspect of the game at the start of the season. He led the team with a season-high 10 tackles last week, tying his single-game career high, and it marked the first game of his career with multiple tackles for a loss. He'll help limit yards after the catch, snuff out underneath routes and can bring the heat as a blitzer.
