His coverage on the Ravens and other NFL teams has been featured on Heavy.com/sports, Maryland Sports Blog and most recently Baltimore Beatdown from 2021 until 2025.

title: The Ravens Inactives For Week 6 With Lamar Jackson Out
full_text:
The Ravens ruled out two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson (ankle) on Friday yet again but still faced numerous critical medical decision to make before Sunday’s kickoff in Cleveland.
Rookie coach Jesse Minter is facing his first AFC North opponent with an injury report that stretched to 19 names midweek. Baltimore ruled out Jackson, center Cam Jurgens (concussion), defensive lineman Broderick Washington (ankle) and rookie tight end Matthew Hibner (hand). The team has had to juggle its offensive line every week all season, Jurgens has not appeared in two games since general manager Eric DeCosta made a desperate move to land him and Baltimore was once again dealing with injuries to guards as well, with John Simpson playing through a groin problem and Andrew Vorhees (foot) and Emery Jones (ankle) both listed as questionable.
And the Ravens had to decide if third-round pick Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) was healthy and conditioned enough to play his first game since Week 1, when the promising youngster suffered an injury in the first half and has not played since. Lane was one of the stories of the summer and the preseason and quickly worked himself into a starting role with the team, and with Baltimore dealing with injuries at tight end and with $13M “move” tight end Mark Andrews struggling mightily , having a big receiver (6-foot-4) available for backup quarterback Snoop Huntley is a big deal.
Lane was cleared to play for the first time since Week 1, while Vorhees was not.
The Ravens welcomed back $30M edge rusher Trey Hendrickson after a two-week absence due to a procedure on his finger. They are as healthy as they have been all season up front on defense – Washington is a rotational run stuffer at this point – all season. The defense in particular has been in better health than the offensive side of the ball, yet the offense has carried the team to the 4-1 start.
Undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano was once again active and serving as the primary backup to Huntley. The Ravens are hopeful that Jackson, who has yet to take the practice field since suffering the ankle injury just before halftime in Week 4, can return to practice this week with the Bengals traveling to Baltimore in Week 7, with Minter continuing to refer to him as “day-to-day” this week and Jurgens should also be cleared to begin practicing fully next week barring any setbacks with his return from concussion protocol.
Rookie receiver Elijah Sarratt was a healthy scratch as was safety K'von Wallace

title: Three Primary Reasons The Ravens Should Beat The Browns Sunday
full_text:
The Ravens were projected to compete for a Super Bowl before the season began. The Browns were projected to compete for the first-overall pick.
While the injury report may be daunting for the Ravens and no Lamar Jackson (ankle) at quarterback is certainly a big deal, this is also a football game Sunday at Cleveland that they should find a way to win. It’s the last time they are certain to be a favorite for a while with teams like the Bengals and Jaguars and Bills looming and it’s Jesse Minter’s first AFC North game and plenty of individuals on this roster realize just how difficult winning in Cleveland has been for this organization.
As always, there are a handful of critical matchups that will go a long way to deciding this football game  and, like most divisional games, this will very likely come down to which team controls the line of scrimmage. Line play will be everything and the Ravens should have the combination of $30M/year edge rusher Trey Hendrickson and $20M/year defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike on the field for longer than ever before, and at closer to full health than ever before ( they’ve played just 32 snaps together all season ).
The Ravens have, on paper, three primary advantages heading into this game that they must lean into and find a way to exploit. They provide the path to victory and explain why Baltimore is still a field-goal favorite on the road despite their injuries. Here’s how and why they should win this game.
Rookie offensive play caller Declan Doyle said Derrick Henry would see a lot of the football and didn’t back off another 300-carry season for him (he’s never done it three straight years) and, well, Henry has run the ball more times through five weeks than any age 32 RB since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger.
Guess who leads the NFL with 113 carries? You got it, with eight more than Jahmyr Gibbs (Lions). The Browns are allowing 4.5/carry and are 30th in Expected Points Added and Success Rate against the run. Their premier defensive tackle and do-everything linebacker are both on the injury report. Every reason in the world to keep this close and test them over and over with volume and multiplicity on the run game (more carries for QB Snoop Huntley, we presume HYPE GAM and some receivers as well and not necessarily just Zay Flowers).
Baltimore is as healthy up front on defense as it has been all season, Madubuike is all the way back after missing more than a year with a neck injury and they just shutdown the best running back in the NFL – Bijan Robinson – on the road in Atlanta last Sunday night.
We wonder if Browns coach Todd Monken, former Ravens offensive coordinator who knows this group well, will even mess around with establishing the run all the much and will just try to throw his way to the lead and attack a suspect secondary . Still, it’s very difficult to win games in the AFC North without being able to sustain a run game and we don’t fancy the Browns rank 30th in the NFL in EPA/designed run play (-0.22).
The Browns QB hasn’t thrown in the towel in the regular season – he certainly tried to do it in the preseason – and he’s been playing decent football. But his legs are not what they used to be, and when he holds the ball he becomes a double agent.
Watson is being sacked on 11.4% of his dropbacks , this Browns offensive line has big issues all around and this guy will turn the ball over. He is also a notoriously slow starter and if the Ravens can run their way to the lead in the first half they should have success taking the air out of the ball in the second half. Watson is in the bottom third in the NFL in air yards per attempt, pushing the ball downfield is not a forte for either QB in this game, but Huntley has the benefit of what should be a robust run game to put him in down and distances to succeed.

title: Five Storylines For Ravens' Divisional Matchup vs. Browns
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens will be on the road again in Week 5 for their first game against an AFC North opponent when they take on the Cleveland Browns on Sunday afternoon.
Coming off a thrilling victory over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 5 in primetime , in which they had to pull off a late rally and force overtime to extend their winning streak, the Ravens are currently holding the best record in the division at 4-1, while the other three teams are tied for second at 3-2.
There are several intriguing storylines surrounding this divisional matchup between these two rival teams. Here are the top four.
With two-time league MVP Lamar Jackson officially being ruled out after missing the entire week of practice for the second week in a row since suffering an ankle sprain midway through the Ravens' Week 3 victory over the Tennessee Titans, his Pro Bowl backup will be making a second straight start this upcoming Sunday. Huntley performed exceptionally well in last week's overtime thriller over the Atlanta Falcons after getting all of the reps with the first-team offense leading up to the game.
The seventh-year veteran went 24-of-32 for 201 passing yards and a pair of touchdowns and scored the game-winning touchdown on a quarterback sneak. He is now 3-0 in his last three starts in place of Jackson since rejoining the team last year, two of which came in primetime and all were against NFC opponents.
As the next man up again, this will mark his first start against a division rival since Week 18 of the 2023 season, when the Ravens had the division crown and the AFC's top seed, and decided to rest several key starters against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Unlike that game, this one has much higher stakes and they'll need Huntley to be on his 'A' game with first place on the line.
"[Huntley]'s a really good player, and he's got a great demeanor," head coach Jesse Minter. "He's got great poise. He has great respect amongst his teammates. He's just [an] infectious personality. Infectious can be different, [but] he's just cool, calm, collected, confident — that to me, that's infectious. When he's in there, that's kind of how the guys feel, and it's really no different with Lamar."
While the Ravens' home record has been abysmal, dating back to last season's franchise-worst six losses, they've been far more successful away from the confines of M&T Bank Stadium. In addition to being perfect 3-0 on the road through the first five weeks of this season, their 21-7 record playing outside of Baltimore since 2023 is the best in the league, as is their point differential, turnover differential and offense with an average of nearly 400 total yards.
Their running game has traveled especially well, averaging over 180 yards on the ground per road game since 2023, with an NFL-record streak of 36 consecutive road games of rushing for at least 100 yards. The Ravens are 4-4 in Cleveland during the Jackson era dating back to 2018, and this Sunday will mark Huntley's second career start against them during that span, with his first coming in Week 15 of the 2022 season.
Through the first four weeks, the Ravens were among the most penalized teams in the league, having been flagged 10-plus times for over 100 yards twice in that span, including season-highs with 13 flags for 131 yards in Week 4. They managed to finally buck that trend in primetime against the Falcons with a season-low five penalties for 40 yards against the Falcons. The bulk of their flags were attributed to the offense, as they were not only still getting acclimated to running the Declan Doyle offense in live action, but they also had shuffling pieces on the offensive line and at the skill positions due to players going down and even being lost for the season due to injuries.
It might've been the fact that they were playing with a small margin of error, with a backup quarterback under a national spotlight for the first time this season, that made them dial in even more last week. Nonetheless, they find themselves in a similar situation heading into this matchup and will need to do their best to repeat the feat or do even better.
Overall, the Ravens rank in the middle of the pack when it comes to passing yards allowed per game with 223.6, and for the past four weeks, nearly half and sometimes more than half of that production has come from the connection between the opposing quarterback and his top wideout. They've allowed a 100-plus-yard receiver in three straight games during their win streak. Even though Chris Olave fell just shy of reaching the century mark in Week 2, he was unguardable when the New Orleans Saints needed him most as they spoiled the Ravens' home opener in an upset.
This trend wouldn't be especially puzzling if the Ravens didn't have one of the league's most talented defensive backfields, which they've invested four first-round picks and free-agent resources in over the years. They've had their top two cornerbacks, Nate Wiggins and Marlon Humphrey, make big plays in key moments against these upper-echelon wideouts, but haven't been able to fully put the clamps on for a full or even most of the game. The Browns' leading receiver through five weeks is second-round rookie Denzel Boston with 330 receiving yards, three touchdowns and a league-leading 20.6 yards per catch.
"Every team has a good one. I feel fortunate that we have good corners," defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver said. "We don't really have to necessarily travel to people. I think we do in certain spots just because of specific skill sets of our guys, but we feel confident in all the DBs that we do have. In terms of the guys that we've faced thus far, we've had our good days and bad days. But I think, just collectively as a whole, that group is starting to gain confidence."
Before becoming Cleveland's head coach this offseason, replacing Kevin Stefanski, a two-time AP Coach of the Year, Todd Monken spent the previous three seasons from 2023-25 orchestrating the most prolific offense in franchise history, including what should've been back-to-back MVP-winning seasons for Jackson in his first two at the helm. Even without their star dual-threat signal caller, Monken is just as familiar with the strengths and weaknesses of several returning players on offense and defense.
"I'm not playing defense. I just know that he's going to try to give us [his] best shot, especially starting the game," Huntley said. "We have to be ready for all the different little gimmicks that he has for our game plan, and we [will] just go from there."
The Ravens have a lot of new pieces on both sides of the ball that Monken is not familiar with, a whole new scheme on offense and a slightly different scheme on defense. It's not like Jon Gruden facing the former Oakland Raiders in the Super Bowl, as the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' head coach in 2002, when he knew his former team's entire playbook. Still, he has some insight into how a Huntley-led offense and overall team will approach this game because he successfully pulled it off twice last year in impressive fashion.
"[Monken] has a great game plan, and he's a great coach," Huntley said "We have to be ready to put our thinking caps on and be ready to go follow our keys and win us a game."
Josh is a writer for Baltimore Ravens On SI focusing primarily on original content and reporting. He provides analysis, breakdowns, profiles, and reports on important news and transactions from and about the Ravens. His professional resume as a sports reporter includes covering local events, teams, and athletes in his hometown of Anchorage, Alaska for Anchorage Daily News. His coverage on the Ravens and other NFL teams has been featured on Heavy.com/sports, Maryland Sports Blog and most recently Baltimore Beatdown from 2021 until 2025.

title: The 3 Matchups That Could Decide Ravens At Browns In Week 6
full_text:
The Ravens are probably not going to blow out the Browns.
Baltimore is just 4-4 in the last eight trips to Cleveland, and these have been almost always one-score games . With backup quarterback Snoop Huntley in for Lamar Jackson and the Ravens dealing with a looong injury list , the margins get even more slim. Divisional games tend to be tricky and this is the first one for Ravens rookie head coach Jesse Minter, while Browns coach Todd Monken, the Ravens former offensive coordinator, has already upset the Steelers.
There will be handful of plays that determine this game. The Ravens quite likely are going to need to navigate a fourth quarter in a manner that has been difficult for them going back six years. These are some matchups I will be paying very close attention to:
The Ravens are doing the right thing here and not getting cute trying to force new center Cam Jurgens into the center spot after making an utterly-desperate trade to land him while in the concussion protocol. Ioane has been better than anyone could have hoped for thrust into the center spot against elite competition and I will say it again – he is quite likely the best center on this team, already.
Mason Graham was selected in the top 10 for a reason, and he has his moments as a rookie but he is blowing people up in Year 2. He is a game wrecker, and he was dominating up until he picked up a knee injury very early in the win over the Steelers. He is listed as questionable for this game. If he plays, I expect him to be a handful. And if Ioane can handle this pass protection assignment the way he did Dexter Lawrence in his first start at center, and he helps the run game crank at the second level like it did against the Falcons the Ravens are going to win this game barring a turnover nightmare.
Graham has four sacks in four games and is tied for the lead among NFL defensive tackles. Cleveland is 30th in run defense Expected Points Added. Road grading will go a long way to winning this game.
The Ravens secondary has been a mess , there are no two ways about it, and coverage for the corners and free safeties has been bad and it’s been particularly awful in the slot where QBs are completing 74% of their passes for a 121.8 pass rating. Yuck.
Concepcion is in the slot 60% of the time he has a skillset that is in the vein of Ravens dervish Zay Flowers and Monken will have big plans for him. He can kill you with YAC and the first-round pick can win downfield, too, and with a well-balanced passing attack I’m not sure the Ravens want top corner Nate Wiggins traveling inside to the slot with him, but maybe they do.
My suspicion is that when rookie slot corner Chandler Rivers is on the field Deshaun Watson is going after him. Watson isn’t pushing it deep, his OL is not good so he will deliver it quickly and he knows how Concepcion can turn it into a big play after the catch.
Rivers has allowed nine catches on 11 targets in the last three games for 120 yards and a touchdown. Marlon Humphrey on Concepcion in the slot would be tricky unless he is jamming and beating him up at the line, but this secondary has issues. Period.
Very interested to see how Minter plays this. Fannin can be a handful and the Ravens have not been targeted much by tight ends in general this season. Do we see some Trenton Simpson here? I have issues with free safety Malaki Starks in coverage and given the volume in the Browns passing game and the quality of options he can’t focus on a one-man funnel like some of the previous offenses they faced.
Hamilton is reading the ball well underneath as are all the LBs, who have accounted for all three interceptions this season. Fannin needs to get particular attention on first down. They like taking shots with him – he isn’t a big air yards guy in general but on first down he averages 11.2 yards per catch and nearly 10 air yards per target and he is a tone setter to get drives going.

title: Breaking Down How The Ravens Should Attack The Browns With Snoop Huntley At QB
full_text:
Hopefully, two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson is back for the Ravens next week to continue his pursuit of a third such award and his first Lombardi Trophy. In the meantime, its up to veteran backup Snoop Huntley to try to manage the team to another win, this time at Cleveland.
The assignment isn’t all that different from a week ago. The Browns, like the Falcons, are getting elite pressure rates without blitzing but Cleveland has superior cover corners and more individual talent overall on defense. And unlike the Falcons, the Browns can’t stop the run at all, and even though Atlanta entered last week leading the NFL in that regard the Ravens still rolled up 200 yards on the ground against them .
Thankfully, the Ravens are not overcomplicating things by trying to force recent trade acquisition Cam Jurgens – a desperate trade by a desperate general manager – into this game as he comes back from a concussion and Huntley gets to work with the same center as a week ago. That would be surging rookie Vega Ioane ( one of their five best players thus far ) and the same offensive line, likely, for that matter, pending final decisions on the injury report regarding guard Andrew Vorhees (might as well stick with Emery Jones).
The Ravens are just 4-4 in their last eight trips to Cleveland and weird things tend to happen there and new Browns coach Todd Monken is the Ravens former offensive coordinator and will have them fired up for this game . It won’t be easy but rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle, who might be on a head coach fast track if he keeps this up, had a great approach to managing Huntley through the road assignment last week and much of that will apply here, too.
No surprise the first play of the game last week was an end around for Zay Flowers, and the Ravens will hunt explosives with YAC horizontally again with Huntley wise not to break with who he is and try to force the ball downfield against these corners. He is best when the ball comes out quickly and the Browns have a legit rush – top four in pressure rate and only 20th in blitz rate.
The ball needs to come out quickly and thee could be more tackle eligible plays with the Ravens further compromised at tight end this week. Exploiting the flats and designing a few more screens for Derrick Henry, like his TD scamper last week, are in order as he is second on the team in YAC.
If Huntley starts patting the ball and holding the ball, problems will rise. Here are his career splits when under duress; he has a 27% sack rate when pressured and Jared Verse and Mason Graham (questionable) will wreck him. We could see reserve RB Justice Hill seeing his highest target rate of the season and catching 3-5 passes.
Huntley when Pressured: 48% comp, 4.9 yds/att, 62.7 rtg
Huntley When Not Pressured: 74% comp, 6.3/att, 91.6 rtg
Henry has already run 113 times – more than any age 32 running back through five weeks since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger. At some point they will need to dial it back (he is on pace for an outrageous number of carries). But not this week.
The Browns are holding teams below 60% completions and tamping down the pass game but are 30th in Expected Points Added and Success Rate vs the run. And they have had their share of injuries to the front seven and missed practices. Now’s not to the time to get too cute. Multiplicity in the run game was everything last week and should be again Sunday.
Henry is averaging 22.6 rushes/game and we suspect he touches the ball upwards of 25 times.
The Browns are playing man coverage 44.4% of the time, far and away most in the NFL. The Bears are second at 31.5% and the league average is 18%. Perhaps they change their spots but they have multiple man corners they love. Problem is, they are a blow average team in QB rating and completion percentage when in man, and Huntley has incredibly tilted splits in this regard for his career.
Huntley vs. Man : 63% comp, 8 TD – 2 INT, 8.3 Air Yd/att, 97.1 rtg
Huntley vs Zone : 70% comp, 3 TD – 8 INT, 7.1 AY/att, 79.1 rtg
Playing all that man means defenders have their back to the play quite a bit and that helps quarterbacks get extra yards on the ground. Huntley can still move pretty well, we expect his legs to be a bigger part of the plan here and the Browns are 24th in EPA vs QB runs and haven’t been tested much. We think that’s about to change. Huntley for a run of 15 yards or more and over 30 rushing yards feels about right to us.

title: Ravens Make Determination On Lamar Jackson's Status For Sunday
full_text:
Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson remained unable to take the practice field at all this week leading to him being ruled out for Week 6 with an ankle injury, while new center Cam Jurgens (concussion) and rookie tight end Matthew Hibner (hand) are also out, head coach Jesse Minter said.
Minter has continued to refer to Jackson’s ankle injury, which caused him to watch the second half of Week 4’s win over the Titans, as a “day-to-day” situation though we reported shortly after the MRI that Jackson was highly likely to miss at least two weeks . There was never any chance of him playing last week, as we heard at the time, and the odds this week were never strong and once he did not take the field at all Wednesday the Ravens began shifting them game plan for back-up Snoop Huntley, who was great in the clutch in an overtime win at Atlanta Sunday night.
The decision to take this course of action was in Jackson’s “best interest” as Minter reiterated after practice on Friday, and while he has not committed to a timetable next week, barring a setback, expect to see Jackson back on the practice field at least in some capacity Wednesday to face the Bengals in another big AFC North game.
Huntley, who spent time with the Browns last season, doesn’t get rattled, though he will be facing an elite pass rush, and the game plan is likely to be very much like last week, with a heavy emphasis on screens and horizontal passes and the perimeter run game and look for Derrick Henry, doing things no age 32 running back has ever done before to carry a heady load against Cleveland’s struggling run defense (30th in Expected Points Added vs the run)
Jurgens was in concussion protocol when Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta made a panic move to trade a second-round pick in 2028 and a fifth-round pick in 2027, for him. Jurgens is still learning this offense, he has not even had a full practice to begin snapping regularly with the quarterbacks and he was ruled our for Cleveland with the sense Week 7 is good for him. Rookie guard Vega Ioane is set to start his third straight game at center and he has been nothing short of a revelation for this football team Hon a shaky offensive line.
Hibner was in line for a bigger role with the Ravens losing “Joker” tight end Durham Smythe for the season and with veteran tight end Mark Andrews taking 16 points off the board against the Falcons and unable to win downfield anymore . However, the hand injury he suffered last week took him off the practice field this week. Minter said the team is not considering an IR stint for the promising player and believes it is more a matter of a week or two.
Trey Hendrickson, the team’s big offseason signing , is set to return after missing two games with a procedure on his finger. He said he knew in Week 1 he would require surgery at some point after suffering the injury, and he and Nnamdi Madubuike have a chance to supercharge a sagging pass defense with more pressure after playing just 32 snaps together thus far and not with either in top form.

title: Four Winners & Two Losers From Bills Hard-Fought Win Over Raiders
full_text:
For the second week in a row, the Buffalo Bills won a game by just three points. Buffalo had two games on the West Coast, playing against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 5 and winning 37-34 in overtime .
They stayed out west this week and played the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. Again, this one came down to the final minutes, as an onside kick recovery from Khalil Shakir secured the 33-30 win for the Bills.
Now at 5-1, they're going into their bye week with plenty of confidence. As for their latest win, let's take a look back and identify a few winners and losers from Week 6.
Buffalo's defense has had its share of issues, but they've been able to make some key plays when needed most. That was the case in this one, with Dorian Williams recording his first career interception in the third quarter.
Intercepted by Dorian Williams ‼️ BUFvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/jJIjSzXYMb
The Bills were up 16-13, and Williams picked off Kirk Cousins at the Las Vegas 32. That allowed Buffalo to extend its lead to 23-13, giving them full control of the game.
Joshua Palmer had a couple of early wins this year, catching a game-winning 34-yard touchdown in Week 1 and a 43-yard touchdown in Week 2. He even had a 37-yard reception in the first half against the Raiders. Unfortunately, he also had a costly mistake near the end of the second quarter.
Buffalo was leading 13-10 with two minutes remaining and facing a second-and-nine from their own 31. Josh Allen hit Palmer right in the numbers for what should have been a first down, but Palmer tried to catch it with his body, and it bounced off his chest. That drop led to a third-and-long, and Allen was sacked. That gave the Raiders the ball back with 1:40 to go, allowing them to tie it up at 13.
This season has been all about redemption for Keon Coleman . The former second-round pick has become a true playmaker and was once again on the right side of an exciting play. On third-and-eight from the 12, Josh Allen somehow avoided what looked like a sure sack and flipped the ball into the end zone. That's where a wide-open Coleman hauled in the pass for a 12-yard touchdown, his third of the year. It was also the third consecutive week that Coleman caught a touchdown pass.
How did Josh Allen make this TD pass to Keon Coleman? BUFvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CNLw6KW2tC
Coleman might not be a WR1, but he just keeps delivering. This week, he had 59 yards and a touchdown on four receptions.
No player was more of a problem for the Bills on Sunday than safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson. It was bad enough that he missed two tackles early in the game, but he also got himself ejected. Following Igbinosun's holding penalty near the end of the second quarter, Gardner-Johnson was ejected for spitting in the direction of tight end Brock Bowers. It was an unacceptable act from Gardner-Johnson and one that's sure to lead to a fine and perhaps even more punishment.
The spotlight was on James Cook after he fumbled twice in Week 5, including one in overtime that was recovered by the Rams. Joe Brady said after the game that Cook needed to take better care of the ball , and he did that on Sunday.
Not only did Cook protect the football, but he put together a sensational drive late in the fourth quarter. Las Vegas had just tied it up at 23, and Cook had 20 yards rushing and added one reception for 26 yards on a seven-play, 66-yard drive. He capped that off with a touchdown, giving Buffalo the lead back for good, 30-23.
Once again, Josh Allen did Josh Allen things.
Allen threw for 255 yards and two touchdowns, but it was his mobility that stood out. He had just one yard rushing, but he spent much of the day escaping pressure and finding the open receiver downfield. It was a tough fight throughout the day and Allen set the tone for the Bills.

title: Dalton Kincaid Injury Update: Latest News on Bills TE's Status in Week 6 Game
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills have an injury concern with tight end Dalton Kincaid in the second half of the Week 6 game against the Las Vegas Raiders.
Kincaid got banged up in the third quarter before exiting the field. He was later spotted going into the medical tent to get checked out. He appeared to be favoring his ribs.
Prior to his exit, Kincaid had six receptions for 24 yards on seven targets. He would have had a touchdown, but his scoring catch was negated due to a penalty.
Follow our tracker below for the latest updates on Kincaid's status for the rest of the Week 6 game against the Raiders.
UPDATE: Great news, as Kincaid has returned to the game.
Certainly a stunning turn of events after it looked like his day might be over when he went to the locker room.
UPDATE: The Bills announced that Kincaid is officially questionable to return with an injury to his ribs.
"Bills TE Dalton Kincaid (ribs) is questionable to return," WGR 550's Sal Capaccio relayed.
The fact that Kincaid went to the locker room is not a good sign for his chances of returning to the game. The good news is, the Bills might not need him with a two-score lead going into the fourth quarter.
After his trip to the medical tent, Kincaid was spotted going off to the locker room to get evaluated more.
Again, we're not sure what exactly Kincaid is dealing with as of this writing. We'll update this page once more information is available.
With Kincaid out for now, the Bills are going to need more work out of Dawson Knox and Jackson Hawes.
Kincaid was phenomenal over the first two weeks of the season and looked to be well on his way to a career year, with the Bills tight end recording 12 catches for 225 yards and one touchdown in that span.
However, since then, Kincaid has just 10 catches for 78 yards and no touchdowns, numbers that include his Week 6 stats before he exited with his injury.
Kincaid's lack of production has been especially glaring because the Bills have been without their No. 1 wide receiver, DJ Moore, for multiple games this season as he tries to get right after suffering a shoulder injury in Week 2 that he re-aggravated in Week 4. Moore has missed each of the last two games with the issue.
"I got to be better," head coach Joe Brady after Week 4. "There's no reason Dalton Kincaid should have two targets, especially with the flow of the game and how that goes. I got to find a way to get the ball in his hands and do a better job of that."
It goes without saying the Bills have to find a way to get Kincaid more involved in the offense. There is just no excuse for how little he has done since his red-hot start.

title: C.J. Gardner-Johnson Ejected: Why Bills DB Was Kicked Out of Week 6 Game
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills are going to be thin at safety for the second half of their Week 6 showdown with the Las Vegas Raiders, with safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson being ejected for spitting in the direction of tight end Brock Bowers.
While trying to protect a 13-10 lead late in the second quarter, the Bills were flagged for defensive holding. The announcing crew of Jim Nantz and J.J. Watt were trying to figure out if the refs got it right, as they said the penalty was on Davison Igbinosun, but it appeared Cole Bishop could have been called as well.
During that discussion, the refs threw a second flag and it was announced that Gardner-Johnson was not only hit with a flag, but he was disqualified from the game. Video was then shown of him spitting toward No, 89.
CJ Gardner-Johnson seen spitting on Brock Bowers leading to his ejection pic.twitter.com/IpTL70ZXe5 https://t.co/pahLVvXTnV
Nantz said it best afterward, stating "This is about as disrespectful as it gets." For Gardner-Johnson, he's also sure to get a fine from the league after the unacceptable act.
In addition to his penalty, Gardner-Johnson was struggling to finish plays. He had two missed tackles during the first two quarters, including one that allowed tight end Michael Mayer to move Las Vegas into field goal range at the end of the half.
Buffalo was decent in pass defense in 2025 under Sean McDermott, but they weren't especially strong at safety. The Bills were forced to roll with veteran Jordan Poyer and this year, they wanted to rebuild that unit.
New defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard is a believer in Cole Bishop , who had a breakout season in 2025. Outside of Bishop, they weren't loaded with talent. To address those concerns, they picked up Geno Stone and C.J. Gardner-Johnson, while also re-signing Damar Hamlin.
Gardner-Johnson has been feast or famine thus far for Buffalo. He has 25 tackles, two pass deflections, and a key interception during their Week 3 win over the Los Angeles Chargers. That said, this was a reminder that he's been a distraction throughout his career.
Gardner-Johnson often finds himself in the middle of drama. Early in his career, he drew the ire of New Orleans Saints teammate Michael Thomas, who was suspended for punching Gardner-Johnson in practice.
He also got into altercations with Javon Wims and Anthony Miller, two players who were ejected for punching the vocal safety after his taunts. Gardner-Johnson has also drawn multiple fines and has struggled to stay with teams due to his attitude. That included him being released by the Houston Texans after just three games in 2025.

title: Josh Allen Missing Top WR in Week 6 as Bills Announce Inactives at Raiders
full_text:
Quarterback Josh Allen has his full arsenal available, sans wide receiver DJ Moore, as the Buffalo Bills battle the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium.
The Bills scratched Moore, their No. 1 wide receiver, for the second game in a row due to an AC joint injury that dates back to Week 2 against the Detroit Lions.
After reaggravating the injury against the New England Patriots in Week 4, Moore was held out against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 5, seemingly to his chagrin. It was the veteran's first missed game since December 2020, ending his streak of 91 consecutive appearances spanning three different teams.
Moore did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday before participating on a limited basis on Friday. He was officially questionable to play .
"No one's gonna be 100 percent healthy right now. We just played a Monday night game. We're five weeks into the season. It's part of the grind. If guys can be out there, the anticipation is for them to be out there," said head coach Joe Brady on Wednesday.
With Moore down, fourth-round rookie wide receiver Skyler Bell is active for the second consecutive week. Even without his top target, who has 178 receiving yards and one TD over 132 offensive snaps, Allen should be able to exploit a vulnerable Raiders' defense.
Meanwhile, wide receiver Josh Palmer, who missed the October 12 win due to a shoulder injury suffered during practice, is active on Sunday against the Raiders .
Like Moore, defensive tackle Ed Oliver will miss his second straight game. Oliver, who followed the same practice pattern as Moore this last week, banged up his knee during the October 4 loss to the Patriots.
Veteran edge rusher Mike Danna along with rookie offensive linemen Jude Bowry and Ar'maj Reed-Adams round out the Bills' five-man inactive list. Buffalo declined to use either of its two practice squad elevations this week.
Along with Palmer, defensive lineman TJ Sanders and slot cornerback Dee Alford all carried questionable tags into Sunday. All three are active.

title: Four Bills' Player Prop Bets for Week 6 Road Matchup vs. Vulnerable Raiders' Defense
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills look to remain perfect on the road when they visit the Las Vegas Raiders for a 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff on October 18.
The matchup sets up nicely for quarterback Josh Allen and the Bills' high-powered offense that leads the NFL in scoring (32.8). Buffalo also paces the circuit in yards per play (6.72).
Meanwhile, the Raiders feature the league's 27th-ranked defense (377.0), which has been dominated by the Kansas City Chiefs and New England Patriots in back-to-back weeks.
Here are four player prop bets that bank on the Bills' offense taking advantage of a prime opportunity in the desert. All odds are provided by DraftKings and are subject to change.
Allen has thrown three touchdown passes only once this season, in Week 2 against the depleted Detroit Lions ' secondary, but this matchup provides a good opportunity for the Bills' touchdown machine to do it again.
The Raiders are allowing 2.2 touchdown passes per game, and Drake Maye threw for four scores against them in Week 5. It simply makes sense for Buffalo to pass more than the 19 times it did against the Rams on Monday Night Football, and with an expected uptick in attempts come more chances to score through the air.
Allen, who has accounted for 15 total touchdowns (7 pass, 8 rush) already this season, threw three touchdown passes in a September 2023 win over the Raiders. At nearly 3:1 odds, it's worth backing Allen for a big day in the desert.
Cook went over 110 yards rushing in all three games that he's seen at least 20 carries. Despite the fumbling issue , I expect the Bills to show confidence and feed their bellcow at least 20 times in Week 6.
The fact that Buffalo is so effective when running the ball, suggests that Joe Brady will continue to lean on the ground game against a vulnerable Raiders' defense. While the Bills average 5.37 yards per rush play (2nd in NFL), the Raiders rank next to last in run defense by permitting 5.21 per play.
The table is set for Cook to feast on Sunday.
Davis has only eight rush yards to his credit all season, but Brady has vowed to get him more involved in the offense. While I don't see Cook's carries decreasing significantly due to the fumble problem, it's more than possible that Davis gets a few more opportunities per game.
Furthermore, Davis showed explosion on multiple occasions in Week 5. After returning the opening kickoff 70 yards, he took a second-half screen pass 31 yards down to the 1-yard line. He recorded a season-high 10 offensive snaps in the 37-34 overtime victory.
If Davis were to see four to five carries on Sunday, he should easily get to the 10-yard mark.
Kincaid made his first, and only, touchdown catch of the season in Week 2, and he hasn't seen pay dirt since. In fact, he's averaged only 2.3 targets per game over the past three weeks.
In Week 5, Kincaid was open for what could've been a walk-in touchdown on the same play where Dawson Knox failed to make a sliding catch in the end zone against the Rams.
Both Brady and Allen have recognized the need to get Kincaid more involved in the pass game like he was in Weeks 1 and 2 (12 receptions, 225 yards).
The Raiders have been vulnerable against tight ends this season, and the Bills may make it a point to target the mismatch as often as possible. It's worth noting that Kincaid caught touchdown passes in seven of his 14 appearances (including two playoff games) last year.

title: Fantasy Football Start or Sit Week 6: Dalton Kincaid, Keon Coleman, Khalil Shakir
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills struggled to move the ball through the air last week and that had a negative impact on two of the team's top three pass-catchers who were in uniform.
Tight end Dalton Kincaid and Keon Coleman struggled, with both Bills pass-catchers each posting just one catch for seven yards.
Meanwhile, Shakir had one of his best games of the season with three catches for 80 yards, although he once again failed to find pay dirt and remains scoreless through five contests.
Now, a look at our fantasy football start or sit decisions with each player for this week against the Las Vegas Raiders .
Kincaid has been nowhere to be found the last three weeks, with the Bills tight end totaling just four catches for 52 yards in that span, ranking as TE48 overall, per Fantasy Pros . Even worse, Kincaid has two catches for 14 yards the last two weeks.
On the bright side, this is a positive matchup for Kincaid against a Raiders team tied for the fifth-most fantasy points per game given up to tight ends this season, according to CBS Sports .
You can certainly justify sitting Kincaid given what we've seen the last two weeks, especially if you have another tight end who has been more consistent.
But with a shallow pool of options at tighe end, a positive matchup and the potential for Kincaid to return elite production like we saw the first two games, we're running him out there again.
Coleman took a step back last week with a lackluster performance after putting up one of the best games of his career in Week 4. But the Bills' third-year wideout still ranks as WR22 overall the last four weeks, which is flex production.
It remains to be seen if DJ Moore will play, but if not we know that two of Coleman's best games this season have come when the veteran wideout left early due to injury. One Bills beat writer doesn't think Moore will play , so take that for what it's worth.
We also know this matchup against the Raiders isn't a scary one, with Las Vegas permitting the 12th-most fantasy points to wide receivers per game in 2026.
If Moore sits, we're deploying Coleman. If Moore plays, you can still justify starting Coleman, but we wouldn't feel as good about it, especially with Shakir coming on strong of late.
Verdict: Start if Moore is ruled out, sit if Moore plays
With Moore leaving early in Week 4 and not playing in Week 5, Shakir has been the team's most consistent receiver.
Over the past two games, Shakir has tallied 11 catches for 162 yards, ranking as WR28 in that span, which puts him in the flex conversation.
As we stated, there is a belief that Moore won't play and that only clears the way more for Shakir, who draws a matchup against a Raiders defense giving up the 12th-most fantasy points per contest to receivers.
Shakir is a viable starter in Week 6, but only if Moore is ruled out.
Verdict: Start if Moore is out, sit if Moore plays

The Buffalo Bills complete their two-game western swing on Sunday afternoon in Las Vegas.

title: Will DJ Moore Play Today? Injury Update, Fantasy Advice for Bills' WR in Week 6
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills and their top wide receiver, DJ Moore, are right back in the same boat they were last week going into the Week 6 game against the Las Vegas Raiders.
Moore is trying to work through a shoulder injury that he has been dealing with since Week 2. Moore was diagnosed with an AC joint sprain after that game and re-aggravated the injury in Week 4.
Last week, Moore was given the questionable label before he sat out, and the Bills were able to overcome his absence with a 37-point performance to beat the Los Angeles Rams.
In Week 6, Moore logged just one limited practice on Friday before he was once again labeled as questionable to play. Here's what we know about Moore's status for Week 6 against the Raiders.
UPDATE: DJ Moore is officially inactive for Week 6 .
UPDATE: Moore isn't doing much during warm-ups, according to The Athletic's Joe Buscaglia .
This is the same situation as last week and Moore was ultimately ruled inactive, so there's a good chance he won't play.
We have not gotten an answer yet, either from the team or via reports.
"We'll see how they field coming off the field. Look at it on tape. See what it looked like and have discussions," head coach Joe Brady said on Friday . "I say it every week, if they're ready to go, they're gonna play."
The fact that Moore only had one limited practice during the week is a definite red flag that he doesn't have a great chance to play.
One Bills beat writer doesn't think Moore is going to play , and for good reason.
WGR 550's Sal Capaccio said on Friday that he believes the Bills are going to sit Moore because they will want to try and get him healthy and now is a good time to do so.
After facing Las Vegas in Week 6, the Bills have a bye, which allows them to give Moore another week of rest without him having to miss another game.
"My feeling is no. Not playing, that's my feeling, that he wouldn't play," Capaccio said of Moore . "He wants to play. We know that, right? He wants to play, that's just in his nature.
"But, guys, I mean, they went to L.A. and won a game without him, still scored 37 points... And then, they have a bye next week. It doesn't seem like it's smart to put him on the field unless he's actually truly healthy enough."
That would be the logical move for the Bills, who are sitting at 4-1 and are fully capable of beating Las Vegas without Moore on the field. The last thing Buffalo can afford is to see Moore's injury worsen and him miss extended time.
We suspect Moore will not play in Week 6.
Even if Moore plays, we wouldn't start him. The risk of re-injury would just be too great and he may end up leaving early again. Furthermore, waiting for him until the late window of games amounts to a roll of the dice in and of itself.
If Moore is out, Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman become starting options in fantasy football. Shakir had three for 80 last week and Coleman only had one for seven and a score, but he has proven reliable this season and ranks as WR24 overall the last three weeks, according to Fantasy Pros .

title: Three Areas Bills Must Exploit During Crucial Week 6 Matchup at Raiders
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills are looking to remain undefeated out West on Sunday afternoon.
After narrowly escaping with a three-point win in an overtime thriller against the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football —a matchup that included fireworks even after the final whistle —the Bills have just one more game before their bye, which makes the upcoming AFC meeting in Week 6 with the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium all the more important.
With the New England Patriots now biting at their heels in the divisional standings, it’s imperative that Buffalo keep stacking wins any way possible.
It won’t be easy for first-year head coach Joe Brady’s squad this afternoon, though, as the Raiders have proven to be much more competitive under fellow first-year man Klint Kubiak this season.
Even still, Kubiak’s club has dropped back-to-back games after starting September undefeated, so there are certainly chinks in the armor, so to speak, out in Las Vegas.
Here are three areas the Bills must exploit out in the desert in order to come away victorious on Sunday.
Fifth-year veteran James Cook III may be the reigning NFL rushing champion from one season ago, but he’s also tied for the lead in fumbles by a running back since 2024. Furthermore, according to StatMuse , he’s third in the league in fumbles by a player at his position since first entering the league as a second-round pick out of the University of Georgia in 2022.
And, after a recent two-fumble performance against the Rams that prompted his head coach to recently use some choice words regarding Cook’s possible usage moving forward, there’s reason to believe that maybe the team might look at some alternatives on offense in the coming weeks.
But, this Sunday against the Raiders shouldn’t be that week.
Las Vegas is 28th in the league right now against the run after allowing 140.6 yards per game through the first five weeks of the season, and—in spite of his struggles with holding on to the ball—Buffalo’s “bell-cow” ‘back is still as talented as they come, which is evidenced by the fact that he’s currently third in the NFL with 532 rushing yards behind only Kansas City’s Kenneth Walker III ( 537 yards ) and Atlanta’s Bijan Robinson ( 580 yards ).
Las Vegas will also be without promising second-year defensive lineman Tonka Hemingway, as he has been ruled out with a concussion that he sustained in the first quarter of the team’s loss last Sunday at Gillette Stadium. So far in 2026, Hemingway has played 51% of the defensive snaps, producing 14 total tackles, three pass deflections, one tackle for loss, and one quarterback hit according to Pro Football Reference .
So, given the Raiders’ struggles on defense, as well as quarterback Josh Allen’s own admitted struggles with some of the finer points of playing the team’s lead offensive position right now, it’d be a good idea for the Bills to stay persistent on the ground during their extended stay out West.
Cook is capable of correcting his mistakes , so hopefully that proves to be the case for Buffalo’s sake, and he’s able to have a big day in the running game.
It’d certainly make the whole operation run more smoothly than it has in recent weeks if the team can avoid losing the turnover battle, while also controlling the clock.
Through the first few weeks of the season, it seemed as if fourth-year tight end Dalton Kincaid was on the verge of a historic breakout campaign in 2026 .
But, after starting the first three games with 14 receptions for 263 yards and an average of 18.8 yards per catch, as well as one touchdown, things have almost come to a complete halt with Kincaid and Allen’s connection in the passing game.
It’s concerning . . . and confusing at the same time.
The former 2023 first-rounder is supposed to be one of Buffalo’s premier playmakers, but right now it’s as if he’s been phased out of the offense since fumbling against the Los Angeles Chargers at Highmark Stadium in Week 3, which is ironic considering Cook’s struggles in that department.
Over the past two weeks against the Patriots and the Rams, the team’s starting tight end has just two receptions on four targets for 14 yards. It’s not nearly enough, and it must be fixed moving forward.
With that said, this might be the week that the Bills can finally get Kincaid back on track as the Raiders have allowed opposing tight ends to catch 32-of-39 targets for 285 yards and six touchdowns so far this season, which accounts for 57 yards per game and 1.2 touchdowns per game, as well as a catch rate of 82.1%.
Last week, New England’s tight ends Hunter Henry (3 catches, 44 yards, 1 TD) and Eli Raridon (5 catches, 57 yards) combined to make eight receptions for 101 yards and a touchdown during the Patriots’ blowout victory against Las Vegas, so it makes sense for the Bills to continue stressing the Raiders’ linebackers and safeties with Kincaid, as well as Dawson Knox and Jackson Hawes.
The third area that Buffalo’s offense should look to exploit against Las Vegas basically ties in with the first two listed above.
If the Bills are able to sustain drives with the running game and manage to make multiple trips to the red zone, then it will be crucial for Allen and Co. to capitalize once within 20 yards of “paydirt”.
It was something the offense struggled with against the Patriots , and Buffalo surely doesn’t want anything wonky to occur in the final moments of a game again this week in terms of having the winner decided by a field goal attempt.
Keeping that in mind, according to FOX Sports , the Raiders are currently 29th in the NFL in red-zone touchdown rate at 77.8%, which is actually worse than Buffalo’s defensive rate ( 76.2% ) at the moment.
Using Kincaid, Knox, and Hawes in that area of the field would be a good idea, too. In Week 3, New Orleans Saints’ tight ends Juwan Johnson ( 8 catches, 53 yards, 2 TDs ) and Noah Fant ( 4 catches, 33 yards, 2 TDs ) dominated Las Vegas down near the goal line.
Running the ball down deep in Raiders’ territory with either Cook or Allen wouldn’t be a bad idea, either.

title: Bills Would be Wise to Claim Rookie Linebacker Released by Texans
full_text:
Linebacker has been one of the weakest positions for the Buffalo Bills this season. They have been leaning on Terrel Bernard and Dorian Williams, but rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr has been proving himself worthy of more snaps lately as well .
As for their starters, Bernard and Williams have each had issues adapting to Jim Leonhard's defense. That's why Bills On SI's Ralph Ventre gave the position group as a whole a C- after the first quarter of the season. Ventre says that "Bernard has looked slow while Williams appears confused at times," and believes the Bills should consider bringing up Shaq Thompson from the practice squad or giving Joe Andreessen more snaps.
Buffalo could also look for more depth, and an intriguing name just became available. On Saturday, Jordan Schultz reported that the Houston Texans would be releasing rookie Aiden Fisher, who will be available to claim on Waivers. The Bills aren't high on the priority list, but they should put in a claim and attempt to bring him in.
Sources: The #Texans are releasing rookie LB Aiden Fisher. The 7th-round pick was an All-American last season en route to helping Indiana win a national championship. He will be on waivers. pic.twitter.com/3f9YR4GCI0
Fisher was a seventh-round pick out of Indiana and has appeared in three games this season. He has 38 snaps, all on special teams, and has recorded just one tackle.
He began his collegiate career at James Madison before transferring to Indiana in 2024. He was vital to their title run in 2025 and finished his two years with the Hoosier with 215 tackles, 16 tackles for loss, six sacks, and two interceptions.
What should stand out with Fisher for the Bills is his high football IQ. During the pre-draft process, NFL.com scout Lance Zierlein praised Fisher for being a coordinator on the field , saying he can run a defense.
"Fisher is a Mike linebacker who can run the defense as an extension of his coordinator. He’s well-built with leadership and football character that are praised by teammates and coaches. Fisher has the instincts and feel of an NFL player but lacks the needed quickness and athletic ability," Zierlein wrote. "He reads play designs and gets to the action at a high rate, but a lack of range, cover talent and plus open-field tackling will make the NFL jump challenging."
The lack of range and coverage skills are what led to Fisher sliding into the final round, and could be a reason for the Bills to be concerned. That said, his intelligence and leadership make him worth taking a flier, especially as Leonhard is looking for players who fit his vision.

title: Panthers Surge Again in Power Rankings After Convincing Win
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are trending in the right direction . They've won two straight contests over preseason NFC playoff contenders and are leading the NFC South in the early going.
Their defense has improved every week since a Week 1 debacle, and the offense has been pretty good (at worst) every single week. They look like a formidable foe for other teams, something that hasn't been true in a while.
That is reflected in their Power Rankings placement. Once again, after another convincing win, the Panthers are moving on up.
The Carolina Panthers came into the game ranked 21st by Sporting News' Vinnie Iyer . Now, after winning an ugly one against the Philadelphia Eagles, Carolina has surged up to 17th in the league.
Iyer wrote, "The Panthers' high-volume passing offense with Bryce Young is now averaging a league-best 294 yards per game, ahead of the Rams, who are down to 284 per game. That game plan by Dave Canales has also opened up the running game and led to winning results."
Now, there is an argument to be had that the Panthers are ranked too low here. They should have come in higher than 21st after not playing and having beat the Detroit Lions the week before. The Panthers are still being underrated.
The Los Angeles Rams ranked ahead of the Panthers, and despite all their talent, there's no argument that the Rams are better than the Panthers right now. They have an ugly loss to the Arizona Cardinals and are 2-4.
The Detroit Lions, the team Carolina beat despite not having both starting cornerbacks, is also sitting ahead of the Panthers, which is frankly ridiculous since the two teams are both 3-2 right now.
You could also make an argument that the Panthers deserve to be higher than the Cincinnati Bengals, too, but that still puts the Panthers in the top half of the rankings rather than the bottom. It's hard to justify saying the Panthers are a bottom-half NFL team right now.
This is better, however, than the Panthers inexplicably dropping in Pete Prisco's rankings last week despite not even playing. The Panthers are trending up, though, no matter which way you slice it.
And in Iyer's list, they are the highest NFC South team, as they should be. Right now, they look like the class of the division, although the bar for that is still admittedly a bit low.

title: The Panthers Edged Out the Eagles, But These 6 Things Matter
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers should've blown out the Philadelphia Eagles. With how the two teams are currently constructed, it should have never been close, even if the final score suggests there was some space between these two teams.
So, the Panthers got a much-needed win after the bye week. But what really matters?
Pass protection on Sunday was significantly better than it has been. The biggest change? Monroe Freeling for Taylor Moton. Freeling hurt his knee, and Moton was finally ready to return, and he immediately made the entire line's performance a little bit better.
The Panthers have struggled with penalties this year. It wasn't a big issue last year, but this year, it seems every single week there's a discussion to be had about the penalties. Today, they made so many brutal mistakes, and it nearly cost them . One day, it actually will cost them a win. They literally set a franchise record for penalty yards.
Dave Canales has had two major bugaboos in his tenure. Coming out of the gate ready to play in Week 1 and bye week preparation. He got the offense rolling early this season, so that wasn't an issue. But once again, the bye week wasn't as fruitful as it's supposed to be.
Two bad mistakes by the Eagles on punts helped the Panthers out a ton. But on the other side, Carolina's inability to field a punt without committing a penalty hurt the Panthers a lot. It ruined several big returns. Special teams matter a whole lot.
When the offense isn't clicking, and the defense isn't generating turnovers, or when penalties come up at the worst possible times, can the Panthers do enough to get an ugly win? Being able to do so is the mark of a good team, and the Panthers proved today that they can do it.
Overall, it was a good day for the Panthers' defense, but that was partly because the Eagles are in utter shambles. Evero was aggressive early on, and he had the Eagles on their back foot. Then, he inexplicable let off the gas, and it allowed the Eagles to crawl back into the game. That never should've happened.

title: 3 Major Takeaways from Panthers' Exceptional Win over Eagles
full_text:
Coming off a Week 5 bye, the Carolina Panthers hit the road and took care of business, beating the Philadelphia Eagles 25-14 . Carolina largely controlled the game from bell to bell, never trailing and leading by as much as 12.
This game felt like a trap spot. The Eagles are dealing with critical injuries on offense: Jalen Hurts and Saquon Barkley are both out, the offensive line is riddled with injuries, and a retirement from RT Lane Johnson.
It was a typical letdown spot for Carolina, but not on Sunday afternoon. The Panthers did what they were supposed to do against a team playing a backup QB and with multiple hurt offensive linemen.
Carolina moves to 3-2. Here are three big takeaways from the victory.
Carolina's offense was quiet at first, but ultimately put together a phenomenal performance. The Panthers totaled 399 yards of total offense; they were close to 400 before Bryce Young took a knee to close out the game.
Carolina hasn't had a game with under 340 yards of total yards this season, and now has three games with over 395 total yards.
Brad Idzik has started the season on fire as Carolina's play-caller, and it's his first year calling the game in the NFL. At this pace, Idzik will warrant consideration for head coaching vacancies throughout the league.
After an adversity-filled 2025 season, real questions arose about whether Chuba Hubbard could once again be a bell-cow back. So far, he's passed that test with flying colors.
Hubbard was a key part of Sunday's win, logging 28 carries for 120 rushing yards and a touchdown. This is Hubbard's second straight game with 120+ rushing yards and 1+ touchdowns.
In a game where Bryce Young played well but was less efficient, Hubbard kept Carolina's offense on the field, fighting for yards after contact and finding gaps to run through.
Normally, against a depleted roster on offense, the run defense wouldn't get too much credit, but this is now two straight games of improvement in that department.
Carolina surrendered just 35 rushing yards total. The defensive line did its job by stopping inside runs, and linebackers like Devin Lloyd and Bobby Okereke made excellent tackles throughout the game, totaling 4 TFLs.
This performance follows Week 4, when the Panthers allowed Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs to rush for just 46 yards on 15 carries. What was seen as this team's weak point after Week 1 is building momentum as the season goes on.
Preston is an experienced sports writer focusing on NFL, College Football, NBA, and MMA topics. He is a passionate Charlotte and Oklahoma sports fan and graduated from the University of Science and Arts Oklahoma in 2025 with a Bachelor of Arts in Communications degree with a focus in journalism.

title: Bryce Young Report Card vs. Eagles: Don't Let One Ugly Number Fool You
full_text:
If you just look at Bryce Young completing 20 of 39 passes, you might come away thinking he didn't play all that well against Philadelphia. I don't think that's really the case.
There were definitely some throws Young missed, and I'm sure there are a few he'd like to have back. But he also threw for 281 yards and two touchdowns without turning the ball over. He wasn't great all afternoon, but he was good when Carolina needed him to be.
That's why I'm landing somewhere between a really good game and a great one.
I went back and forth between a B+ and an A- because there was a lot I liked from Young . He averaged more than seven yards per attempt, threw two touchdowns, and didn't give Philadelphia the ball with a bad turnover.
But 20-of-39 is still 20-of-39. Young missed some throws he should've made, and there were chances for Carolina to do even more through the air. That's enough to keep me from putting this one in the A range.
I did like that the misses never seemed to change the way he played. Young kept taking his shots and going back to his receivers instead of getting conservative. He hit enough of them to finish with 281 yards.
We've been waiting to see what this offense would look like with Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker on the field together, and we finally got a pretty good look at it. Coker had six catches for 97 yards, while McMillan finished with six for 86.
That's 183 yards between the two of them, and you could see the difference. Teams still have to worry about McMillan, but now Young has Coker on the other side making plays, too. That's something this offense hasn't had enough of.
Tommy Tremble ended up being a big part of Young's day, too. He caught both of Young's touchdown passes, including the 19-yarder in the fourth quarter after Philadelphia had cut Carolina's lead to 19-14.
That was probably Young's biggest moment of the game. Philadelphia had finally made a push and gotten itself back into it, and Carolina needed an answer. Young gave them one.
For me, it comes back to the missed throws. If Young completes a few more of those, I'm probably giving him an A- and not thinking twice about it.
But I don't want to overlook what he did well, either. Young threw for 281 yards, had two touchdowns, didn't throw an interception, and came up with a big throw when Philadelphia was trying to get back into the game.
Was it his best game? No. But it was a good day for the Panthers' quarterback, especially on the road in Philadelphia.

He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: 7 Winners and 4 Losers from Panthers' Sloppy Win Over Eagles
full_text:
Can the Carolina Panthers win ugly? They had a chance on the road against the surprisingly good Cleveland Browns, falling just short. Once again on the road and in an ugly dogfight, could the Panthers win?
They answered that question with a yes, even if it wasn't a resounding yes in a game they should've run away with. But which players stood out, for better or worse?
Taylor Moton's return was such a welcome sight. The right tackle slid back in and immediately improved the play on that side of the line. He was reliable and looked like he hadn't missed a beat after missing all of training camp and the first five weeks.
CB Will Lee has been great today, outside of one or two plays. You have to love how much the rookie has grown since Week 1. Love how he is staying at the hip pocket and playing through the catch point. An aggressive defender who is beginning to find his groove.
It is undeniably hard to be in Will Lee's position, but he is struggling. Despite facing a backup quarterback and a really disappointing offense, Lee didn't have his best day, including a really egregious early pass interference that gave the Eagles their first conversion. Another DPI gave the Eagles first-and-goal.
He also nearly undid a great play by taunting Devonta Smith. It certainly wasn't all bad, though, as Lee had some incredible coverage plays late in the game and even broke up a big play. The rollercoaster experience continues. So, he is both, because both aspects of his game need to be mentioned.
Dave Canales has to challenge that catch this is what you do when you don't call plays missed opportunity
Coming off the bye week, Dave Canales-led Panthers teams often struggle. He inexplicably does not have them ready to go after all that time off and preparation . It may not have hurt the Panthers badly this week, but it was still a frustratingly sluggish game for the Panthers . Once again, penalties hurt the Panthers badly. He also didn't challenge a clear incompletion that led to an Eagles touchdown.
It won't count in the box score, but the Panthers got a wonderful return from Trevor Etienne on special teams. Two penalties wiped out great returns, otherwise his stats would look a lot better. But he immediately made an impact and proved his worth upon return from Injured Reserve.
just a pointless penalty due to a lack of awareness erases a 23 yard gain and erases a likely scoring drive https://t.co/xj9qPKU9CA
Robert Hunt can't get out of his own way this year. Not only is he not playing up to his standard, but he's also making inexplicable penalties that crush drives. He has been illegally downfield multiple times this season, and that's a basic rule to adhere to. Running behind Hunt was also not productive today.
The Panthers didn't get a whole lot, strangely enough, from Devin Lloyd, who was quiet for long stretches of the game. But Bobby Okereke stepped up and made big plays all day. He was all over the field as a run-stopper, blitzer, and coverage linebacker.
It feels like Idzik is playing right into Fangio's hands. Play-calling has been off today, especially with a lack of run game emphasis early on and not attacking the MOF, which has looked open at times, but no concepts to attack. Really frustrating showing from this unit today.
Brad Idzik was weirdly conservative today, and a lot of his calls just didn't work. He was outcoached by Vic Fangio by far, although that's kind of to be expected. The growing pains of a rookie play-caller were evident for much of today. Second-half adjustments weren't really beneficial, either.
Two questions permeated the Panthers' WR room. How would Tetairoa McMillan do with Jalen Coker back to take targets from him, and how would Coker do after struggling to get healthy? Both players looked good, and there seemed to be plenty of balance between them, too. It was an ideal game for both of them.
Chuba Hubbard's 1-yard TD run in the fourth quarter marks his 6th TD of the season and 4th rushing TD. He becomes the 5th player in team history and 2nd running back (Christian McCaffrey) to record a TD in 4 of the team's first 5 games of a season.
Chuba Hubbard has been quietly excellent this year. He's been a scoring machine, which continued on Sunday with a decisive one-yard rush, but he was also good despite facing a pretty stout Eagles' defense. They have a very good front, but Hubbard continued to find yards in a slow and steady second half.
Zachary Roberts is a journalist with a wide variety of experience covering basketball, golf, entertainment, video games, music, football, baseball, and hockey. He currently covers Charlotte sports teams and has been featured on Sportskeeda, Yardbarker, MSN, and On SI.

title: Panthers Are Beating the Eagles Despite an Almost Unbelievable Halftime Stat
full_text:
The Panthers have looked like the better team for most of the first half in Philadelphia, but they haven't exactly made things easy on themselves. Carolina leads the Eagles 10-7 at halftime and has outgained them 178-110. Bryce Young has thrown for 162 yards and a touchdown, while the Panthers' defense hasn't let Tanner McKee get much going.
But there's one number you just can't get past: eight penalties for 105 yards.
Seriously, 105 penalty yards in one half? Carolina has moved the ball better, hasn't turned it over, and has held Philadelphia to just 3.3 yards per play. But every time it feels like the Panthers are about to take control, another flag seems to hit the field.
It happened again late in the second quarter. A holding penalty wiped out a Chuba Hubbard run, and another holding call on the kickoff cost Carolina good field position after Philadelphia cut the lead to three. Those are the kinds of mistakes that can turn a game pretty quickly.
Here's the crazy part: The Panthers have more penalty yards than McKee has passing yards. McKee has thrown for 94 yards, while Carolina has given up 105 on penalties. You can't keep doing that and expect to get away with it.
Young hasn't been perfect, but I like what I've seen from him. He's 12-of-21 for 162 yards, a touchdown, and no interceptions, and he's done it with Carolina getting almost nothing from the running game. That's put even more on Young and his receivers.
Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker have been a big reason why. McMillan has five catches for 79 yards, while Coker has five for 65 in his first game back. That's 144 yards between the two of them already.
This is exactly why getting Coker back mattered. Philadelphia can't just worry about McMillan anymore, and Coker has given Young another guy he can trust. It didn't take long for the two of them to get going again.
Carolina has needed every bit of it. Hubbard has only 24 yards on eight carries, so this offense has pretty much gone as Young and his receivers have gone.
One of my biggest questions coming into this game was what Carolina would do with McKee. He's starting in place of Jalen Hurts, and the last thing the Panthers needed was to let a backup quarterback get comfortable and suddenly look like a Pro Bowler against them. We've all seen that movie before.
So far, that hasn't happened. McKee is 13-of-23 for 94 yards, and Philadelphia has only 110 total yards. The Eagles finally got into the end zone late in the second quarter on a two-yard Dameon Pierce run, but outside of that, they haven't done much offensively.
That's what makes all these penalties so frustrating. The Panthers have played well enough to have more than a three-point lead. Young is moving the football, McMillan and Coker are making plays and the defense has kept Philadelphia from getting much going.
Carolina doesn't need to reinvent anything in the second half.
Just stop getting in your own way.

title: Panthers HC Dave Canales Just Cost Carolina With Mind-Numbing Coaching Decision
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers were driving when they faced a fourth-and-one in the territory. They often go for it there, and with three timeouts and more than 30 seconds left to try and score before the half, what transpired next was mind-boggling.
Neither Dave Canales nor Bryce Young opted to call a timeout, although that ultimately comes down to the coach. Canales made the call to simply let the game go, and the Eagles weren't willing to give the Panthers time to decide to go for it and score. That's telling.
Canales said he didn't want to go for it on a fourth down, and he didn't consider a nine-yard gain on third-and-10 a positive result. It's mindboggling. It wasn't the most perfect outcome, but the Panthers should've called one of their three timeouts to decide something instead of going hurry-up and then letting the clock run out anyway.
I thought that was poorly done by Panthers at end of first half: 4th and 1 at own 45, with timeouts. What is the harm of letting clock run down to 0:03, call the timeout and then throw it into the end zone? Bryce has the arm. Instead, Carolina runs clock out completely. Ugly.
Even if the Panthers believe they can't get a first down to try and continue the drive, there is no reason not to call a timeout with a few seconds left to set up a Hail Mary or some sort of play. That should've been the worst-case scenario there.
And if nothing's happening, Young can simply run out the last seconds of the half. In every way, it is a curious decision, and Canales' response before heading into the tunnel doesn't really justify the thought process.
It has not been a good day for Canales. He missed an easy challenge that led to the lone Eagles touchdown of the half. He did not have the Panthers ready to go after the bye week, which has been a consistent problem in his tenure.
Bryce Young had something to say to Brad Idzik after the Panthers chose not to run a play from their own 45 as the half ended. Panthers lead 10-7 and will receive the 2H kickoff.
These are the sorts of things that were supposed to improve with Brad Idzik taking over play-calling. For the most part, they have, but today, Canales regressed badly.
Plus, the Panthers remain prone to awful penalties. That comes back to coaching. It's a discipline issue, and many of the penalties occurred on offense, which is Canales' bread and butter.
Despite all of that, the Panthers are up at halftime and will be getting the ball to start the second half. It has been a ridiculously ugly game, but should this result hold, ugly wins count all the same.
But if the result is going to hold, Canales needs to improve in the second half and make sure the Panthers don't experience a catastrophic upset.

title: Fantasy Football Start or Sit Week 6: Bryce Young, Jalen Coker
full_text:
Back on the road, the Carolina Panthers return to action in Week 6 of the NFL season. Carolina travels to face the Philadelphia Eagles in a 1:00 PM ET kickoff on CBS.
As Week 6 begins, millions across the country are setting their fantasy football lineups and may need to navigate players who are unavailable due to the Week 6 bye week or injuries.
Panthers at Eagles has become a sneaky fantasy game to watch. Carolina is coming off its best performance of the season, with a 32-26 win over the Detroit Lions. Now coming off a bye and getting healthier in the receiver room, theres potential for another great offensive showing out of the Panthers.
Before Week 4, Bryce Young's top target was Jalen Coker, who led the team in both targets and receiving yards.
With Coker back now after missing Week 4 with a minor quad injury, Carolina's passing game is more dynamic, but does that make both Young and Coker automatic fantasy starts? Here's start or sit for Bryce Young and Jalen Coker.
The Eagles are a slightly below-average defense against QBs in fantasy football, surrendering 18-22 points per game depending on league format.
Bryce Young is currently a top-seven QB in fantasy football, and led the NFL in passing yards prior to the Week 5 bye.
Outside of Josh Allen and Brock Purdy, Young is as viable a starter as any QB in the league, especially with downslides in production for guys like Tyler Shough and Bo Nix having downslides in production.
Young has thrown for under 300 yards once in four games; don't overthink it if Young is available.
Before leaving the Week 3 game against the Browns, Coker hadn't scored fewer than 14 points in either of the two full games he played. Coker was WR1 in Week 1, posting over 35 fantasy points against the Chicago Bears.
According to Matt Okada of NFL.com , Philadelphia's defense has given up the most fantasy points to wide receivers since Week 3, totaling 134.4 points.
Against a defense that's been so abysmal against wide receivers, Panthers OC Brad Idzik will dial up downfield routes to set the offense up for explosive plays.
Coming off injury and the sharing of targets with Tetairoa McMillan, there should be room for both to thrive. Coker has already proven he can be the lead receiver when both are on the field.
It's a no-brainer start; Coker is a high-end flex and low-end WR2 this week.
