title: Fantasy Football Start or Sit: Tetairoa McMillan, Chuba Hubbard & Darren Waller
full_text:
If you've got Panthers players on your fantasy team, there are a few decisions to make before Sunday's game in Philadelphia. Chuba Hubbard is coming off his best game of the season, Tetairoa McMillan continues to emerge as one of Bryce Young's favorite targets, and Darren Waller is good to go after dealing with a toe injury during the week.
But I'm not making these calls just based on what happened against Detroit. The matchup matters, too, and all three are walking into very different situations against the Eagles.
So, who should you start and who should stay on the bench?
I'm starting Hubbard without much hesitation. He ran for 122 yards and two touchdowns against Detroit before the bye and is averaging 5.0 yards per carry this season. Carolina has also given him 39 carries over the last two games, so I'm not worried about whether he's going to get enough chances.
I don't mind the matchup, either. The Eagles have been pretty much middle of the pack when it comes to fantasy points allowed to running backs this season. We also saw Rams running back Kyren Williams put together a huge fantasy day against them earlier this year.
That doesn't mean Hubbard is going to run for 120 yards and two touchdowns again. But if Carolina can stay in this game and keep giving him the football, I like his chances of putting together another solid fantasy day.
There's just not enough here to talk me into sitting him.
McMillan is a little more interesting because this isn't a matchup I love. He's coming off a monster game against Detroit and now has 26 catches for 385 yards and two touchdowns through four games. Philadelphia's secondary should give him a much tougher afternoon.
The Eagles have been one of the better teams in the league at limiting outside receivers, and McMillan could see plenty of Quinyon Mitchell. That's enough for me to lower expectations after watching McMillan put up 192 yards and two touchdowns against Detroit.
It's not enough for me to sit him.
McMillan has become too big a part of Carolina's passing game. Young continues to look his way, and McMillan has shown he doesn't need a ton of room to make a big play. Having Jalen Coker back also gives Philadelphia another receiver to worry about.
I'm definitely not expecting another 192-yard afternoon. Give me the targets, and I'll take my chances with McMillan.
This is the toughest call of the three. Waller is good to go after dealing with a toe injury during the week, so his health isn't really what bothers me here. It's what Philadelphia has done against tight ends.
The Eagles have been one of the better defenses in the league against the position and haven't allowed a receiving touchdown to a tight end this season. That's a pretty big deal with Waller because a touchdown can be the difference between a good fantasy day and one that doesn't help you much.
Waller has 13 catches for 148 yards and two touchdowns this season, but he had only three catches for 36 yards against Detroit before the bye. His role in the offense has been growing, so I'm not saying he can't have a good game Sunday.
I just don't love this spot.
If you've got another tight end you feel pretty good about, I'd probably go that direction. If your other option isn't much better, Waller is still playable because one catch around the goal line can change everything.
Against this Eagles defense, though, I'd rather look somewhere else if I can.
Verdict: SIT if you have another solid option
Hubbard is the easiest decision for me. The Eagles haven't been dominant against running backs, he's coming off a 122-yard game, and Carolina continues to give him enough work to make him worth starting.
McMillan has the tougher matchup, especially if Mitchell spends a lot of Sunday lined up across from him. But there's a difference between expecting his numbers to come down and actually sitting him. I'm keeping McMillan in the lineup.
Waller is where I'd check my other options. Philadelphia has been good against tight ends and hasn't allowed one to catch a touchdown yet, so that's enough for me to stay away if I've got somebody else I trust.
And if Waller catches two touchdowns Sunday, you can come back and yell at me.

title: Will Panthers Beat Eagles? Here Are Our Staff Predictions Week 6
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are heading to Philadelphia this week to take on the Eagles. It would ordinarily be a tall task. They have been to two Super Bowls in the last five years, and they have one Lombardi. They're a perennial playoff team.
But this week, Jalen Hurts is out, and others are likely to join him. The Panthers are rested, and the Eagles are coming back from London after a tough loss. The Panthers also seem to be on the rise, while the Eagles are decidedly not.
Does this mean the Panthers will win? Here's what the Panthers on SI staff believes.
Carolina had some extra time to get ready for this clash of defending division champions. Ejiro Evero's defense is still shorthanded, but the Eagles are in the midst of a three-game losing streak. Philadelphia's defensive line could make things difficult for Bryce Young.
Nick Sirianni's team, which will be without quarterback Jalen Hurts, has been outscored a combined 66-23 in the second half this season and will struggle to close out the surging Panthers.
Going into Philadelphia is never easy, but this is a game the Panthers should win. The Eagles have lost three straight and now have to turn to Tanner McKee with Jalen Hurts out. Carolina is coming off the bye, the offense has been playing well, and I think Bryce Young makes enough plays for the Panthers to leave Philadelphia with a big road win.
The Eagles' defense has struggled against the pass, allowing the seventh-most passing yards per game. Bryce Young has taken on the defenses ranked first and sixth in passing yards allowed and shredded them both, so the Panthers, who are getting healthier, should have no issues moving the ball.
The Eagles' offense, meanwhile, is without Jalen Hurts. Saquon Barkley probably won't play. Will Shipley is out. Devonta Smith might miss Week 6, too. The Eagles just lost Lane Johnson (retirement) and Cam Jurgens (trade) on the offensive line. Where are they supposed to get any sort of production from?
Everything says the Panthers should win this game, so naturally, they could find a way to lose it. But I think we've seen this year that these aren't the same old Panthers, and this is the sort of statement win they've been building to and getting more of over the last two seasons.
This feels like a trap game spot for the Panthers. Even with no Jalen Hurts, no Saquon Barkley, and a suspect offensive line, the Eagles are going to play Carolina close.
That said, if the offense maintains the rhythm it’s had almost all season, then Carolina's defense should be able to do just enough against backup personnel. Chicago’s third-string QB diced this Philadelphia defense up, so there's no reason Young can't do the same.

title: Chicago Bears QB Caleb Williams Sets Impressive Record in Win Over Falcons
full_text:
Caleb Williams was the best player on either side of the field (for either team) in the Chicago Bears' 31-23 win over the Atlanta Falcons.
He showed the Bears faithful what they've been missing over the past month and continued cementing his status as one of the league's most promising young quarterbacks. Williams also got everyone involved, as eight players caught at least two passes today.
Some questioned whether Williams could maintain his upward trajectory with his hamstring being less than 100%. He answered those questions emphatically today, completing 30 of 36 attempts for 305 yards and a touchdown. He did so while rushing for only three yards, tied for the third-fewest of his career.
Notably, Williams also went 26/26 when the Falcons defense failed to get pressure on him. That mark set the record for the most attempts without an incompletion since ESPN began tracking pressures in 2009.
The fact that the Bears offensive line only gave up ten pressures against Atlanta's defensive front is a testament to their performance (although many of Williams unpressured looks were roll-outs). However, that fact isn't nearly as impressive as the Bears' signal-caller batting a thousand .
It's also worth noting that four of Williams' six incompletions were intentionally thrown away. He only had two incompletions where his intended target didn't come down with the pass (and one was the result of Colston Loveland seemingly getting ahead of his skis in the end zone).
Some of Caleb Williams' best performances have come with Tom Brady in the booth, as he also called their Week 3 matchup against Dallas and both regular-season contests against Green Bay last season.
Brady named Williams the Player of the Game in two of those contests (against the Cowboys and in their Week 16 matchup against Green Bay). That trend continued today, as the seven-time Super Bowl winner once again spoke to Williams after the contest.
Caleb Williams always performs when @TomBrady is in the building. The @ChicagoBears QB is the #LFG Player of the Game. @CALEBcsw @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/V2bYXFuHen
Brady obviously knows quality quarterback play when he sees it, as he's arguably the greatest to ever step on the field. As if the eye test and gaudy passing numbers weren't enough of an indication, Brady's consistent praise for Williams (he specifically said this was the best performance of his career during the broadcast) certainly cements the fact that the Bears got a good one.
Williams' 72.5% completion percentage currently leads the league. Another question answered emphatically.
The Bears will only go as far as Williams can take them, and his triumphant return will surely strike fear in the hearts of other NFC hopefuls. So will the fact that he was only focused on the negatives after the contest.
"I missed a couple things, especially there was one late in the game [where] I should've went to Rome [Odunze] and I went in the opposite direction," Williams said. "Things like that, I missed another route that I felt like I should've hit.. We'll go back and look in the mirror and figure out what we need to fix and get better at."
Jerry Markarian has been an avid Chicago Bears fan since 2010 and has been writing about the team since  2022.  He has survived the 2010 NFC Championship Game, a career-ending injury to his favorite player (Johnny Knox), the Bears' 2013 season finale, a Double Doink, Mitchell Trubisky, Justin Fields, and Weeks 8-17 of the 2024 NFL season. Nevertheless, he still Bears Down!

title: Bears' Bad Injury Luck Continues in Atlanta as Chicago Barely Survives Falcons Comeback
full_text:
The Chicago Bears escaped Mercedes-Benz Stadium with a 31-23 victory over the Atlanta Falcons that should have never been that close. Chicago led by 24 points in the fourth quarter but allowed Atlanta to trail by one score at the game's end.
Quarterback Caleb Williams had a smooth return from injury after three weeks away, though he was sacked four times. Part of the problem was the Bears losing a key piece of the right side of their offensive line, guard Jonah Jackson.
Jackson injured his hip in the third quarter and was ruled doubtful to return by the team before not making it back by game's end. After the game, Coach Ben Johnson provided a brief update that it was his left hip.
Johnson didn't provide any further updates. Now, Chicago runs the risk of missing Jackson for a short turnaround for a Thursday Night Football clash with the New England Patriots.
Luke Newman got his first taste of meaningful action for the Bears this season on Sunday in Atlanta. Previously, he had played on special teams and in late-game garbage time outside of the occasional rotational looks.
Newman helped the team build its biggest lead, holding strong during a seven-play, 52-yard drive that ended in a Roschon Johnson touchdown run.
Newman can move around the interior, having moved from the tackle spot to the interior during his time at Michigan State. That's what got him drafted to the Windy City, according to Chicago director of college scouting Brett Ackley.
"You see him play center there, so that's really when it kind of piqued the interest, the versatility piece," Ackley said in 2025 after taking Newman in the sixth round. "He was one of those guys that as you went through the process, he slowly checked every box and did everything right."
Newman may get his chance to prove Ackley right with a short week potentially keeping Jackson out of "TNF."
The other intriguing option is rookie Logan Jones, the team's second-round pick out of Iowa.
While Jones is a center by trade, he has the versatility to be moved around the line, just like Newman. Jones has been used primarily as a special teams player thus far.
It's unlikely Johnson risks throwing Jones into the fire too soon. With Garrett Bradbury's struggles at the starting center spot, Jones is an obvious successor there at some point in the near future.
Expect Newman to continue getting looks if Jackson can't play. Given the short turn around for Week 7, prepare for Newman to get the start against the Patriots.

title: Ben Johnson Forced to Explain Why Bears Took Their Foot Off the Gas
full_text:
Without question the Bears took their foot off the gas Sunday after assuming a 31-7 lead over the Atlanta Falcons with just over 12 minutes remaining.
They nearly paid for it but afterward coach Ben Johnson tried to explain his thinking to reporters about why they began substituting for what had been a very effective defense all game. After the substitutions, the lead quickly shrank when Roschon Johnson fumbled it away, leading to couple quick Atlanta touchdowns before they held on to win 31-23.
"Yeah, you're trying to thread the needle a little bit," Johnson said told reporters afterward. "If we didn't have the Thursday night game, I don't know that we would do things like we did. So that's part of the equation."
In other words, they have a Thursday night game coming up with the Patriots and the thought was to get starters rest once the game seem salted away. Only, the game hadn't been salted away and the Falcons nearly burned them.
Kyler Gordon's strip sack on a slot cornerback blitz and a recovery Devin Bush at Atlanta's 28 sealed the win anyway, and prevented a possible Falcons tying drive. It was an embarrassing turnaround.
The Bears have their backups in on defense: Jack Sanborn, Skyler Thomas, Elijah Hicks ... etc.
The defense had people like Jack Sanborn, Nick McCloud, Josh Blackwell and Elijah Hicks playing, among others.  After Altlanta's first TD, the starters returned. By then Big Mo had left the building and the Falcons were coming. The problem with putting in backups when backups are already playing as starters at positions is you're substituting with third-stringers.
Michael Penix Jr. hit Kyle Pitts with the 10-yard TD pass and Zacharaiah Branch with the two-point conversion to end an eight-play, 91-yard drive and then the Falcons got it right back with Roschon Johnson's lost fumble at Atlanta's 22. It led to a quicker scoring drive of five plays, aided by a 41-yard Penix completion to Jahan Dotson. The two-pointer suddenly meant the Bears needed ball possession after they'd done it all day but suddenly they couldn't. But Gordon's strip sack preserved the win.
Great throws on this drive! This one and Drake London! Falcons offense starts slow and is finding some rhythm. Drake London still looking for his first touchdown! Let’s see more Bijan! pic.twitter.com/DSGqXpcjRB
Johnson blamed it more on the turnover by Johnson than the tactic of looking ahead to get rest for the Patriots game.
"I do believe if we hadn't had that fumble on offense then maybe we would have gotten out of there the way that we wanted," Johnson said. "We know that's the case, especially with an offense like that.
"Once again we were trying to thread the needle and do what's best for us. We had to win the game first and foremost, which we did, but of course we wanted to think long term also."
Long term doesn't count if they're going to lose in the short term. In the future, Johnson needs to think about closing out the victory.
Bears’  Roschon Johnson coughs up the ball at midfield where the Atlanta Falcons took over. Penix and the Falcons’ offense took advantage by scoring a touchdown and the two-point conversion to make it a one-score game. #NFL #ETOSports https://t.co/y1o7AAd4bP
For a while on Sunday it had begun to take on the look of last year's Cincinnati game, when the Bears had to score at the end to win a game they seemed to have locked up already with a two-score lead.
They didn't need it but this needs to be a lesson for them going forward. Many of their backups were already playing and then third-stringers were coming in and trying to stop starters. Too much can happen in the NFL too fast for any team to assume victory when there is 10 minutes or more remaining.
It wasn't the opening game when the Bears scored 59 points. Instead, penalties kept them in check all day and the idea should have been escaping as easily and quickly as possible.
Besides. why would they worry about resting defensive players when they had more than 40 minutes of possession time for the second time in three games?  The defense hardly put in any reps. The Bears ran off 75 plays to 50 for the Falcons. Three weeks ago the defense only was on for 32 plays.
The W is more important than the R and R and Johnson needs to realize this going forward regardless of their coming schedule.
Kyler Gordon finished with 3 sacks with 2 being strip sacks today. pic.twitter.com/bBqcMJMmTR https://t.co/0Bj5Bq6e5V

title: Kyler Gordon Makes NFL History With Electric Performance in Bears' Week 6 Win
full_text:
The Chicago Bears waited a long time for Kyler Gordon to make his 2026 debut, but it was very much worth the wait.
Gordon suffered a calf injury in the offseason and was sidelined through the offseason program, training camp and the first five games of the 2026 campaign.
There was no shortage of controversy surrounding his absence, also, as fans were frustrated with the oft-injured defensive back and both head coach Ben Johnson and general manager Ryan Poles publicly voiced frustration as well.
However, that was thrown in the trash after just one game. Gordon made his debut in Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons and was the best defensive player on the field, and maybe the best player regardless of position in the Bears' 31-23 victory.
Gordon finished with four tackles, tied for the third-most on the team, and he notched four pressures, three sacks, three tackles for loss and two forced fumbles.
The veteran defensive back's biggest play of the game came in the fourth quarter, when the Falcons were driving to tie the game and Gordon sacked Michael Penix Jr. and forced a fumble that the defense was able to recover.
Gordon dropped back into coverage for just six snaps, per Pro Football Focus, and didn't allow a completion on the only pass thrown his way.
Gordon's success when asked to blitz was especially important with the Bears missing two of their best edge rushers , Montez Sweat and Dayo Odeyingbo, who were out on Sunday due to suspension and injury, respectively.
Gordon is the first defensive back in 40 years to have three sacks and multiple forced fumbles in the same game, according to Novig. Gordon is also the lightest NFL player by weight since 1985 to record that many sacks and forced fumbles in a game, per OptaStats .
Adding to all that, Gordon's three sacks are tied for the most ever in a game by a cornerback, Pro Football Focus noted.
"He makes us better as a team," Grady Jarrett said after the game. "We're super excited to have him back, and just continue to elevate not only this defense, but the whole team."
"I feel like I just picked up where I left off," Gordon said when asked if he thought his debut was a reintroduction for what he can do. "Just continue to stack and try to be the best I can be."
Gordon's contribution in the pass-rush was enormous, but his return also allows the Bears to deploy their best cornerback combination.
With Gordon now in the slot, the Bears can put Malik Muhammad on the boundary in place of Tyrique Stevenson, who has been a liability all season long.
If Jaylon Johnson can get back on track, and Muhammad can keep playing at a high level like he has this season, Chicago's secondary is going to be very good.
And, lest we forget, Coby Bryant has yet to play a snap in 2026 as he recovers from an injury. Bryant was spotted walking around before the game and he looks to be on track to return at some point this season.
Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report.

title: Game Balls in Bears' Bounce Back Week 6 Win Over Falcons
full_text:
There are few things more satisfying for an NFL team than to score a big win after a frustrating loss, and that’s exactly what the Chicago Bears got on Sunday. The Bears absolutely dominated the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, cleansing their pallet of that ignominious loss to the Green Bay Packers last week. The Falcons did make it interesting near the end, but the Bears were never in serious danger.
The return of Caleb Williams from his hamstring injury could not have gone much better than it did, and I’ll speak on that more in a moment. Also of note was the return of Ozzy Trapilo. He got his first NFL action since rupturing his patellar tendon in January. Unfortunately for Trapilo, his 2026 debut was marred by an untimely holding penalty that erased a big pass play to Rome Odunze.
This wasn't a perfect game by any means, and the Bears face a short turnaround with the resurgent New England Patriots coming to Soldier Field on Thursday. But for now, let's hand out some game balls for this Week 6 win.
If it wasn't already on life support, the narrative that head coach Ben Johnson's offense could be run better by another quarterback in Chicago should now be truly dead. Williams started the game with two perfect drives that ended in touchdowns, going 10-for-10 passing for 120 yards and a touchdown in that time, and never looked back.
Though he only threw for one touchdown, Williams racked up over 300 passing yards and completed an absurd 83.3% of his passes, surpassing two of three expectations in my stat predictions for this Bears-Falcons game . More importantly, he reminded the NFL that he is a budding superstar at the quarterback position. So long as he’s under center, the Bears are a threat to beat anyone.
Welcome back, Kyler Gordon! In his first game of the 2026 season, Gordon racked up an insane stat line that includes not one, not two, but three sacks. When he's on the field, Gordon is exactly the kind of playmaker that the Bears signed to a market-setting contract extension last year. The problem has been the fact that he's not on the field very often. He played in just five games last year, which includes the Bears' two playoff games, and he missed the first five weeks of this season.
If Gordon can keep playing like he did on Sunday, and if he doesn't miss another game the rest of the year, he's going to force the Bears into a very difficult offseason decision regarding his contract. Clearly, he's a difference maker, but can he stay healthy? That's a question for Ryan Poles to answer in the spring. For now, however, he's earned this game ball.
It took far longer than anyone anticipated, but Colston Loveland finally got on the board with his first touchdown of the 2026 NFL season. He caught an absolute dart from Caleb Williams in between two defenders in the red zone on the Bears opening drive and held on to put up six points. He finished the game with six receptions for 65 yards and a touchdown, and for that he gets this last game ball.
A former Marine and Purdue Boilermaker, Pete has been covering the Chicago Bears since 2022 as a senior contributor on BearsTalk. He lives with his wife, two kids and loyal dog.

title: Roschon Johnson Among Chicago Bears Top Losers in Week 6 Win Over Falcons
full_text:
The Chicago Bears came away with a 31-23 win over the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday afternoon.
The Bears controlled the tempo for the first 49 minutes before the Falcons caught fire late. Caleb Williams made his triumphant return and immediately reclaimed his status as one of the league's rising stars. He was the best player on the field .
Unfortunately, a few players didn't find nearly as much success against Atlanta. Which players hurt their stock the most in the Week 6 loss?
Roschon Johnson can't seem to get out of his own way. The veteran running back was having one of the best games of his career before coughing up a fumble late in the contest. If the Falcons had pulled off a miraculous comeback, Johnson might've been a surprise cut candidate this week (or as soon as Kyle Monangai can return to the lineup , anyway).
To his credit, Ben Johnson did go right back to him on the final drive to ice the game. He also led the team with 51 yards on the ground. Still, the fumble was costly and, if not for a masterclass by cornerback Kyler Gordon , could've been deadly.
Elijah Hicks got exposed late in the contest. Tight end Kyle Pitts stole the ball from him on a 29-yarder, and he gave up a touchdown a few plays later. He was left on an island on both plays (due to Dennis Allen's blitz-heavy gameplan), and it's not like All-Pro play should be expected from the backup safety, but it was still a rough showing.
The Bears will be relying more heavily on Hicks after cutting ties with Xavier Woods earliet this week. He'll hopefully bounce back with a better performance in Thursday night's matchup against New England.
Penalties, penalties, penalties. The Bears lost more yards due to penalties than the Falcons gained on offense until the Bears pulled many of their defensive starters (who all promptly returned after Johnson put the ball on the ground) at the start of the fourth quarter. They finished the contest with 12 penalties for 133 yards, including a few costly ones that took big plays off the board.
The Bears did a great job limiting penalties over their previous three games after struggling mightily in that department over the first two weeks. They had 13 penalties for 99 yards in Weeks 3-5 combined. A rough bit of regression that Ben Johnson will be eager to iron out.
Jahdae Walker was responsible for two consequential penalties today. The first occurred when he dove to block a punt and ended up roughing Atlanta's punter. That gave the Falcons a new set of downs.
His second was an unnecessary roughness call that led to an ejection from the contest . Today's game will be one to forget for the second-year receiver. He's not in danger of losing his spot on special teams, but another performance like today's could see him losing snaps.
Jerry Markarian has been an avid Chicago Bears fan since 2010 and has been writing about the team since  2022.  He has survived the 2010 NFC Championship Game, a career-ending injury to his favorite player (Johnny Knox), the Bears' 2013 season finale, a Double Doink, Mitchell Trubisky, Justin Fields, and Weeks 8-17 of the 2024 NFL season. Nevertheless, he still Bears Down!

title: Bears Defensive Coordinator Dennis Allen Turns Shortage Into Surplus
full_text:
The Bears have already given defensive coordinator Dennis Allen a couple of game balls, so doing this is no longer sufficient.
Maybe they need to give him a whole bag of game balls.
On Sunday his defense took the Atlanta Falcons straight out of their game plan from the beginning of the game until the subs came on far too early in a 31-23 Bears win. The phrase "his defense" is being generous.
No Montez Sweat. No Dayo Odeyingbo. No T.J. Edwards. No Tyrique Stevenson, for what it's worth. They cut Xavier Woods, who had started at safety and got burned by the Packers.
They were starting two defensive tackles the Atlanta Falcons didn't want any longer. They're using James Lynch and Daniel Hardy at defensive end, Noah Sewell at linebacker, Malik Muhammad for Stevenson, Kyler Gordon playing for the first time this year and even Elijah Hicks got an appearance.
Kyler Gordon strip sack 🔥🔥🔥 pic.twitter.com/iGsoixrv3J
Yet, NFL rushing leader Bijan Robinson was rendered a non-factor. Michael Penix Jr., the savior of the Falcons franchise, couldn't find targets most of the game as he rushed throws or was sacked. Gordon came up with three sacks, including the clincher with his second strip sack of the game, Hardy made his first career sack. Sadly, Allen couldn't make Nick McCloud look good in coverage, and why he's even back on the roster isn't known, but everything else he did looked golden.
About all Allen didn't do right was putting subs in once the Bears led by 24 points in the fourth quarter. It nearly opened the way for the Falcons to get back intot he game before Gordon's big sack.
It's as if Allen reaches into a bag and grabs players and throws a bunch on the field, says go get 'em, and they do.  Instead of giving him drafted players, they'd be better off giving him an entire defense of waiver-wire castoffs and they'd shut teams out every week. OK, it's an exaggeration but he's almost doing it anyway with the lack of help the personnel department gives him.
The Falcons had only 97 yards in the first half and only scored after they briefly seized momentum following a Cairo Santos' field goal miss from the 46-yard line. A 56-yarder shouldn't be a big risk for a big boy kicker with the roof shut in the stadium.
Kyler Gordon in his 1st game back: • 3 tackles for loss • 2 sacks • 1 QB hit • 1 forced fumble pic.twitter.com/xKvoQkphrJ
The offense contributed some points, lots penalty flags and good possession time. The defense won the day, though.  And it was lopsided, so Atlanta obviously needs to add talent. Maybe their personnel guru Matt Ryan can do this for them. Meanwhile the Bears head on toward a Thursday night showdown at home with defending AFC champion New England at 4-2 on the year and in good shape.
Allen always says it's the next man up. For the Bears, it was next man and then next man and then next man up and they all kept producing like starters or even better than starters.
Allen seems at his best when the assignment is to take subs and make them start. He did this last year with the first four linebackers gone and their best two cornerbacks. He did this again Sunday, no sweat, or Sweat.
There is a constant barrage of Bears social media traffic blasting GM Ryan Poles for not drafting defensive linemen but what's the point? Allen simply takes refuse from other teams and uses them effectively.
Street wasn't just a player the Falcons let leave, he didn't even make their roster last year. He was a practice squad player for 10 games. And he was breaking up a screen pass in the first half the way an All-Pro does it. Then Jarrett reminded the Falcons of his long servitude there with a sack in the second half as Atlanta threatened after yet another penalty, this for defensive pass interference.
The Bears' defense not only overcame their own injuries but all the penalties against their own offense and themselves with a referee crew that just loved throwing yellow things.
Kentavius Street and Devin Bush absolutely BLEW UP that screen my word
Eventually this type of thing can't work, but the Bears had ball control and Williams looking better than ever in his return working on their side Sunday to compensate.
Sure, they'll need Sweat, Edwards and Odeyingbo back in the future.
It's unlikely they'll get back many starters with only four days time until the next game, but that's the way Allen likes it. Lack of talent along with lack of prep time should probably mean a shutout win based on the way Allen does things.
Don’t even say anything bad about Dennis Allen man.  He be putting defenses together with duct tape and WD-40.

title: Caleb Williams Headlines Biggest Winners From Bears Week 6 Win in Atlanta
full_text:
The Chicago Bears came away with an impressive 31-23 victory over the Atlanta Falcons today.
The final score doesn't tell the full story, as the Bears controlled the tempo for the first 49 minutes before the Falcons scored twice in the span of four minutes midway through the fourth quarter.
While it wasn't a flawless showing by any means (largely due to 12 penalties for 133 yards), a few players enjoyed great performances. Who managed to stand out from their peers in that regard?
Caleb Williams showed Chicago's offense what they've been missing over the past month against Atlanta. The Bears star signal-caller was electric from start to finish, hitting throws all over the field and getting all his playmakers involved in the process. He completed his first 12 attempts (a career-high) and diced up the Falcons' talented secondary to the tune of 30 completions off 36 attempts for 305 yards and a passing TD.
Most importantly, he also wasn't slowed by the hamstring injury. The Bears ran their normal complement of roll-outs, and he also didn't shy away from navigating around the pocket (and out of it). The sky wasn't falling with Williams out of the lineup , but they have a limitless ceiling when he's under center.
We finally saw the Colston Loveland we expected to see this season against Atlanta. The pass-catcher started the game with a bang, catching three passes for 36 yards and an impressive touchdown grab in traffic on the first drive. He finished the contest with six catches for 65 yards.
He wasn't perfect (he dropped a pass in the end zone and committed one holding penalty and another EXTREMELY weak offensive pass interference penalty), but today was by far his best game of the season. Loveland will hopefully use today's performance as a launching pad for the rest of the year.
Tom Brady sang Luther Burden III's praises early in the FOX broadcast, and the pass-catcher promptly showed everyone why the seven-time Super Bowl winner is so high on him. Atlanta's defense had few answers for him, and he led the team with with eight grabs for 95 yards.
Burden is electric with the ball in his hands, and he gained a ton of yards after the catch today. His 25-yard catch midway through the third quarter was arguably his most impressive play, as he high-pointed the ball and managed to come down with it despite being hit by two defenders.
Now we know why Dennis Allen was so excited to see Kyler Gordon in his defense. Was anyone more impactful on a play-to-play basis than cornerback Gordon today? We don't yet know how many plays he was out there (it felt like roughly 15-20 defensive snaps), but he still made a major impact despite the limited snap count .
Few cover men are as aggressive near the line of scrimmage as Gordon, and he showed those traits in the Bears' win. He nabbed three sacks (two of which resulted in fumbles) and an impressive TFL in which he shot a gap to bring down Bijan Robinson in the backfield.
The Bears have a ton of injuries on defense, but you wouldn't know it from today's contest. They got major contributions from reserve players across all three levels. While they gave up two scores on consecutive drives in the fourth quarter, that was partially due to having backups on the field (no way of knowing where the blame goes with that decision).
The fact that it was difficult to narrow down any other significant individual defensive performances is a testament to the unit's overall performance. Chicago's defense has struggled mightily in two games this season, but has performed admirably in every other contest. Allen deserves a world of credit for that fact.

Nevertheless, he still Bears Down!

title: Biggest Takeaways From Bears' Week 6 Win Over Falcons in Caleb Williams' Return
full_text:
The first game back for quarterback Caleb Williams was a good one, as the Chicago Bears notched a 31-23 victory over the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday in Week 6.
The Bears were in total control for most of the game before the Falcons flipped the script in the fourth quarter. Thankfully, the Bears were able to hold them off to pull out the road win.
Other than that, there were a ton of positives to draw from this win for the Bears, including the performance of Williams.
We'll go over that and more as we take a look at the biggest takeaways from Chicago's win over Atlanta.
The Bears dominated to the point they held a 31-7 lead with under 10 minutes left in the fourth quarter, but the Falcons came roaring back to make this game way too close for comfort.
After a scoring drive for the Falcons, Roschon Johnson coughed up the football on the next series and Atlanta went on to turn that into a touchdown and two-point conversion to pull to within one score.
After a Bears three-and-out, the Falcons had an opportunity to tie the game up, but Chicago's defense held to prevent the collapse.
Williams looked to be just fine in his first game back , as he was moving around just like he always does, so he was not at all hampered by his hamstring.
The former No. 1 overall pick was sharp, also, with Williams completing 30-of-36 passes for 305 yards and one score.
And, as you'd expect with that kind of performance, the Bears' offense got back on track. Luther Burden had his best game of the season, as did Colston Loveland, who even scored a touchdown.
Chicago's offensive success also allowed the Bears to dominate time of possession, which kept Bijan Robinson and Drake London off the field.
Gordon reminded everyone why the Bears need him as much as they do, as the slot cornerback made an immediate and massive impact during his 2026 debut.
Gordon was everywhere on Sunday, even getting some snaps on special teams, where he nearly blocked a punt.
Gordon's biggest impact came on defense, and more specifically, when he was asked to blitz. The veteran corner notched three sacks, four pressures, three tackles for loss and two forced fumbles.
His biggest play of the game came in the fourth quarter when the Falcons were driving to tie it up. On a third-and-long, Gordon not only recorded his third sack, but his second forced fumble, also, which the Bears recovered.
Just a monster day for Gordon, who was one of the best players on the field on Sunday.
Things got messy in the fourth quarter, but the Bears' defense still got the stop it needed to get and played much better overall over the first three quarters than it did last week.
Chicago held Bijan Robinson to just 61 yards and the Falcons posted just 257 yards of total offense and were 3-for-12 on third downs and 0-for-3 on fourth downs.
The Bears' pass-rush notched several pressures and five sacks in total, which was impressive considering the defense didn't have its best pass-rushers in Montez Sweat and Dayo Odeyingbo. Gordon notched three of those sacks and Daniel Hardy and Dillon Thieneman had one apiece.
Sure, most of the sacks didn't come from the edge rushers, but Dennis Allen found a way to replace Sweat and Odeyingo in a different way. It was a true masterclass from Allen on Sunday.
The Bears committed a whopping 12 penalties for 133 yards, with eight of those coming in the first half alone.
There were way too many holding penalties on offense, and more than one drive was wrecked as a result of them. It goes without saying the Bears need to clean that up.
Jackson got injured in the third quarter and never returned to the game.
Given the fact that he was immediately ruled doubtful suggests it's more than a minor issue. We'll see what kind of update head coach Ben Johnson can offer after the game.
Jackson has been phenomenal this season and an absence for any period of time would be a big blow to Chicago's offensive line.
Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report.

title: Jahdae Walker Ejected: Why Bears WR Was Kicked Out of Week 6 Game vs. Falcons
full_text:
Chicago Bears wide receiver Jahdae Walker was ejected from the Week 6 game against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday afternoon.
Walker was kicked out of the game in the fourth quarter after head-butting a Falcons player after a kickoff. Walker and the Falcons player exchanged words before Walker delivered a headbutt to him.
The Falcons player on the receiving end of the headbutt was wide receiver Chris Blair.
"Bears WR Jahdae Walker has been ejected for head-butting a Falcon," The Athletic's Kevin Fishbain wrote.
Here's video of Walker's infraction that got him ejected from the contest.
Jahdae Walker ejected for a headbutt Ben Johnson not happy on the sideline pic.twitter.com/ypkUa1zjjm
Walker's ejection came as the Bears had the game well in hand with a 31-7 lead over the Falcons, who they were dominating all game long on both sides of the ball.
Now, it'll be interesting to see if Walker will face a suspension for the infraction. At the very least, he's going to get a fine this week.
The ejection isn't going to have much of an impact on the Bears for the rest of the game. Walker doesn't play snaps on offense and is strictly a special teams contributor.
Walker was an undrafted free-agent signing of the Bears in 2025. He appeared in nine games last season and recorded six catches for 87 yards and two touchdowns during his rookie campaign.
He's most known for his Week 16 touchdown catch against the Green Bay Packers that forced that game into overtime before Chicago pulled out the victory later on. His second touchdown came in the Week 8 contest a few weeks later.
This season, Walker has tallied just one catch for one yard and one touchdown on two targets over five contests. He had seen just 53 snaps on offense entering Week 6.
Walker is well-known by his teammates as a high-energy player, so it's not totally surprising he allowed his emotions to get the best of him.
"His energy feeds off everyone," Kalif Raymomd said of Walker . "Watching him in Tennessee in the joint practice, even if I'm tired, the sun's beaming down and Jahdae's like, 'I do this!.'"
"An infectious energy like that, even watching him on special teams, it's like, 'that's my receiver right there,' you know, it's so cool watching him go, but it's infectious," he added. "It brings the game back to what you enjoy, being around a player like that. And then watching that infectious personality go and make plays, it gets everybody hyped. So he's just one of those people."
Caleb Williams was asked during his appearance on "Hot Ones" which teammate never shuts up and he didn't hesitate at all to name Walker.
“Jahdae Walker. You hear Jahdae Walker when you wake up. You hear him when you go to sleep," Williams explained. "You hear him in the locker room as soon as you get to the locker room."
Walker is surely going to learn from his mistake. He's just fortunate it didn't hurt his team on Sunday.

title: Bengals Standard Betting Underdogs Against Ravens in First 2026 Season Matchup

title: Bengals' Meeting With Ravens Gets Even Bigger After a Chaotic Week 6
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals had Week 6 off, but that didn't stop the rest of the AFC North from creating absolute chaos.
The Pittsburgh Steelers took an overtime victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, while the Cleveland Browns shocked the Baltimore Ravens with a last second field goal. We live in a world where the Browns lead the AFC North at 4-2, with the Ravens and Steelers also at 4-2, and the Bengals still at 3-2, placing them last.
Yes, the Bengals may be last in the division heading into Week 7, but the outcome of the Browns-Ravens game was exactly what Bengals fans should have been rooting for, and one that makes the Week 7 matchup even more important.
The Bengals are getting the chance to come into a physical divisional contest fresh, due to the bye week. They will also have the chance to get ahead of the Ravens in the division with a win.
After stumbling in their first division game this season against the Steelers, this meeting with the Ravens was already massive. Now, the Bengals have a chance to put the Ravens behind them in the standings, just before they take on a Tennessee Titans team that just picked up its first win.
Coming out of the bye week on the right foot would be huge for this team's playoff implications. It also could be the start of a winning streak that will keep the rest of the division on their toes.
Getting a victory in the AFC North is never easy. It's been especially difficult for the Bengals when they've played the Ravens in recent years.
The Bengals are 1-5 in the last three years in the regular season against the Ravens. Want to change the thinking around the league about your team? Then you have to beat the Ravens.
It's not the Bengals who are facing an injury at quarterback when these two teams meet on Sunday. (Knock on wood)
Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has missed the team's last two games after suffering an ankle sprain in the team's Week 4 win over the Titans.

title: 'I'm In The Teens' - Ja'Marr Chase Breaks Down Body Tattoo Designs, Meanings

Ja'Marr Chase is resting during his bye week along with the rest of the Bengals . Fabletics recently dropped a short video showing the star wide receiver explaining all of the big tattoos he has scattered across his upper body.

Young Thug quote: I was a big Thug fan growing up—other arm are cars. See no evil, hear no evil, speak no evil. I have risk makes you rich—some dice. Weak messages create bad situations. Rise above all madness. Got a red card on the back of my neck. This is my spirit animal. Looking at my grandmother. Got her portrait. Now you got your tattoos from the one."
Chase is opening up more of his personal life as he gets deeper and deeper into his NFL career .

title: Cris Collinsworth Reveals What Bengals Must Change to Win AFC North
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals' offense has been the main topic of the franchise since they selected quarterback Joe Burrow.
Burrow was given the keys to a franchise that was starving for success and helped lead the team to a Super Bowl appearance in the 2021 season. However, the superstar quarterback didn't do that alone.
The Bengals have given Burrow the weapons to have one of the most dangerous offenses in the league, this year is no different. But there is one unit on the offensive side of the ball that has to catch up to the rest if the Bengals are playing on making another deep postseason run.
The Bengals' run game has hindered the offense this season. After five games, the Bengals are averaging 82 yards per game on the ground. That puts them in the bottom ten of the league in that category.
Recently, Cris Collinsworth and his son, Jac Collinsworth, discussed how the run game has to get better for the Bengals to be able to compete in the physical AFC North.
"The Cincinnati Bengals are going to have to establish [the run] if they're going to knock off the Pittsburgh Steelers, the Baltimore Ravens," Collinsworth said .
Jac also made a great point about the other elite quarterbacks in the league having a talented backfield and using that to their advantage.
"Look at Kansas City and what they do with Mahomes," Jac explained.  "It's Kenneth Walker. Josh Allen; they're running the ball like crazy with (James) Cook."
The younger Collinsworth also pointed out that it felt like Samaje Perine gave the Bengals that throwback running style the team has been looking for in their win over the Miami Dolphins.
It would be coaching malpractice if the Bengals didn't try a way to get the run game going moving forward.
Everyone in that Bengals locker room knows that if the team begins running the ball with success, this offense becomes nearly unbeatable. But are Perine and Chase Brown enough to get this run game going?
To say time is running out when we're only in Week 6 must seem like an exaggeration, but really, there's no time to waste in the NFL.
If the Bengals want to be in the playoff race in December, they must find a way to find success on the ground, and it starts against the Baltimore Ravens in two weeks.

title: Bengals Offensive Line Cementing Among NFL's Top Half as Bye Week Rolls Forward
full_text:
The Bengals offensive line is cementing itself as one of the better blocking units in the league this season. Entering their Week 6 bye, Cincinnati is ranked 13th on Pro Football Focus's latest weekly OL ranking.
They jumped up one spot from the previous week as the continuity from last year is paying off in a big way.
"Four of the Bengals’ five starters on the offensive line have garnered PFF pass-blocking grades above 60.0, and the lowest-graded of the five, Ted Karras, has only been slightly below that mark at a 59.2. Right guard Dalton Risner is having an impressive season as a run-blocker, ranking third among right guards with an 80.7 PFF run-blocking grade," Gordon McGuinness wrote .
The raw PFF grades drive home what could be an even higher ranking. Cincinnati is now sixth in the NFL in PFF pass-blocking grade (70.8), while the run blockin g leaves more to be desired (17th, 62.7 grade).
It's not just PFF that loves the Bengals' blockers; Pro Football Network has the unit ranked 12th overall in its impact rankings . They've seemingly pulled off the long-time goal of blocking competence surrounding Joe Burrow.
Bengals head coach Zac Taylor knows his team can keep getting even better, including the offensive line.
"There's a lot of moments where all the units played really well and did some really good things to build on," Taylor said on Monday. "And so coming out of Week 5, I think we recognize some things that we're doing really well, and then there's a couple of things that are really easy to clean up, real easy. So the good news is it's not a concern that Oh man, this is unfixable. We got a real problem here on this part of a scheme or a player, and we don't feel that at all. It's just a couple of things that we gotta get cleaned up going into the next division game."
Cincinnati's allowed one of the five lowest pressure rates this season as well.

title: Cincinnati Bengals Players Fined For Separate Plays Following Dolphins Win
full_text:
A pair of Bengals took on fines for separate plays in this past Sunday's win over Miami. Our Jay Morrison noted on Saturday that Erick All and Jordan Battle got infractions handed down from the league.
"Erick All Jr. fined $7,073 for an unnecessary roughness penalty against Miami. Jordan Battle fined $21,623 for illegal use of helmet," Morrison posted on X .
Cincinnati got physical in the win over one of the few winless teams remaining in the NFL. All and Battle were huge parts of those wins to help Cincinnati get to 3-2 on the season.
It was a hot, tightly contested game filled with tough hits like the ones that got those players penalized.
"Nothing really at this point in October gets you ready for this heat. Somebody told me it started as the hottest game here in October history, which I can attest to," Taylor said about the hot Miami weather after the 31-24 win. "I've coached here for four years, and this was, I mean, in pregame, I was worn out. Our players fought through that, and I made that statement to them because I know they're dead tired right now. I didn't want them to think that's just in their mind, like, what's wrong with me? It was a hot day, and they battled through it, and they found a way to win. I don't discount that at all."
Cincinnati has a couple more days off before returning to practice on Monday ahead of the most important game of the season so far.
An AFC North matchup against Baltimore awaits .
"You kind of like it more towards Thanksgiving," Taylor said about the bye week placement on Monday. "But I do think just where our team is right now, and the way that these last three games have gone down to the wire, and guys playing through some stuff right now, it is a good time to get a bye and get our legs back underneath us, get some guys healthy, and go full force when we come back for Baltimore."
Cincinnati takes on the Ravens next Sunday in Baltimore.

title: 3 Potential Trades the Bengals Could Make Prior to 2026 Deadline
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals rolled into the bye week 3-2.
Work needs to be done, but this team still has the pieces to make a long run in the postseason. It cannot be denied that fixing the issues needs to happen quickly.
What do those changes look like? The easy answer could be in the form of a trade. Here are three potential trades the Bengals could make if they plan on being all-in on a Super Bowl run this season.
The Bengals' linebacker play has not been on par for a team that is chasing a deep playoff run. That's where Tennessee Titans linebacker Cody Barton comes into play.
Not to bash on the Titans, but they are a team that is far away from being a competitor. If they have pieces that can bring back value, they could be a very active team at the deadline.
Barton is a piece that can bring them back some value while also giving a competitive team a nice addition to their defense.
Pro Football Focus currently has Barton graded as the 27th-best linebacker in the league. The cap hit for the 30-year-old linebacker is over $4 million for the 2026 season.  If it's an all-in situation, Barton would fit the bill.
If the Bengals are looking for secondary depth, Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Tariq Woolen could be an option.
The Eagles seem to be unsure what the future holds. The NFC East has looked like a train wreck, as the Eagles are 2-3 but still in second place.
Woolen's cap hit would only be $910,000 if a team were to make a trade. That could make this a high-upside situation for the Bengals.
A familiar name for Bengals fans, Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates III would be a major move. After spending five seasons with the Bengals, including the 2021 season when the team went to the Super Bowl, Bates has spent the last four seasons in Atlanta.
It would be a heavy cap hit to bring Bates back in the fold. But would a $9 million hit to the cap be worth Bates' veteran presence in the secondary? Not to mention, this homecoming could have the fan base buzzing.

title: Ravens Star Quarterback Lamar Jackson Carrying Injury Into Bengals Game Week
full_text:
The Bengals may not be facing Lamar Jackson next week.
The Ravens star quarterback injured his ankle in the team's Week 4 win over Tennessee, and he has not practiced in any session since then, with the Bengals up next in Week 7. He is not playing in Week 6 when the Ravens suit up in a couple of days.
“It’s Wednesday. There’s a lot of time between now and Sunday,” Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said last week. “To Lamar’s credit, he’s getting a lot of treatment and doing things. There’ll be a point later in the week where we’ll kinda figure out where it’s at ... When he’s ready to play, he’ll be ready to play.”
It would be a massive loss for Baltimore, which has dominated Cincinnati in Jackson starts. The team is 11-3 against Cincinnati when Jackson is on the field.
He's been lights out, with 7.9 yards per attempt, 24 passing touchdowns, six interceptions, and a 101.9 passer rating in those games. Whether it's Jackson or Tyler Huntley out there next week, Cincinnati is aiming to be ready.
Zac Taylor is hoping to have as many healthy players as possible after Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins gutted through injury in Miami.
"Hats off to them. They wanted to play, and Ja'Marr had to clear protocol on Saturday," Taylor said about the duo. "His mindset all along was, 'I'm playing." Now I hadn't seen him on the field enough to know. I appreciate him saying that, but I need to see him do it in practice, and he did. For those guys to go out there and make plays that they did for us is a big time. I don't ever question that.
"Those guys have been here seven years, six years, and they show up for us every chance they get. We have leaders and great players like that on our team. It sets the tone for everybody else when those guys are playing through injuries and doing everything they can to come down here and play in Miami before bye week. They could easily say, give me a week off, we'll get the bye week, and we'll come back for the divisional game, but they didn't want to do that."
Cincinnati battles the Ravens at 1 p.m. ET next Sunday.

title: Bengals Bye Week Self-Scout Reveals What's Working and What Must Change
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals are off to a solid start after five games with a 3-2 record and normally we would dissect the opponent and dive into the data to get a feel for how they're performing this season, but with the bye week already here, it's time for some self-scouting and dissecting where the Bengals stand after five games.
Let's start on offense where they avoided the dreaded slow start and rank 10th in EPA per play and PFF has them as the 5th highest graded offense.
Joe Burrow is again PFF’s highest graded passer on plays without play-action. He has been ranked number one in 2021, 2022, 2024, 2025 and now holds that top spot in 2026.
Does it feel like Burrow and this offense hasn't been explosive this year? I'm sure they want to create more big plays, but Burrow leads the league in 20+ yard touchdown passes with five. He's also one of four quarterbacks without a “turnover worthy throw” on deep passes. His 137.9 passer rating on deep balls leads the entire NFL.
But it's really the Intermediate area where Burrow is doing his damage to opposing defenses.
22.8% of his total passes are targeted between 10-19 yards this season and his 95.7 PFF grade leads all quarterbacks.
He's completing 74.4% of his passes in this range and that also tops all QBs. And the Bengals are getting big plays out of it as Burrow averages 12.0 yards per attempt in this area.
It probably helps that he's getting protected up front with the best offensive line of his career. This Cincinnati line ranks 6th in PFF’s Pass Block Efficiency.
Their 4.5% sack rate - 5th Best in NFL and they were 10th last year and 19th in 2024. Looks like steady progress for a QB and offensive line that has been heavily criticized for allowing too much pressure and taking too many sacks.
Look no further than right tackle Amarius Mims and his 98.8% pass block efficiency which is second amongst all offensive tackles.
Dalton Risner at right guard is the 5th highest graded pass blocking guard in True Pass Sets from PFF and he's enjoying a career year as a run blocker as well.
Despite allowing pressure on just 36.3% of all dropbacks this season, which ranks 7th best, the Bengals are allowing pressure on 3rd downs at a higher rate than I'd like. On 51.9% of their 3rd down passes, Burrow is facing pressure and yes, they're  converting 50% of third downs this season, that's tied for second-best.
The issue is that they're seeing the 11th most 3rd downs in the NFL. You don't want to put your QB under that much pressure on critical down and the other two top teams in 3rd down conversions, Buffalo and San Francisco, are seeing 3rd downs at the lowest rate in the league.
The run game has been a big topic the last few weeks as they've struggled to get Chase Brown going despite some decent blocking overall.
Brown is currently outside the top 35 backs in average yards AFTER contact at 2.1 and his Elusive Rating from PFF ranks him 22nd amongst the 32 starters in the league.
Last season, Brown averaged 3.4 yards after contact per carry.
It's not all Brown either, as a whole the Bengals sit at 2.03 Average Rush Yards After Contact - 31st in the NFL
The Bengals running scheme should be helping him here: They've only been “Stuffed” on 13.2% of rushing plays - 8th best in the league – They led the NFL last season at a 10% stuffed rate.
But, they're not converting that into explosives or successful runs.
Their 39.5% Rushing Success Rate ranks 20th after being 11th-best last season at 42.8%
Where are the issues with the blocking? Amarius Mims is the 4th lowest graded offensive tackle in Run Blocking from PFF.
Drew Sample ranks 37th and Erick All 44th of 51 total right ends in PFF run blocking.
With the lack of success running the ball, the offseason plan of getting under center and running the ball and exploiting defenses with play-action has been thrown out. The Bengals have the 2nd lowest rate of play-action in NFL this season.
So it's back to the Bengals offense of old. Even if they figure out the run game, I expect this shotgun offense to lead the way and that's not a bad thing.
The offense usually fires up at this point in the season. Since 2021, the Bengals are the very best offense in the league (EPA per play) in weeks 6 through 12.
That's 5 years of sustained elite offensive success and that includes 10 games started by the combo of Jake Browning and Joe Flacco.
Is it the same old Bengals on defense?
Cincinnati owns the 12th ranked defense based on EPA per play. We would take that all season long.
They're 5th in passing EPA, but rank 26th on defense for PFF and they're dragged down by the 28th ranked Coverage grade and 26th ranked Tackling grade.
They're currently the 7th best defense in terms of EPA per play when in their base 3-4 defense. That ranking drops to 22nd when they're in Nickel defense.
A run defense that boasts a league-leading 30% Run Stuff Rate, but 21 runs of 10+ yards allowed leads the NFL also.
They're very home run or strikeout in run defense.
The Bengals are doing this all with a Light Box (less defenders near the line). They lead the league in light box rate at 59.6% of their total defensive snaps and that would explain some of the long runs that have gashed this defense.
You can play with less defenders in the box when Dexter Lawrence accounts for two people. He's been everything we could've hoped for as he enjoys a bounce back season on the stat sheet. Lawrence is on pace for 65 pressures and 10 sacks this season and currently owns PFF’s second highest grade for defensive tackles.
As a whole, the Bengals defense is generating pressure on 41.6% of pass plays and that ranks 12th best in the league.
Much of that is thanks to free agent prize Boye Mafe and his 25 pressures through five games. That's a pace of 85 pressures for a full season. Only three players had more last season and 83 is the most Trey Hendrickson ever had with the Bengals (2024).
And they're doing with the frustratingly low Blitz Rate of 17.3% – lowest in the NFL.
So what are they doing on defense? They play the 10th-most single-high safety coverages with  the 9th-most Man Coverage calls.
They're also not disguising their coverages. They rotate safety coverage at the snap on 29% of plays and that's 9th least in the NFL.
But coverage has been tight. DJ Turner looks just as good in coverage as he did last season, but quarterbacks are avoiding throwing in his direction.
And why would they throw at him or Dax Hill when the linebackers and safeties offer easier completions?
The trio of Demetrius Knight, Barrett Carter and Jordan Battle have allowed 46 passes to be caught out of 58 targets. That's a completion percentage of 79.3% when you target those guys in coverage.
The coverage hasn't been all bad as 15.9% of all throws have been contested by the Bengals defense - 7th best rate in the NFL.
But when you play as much Man coverage as you do, you leave yourself open up the middle and they've allowed 145 QB scramble yards and that's 3rd most in the NFL. They'll have to figure that out before seeing Lamar Jackson this season.
Finally, they're currently averaging 8 penalties per game which is 19th worst and up from their 5 penalties per game last season. This is an area under Zac Taylor where they've always been exceptional and because it's always been good during his run as head coach, I expect it'll be smoothed out, but it is something to watch as it has affected their games to start the season.
Overall, they've got things to clean up and figure out as every team does. Zac Taylor teams do a good job at figuring those things out as they do and they tend to play their best as the season progresses. Since 2021, Zac Taylor and Joe Burrow together have won 75% of all games after the bye week. With 12 games to go, that's another 9 wins.
I'll take 12-5, even if it feels harder than it should.
Joe Goodberry has been analyzing, critiquing and writing about the Bengals for more than a decade. His various works have been featured on every major…

title: Browns May Have Beaten Ravens, But Deshaun Watson's Struggles Put Team in Difficult Spot
full_text:
The late great John Madden used to say that “winning is the greatest deodorant”, but the AFC North leading Cleveland Browns might be considered an exception.
Even standing at 4-2 and owning the first two tie-breakers over the Ravens courtesy of their Week 6 victory at Huntington Field on Sunday, 13-10 , Deshaun Watson has been stinking it up at the quarterback position.
Against Baltimore, Cleveland had all of 11 passing yards at the halfway mark, at which point Watson had completed just 3 out of 9 pass attempts, and had been sacked three times. At halftime, Baltimore was leading 10-0, and over the course of the following two quarters did everything in their power to end up with the “L”, but that doesn’t erase just how awful Watson was playing up to that point.
In the third quarter, Watson went 5 for 5 for 46 yards before finding a little rhythm late with an 8 for 12 fourth quarter for 94 yards, bringing his final stat line of 16 for 26 for 164 underwhelming but at the same time deceiving yards against the Ravens, while also getting sacked two more times over the final half. His QBR for the game was a miserable 22.8.
The Browns have been winning despite a subpar performance by Watson all season long. Yes, he’s been able to engineer four game winning drives so far , but the fact remains that Cleveland’s offense has barely resembled a professional outfit throughout most of the team’s six games to date.
And while there are several issues on offense that don’t depend on Watson -- like the team’s still struggling ground game -- the quarterback is literally putting the Browns behind the 8-ball. Before today’s game against the Ravens, Watson had been sacked a league-leading 19 times, most of them his responsibility.
Out of those 19 sacks, eight had come on first down, and 13 of them with 10 or more yards to go, including three on third and 10+ to go. Among today’s five sacks, one came on first and 10, another on second and 10, and the other three on third down, including a third and 14 to go.
Another interesting split is that before today’s game, he was completing just 47.2 percent of his throws on third down. Facing Baltimore, he managed to convert three times out of 16 pass attempts on third downs for the game.
Watson entered today’s matchup ranked 26 out of 33 qualified passers in Total QBR, while the Browns are currently third in the league with 31 punts so far, including all five first half drives against the Ravens today.
A win is a win, there’s no denying that, and any Cleveland Brown will appreciate it. But the current trend of winning despite Watson is unsustainable.
To make matters worse, there is no Plan-B ready to go for the Browns.
Cleveland went all in with Watson when the team decided back in preseason that they were sticking with the 31 year-old veteran as the starter after not playing an official game in almost two years. After all that has transpired since second-year passer Shedeur Sanders led the team to three victories over the second half of last season, including the firing of Kevin Stefanski as head coach and the hiring of Todd Monken to replace him, and a quarterback battle between Sanders and Watson that nobody expected -- while leaving fellow second-year passer Dillon Gabriel on the sideline -- only to hand Watson the starting gig, the only way to sit Watson now is to do it in a definitive manner.
The Browns have been overselling Watson so hard throughout the last few months, that Cleveland can’t bench him unless it’s for good, and that won’t happen while the victories, no matter how narrow, keep coming.
On one hand, Watson has at least shown enough resiliency to bring those four wins home. On the other, the Browns don’t seem to have a plan anymore for Sanders -- nor Gabriel, for that matter.
So it’s become Watson or bust for the Browns, and with the team installed in first place of the AFC North, some would say you don’t need to fix something that isn’t broken. However, the team’s offense, especially at the quarterback position, is evidently broken -- just not broken enough for Cleveland to be losing the games that would inch them closer to one of the top quarterback prospects for next year’s draft .
In that sense, winning despite Watson playing so poorly has become Cleveland’s most recent quarterback curse, because if we’re being honest, how long do you expect to continue to win with this caliber of play at the trigger. And if you do continue to win a few more games, are you really entertaining the idea of extending one of the worst contracts in league history, with what Watson has been showing so far?
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: Where's the Extension? Browns' Andre Szmyt Deserves One After Game-Winner vs. Ravens
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have one of the league's best kickers under contract.
Yet, the 28-year-old, Andre Szmyt, sits on just a one-year, $1.015 million deal.
On Sunday, Oct. 18, Szmyt added to an already impressive resume that he has built up over the last two seasons, smacking through a 37-yard field goal to walk off the Baltimore Ravens at home, 13-10. His game-winner was his second made field goal of the day, with his first being a 48-yard attempt.
Leading him down the field to give the Browns the win was starter Deshaun Watson, who has routinely put Szmyt in positions to help propel the team to a win.
This season, Szmyt has made 12 kicks on 13 attempts, making him one of the more consistent legs in the league.
Now, especially after Sunday, would be the perfect time for the Browns' front office to reward the second-year pro.
Nobody is asking them to give him a four-year deal or break the bank, but extending him for another year would at least give him more comfort. Such a decision would also show loyalty from the organization.
Szmyt walked into Sunday's outing against the Ravens needing just five made field goals to tie the franchise record for the most consecutive field goals made. He had 24; Browns legend Phil Dawson had 29.
He would start off the day making his first kick, an attempt from 48 yards, but would later go on to miss one from the same distance, thus ending his chance at breaking Dawson's record.
Just four kicks back from tying the record at a mark of 25, though, Szmyt showed remarkable consistency. He now sits third in the Browns' all-time rankings in consecutive made field goals.
Routinely, Szmyt has been called upon to make a kick to give the Browns the lead or tie the game.
Across the past two seasons, he has had four game-winning kicks , two of which have been in the last three weeks. He walked off the Pittsburgh Steelers just a few weeks ago during a Thursday Night Football showdown, giving the Browns a 27-24 edge.
The best part, too, is that Szmyt isn't afraid of situations like that. He understands the pressure, but welcomes the opportunity.
"No, it doesn't; it's exciting," he said following Sunday's game-winner. "It's a love-hate feeling when you go out there for it. It's obviously a lot of pressure, but that's what we train for; that's what we prepare for.  You want to be in those situations, walking it off."
Caught up with Andre Szmyt in the locker room after hitting the game-winning, walk-off field goal in the #Browns 13-10 victory over the Ravens. Asked him if it ever gets old. I'm sure you can guess the answer. "No, it doesn't; it's exciting. It's a love-hate feeling when you go… pic.twitter.com/E5vY6Ne6Zh
And while Szmyt being as good as he is justifies a contract extension on its own, the fact that the Browns have struggled to find a consistent leg over the last few seasons does as well.
Since Dawson left the team way back before the 2013 season, the team has shuffled through kickers left and right. Back in the 2022 NFL Draft, the front office even tried to land the future at the position with a fourth-round pick. Ultimately, it didn't end up working out.
Finally, it seems like they have a long-term option.
Why risk the chance of him leaving in the offseason?
While the Browns have been cheap in recent years, mainly due to the contractual obligation following the trade for Watson, it feels hard to imagine the front office will ignore just how impactful Szmyt has been over the course of the last two seasons.
Returning to the gridiron on Sunday, Oct. 25, the Browns and Szmyt will look to continue chasing the top spot in the AFC North as they take on the Tennessee Titans on the road in Nashville.
The two sides will collide at 1:00 p.m. EST.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Deshaun Watson Extends League-Leading Statistic As Andre Szmyt Comes Up Clutch Again
full_text:
It wasn't a pretty day... not by any means.
But yet again, somehow, someway the Cleveland Browns have won another football game.
"Our guys are a scrappy group," said head coach Todd Monken.
On Sunday, Oct. 18, the Browns took down the Baltimore Ravens at home in a Week 6 in-division clash , 13-10. Starting quarterback Deshaun Watson, who began the season strong before falling off in the last few weeks, struggled mightily throughout the contest.
He finished with just 164 passing yards on 26 attempts, completing 16, but led the team to a game-winning drive that saw a 33-yard connection to wideout Jerry Jeudy.
He now leads the league in game-winning drives with four.
The game was then capped off by Browns kicker Andre Szmyt knocking through a 37-yard field goal to push the Browns to 4-2 on the season.
"It's been the last five weeks. It's been an unbelievable credit to our team," Monken said. "Especially our defense, early on, you know, after 10 points, shutting them out...it gives us a chance to win...
"Just the way our guys work and the way they believe, there's just something about this group that makes them special... We have a lot to work on and we'll go back to work tomorrow...But that was pretty cool."
Szymt had his initial attempt to win the game blocked, but Ravens defensive back Keyon Martin was ruled offsides.
For the Browns, it was a big sigh of relief.
Earlier in the contest, Szmyt, one of the league's most consistent kickers, had missed wide left on a 48-yard attempt that would have put the team up 13-10. Fortunately, he got his redemption.
Now, on the campaign, the 28-year-old is 12-for-13 on field goals while also making eight of his nine tries on PATs.
It is obviously a great sign to see Cleveland establish a consistent and reliable leg, but such circumstances show just how rough the offense has been this season. Both the passing and rushing attack have been incredibly inconsistent, which has led to the Browns having to rely on Szmyt far too often.
As a team, the Browns finished with a combined 237 yards of offense, 144 of which came from the passing game. The other 93 came from the rushing attack, with Jaleel McLaughlin leading the charge, taking nine carries for 41 yards.
With injuries and inconsistencies smacking the Browns left, right and center, players like McLaughlin are going to have to continue stepping up to try and light a spark for the offense, even if you'd rather see your $230 million quarterback do it.
He has simply not lived up to expectations over the last two weeks, throwing for a combined 319 yards and one score. He has also completed just 52.5% of his tries.
The Browns can scrape and claw to wins all they want in the early parts of the season, but when the playoff-deciding games start to arrive in a few weeks, teams are going to be at their best. And if the Browns want any chance of playing competitive football beyond the regular season, the offense is going to need to be better , Watson included.
“We just got to flatten out some of the other ups and downs that we have … It’s a we thing, not an individual thing," Monken said Sunday.
Returning to the field on Sunday, Oct. 25, the Browns will have a chance to reestablish the offense in an outing against the 1-5 Tennessee Titans.
The two sides will play at 1:00 p.m. EST from Nissan Stadium in Nashville.
