title: How the Browns' Week 6 Injury Report Will Make or Break Matchup with Ravens
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are set to host the Baltimore Ravens in week six of the 2026 NFL season.
For the Browns, they have had some key players go down with injury. Let's look at the full report and break down how each injury will affect the team.
For the first time this season, the Browns will have to play without their starting running back Quinshon Judkins .
Judkins finished the game last week against the New York Jets, but ultimately is out with an ankle injury.
So far this season, Cleveland has already struggled to find offensive production through the running game. Now, they will have to try to run the ball without their starter against a top-10 run defense in the NFL.
The good news for Browns fans is that Judkins did practice on Friday, but he ultimately still needs more time before he gets back on the field.
Along with Judkins, Schwesinger finished last Sunday's game against the Jets but is also dealing with an ankle injury.
Despite only getting one limited practice in on Friday, Schwesinger is going to suit up against Baltimore.
For the Browns, it is huge to have their defensive anchor out there on the field, but they do need to be careful. With such limited reps, you can't risk worsening the injury and putting even more of the season at risk.
Mason Graham has been out since week four, when he injured his knee and ankle against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
While limited, the good news for Cleveland is that Graham was able to practice on Friday.
It still may be another game or two, but the team's sack leader is slowly getting back out there on the field.
For the Browns, they have done a great job on the field of still getting pressure and sacks without their top guy. Maliek Collins deserves some major flowers after his great performance a week ago.
Browns - Ravens Friday injury report https://t.co/fGHYpgS4vj pic.twitter.com/aa3ndpPXW4
For the Browns, they continue to go without their other running back, Dylan Sampson.
Sampson was placed on IR after week one with a knee injury, but was back at practice this week with limited reps on Thursday and Friday.
One big injury, or really the lack thereof, that most people are overlooking is the fact that KC Concepcion won't miss this game.
Last week, Concepcion took a controversial hit from Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick to the head and was instantly ruled out of the game. While many thought the 2026 first-round pick would miss extended time, he is good to go in the very next week.
#Browns inactives: RB Quinshon Judkins QB Taylen Green (3QB) CB Noah Igbinoghene DT Mike Hall Jr. C Parker Brailsford G Teven Jenkins DT Mason Graham
While this is a focus on Browns' injuries this week, the Ravens have the biggest loss with Lamar Jackson being ruled out once again.
While it is by no means a free win against Tyler Huntley, the Browns must take advantage of one of the NFL's best being out.
A win here is incredibly important, especially since this is a divisional battle.

title: Browns Still Without Mason Graham, Make Moves To Fill Void Ahead of Sunday
full_text:
For a second straight week, the Cleveland Browns will be without standout second-year defensive tackle Mason Graham.
On Saturday, Oct. 17, the Browns announced that Graham, due to a lower-body injury, was questionable for Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens . The 23-year-old suffered his injury in the Browns' Thursday Night Football showdown with the Pittsburgh Steelers just a few weeks ago.
Along with Graham's absence, the Browns will be without defensive linemen Mike Hall Jr. and Kalia Davis.
Each has been slowly but surely recovering, but to be safe, the front office has made a few moves to fill their voids.
In the wake of Graham's "questionable" diagnosis and Hall Jr. and Davis being ruled out, the front office has elevated defensive tackles Chris Williams and Sam Kamara to the active roster.
This isn't the first time the Browns have had to use either, though.
Kamara waltzed out in front of a packed MetLife Stadium last weekend, recording three tackles and the first sack of his NFL career. Williams, on the other hand, didn't get in the stat sheet, but will continue to help the Browns' depth at the position.
While both weren't able to do enough to guide the Browns to a victory over the Jets last weekend, they did receive praise from head coach Todd Monken.
The first-year leader shared that they both provided the team with valuable time on the field.
“Those guys that got elevated really gave us some valuable minutes,” Monken said following the 27-20 loss.
The defensive line is now expected to see the likes of Williams, Kamara, Maliek Collins and Adin Huntington. On the outside, Jared Verse, Sam Williams and Isaiah McGuire will eat up a majority of the snaps.
The line is certainly banged up , more than it has been in quite a while in Cleveland, but that shouldn't stop the young, hungry group that is available from putting together a strong showing against the Ravens.
It is never good to see a player injured, especially one as talented as Lamar Jackson, but with the Browns' recent injury spell, being able to face a Ravens squad that will not have him available is a big break.
Jackson is recovering from an ankle injury he suffered against the Tennessee Titans back in Week 4. Since then, he hasn't practiced.
In his place, the Ravens will turn to Tyler Huntley to be the man under center, someone Cleveland is relatively familiar with. While he doesn't have the speed that Jackson does, he is pretty mobile, and the Browns' defensive line will have to be ready to track him down if he starts to roll towards the hashes.
With how Kamara stepped up last week, and the opportunity available in front of Williams, there should be little concern for how the Browns will look defensively.
As long as the rest of the squad does its job, they should be good to go.
The Browns and Ravens will clash from Huntington Bank Field on Sunday, Oct. 18, at 1:00 p.m. EST.

title: Ranking the Browns Players Most Likely to be Traded Before the Deadline
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is less than a month away, and the Cleveland Browns sit at 3-2 with four more games to decide if they should be buyers or sellers .
The deadline in the NFL is different from what it is across other sprots, as it does not have a flurry of players changing teams. However, should the Browns fall in the standings over the next four games, then these are the most likely players to be moved.
Delpit signed a contract extension in the offseason, but a team may be willing to give a haul for the veteran’s services. The Browns used a second-round pick on Emmanuel McNeil-Warren, and he has been getting more playing time as the season has progressed. Delpit is a terrific defender, especially around the line of scrimmage and a return would require several picks, including as high as the first round due to his contract length. The 2027 draft will be loaded and the Browns could go in with three first-round picks.
Possible fits: Detroit Lions, Dallas Cowboys, Carolina Panthers
McNeil-Warren has been playing free safety, which is Hickman’s position. Hickman is also a free agent and the Browns spent big money on Delpit, so he may be too expensive for an extension next season. While Hickman will not get the same return as Delpit would, he can still  get some good picks. He was an undrafted free agent and the return for him would be a big win for the Browns.
Possible fits: Detroit Lions, Dallas Cowboys, Carolina Panthers
The defensive line would not be as productive without Collins. He has been a monster since signing with Cleveland, but he is on an expiring contract and can really bolster a contender’s defense. Mason Graham and Mike Hall Jr. will return from injury to fill in for Collins and if he does not resign with the team in the offseason, then it is best to get a return for him should the Browns find themselves down in the standings. The return could be two middle-round picks, which the Browns have plenty of to be able to package and move higher in the draft.
Possible fits: Cincinnati Bengals, Chicago Bears, Denver Broncos
Jenkins is currently out with a back injury and rookie Austin Barber has usurped him in the depth chart. He is a free agent at the end of the year, and playoff teams get desperate for offensive line depth to make it through the end of the season. Jenkins will not garner much in terms of a return, but he can be packaged with a late-round pick to move up one round.
Possible fits: Seattle Seahawks, New Orleans Saints, Los Angeles Rams
The inconsistent wide receiver could be intriguing for a contender. The Arizona Cardinals got a second-round pick for the disappointing Marvin Harrison Jr. , but Jeudy is older and would not be reuniting with his college quarterback. The wide receiver room got full with the emergence of Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, so Jeudy’s role has been limited. The Browns could get two middle- round picks in return for trading him.
Possible fits: Buffalo Bills, Philadelphia Eagles, Los Angeles Rams
Sanders hired an agent, which could mean that he wants to be traded out of Cleveland as Deshaun Watson has been the starting quarterback all season. Harrison Jr. also hired an agent to explore a trade prior to his transaction. Dillon Gabriel has to come off the injured list in the next couple of weeks, and he can move to the backup role. A return for Sanders is questionable as he was a fifth-round pick and did not play particularly well in his limited time last season.
Should losses pile up, then it may be wise to consider moving some pieces for future capital. The Browns have two-first round picks and three-fourth round picks for the draft. Andrew Berry has been stocking up and these players can bring in what Berry is seeking. For now the Browns have a winning record, but the NFL season moves fast and big decisions will have to be made.
Graduated from Bowling Green State University with a Journalism degree. Written and contributed to numerous media outlets. Cleveland sports victim.

title: How Andre Szmyt Has Evolved His Game to Earn a Big Contract Extension
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns haven't had the best luck in the past signing or drafting kickers.
Just a few years ago, the front office drafted kicker Cade York out of LSU in the fourth round of the 2022 NFL Draft. At the time, it was a controversial decision. And years later, it still is, as York would end up going 24-for-32 in his first season before being waived.
Since Phil Dawson left the organization in 2013, 16 different players , including York, have served as placekickers.
Finally, though, the Browns may have ended such a cycle.
Ahead of the 2025 campaign, the front office signed undrafted free agent kicker Andre Szmyt, a standout at Syracuse University. While he was initially brought in to serve as extra depth for the organization during training camp and offseason work, he stole the spotlight from Dustin Hopkins and won the job.
Across the last two campaigns, Szmyt has been remarkable , making 34 of his 37 field goal attempts. He has also connected on 32 of 34 extra-point attempts.
One of the most impressive parts, though, is his consistency from deep.
He has knocked through seven field goals from 50 yards or further on eight attempts , with a long of 55 yards in 2025 and 56 yards in 2026.
ANDRE SZMYT FROM 56 YARDS FOR THE WIN! pic.twitter.com/64qGSekF7q
Not only does the 28-year-old have a pretty powerful leg, but a consistent one as well.
He is approaching franchise history, sitting with 24 consecutive field goals made, dating back to the 2025 season. Heading into a week six matchup against the Baltimore Ravens, that mark is the third-longest in Browns history.
If he can knock through a few more over the course of the next few weeks, he may be able to steal the No. 1 spot.
Currently, the top two spots are being held by Dawson, who recorded streaks of 27 and 29 consecutive made kicks.
🚨 UNDER THE RADAR: Browns kicker Andre Szmyt is quietly approaching franchise history. Szmyt has made TWENTY-FOUR consecutive field goals. That’s the THIRD-LONGEST streak in Cleveland Browns history. pic.twitter.com/YSYfAd8Hfo
But it is hard to imagine that a kicker with such a strong start to his NFL career is sitting in long-term limbo.
After putting together that strong rookie stint in 2025, he was a free agent this past offseason. Eventually, the Browns and Szmyt met on a one-year, $1,005,000 deal to bring him back to Cleveland for the 2026 season.
With how well he has started the year, though, and the historic record he is approaching, a contract extension has to be on the minds of both Szmyt and the front office.
Due to the immense struggles the organization has faced in the position over the last decade, locking down a leg like Szmyt's has to be a priority.
Most FG made without a miss this season Spencer Shrader          16 Will Reichard                 15 Andre Szmyt                  10 Chase McLaughlin       10 Evan McPherson          10 Jason Myers                   10 pic.twitter.com/YGELg0GDjy
Recent high-end kicker contracts have seen Chris Boswell of the Pittsburgh Steelers land a 4-year, $28 million deal, and Brandon Aubrey of the Dallas Cowboys sign a 4-year, $28 million deal with $20 million guaranteed.
While Szmyt is not at that level just yet, he could see a two-to-three-year deal worth roughly $4.5 million a season. That would give him a bigger picture of 3 years at $13.5 million.
For a kicker like Szmyt, who is still establishing himself in the NFL, a multi-year contract would provide the security and confidence to develop while protecting the Browns from making too significant of an investment in a relatively questionable position.
If he keeps this up, maintaining the consistency he has shown through the last 22 games, a piece of paper with a good chunk of change should end up on his desk in due time.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Browns Get Much-Needed Injury Boost Ahead of Ravens Showdown
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have a chance to top the AFC North again. Luckily for them, they just received big injury news.
The Browns lost to the New York Jets in Week 5 of the NFL season in a sloppy, rainy game. Cleveland emerged from the loss with additional injury concerns and opened Week 6 with 17 players on its injury report. Important players on that list included Carson Schewsinger, Mason Graham, Quinshon Judkins, and Derek Barnett.
The Browns got some big names back at practice today: Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham, Quinshon Judkins and Derek Barnett. Not practicing: Mike Hall, Teven Jenkins, Kalia Davis. pic.twitter.com/FMTfDWDLkW
All four players returned to practice Friday, according to ESPN’s Daniel Oyefusi. Their return raises the possibility that all four could play in the pivotal division matchup vs. the Baltimore Ravens.
The Browns' run game has been less than desirable early in the NFL season. However, those struggles could worsen Sunday if the Browns are without their lead back, Quinshon Judkins.
Without Judkins, Cleveland would likely lean on Jaleel McLaughlin and Audric Estime, who joined the team from Minnesota’s practice squad this week. Dylan Sampson’s potential return could also affect the backfield. Judkins’ return to practice offers encouragement for a Browns rushing attack still searching for consistency.
Arguably, the three most important players to return to practice are Mason Graham, Carson Schwesinger, and Derek Barnett. Graham got hurt during the Browns' Thursday Night Football game vs. the Pittsburgh Steelers in a scary injury many thought would take him out for multiple weeks. Now, just two weeks later, the star defensive tackle has returned to practice.
Having Graham, Schwesinger, and Barnett available matters because the Browns need to stop the run against one of the league's best backs, Derrick Henry . The Ravens' starting quarterback, Lamar Jackson, hasn't practiced all week leading up to the Browns matchup.
Ravens QB Lamar Jackson is not present during media viewing portion of Friday’s practice, which indicates Tyler Huntley will likely start for the second straight week. Jackson missed every practice this week and hasn’t suited up since spraining his left ankle in a win over the…
Considering the Browns allowed 134 rushing yards just a week ago to a less talented Jets team, Henry will get his fair share of carries. Graham missed that matchup, and having him available alongside Schwesinger and Barnett would give Cleveland a better chance to contain Baltimore’s ground game.
The Browns now have several key players back at practice ahead of Sunday’s matchup with the Ravens. With Lamar Jackson, the Ravens' MVP quarterback, potentially unavailable Sunday, the Browns have a real chance to reclaim the AFC North.
The question now is whether the team will rise to the occasion as it did in Weeks 2 through 4 or fumble an opportunity as it did in Weeks 1 and 5.
Noah Olson is a Northeast Ohio native and lifelong Cleveland sports fan. He graduated from The College of Wooster with a major in Communications and has been sports writing since 2024. As a writer for BIGPLAY On SI, Noah brings a blend of local pride and an insider’s perspective, focusing on thoughtful analysis and storytelling rooted in Cleveland sports culture.

title: 4 Burning Questions Facing the Browns This Week
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are set to host the Baltimore Ravens at home in week six.
After last week's loss to the New York Jets , the Browns have a couple of questions they need to answer.
So far this season, Quinshon Judkins has yet to get back to his rookie-season form.
Through 73 rushing attempts, Judkins has only 221 yards and one touchdown. That averages out to just over three yards per carry.
Last week against the Jets, Cleveland had their chance to finally find out who they were on the ground. New York ranked 25th in rushing defense, yet the Browns still couldn't run the ball.
Now, Cleveland faces a Baltimore defense that ranks 11th in run defense and always brings an extra juice against AFC North rivals.
WOW: #Browns defense guilty of THREE penalties on ONE play and lose Mason Graham #NFL #TNF pic.twitter.com/PzHiPklMOk
Last week, the Browns did a better job of not hurting themselves with penalties. Still, they committed six penatlies for 30 yards.
On the season, Cleveland has the most penalties in the NFL with 49.
It has even been so bad at times that somehow the Browns managed to draw three penalties on one play.
A big key to getting the win on Sunday is playing clean football.
Through the first four games, Todd Monken called easy plays where Deshaun Watson just had to get the ball out to his playmakers.
This allowed the Watson to find confidence, the Browns to score points, and ultimately was the recipe for that 3-1 start.
Then the Jets game happened. It seemed as if Todd Monken was not play-calling as usual. While the rain may have played a factor, Cleveland still has to stay true to what they can do well.
Time after time, Deshaun Watson has proved that he is not the best at pushing the ball downfield. Even if he had a good throw, receivers like Isaiah Bond weren't able to make the plays happen.
It is incredibly important that the Browns call simpler plays for Watson and the Offense, especially when navigating the Ravens' defense.
Again, once the Browns called bad plays, dropped passes, and got themselves in a hole they weren't able to bounce back.
Coach Monken needs to rally his troops and get their heads back in the game in times of poor performance. Let's be honest, there is almost guaranteed to be at least one of those moments every game.
Overall, they will need to have their heads in the full 60 minute game.
No matter what happens, neither team will give up. That's AFC North football.

title: Browns Rookie Receives Highest PFF Grade among 2026 Draft Class
full_text:
After five weeks of the 2026 NFL season, PFF put out their rookie rankings by overall grade.
While many believe Cleveland won the 2026 NFL Draft , the rookie who ranks atop all the others may not be the one you're thinking of from the Brown and Orange.
Emmanuel McNeil-Warren is looking special pic.twitter.com/zcF1Nj0Bsb
Emmanuel McNeil-Warren has the highest PFF grade of any rookie this season through the first few games.
Somehow, the prospect fell all the way to pick 58 overall in April.
McNeil-Warren currently has a PFF grade of 89.9.
This number not only ranks him as the best of all rookies, but also the best of all 96 NFL safeties.
As for the stat line, EMW has 22 total tackles with only 4 targets allowed over 109 total snaps. Additionally, his average passer rating allowed per game is only 27.6.
But it's not necessarily the numbers that are the reason why the rookie is so great.
If you showed a regular fan highlights of the Browns defense, they could never tell McNeil-Warren is only five games in to his pro career.
The reason? His instincts.
Emmanuel McNeil-Warren is ready for primetime Watch how he closes QUICK on both of these balls intended for DK Metcalf to make two high quality pass breakups 👀 pic.twitter.com/brnADB0XoX
Just watching the young stud is incredible. He is already out there jumping passes, making reads, and ultimately playing like a seasoned veteran. The Browns truly have found a playmaker for their secondary
At this point, he is just having to split snaps with Ronnie Hickman. Ultimately, the Browns may decide at some point in the future to move on from Hickman as well, which would free up more snaps for EMW.
Something else we can't just overlook is the other rookie on this PFF top-graded list, who you may have thought sat at the top. Denzel Boston has simply been a beast for the Browns this season.
In five games, the second-round pick out of Washington has 16 catches, with three of those being touchdowns.
Not only does he lead all rookies in receiver yards with 330, but here are some elite NFL names who Boston has out gained:
Clearly, the Cleveland Browns knew what they were doing in the 2026 NFL Draft, especially in the second round.
Outside of Emmanuel McNeil-Warren and Denzel Boston, the Browns have had great success from KC Concepcion, Austin Barber, and Spencer Fano.

title: Dallas Cowboys Injury Updates After Week 6 Loss Include Another Starting Defender
full_text:
As if everything else that has gone wrong for the Dallas Cowboys' defense hasn't been enough, the unit has also been ravaged by injuries to make matters worse.
The Cowboys are missing starters at cornerback, safety and linebacker, and now they are in danger of losing yet another linebacker from the starting lineup.
Dee Winters suffered what was labeled an ankle injury in the first half of the Week 6 loss to the Green Bay Packers and the veteran wasn't able to return after that. It figures that Winters would get hurt during a game in which he made an impact play with an interception he nearly returned for a touchdown.
Winters wasn't the only notable player to get hurt, as wideout and returner KaVontae Turpin came down with a ribs injury on the opening kickoff and did not return, either.
After the game, head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Winters is actually dealing with an Achilles strain. Meanwhile, Turpin has a rib cartilage issue, with the good news being that X-Rays came back clean on the wideout's injury.
"Cowboys LB Dee Winters has an Achilles strain and WR KaVontae Turpin is dealing with a rib cartilage issue. X-rays clean," Nick Harris of the Forth Worth Star-Telegram relayed.
There was some concern about Dak Prescott's ribs after he took a shot to the area during the game and seemed to favor them, but Schotty said he is not aware of the Cowboys quarterback receiving any X-rays , so Prescott seems to be OK.
It isn't immediately clear if either player will miss time.
The Cowboys replaced Turpin with wide receiver Jonathan Mingo on punt returns and running back Tyler Goodson on kickoffs. The former averaged six yards per return and had a long of 16 yards and the latter broke off a 30-yard return and averaged 24.4 pre return over five attempts.
At linebacker, Shemar James took over for Winters and finished with five tackles.
Remember this guy? Sure you do!
With Winters hurt and possibly in danger of missing time, it would be nice to get DeMarvion Overshown back in Week 7.
Overshown suffered a hamstring injury in Week 1 and has missed the last five games. The length of his absence has been a surprise because the belief was Overshown wouldn't miss more than three games after the team didn't place him on injured reserve.
Putting that aside for now, Overshown finally returned to practice last week and turned in two limited sessions in total, so it appears he's at least getting closer to returning.
That said, we have expected Overshown back for a few weeks now, yet the veteran is still out, so nobody should get their hopes up for Overshown returning to the field this week.
The good news for all of the Cowboys' injured players is they have an extra day to get right this week with Dallas playing the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night.
We'll know more on Thursday, when the Cowboys drop their first injury report of Week 7.

title: 2 Winners & 4 Losers From Lackluster Cowboys in Week 6 Loss to Packers
full_text:
Another weekend and another round of heartache for Dallas Cowboys fans.
Despite having 10 days to prepare for the Green Bay Packers , they went into Sunday Night Football looking like a team that had less than 24 hours to put together a game plan. They were disjointed on offense and defense, going into the intermission facing a 17-0 deficit.
Their defense did some decent things in the second half to give them a chance, but the offense completely failed the Cowboys. In the end, they lost 23-13 and fell to 2-4 on the season. Here's a look at who stood out as both winners and losers during their latest frustrating loss.
The Cowboys felt they could move the ball on the ground this week, but that didn't happen. Javonte Williams did score a touchdown in the third quarter, but overall, he wasn't much of a factor. Williams finished with just 41 yards on 11 attempts. That average of 3.7 yards per attempt is concerning, but it's right at his average for the year. There are a lot of problems on offense for Dallas, and sadly, Williams (other than at the goal line) has been one of them.
Before Week 6, the Cowboys had not recorded an interception since Quinnen Williams had one in Week 15 of the 2025 season. That horrendous streak finally ended when Dee Winters picked off a pass from Jordan Love intended for Matthew Golden. Initially, he returned it for a touchdown, but on replay, he was ruled down by contact. The Cowboys wasted the turnover when Dak Prescott threw an interception of his own, but Winters still gave them a chance, which is all they need from this defense.
Dak Prescott named this offense GOTI , which is the "Greatest Offense There Is." He also said he loves it when teams blitz because it gives his players one-on-one chances. All of that is fine, but it needs to be backed up.
Over the past two weeks, that hasn't been the case. The Dallas offense has been chaotic. Turnovers have become a major issue, and Prescott struggled mightily with the blitz against Green Bay. One crushing example was early in the fourth quarter when he had CeeDee Lamb wide open but threw it short off his back foot.
Packers bringing the blitz on third down 😤 DALvsGB on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/9iGvH2y3T7
Sure, it was a tough throw, but Prescott is a $60 million quarterback who hasn't been shy about praising his offense. He has to make those types of throws if he wants to back that talk up.
Not only did Jake Ferguson lose his starting spot to Brevyn Spann-Ford , but he also failed to make anything happen once he was on the field. Ferguson had just 13 yards on two receptions. Ferguson is in a terrible slump right now, and it's fair to ask what the plan will be for him going forward.
Dallas wasn't sure if they would have Joey Porter Jr. in this game since he was dealing with an ankle injury. Not only did he suit up and play, but he was one of the best players on the field. Porter played blanket coverage once again and broke up two passes while recording a tackle for loss as well. His only mistake was a questionable pass interference call, but outside of that play, it was nothing but positives for Porter.
So much attention has been centered on the defensive coaching staff, and rightfully so. The Dallas defense has been atrocious, and first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker has to be better . That said, this defense was bad in 2025 and is bad in 2026. The one common denominator is head coach Brian Schottenheimer .
Not only does he deserve blame for these shortcomings, but he continues to make poor decisions. Schottenheimer took the ball first when winning the toss, which meant the Packers got to take the ball first in the third quarter after scoring at the end of the second. He also dialed up a pass despite seeing Dak Prescott take an absolute shot on the previous play, which led to an interception. There was also a fourth-down play where he called a timeout which actually prevented the Packers from being called for a delay of game.
These in-game decisions are questionable, but nothing is as inexcusable as the way the Cowboys came out in this game. After playing on Thursday Night Football in Week 5, Schottenheimer had 10 days to get his team ready. Those 10 days led to a scoreless first half with two turnovers on offense. On defense, they gave up nine third-down conversions, hardly any of which were short-yardage. All of that falls squarely on his shoulders, and it's time to start discussing how hot his seat should be .

title: Ex-NFLer Goes Scorched Earth on Jerry Jones, Cowboys For Repeated Front-Office Failures
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys will spend another week looking internally at where things went wrong after another embarrassing effort on the field in the primetime spotlight. Dallas fell to the Green Bay Packers in Week 6 , in a game that was much more lopsided than the scoreboard suggests.
Dallas struggled to get anything going on offense, which came as a surprise, while the defense had its usual mishaps. What really rubbed everyone the wrong way was the utter lack of preparation, which should never happen after 10 days of rest.
Something needs to change for the Cowboys if they are ever going to get over the hump, and it starts at the top. The front office, specifically owner and general manager Jerry Jones and EVP Stephen Jones, is going bargain-shopping for coaches who don't appear to be doing much coaching , and the players are underperforming.
After Sunday's loss, former NFL player turned social media provocateur Breiden Fehoko sounded off on the Cowboys' front office in an "unfiltered rant" and went scorched earth on everyone involved in the franchise's recent downfall.
"Jerry and Stephen Jones don’t know a lick of football and think money buys everything . Yeah, it can buy a nice Highland Park home, Jerry, but not heart or guys who’ll knock a [expletive] head loose. The Jones family are all micromanagers from grandpa Jerry to his kids. Jerry only wants yes men who’ll say, 'Yes, Daddy, you’re right and everything you say is gospel," Fehoko wrote.
"Schottenheimer is a fraud; he’s a friend to these guys rather than a grown man with nuts who’ll keep guys accountable. $200 million in contracts on the defensive line alone, and your sack leader is Caleb Downs. Guys are celebrating first downs while down 16 in the 4th quarter. They hired a defensive coordinator who wears [expletive] Cartier glasses with studs in his ear. Their talent evaluator front office guru is outdated. You got [expletive] CeeDee smiling, hugging opposing team DBs in the fourth quarter. This [expletive] is pathetic. These draft classes have stunk. They’ve maybe hit on six players since 2019. Jerry is an oil man; remember that. He’s a business guy before a football guy."
Tell us how you really feel, Breiden. While Fehoko used language that is a little more colorful than it may need to be, he does echo some common talking points regarding Jerry Jones and the Cowboys' from office.
Micromanagers, hiring 'yes men,' players who don't take the game seriously... it's nothing we haven't heard before. But Fehoko wasn't done unleashing on the Cowboys. He also went into another unhinged rant about Brian Schottenheimer being too nice to player.
"I grew up in an era where a Coach was a Coach and players played. There was no 'friend, homie' peer to peer bullsh*t," he added. "If you can go have drinks partying with your players, you can’t expect these players to take you serious when you try to keep em accountable."
"The Cowboys are a result of Brian Schottenheimer being a friend to these cats instead of a coach. This culture on the field stinks. They celebrate first downs down 16 in the 4th. It’s a bunch of guys wearing chains while playing. Late hits after the whistle wannabe UFC fighters."
Fehoko may not be the most reliable narrator or messenger, but his point here does stand. Schottenheimer has to be firmly on the hot seat after the team's latest disappointment, and it's a serious conversation that the team must have.
Now that they have an old-school leader in the building like Mike Pettine, it will be interesting to see if Jerry Jones is more willing to pull the trigger on a move. After all, the last time the Cowboys made a mid-season coaching change came after an embarrassing loss to the Packers. Sorry, Wade Phillips.

title: Biggest Takeaways From Cowboys' Latest Debacle  Against Packers in Week 6
full_text:
In what has becoming a weekly occurrence, the Dallas Cowboys put up a pathetic performance in the 23-13 Week 6 loss to the Green Bay Packers on Sunday night.
We heard the excuse all week that three games in 11 days might have been a big factor in the Week 5 loss . Well, the Cowboys had 10 days of rest before Week 6 and still came out flat.
The Cowboys actually should have lost by more than that, as the Packers dropped multiple easy touchdowns during the game.
With the loss, the Cowboys fall to 2-4 on the season and are set to take on an equally broken team in the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 7. The only saving grace for Dallas right now is the fact that the NFC East is a total mess and is completely up for grabs.
Before we turn the page to the upcoming NFC East matchup, here are the biggest takeaways from the latest Cowboys debacle against the Packers in Week 6.
There's no need to rehash all the issues this team has. It has been the same story all season long and nothing changed in Week 6.
The Cowboys might not be the most talented team in the NFL, but they have more talent than what their performances would suggest, especially on offense.
There are so many players underperforming on this team on both sides of the ball, execution is sorely lacking, to say the least, and the Cowboys are undisciplined, too.
Making matters worse, Brian Schottenheimer and Christian Parker are inept as play-callers and have no answers for how to improve things. Not that this needs to be pointed out, but both should be fired .
The Cowboys can make all the changes they want with personnel, but it's the equivalent of rearranging deck chairs on the Titanic. There is no hope things will get better, plain and simple.
The Packers entered the game with the worst third-down offense in the NFL with a success rate of 27.59%. But all they needed was a matchup against the Cowboys to get right, as the Packers converted on 61.1% of their third-down tries.
What's especially glaring is the Cowboys' inability to stop teams on third-and-long. Bobby Belt of 105.3 The Fan noted that teams are converting 50% of third-down attempts of nine-plus yards on the Cowboys this season and the league average is 21.8%.
If there was one bright spot from the loss, it was the performance of Joey Porter Jr., who played like the CB1 the Cowboys hoped to get in the trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers .
Porter shut down every Packers wide receiver he covered during the game. If only the Cowboys could clone him a few times they might be able to turn this thing around.
In all, Porter finished with three tackles, including one for a loss, and a pair of passes defensed.
We saw personnel changes on both sides of the ball, as Schottenheimer promised .
Brevyn Spann-Ford started and played ahead of Jake Ferguson, and Malachi Lawrence got the start over Donovan Ezeiruaku.
Unfortunately, as we expected, those changes did nothing to alter the performance of a Cowboys team that just cannot get it together.
The Cowboys saw two players leave the game early with injuries.
KaVontae Turpin suffered an injury to his ribs on the opening kickoff and did not return. Dee Winters came down with an ankle injury in the first half, also, and never got back into the game.
The Cowboys are already banged-up at linebacker, so the Winters injury is especially notable. We'll see if DeMarvion Overshown can finally return from his hamstring injury in Week 7.

title: Dallas Cowboys Lose All-Pro KaVontae Turpin on Opening Play vs Packers
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys got hit with a notable injury to both their offense and special teams unit on the first play of Sunday night's Week 6 matchup against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field.
On the opening kickoff, Cowboys wide receiver KaVontae Turpin took a hard hit from multiple players and had to be tended to by the training staff on the sidelines shortly after.
Turpin was eventually ruled out for the rest of the game with a rib injury as the Cowboys headed into halftime trailing 17-0 to Green Bay.
According to NBC sideline reporter Melissa Stark, Turpin visibly had trouble breathing when team doctors checked out his rib area and that he nearly fell to his knees due to the pain.
"When he came off the field, he was holding that left rib area. And when doctors started poking that area, his knees buckled out from underneath him. He was in obvious pain, had a hard time moving, had a hard time breathing."
Rib injuries are painful but depending on the severity, Turpin could avoid being placed on injured reserve. However, that's purely speculation at this point. Cowboys fans will have to wait for an official update from head coach Brian Schottenheimer after the game or during the week once the team returns back home to The Star in Frisco.
Turpin is a three-time Pro Bowler and one-time First Team All-Pro selection as a returner. He currently leads the league in kick return yardage during the 2026 season and has finished as the league leader in that category the past two years.
On offense this season, Turpin has posted four carries for 39 yards along with two carries for 10 yards and a touchdown.
With Turpin out, Cowboys running back Tyler Goodson took over on kickoff return duties during the first half.
Caleb Downs could take over punt return duties if Turpin misses extended time. He's listed as the backup on the depth chart along with wide receiver Jonathan Mingo.
Downs had two punt returns during his college career and could provide a spark in that regard if Turpin misses Week 7's matchup with the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football.

title: Cowboys, Packers Get Into Heated Exchange Before Week 6 Kickoff
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers are carrying some extra animosity toward each other into the Week 6 game on Sunday night.
We say that because the two teams were involved in a little dust-up before kickoff in one of the end zones. Several players on both teams got involved.
Based on video, the two teams met in the end zone prior to kickoff and there were no doubt words exchanged, althought it does not appear that any punches were thrown.
Check out video of the heated exchange between the two teams below.
A little pregame Cowboys-Packers fun in Green Bay pic.twitter.com/5FCNH8cAcp
According to ESPN's Todd Archer , Cowboys players such as cornerback Joey Porter Jr., linebacker Jaishawn Barham, offensive tackle Broderick Jones and tight end Jake Ferguson were among those involved in the pregame festivities.
A little dust up between the Cowboys and Packers at the end of pregame," Archer wrote. "Saw Joey Porter Jr. getting into it. Maybe some Jaishawn Barham, Broderick Jones and Jake Ferguson too. Didn’t see any punches thrown. Referees were able to break things up."
All of this occurreed about 26 minutes before kickoff, Archer added. We'll see if any of the tension carries into the game.
It has been 10 days since the Cowboys played in Week 5 and there is no doubt they are champing at the bit to get back on the field.
Dallas' last game was an ugly loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers that saw the Cowboys fail to show up en route to an upset defeat at the hands of one of the worst teams in the NFL that was also starting an undrafted rookie quarterback.
Since then, the head coach Brian Schottenheimer has promised that changes will be made in Week 6 .
"I’m not going to get to a bunch of them. Obviously, there’s a competitive advantage. But there’ll be some roster adjustments you guys will see. Some will be more noticeable than others, and some will be subtle as you look at it," Schottenheimer said, per Tommy Yarrish of DallasCowboys.com .
One of those changes is the Cowboys starting rookie edge rusher Malachi Lawrence over Donovan Ezeiruaku. Schottenheimer did say that Lawrence could get more run this week and clearly he wasn't kidding.
The Cowboys also hired a former Packers coach in Mike Pettine, who is serving as a consultant to another former Packers coach, Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker.
Dallas is hoping those two changes, along with any others the team makes, will help a defense that has been among the league's worst through five games.

title: Dallas Cowboys Make Change to Starting Lineup on Defense vs Packers
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have struggled mightily on defense so far this season. That doesn't appear to be changing anytime soon ahead of Sunday night's matchup against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field.
However, the Dallas coaching staff is leaving no stone unturned to find some sort of spark on defense. Ahead of kickoff in Green Bay, the Cowboys are making a change to their defensive depth chart.
The Cowboys are starting rookie outside linebacker Malachi Lawrence over Donovan Ezeiruaku against the Packers, per reports from team sideline reporter Kristi Scales.
This will mark the first-career start for Lawrence, who the Cowboys selected with the No. 23 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft this past spring. So far this season, he's played in five games while posting 12 total tackles (six solo), one sack and one pass breakup.
Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer had said that Lawrence would be getting more opportunities moving forward, and he's making good on his promise in a move that will hopefully bring something positive to the defense.
"He's played very well. I think he's starting to show the flash and the acceleration and the ability to rush the passer that we knew we were getting when we drafted him. I think he had a very good game against Tampa Bay, and you'll see him get more opportunities," Schottenheimer said, per Nick Harris of the Fort Worth-Star Telegram.
Lawrence himself has said he has confidence in the defense turning things around. Fans will believe it when they see it, though it's important for the players to keep the messaging positive regardless of what the first five games has looked like.
“We’re gonna turn it around for sure. We know what we have in this locker room. The offense has great players. The defense has great players as well. We just got to come together, just build our identity and grow on it.”
Despite the Cowboys' strugges on defense, the rookie class has shown flashes. Along with Lawrence, Dallas defensive back Caleb Downs and linebacker Jaishawn Barham have made some impact plays.
This group gives Cowboys fans hope for the future on defense. Whether that will be with defensive coordinator Christian Parker remains to be seen, but for now, the focus is on trying to save the 2026 season.

title: Broncos' Mini-Bye Player Grades: MVP, Standouts & Underachievers
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are 4-2 after their first six games, which nearly no one expected given the toughness of their initial schedule.
It hasn't always been pretty. The Broncos' offense has struggled, outside of a few moments, and the defense has been mostly great. Still, they got out to a 4-2 start , tying four other teams for the third-best record in the AFC.
Both of the Broncos' losses came at the hands of the only two remaining undefeated teams entering Week 6: the Kansas City Chiefs and the San Francisco 49ers.
With that first six-week gauntlet now in the rearview, we're taking a look at how the individual Broncos have graded out. After every game , I grade each player on a snap-by-snap basis, but this "mini-bye" was a great opportunity to look back at the season so far.
To qualify for a grade, a player needed at least 175 snaps. Only 10 Broncos on offense and 15 on defense qualified.
These grades will cover the Broncos' MVP on both sides of the ball, the highest-graded players, the quarterback, the second- to fourth-highest-graded player on each side of the ball, and the three lowest-graded players on each side of the ball. So, let’s get into it.
This season, Meinerz has allowed six total pressures, tied for the seventh-fewest among 41 guards with at least 300 offensive snaps, and his pass-blocking efficiency is the same. Meanwhile, he has been the NFL's best guard in run blocking across multiple metrics.
Allen has been a monster at the start of the season, and while he has some down moments as a run defender, he still looks improved from where he was a year ago. He leads the Broncos with 26 pressures and leads all NFL interior defensive linemen.
Including edge rushers, Allen ties for the sixth-most pressures in the NFL. With defensive stops, he is tied for the fifth-most among all defensive linemen and edge rushers and is tied for third among interior defensive linemen.
This season has been rough for Nix, with his average depth of target dropping from 7.51 in 2025 to 5.56 in 2026 and his air yards per completion dropping from 4.74 to 3.6. He has taken a massive step back in his play , grown too comfortable in the dink-and-dunk game, and isn’t pushing the ball.
Nix's percentage of throws of 10 or more air yards has also dropped significantly. Denver is 4-2 and through the toughest part of its schedule, but this team needs Nix to be better.
Garett Bolles | LT | Grade: 72.8
Bolles has allowed three pressures on the season, which is the fewest of the Broncos' starting five offensive linemen, and three fewer than Meinerz. Among 45 tackles with at least 300 snaps, Bolles is tied for the fewest pressures allowed and has the highest pass-blocking efficiency.
Nik Bonitto | OLB | Grade: 71.6
Bonitto has the second-most pressures on the team, but his impact was limited over the first four weeks. He totaled just a single sack over that span, 12 of his 20 pressures, and had serious issues as a run defender.
Bonitto has surged over the last two weeks, though, with eight pressures, three sacks, a forced fumble, and improved run-defense play.
Talanoa Hufanga | S | Grade: 64.7
Hufanga has had a good season, but not as good as last year. His run-defending issues and unreliable tackling have contributed to the Broncos' inconsistencies against the run.
Still, Hufanga has done well in coverage and is moving around a bit more to create confusion for opposing quarterbacks. He also has two interceptions, including a pick-six, which helped swing Week 3's victory over the Los Angeles Rams.
Malcolm Roach | DL | Grade: 63.9
Roach has the third-most pressures on the team, the fourth-most stops, and leads in batted passes, but his seven missed tackles are the fifth-most. He's had some huge moments in the passing game and has improved as a run defender each week after a terrible season opener.
Jaylen Waddle | WR | Grade: 59.7
The second game of the season highlighted Waddle's upside, but he has struggled since then. He has four drops through six games, and he needs to clean that up.
However, Waddle's routes have been clean, and his 3.5 yards of average separation is the 15th-highest among 74 receivers.
Ben Powers | LG | Grade: 55.6
Powers has been hit or miss and has allowed the second-most pressures on the Broncos, with 13. His run blocking has helped his grade some, but this still isn’t ideal for a six-game sample size.
Powers is the fourth of 10 offensive players who qualified for a grade over the first six games, with him being 0.3 points higher than tight end Evan Engram and 2.2 points higher than wide receiver Courtland Sutton, before getting to Nix and those in the negative group.
Adam Trautman | TE | Grade: 43.1
Trautman has been rough this year, and his issues as a receiver and blocker have been a detriment to the offense. Nate Adkins has outplayed Trautman, falling short of the snap count for the overall grade, but in the three games Adkins qualified for a grade, he was in the 70s. Trautman's season high was 55.2, and he finished four of the six games under 50.
Eyioma Uwazurike | DL | Grade: 44.7
The Broncos gambled on Uwazurike as a key piece, but he has been mostly a liability on the field. He has easily been the Broncos' worst defender this season, and is having maybe two good or great plays a game, which isn’t ideal for someone averaging 37 snaps per game.
Maybe it's time to get Tyler Onyedim involved on defense. The rookie has been a healthy scratch all season, despite being the Broncos' first pick in the 2026 draft.
Luke Wattenberg | C | Grade: 48.5
Wattenberg has been bad, allowing the third-most pressure on the team and the second-most among 25 centers with at least 300 snaps. His pass-blocking efficiency is tied for second-lowest.
Wattenberg's run blocking has been an even bigger detriment to the offense, and he ranks in the bottom three in almost every run-blocking metric for centers.
Jonah Elliss | OLB | Grade: 51.1
Elliss is a technical player, but he isn’t overly explosive, which hurts in the modern NFL where explosive plays and explosive potential matter so much. He's had some awful moments, but overall he was solid, though he showed he isn’t a starting-caliber player but rather a solid depth piece.
Elliss's injury against Seattle looked severe , but at least the Broncos are getting Jonathon Cooper back . In other positive developments, Que Robinson vastly outperformed Elliss in five of the six games so far.
Mike McGlinchey | RT | Grade: 52.9
McGlinchey has allowed the most pressure on the team with 14, which is tied for the 15th-most among 45 tackles with at least 300 snaps. He has always been a bit inconsistent as a pass protector, with his run blocking as a strength, but he's been even more inconsistent in that area this season.
Ja’Quan McMillian | CB | Grade: 53.1
McMillian has made some big plays in big moments, both in his career and this season, but he hasn’t been the most consistent player. His lack of size has been a detriment in the slot, as opponents have looked to take advantage of it both in the passing game with bigger slots and in the run game.
McMillian's missed tackles stem from his lack of size, and opponents have generated multiple explosive plays targeting him. That said, he's been solid, and a 53.1 grade is slightly above average; he just finds himself in the negatives because most of Denver's defenders have been good or great.

title: Insider Reveals Sean Payton's Latest Move to Revive Bo Nix
full_text:
During Denver Broncos training camp, we heard from head coach Sean Payton and a few players that new offensive coordinator Davis Webb had tweaked the verbiage.
Payton spoke publicly about Webb's verbiage tweaks this past summer. Payton made the changes sound like no big deal — a few simple tweaks to streamline the play-calling and help Bo Nix get to the line of scrimmage faster.
Alas, Webb's run as the play-caller was much shorter-lived than expected, as Payton took back the responsibilities after the Broncos' Week 4's loss to the San Francisco 49ers. Payton acknowledged the terminology changes as a factor he had to get accustomed to now that he was calling the plays again.
Fast forward to Week 6, and the Broncos are 4-2. Denver won both games in which Payton has called the plays, but Nix has not looked any better than he did with Webb making the calls. On Sunday, FOX Sports ' Jay Glazer reported that Webb's terminology changes were far more extensive than the Broncos let on, and that Payton has also gone back to using his own terminology.
That's a big shift. These on-the-hoof changes to the offense have only consumed more of Nix's mental bandwidth amid his ongoing slump.
"I asked a bunch of people at the Broncos about that [Nix's struggles], and I didn't know this until this past week is that when Davis Webb took over, he completely changed the terminology on the offensive side of the ball for Bo Nix," Glazer said on FOX NFL Sunday . "Now that Sean Payton has taken it back over, it's like going back to a whole different language that you used to know."
What Glazer reported may be true, but I question the timing of it. Nix has been under fire , with open calls to bench him coming from both the local and national media. Even many Broncos fans have pounded the table for the bench since the team's 17-14 overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks.
Nix only passed for 107 yards against Seattle, and although he didn't turn the ball over, he and the Broncos' offense were a non-factor in the second half.
This feels a bit like a PR move to ease some of the pressure on Nix and quiet the noise, at least somewhat. That doesn't mean it's not true, though.
I guess what I'm saying is that Payton, who keeps his cards extremely close to his chest, especially during the season, opted to tell this to Glazer at this time for a reason.
However, Payton also believes this reversion to his offensive terminology will help Nix return to his 2025 form.
"So I think at this point, man, his head is just spinning," Glazer said of Nix. "You guys know, an offensive terminology, it's like learning a whole different language out there. But Sean Payton is like, 'I have confidence that he's going to get back to the Bo Nix that we saw the last couple of years.'"
If Webb's terminology changes really were wholesale, I question Payton's wisdom in changing it in-season, let alone co-signing on doing it at all. But if it's true, and Nix is now having to dump all this Webb information on the fly and replace it with past verbiage, that can only slow down his processing.
NFL On Prime 's James Palmer reported that Webb changed " about 30% of the terminology ." That could be more than enough to throw a wrench in things for Nix, from a processing perspective.
Given that it's information Nix has mastered before, it shouldn't take him long to relearn it. For that reason and more, I can buy into Payton's confidence in Nix returning to form.
However, Nix has looked off this whole season, not just since Payton took back the play-calling, so there's obviously much more going on than just the changes in terminology. Hopefully, Payton can get to the bottom of that stuff, too.
The Broncos continue to win games, but it's been with minimal help from the offense, while weapons like Jaylen Waddle, Courtland Sutton, and Evan Engram are squandered. Nix is on pace to pass for under 3,000 yards this season and 17 touchdowns, both of which would obviously be career-low numbers and far, far from the big Year-3 leap Broncos Country expected to see.
Still, I don't believe the Nix who passed for 7,500-plus yards and 50-plus touchdowns, while winning 24 games, over his first two seasons has just disappeared, never to be seen again. That quarterback is still in there somewhere, so at the very least, fans can only hope Payton reaches him soon.

title: Film Room: Broncos Aren't Panicking About Bo Nix—Tape Shows Why
full_text:
The discourse around Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix is at a fever pitch . The offense hasn’t been playing well over the first six weeks of the season, and his poor play has been at the forefront of the conversation.
Expectations were high for Nix entering Year 3, especially after leading the Broncos to the AFC championship game in 2025. He showed tremendous growth down the stretch last year, and his ability to manufacture game-winning drives when the chips are down has been nothing short of spectacular over his first three NFL seasons, including 2026.
But consistency issues have plagued Nix this season, and he doesn’t look like the same player he was before he broke his ankle in the playoffs. Between two offseason ankle surgeries, a new play-caller to open the 2026 season, and his incessant need to avoid negative plays, his performance has almost hurt the offense more than helped and put the team in some bad situations.
It’s not all bad, though, and the two touchdown drives Nix led against the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday night showed that with a little better execution, this offense isn’t far from getting back on track. If these drives had settled for field goals instead of touchdowns, the Broncos don't beat the Seahawks in overtime, 17-14 .
Let’s break it down in this week’s film room.
Look what happens when you finally execute! pic.twitter.com/HOzESGQh3r
Fans have been critical of the play-calling this season because the Broncos run so many screens. Sean Payton has always used screens as an extension of the running game, and the offense usually executes them well.
This first play is a great example of that. Watch center Luke Wattenburg and left guard Ben Powers release out and pave the way for running back RJ Harvey to get the drive going. Nix does a nice job of hanging tough to let this play develop in front of him, and Harvey does the rest.
It may not move the needle very much in terms of a spectacular play, but finding and maintaining execution like this is going to be a major key in turning the ship around offensively.
I like where Bo's eyes are on this play. Looking to Waddle draws the safety and opens up the shot to Mims. Shame they can't connect, but that's good process. pic.twitter.com/oJXXhYMlUB
A couple of plays later, Payton dials up a shot play to Marvin Mims Jr. near midfield. I like this play call, because it signals that Payton intended to go for it on fourth down regardless of the outcome of the play. That kind of aggressiveness can help boost morale for your offense, signifying a certain level of trust in your guys to get the job done.
Despite missing on this connection, the process of the play is well done for Nix. Jaylen Waddle is running a pivot route to his right side, and Nix flashes his eyes that way to draw the deep safety in that direction and open up the shot to Mims on the post. Nix hits his back foot and lays out a good ball to Mims, who nearly makes the catch in tight coverage.
Taking these shot plays can help open up the defense, even if you don’t connect. Nix hasn’t been taking these kinds of shots down the field often enough, so it was great to see him air it out against a tough Seattle defense.
Take what you can get on 3rd down. Jones gets too much depth in the hook zone, opening up Engram for a 1st down. Nice job, Bo. pic.twitter.com/QqyxsYSlez
On the ensuing third down, Nix takes what is given to him on a quick throw to tight end Evan Engram underneath. This isn’t anything special, but it's the right play to keep the offense on track. It’s alright to hit the checkdown when you need to.
Seattle linebacker Ernest Jones gets drawn up the field by Courtland Sutton running an in-breaker, opening up a soft spot in the zone for Engram to release into. This is easy pitch-and-catch.
I like that Bo doesn't look flustered with the pocket collapsing on this throw to Sutton. If he can keep this kind of composure in the pocket, he can start to open things up downfield. pic.twitter.com/EK0ecPOl0z
This next play is probably the most promising throw Nix made, because it’s the right read, on time, and allows  Sutton an opportunity to run after the catch over the middle of the field.
Seattle is in man coverage across the board, and the Broncos run a natural pick play with Sutton on the shallow crossing route. Nix hits his back foot and delivers a good ball to Sutton with pressure in his face. Running back Tyler Badie does a great job of picking up the blitzing linebacker, and Nix shows composure to deliver the ball, with right tackle Mike McGlinchey getting pushed into his lap.
Nix’s pocket presence has been rough this season. He’s been vacating clean pockets and running himself into pressure too often, so it was good to see him stay in the play despite having little room to throw.
Bo see's Okada vacate to the middle on the rotation, so he takes a shot to Waddle. Bad ball, but good process. He needs to take more of these shots and good things will happen. pic.twitter.com/jsD9KMlKpb
On the next drive, Nix takes another shot downfield, this time to Waddle.
I love this decision and the process behind it. Seattle has two safeties deep, but they’re in man coverage across the board, and they rotate into a single-high look at the snap. Nix sees safety Ty Okada bail to the middle of the field, opening up one-on-one coverage against Waddle on the go route.
Even though Nix misses on the throw, I like him being aggressive against Devon Witherspoon in coverage. Witherspoon is an incredible cornerback, but Nix trusted Waddle’s playmaking ability to give him a chance downfield.
Again, taking these shots more often can help open up the offense simply by making defenses have to respect the deep passing game.
4 things can happen on a pass play, 2 of them are good for the offense. Reception or penalty. Keep taking shots. Good things can happen. pic.twitter.com/rDK3IgTfsk
The other added benefit of taking those shots is drawing penalties. There are four outcomes to a passing play, and two of them are positive for the offense.
You either make the catch or get a penalty. This shot to Sutton put the Broncos at the 1-yard line due to a Witherspoon pass interference penalty in the end zone.
Nix identifies Sutton against Witherspoon in man coverage and lays it out there. Even though Sutton has struggled in contested-catch scenarios all year, trying to let him make a play for you is a great decision in the red zone. The Broncos would score their second touchdown of the game one play later.
Rumors are flying throughout the media of a possible Nix benching here soon, but that would be a massive mistake. Sure, he needs to play better and within the scope of the offense as it is designed. His inefficiency and lack of willingness to take chances with the football are a big part of the offensive play through six games.
But there is some good in there. It’s not all bad, nor is it all Nix's fault.
Cleaning up some execution , staying in the pocket and allowing plays to develop, and taking some chances can go a long way to improving his play as a whole. With the way the defense is playing this year, the Broncos could start scoring 30 points a game and blow teams out down the stretch with these improvements.
The Broncos' offense is getting extra possessions nearly every week thanks to defensive takeaways. Nix and company need to do a better job of taking advantage of that and sustaining some drives.

title: Concerning Jonah Elliss Injury Development Emerges After Broncos Win
full_text:
Jonathon Cooper's return from the commissioner's exempt list couldn't have come at a better time. On Thursday night, third-year outside linebacker Jonah Elliss suffered a lower-leg injury late in the fourth quarter of the Denver Broncos' 17-14 overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks.
As Elliss turned the corner on his pass rush, Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton laid a hit on Sam Darnold, and the pair fell into Elliss's lower right leg. In a gritty heads-up move, Elliss was able to hobble off the field, one-hopping it to avoid a timeout that would have stopped the clock.
He was carted from the sideline to the locker room and did not return on Thursday night. We've heard no updates on Elliss's status.
However, on Saturday night, Elliss was at Folsom Field to root on his Utah Utes against the Colorado Buffaloes and was pictured with crutches and a boot on his right leg, courtesy of CBS Colorado 's Romi Bean.
Jonah Elliss in a boot and crutches at the Colorado Utah game last night. https://t.co/lCAMTesL20 pic.twitter.com/c64QW3ZbhI
Sean Payton will hold a zoom press conference on Monday afternoon, which will be our first chance to potentially hear an update, but knowing the Broncos' head coach, he's extremely unlikely to spill the beans on Elliss or any other injured player.
Elliss's boot-and-crutches combo implies a more serious injury, but perhaps we shouldn't rush to judgment. Remember, after Jaylen Waddle was seen exiting Empower Field at Mile High in Week 2 in a walking boot , Payton said later that it's much more common than people realize. Waddle practiced that week and played in Week 3.
Elliss has the escalating factor of the crutches to go with the boot, though. It doesn't look good, but that only makes Cooper's return all the more timely.
Elliss has started in place of Cooper in all six games thus far. Elliss has been a solid relief starter, but has lacked the consistency as a pass rusher.
Against the Seahawks, though, Elliss totaled six QB pressures and notched his first sack of the season. In one game, he nearly matched his season total in pressures, so he may have been turning a corner. That makes this injury uniquely sucky for Elliss.
A 2024 third-round pick out of Utah, the Broncos have been looking for ways to get him on the field more, even exploring a few packages with him at inside linebacker . Cooper's legal troubles solved that problem for Denver, with Elliss taking over as a starter.
With Elliss injured, it will be interesting to see how the Broncos work Cooper back into the rush linebacker rotation. The seventh-year veteran is playing on his second contract and has totaled 27 sacks over the past three years as a starter.
Que Robinson has become a consistent impact player, and while I know many Broncos fans would love to see him start opposite Nik Bonitto, the team stood behind Cooper amid his off-the-field legal troubles for a reason.
The Broncos love Cooper, and even if Elliss hadn't gotten hurt, he was always going to step right back into his starting role opposite Bonitto. Now, that doesn't mean that Denver will throw Cooper straight into the fire; he'll likely be eased back into full starter's snaps, but he's the guy, and he's a highly paid veteran.
The Broncos' pass rush has begun to come alive over the past two games. Elliss has been a part of that resurgence, especially in Week 6.
The Broncos get a one-game roster exemption with Cooper's return, but it wouldn't be a surprise if Elliss ends up on short-term injured reserve. With Cooper back, the Broncos have a healthy Bonitto, Robinson, and Dondrea Tillman, so the edge-rushing party can continue.
We'll keep you updated on what happens next with Elliss.

title: 5 Broncos Who Must Step Up After Surviving Brutal 6-Game Gauntlet
full_text:
The season is far from over, but the 4-2 Denver Broncos already have much to celebrate .
Facing five of the NFL's best teams in their first six weeks, the Broncos weathered their initial gauntlet about as well as could be reasonably expected. All four of Denver's wins have come against opponents that won 12-plus games and made the playoffs last season.
The Broncos already played all three of the NFC West's juggernauts, going 2-1 against them, while their AFC West opponents still have to face the Seattle Seahawks, Los Angeles Rams, and red-hot San Francisco 49ers.
The Broncos overcame some serious obstacles to get to 4-2, but if they're going to maximize the NFL's fourth-easist remaining schedule, a handful of players have to step up and perform at a much higher level. Let's break each one down.
Let's get to the most obvious one: the quarterback. If Sean Payton can get Nix back to playing like his 2025 self, the trickle-down effect will benefit several other Broncos on this list.
Nix has looked hesistant and unpoised, but he's also delivered several signature, magical moments. The consistency simply hasn't been there, and he looks like he's suffering from a confidence crisis of some sort.
Nix is on pace to pass for just 2,972 yards and 17 touchdowns this season, which would represent a significant statistical regression. Given the level of defenses he's faced, though, his lack of Star Wars numbers is understandable, but now it's time to flip the switch and silence the increasingly vocal haters thronging across the Fruited Plain.
You'd be forgiven for thinking Sutton's been on injured reserve to start this season, but he's been out there for every game thus far. With just 13 receptions for 123 yards and one touchdown, the two-time Pro Bowler is angling for a career-low season, but his slumping quarterback has much to do with it.
Still, there have been times when Sutton's effort has seemed questionable. Nix has looked his way 25 times, but they've only connected on 13 completions. Sutton has had some opportunities to make a big play, but he's not fighting for the ball like we're used to.
As a receiver, creating separation is key in the NFL, but that seems to be another area Sutton has struggled with to kick off the campaign. But it could be a byproduct of the insane defenses and secondaries he's had to go against every single week.
Wide receiver is a quarterback-dependent position, so amid Nix's struggles, we shouldn't expect Waddle and Sutton to be putting up insane numbers. But both veteran wideouts could be doing more to help their quarterback.
In Waddle's case, he has dropped four passes and his body language is starting to speak volumes. After Week 2's breakout performance, Waddle has failed to eclipse 35 receiving yards in a game.
Nix needs to improve, but Waddle and Sutton can do more to help pull their quarterback out of his slump. There's time yet to make some hay this season, now that the worst is behind Denver, but it's safe to say that Waddle's impact has been far from the first- and third-round draft capital given up to get him here.
Dobbins has been too patient at times, and the burst we saw last season for 10 games hasn't been there. But he did nurse a hip injury through the first few weeks.
The Broncos' offensive line hasn't been great run blockers, but Dobbins has left yards on the field because of his hesitancy in the backfield. He's got to hit the hole with burst, and get downhill much faster than he has been.
Dobbins has 81 carries for 270 yards and two touchdowns thus far, but he's angling for a career-low yards-per-carry average (3.3). I expect that to improve dramatically as the season continues to unfold, but after the Broncos re-signed him to a 4x raise, they need more from their No. 1 running back.
Wattenberg has been one of the NFL's worst centers this season. That's a frustrating development, given the four-year, $48 million extension Denver gave him at the bye last season.
The fifth-year center has been a colossal disappointment, and he's been a big reason for the Broncos' offensive inconsistencies on the ground and through the air. His run blocking has been meh; his pass protection has been absolutely terrible, and he's had too many bad snaps.
Wattenberg hasn't had it easy with the defensive lines he's faced thus far, but he's been so bad, the Broncos have to be considering replacing him with Alex Forsyth.

title: J.K. Dobbins Gets Real About What's Ailing Broncos' Offense
full_text:
Entering Thursday night's matchup with the Seattle Seahawks, the Denver Broncos' rushing offense ranked 25th in the NFL, averaging just 86.2 yards per game. And people wonder why Bo Nix hasn't looked like himself.
Against the Seahawks, the Broncos rushed for just 74 yards, but they did score two touchdowns on the ground. That pair of touchdowns created a two-score lead that the Broncos' defense was able to protect for most of the game, forcing Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold to throw the ball 51 times.
Seattles's defense adjusted at halftime, and stopped the Broncos' run game in its tracks in the second half. It was one three-and-out after another, with the Broncos playing an excruciatingly impotent brand of offense.
The game went to overtime, but the Broncos got the win, prevailing 17-14 over the Seahawks . Despite Denver sitting at 4-2 after a brutal first six-week schedule, the narrative around the Broncos has centered on heavy criticism of Nix and the offense.
Echoing his head coach , Broncos running back J.K. Dobbins doesn't sound worried, pointing to how tough Seattle's defense is to explain why the offense could get nothing going in the second half.
"It's the Super Bowl champions," Dobbins said post-game. "They got a great defense. They adjusted... That's part of being in the NFL and part of playing these great teams with great defenses. They adjusted, and they did a good job."
Although Nix only passed for 106 yards, Seattle held the Broncos to just 94 net passing yards, due to a pair of sacks. It was pretty painful to watch at times, but Dobbins isn't wrong about the caliber of defense Seattle plays.
The Seahawks entered Week 6 ranked No. 2 in net yards and passing defense, No. 1 in yards per play and takeaways, and No. 3 on third down. The Broncos struggled to run and pass in the second half, and they obviously couldn't convert on third down much, but they protected the ball. Zero turnovers was a big reason Denver won that game.
Seattle's defense led them to a Super Bowl championship last season and is poised to defend its crown this season, if Darnold and company can get off the schneid. But Seattle was only the latest in a long line of top-tier defenses the Broncos have faced to start this season.
You can look at almost any of the key metrics; the Broncos have a bottom-five offense. Lest we forget, though, the Broncos have faced the second-toughest schedule thus far when it comes to opposing defenses, and the toughest in opposing offenses.
With the worst of it behind the Broncos now, Dobbins sounds optimistic that the offense can finally take flight — if everybody does their part.
"Shoot, we just have to execute," Dobbins said. "You know, we've played some really good defenses. Every single team we've played has a really good defense."
That's not an excuse, by the way. Dobbins is simply pointing out the obvious. He understands that for the Broncos to turn the ship around offensively, the individual players have to bow up, take accountability, and excute.
"You've just got to go to the drawing board, and figure it out and execute," he said. "That is what it comes down to: execution."
Dobbins has carried the ball 81 times this season for 270 yards and two touchdowns. His 3.3 yards-per-carry average would be a career-low, if the rest of this season tracks the way it has started.
The soon-to-be 28-year-old has suffered a torn ACL, a torn Achilles, and a bad plantar fascia injury last season, leading some to wonder whether all the wear and tear has finally caught up to him. But given the level of competition the Broncos have faced so far this season, it's too early to say whether Dobbins has slowed down. The jury is out on that question.
Dobbins doesn't look quite as explosive, and nowhere near as decisive, as he did last year. Meanwhile, the Broncos' offensive line has struggled to consistently get push in the run game, which is all the more reason why he shouldn't be dancing around in the backfield; he needs to hit the hole with burst and get downhill.
Time will tell whether Dobbins and the Broncos' ground game can finally get rolling this season. But becoming more reliable on the ground would offer Nix the best chance to dig out of his slump.
As head coach Sean Payton said last week , "The hardest thing to do in this league is play that position if you're not rushing the ball."
Because the Broncos played on Thursday night, they're now enjoying a "mini-bye" — three extra days of rest and preparation between the Seattle game and Week 7's trip to take on the Arizona Cardinals. That might not be enough time to fully recharge the run game, but not having to play an elite defense for the first time since last season could do wonders for Dobbins and company.
And the same goes for Nix.
If the Broncos don't start producing better on the ground and rise up the rankings to at least somewhere in the teens, it's hard to see them cutting deep into the playoffs, even with a lights-out defense and even if Nix suddenly returns to 2025 form.
