title: NFL Insider Reveals Broncos' True Feelings on Bo Nix Amid Bench Talk
full_text:
Since the Denver Broncos' 17-14 overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks , the sharks have been circling around Bo Nix.
From NFL On Prime 's Ryan Fitzpatrick criticizing Nix's effort, saying it was "almost disrespectful to the quarterback position," to a former Broncos teammate, Ben DiNucci, piling on , to local and national talking heads (and some fans) calling for Bo to be benched , it's been a rough couple of days for the third-year pro.
Lost in the rush to pile on Nix is the fact that the Broncos are 4-2 after playing the NFL's hardest schedule through the first six weeks. Unsurprisingly, that's what matters most to the Broncos, which is why the team isn't questioning Nix.
Long-time NFL insider Tom Pelissero further emphasized that on Saturday morning.
"The Broncos are 18-3 in Bo Nix’s last 21 starts. And while Nix and the offense clearly need to improve, there are no questions in the building about Nix’s competitiveness, drive and ability to get things rolling again," Pelissero wrote on X .
You'll notice that Pelissero stopped short of reporting that Denver isn't considering benching Nix, but it amounts to the same thing. The Broncos are confident that Nix can and will find his footing as they emerge from this tough first six-week gauntlet.
Since entering the league, Nix has been one of the NFL's winningest quarterbacks. He's 28-12 as a starter in the NFL, and currently sitting on a .700 career winning percentage.
The only active NFL quarterbacks with a better career winning percentage are Patrick Mahomes (.762) and Lamar Jackson (.712). Josh Allen is right behind Nix at .697. Nix has 40 regular-season starts under his belt, plus two playoff games (1-1).
In his second NFL season, Nix led the Broncos to a 14-3 finish, snatching the AFC West crown away from the Kansas City Chiefs, and earning the No. 1 playoff seed in the conference. He outdueled Allen in the divisional round of the playoffs, and we all know he would have gotten past the New England Patriots at home in the AFC championship game if he hadn't broken his ankle.
After what we saw on Thursday night, is there any doubt that Nix and the Broncos would have had every opportunity to beat the Seahawks in the Super Bowl? 2025 was such a magical season; the only thing I could have seen stopping Nix and the Broncos from hoisting the Lombardi Trophy was the injury bug, and sadly, that's exactly what happened.
But it's all water under the bridge. Woulda, shoulda, coulda.
In the present, Nix has the Broncos at 4-2 and very much on target for all their goals, which includes winning the division again, the No. 1 playoff seed, and going all the way. The Broncos' first six-week schedule was the toughest in the NFL, but their remaining schedule? The fourth-easiest.
The Broncos believe in Nix. The stats haven't been there this year, but the victories have. And as Sean Payton often says , it's much easier to fix a team's problems when you're winning.
Nix hasn't been great. He hasn't looked like his pre-injury self, but he's still doing enough to get past some top-tier opponents. Despite his slump, he's finding ways to win, which is another testament to him as a competitor.
Broncos believe Nix will turn things around. And with this remaining schedule, I believe they're poised to go on a run and really capitalize on how well they navigated those first six games, because guess what?
The Chiefs, Chargers, and Raiders still have most of those tough NFC West opponents to play, while the Broncos are through the worst of them, with only a road trip to face the Arizona Cardinals left.
When it comes to the Broncos' immediate schedule, there's really only one tough game to circle: Week 8's rematch against the Chiefs. But that'll be at Mile High, where Nix has never lost to Kansas City.
From there, Denver's road games against the Carolina Panthers (Week 9) and Pittsburgh Steelers on Black Friday (Week 12) could be tougher than people realize, but compared to what the Broncos have already faced, the scariest thing about those two opponents are that their East Coast away games.
We're still waiting to find out how much of the Raiders' 3-2 start was real. The Broncos will get to cross swords with them in Denver coming out of their Week 10 bye. Meanwhile, the Chargers are already out of the division hunt.
But really, it's all about the final three games, where the Broncos will play the Buffalo Bills at home in Week 16, the Patriots on the road in Week 17, and then the Chargers at Mile High in the season finale. Meanwhile, the Chiefs are undefeated at 4-0, but they still have to face the Seahawks, Rams, 49ers, Bills and Patriots, plus rematch the Broncos at Mile High.
Whatever is going on with Nix, I believe the early schedule has had a bigger effect on his play and statistical production than people realize. He may still be dealing with lingering effects of his ankle fracture, or perhaps something else has happened, but if the best predictor of future outcomes is past outcomes, he'll get it figured out.
There's a reason the Broncos have "no questions" about Nix's ability to get himself and this offense rolling, as Pelissero reported. In a league in which it is exceedingly difficult to win, Nix is 18-3 in his last 21 starts.

title: How Broncos' Week 6 Win Changed Their NFL Trade Deadline Outlook
full_text:
The Denver Broncos sit at 4-2 and are now enjoying a mini-bye after beating the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday night .
The Broncos' offense did just enough in that game — establishing a two-score lead in the first half against Seattle's smothering defense — to allow Vance Joseph's unit to pin its ears back and bring home the win.
People are still understandably worried about Bo Nix and Sean Payton's offense, but the Broncos' wounded defense is absolutely rolling right now. And it's possible that game against the Seahawks could have altered the Broncos' outlook ahead of the November 10 NFL trade deadline.
I'll explain why here shortly, but before I do, keep in mind that Denver is unlikely to be a seller at the deadline. The Broncos weathered a brutal first six games and now get to benefit from the NFL's fourth-easiest remaining schedule; they're going to be in the conversation for the AFC West crown and likely the No. 1 conference seed, and such teams rarely go selling off roster pieces.
That being said, Thursday night's 17-14 overtime win over the Seahawks gave me two thoughts realitve to the Broncos and the trade deadline.
First off, I am not advocating for the Broncos to trade Moss; I've been pounding the table since the summer for the front office to get him extended. But while he's missed time and was limited on Thursday night with a rib injury (20 snaps out of 85), Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine have stepped into the spotlight .
Against a desperate Seahawks passing offense that featured Sam Darnold as the trigger man and Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp as the receiving targets, Barron and 'K.A.D.' were targeted a combined 26 times (!). The Broncos' duo gave up plenty of completions, but they had their work cut out for them and did enough to limit Darnold and win the game.
KAD had a crucial interception late in the fourth quarter, too, while Barron played 100% of the Broncos' defensive snaps, which amounted to a whopping 85 plays. Neither young cornerback was perfect, but with two-plus games now as starters, the Broncos are realizing just how deep they are at the position.
With Moss in a contract year, it makes me wonder how secure his spot is. I don't think Denver would go looking to actively trade him, but if the phone rang, we know GM George Paton is always down to listen.
Beyond the emergence of Barron and Abrams-Draine, what further complicates the Moss issue is Ja'Quan McMillian's contract year status. As the Broncos' nickel, McMillian is a takeaway machine and one of the NFL's best, most clutch-time defensive backs.
And you can't pay everyone. So if the phone rings at Broncos HQ and the caller is interested in Moss, Paton is likely to listen. But one thing to keep in mind: in each of the past two seasons, the Broncos' cornerback depth has been tested by the injury bug, and without the quality personnel going five-deep, it would make it much harder to weather the storm, if something, say, were to befall the group later this season.
Keeping Moss around through the 2026 season would maintain that five-deep buffer at cornerback.
We've talked a lot about Nix not looking like himself this season, but the same is true of Mims. The fourth-year wideout/returner has dealt with two injuries since training camp started, which could be part of the explanation, but Mims doesn't look like he's giving the same full effort he always has.
Mims's low effort was apparent against the Seahawks. He failed to come down with a deep shot that would have put the Broncos on the goal line (thankfully, they still got there on that drive and scored), and there were several routes on tape where Mims wasn't even looking for the ball.
Now, it's possible some of that not-looking-for-the-ball thing was by design, but I doubt it. Mims's greatest value to the Broncos has always been his returner impact, and even that has been sub-par this season.
Mims's return yardage hasn't been there, even though we know teams try to punt away from him, and he lost a fumble on a return in Week 4 that led directly to the Broncos' second loss of the season. Whether his attitude is being affected by his expiring contract , the injuries, or the arrival of Jaylen Waddle , Mims hasn't looked like the same player of the past.
Given that Denver was very focused on bringing in returners this summer, and has Kolbe Katsis and Cameron Ross on the practice squad, it wouldn't surprise me in the least if Mims was traded before the deadline. If there's a market for his services, that is. But he is a two-time All-Pro/Pro Bowl returner, and he's only 24.

title: Jensen's Judgment: Bench Bo Nix? Don't Make Me Laugh
full_text:
Hot on the heels of defeating the defending Super Bowl champions on primetime , questions are being asked around the Mile High City about whether the Denver Broncos should bench Bo Nix.
On the local airwaves, the blogs, the podwaves, or just about any social media comment section, people are seriously advocating — or at least contemplating — whether the Broncos would be better off with Nix on the bench , even if it's just for a game or two to give him a mental and emotional breather.
I can only sit back in amazement at such questions. How quickly people seem to forget what the Broncos were before Nix arrived in the 2024 NFL draft.
The Broncos went eight long years without making the playoffs after winning the Super Bowl, which was an NFL first. One quarterback after another — from first-round picks to high-dollar free agents to big-name trade acquisitions — went through the carousel in Denver over that time period.
This team couldn't get the quarterback or head coach right. Then the Broncos made the fateful decision to hire Sean Payton , acquiring his coaching rights from the New Orleans Saints after the 2022 season.
Payton began to put things in order, but even he couldn't much out of Russell Wilson. After Payton benched him, the Broncos released him in the spring of 2024 with a then-NFL-record $85 million dead-money hit to the salary cap.
From there, Payton scouted the 2024 draft class, and identified Nix as his guy. The Broncos drafted Nix with the No. 12 overall pick in the first round, and he would go on to vanquish Jarrett Stidham and Zach Wilson in a training competition to become the first rookie quarterback to be the day-one starter since John Elway in 1983 — a harbinger of things to come.
Nix's rookie year was ugly at times, especially early on, and while he bumped his head along the way, he soon had the Broncos on the winning track. He almost beat the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium, and later actually pulled it off at home, and would go on to win 10 games as a rookie starter.
The Broncos qualified for the playoffs, snapping their near decade-long drought. The upstart Broncos were quickly bounced in the wildcard round by the Buffalo Bills, but the floodgates had opened.
Nix ended his rookie season injured, playing with fractured vertebrae in his back for the entire stretch run. Finishing as a Pro Bowl alternate, he was actually invited to the Games, but declined, deciding instead to undergo a " minor " procedure on an undisclosed body part unrelated to the transverse process fractures in his back.
Nix was healthy and good to go in time to kick off OTAs, and the Broncos hit the 2025 season. If you recall, the Broncos won their season opener last year in ugly fashion, then lost two straight on the road.
Sitting at 1-2 for the second straight season, it wasn't looking good. But then Nix found his groove with a big win over the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 4, and the Broncos went on an 11-game winning streak.
Along the way, the Broncos knocked off the defending World Champion Philadelphia Eagles on the road, vanquished the Houston Texans and their fearsome defense on the road, beat a desparate Patrick Mahomes-led Chiefs team at Mile High, and steamrolled the Green Bay Packers at home as underdogs.
Nix won 14 games in Year 2, dethroned the Chiefs in the AFC West, and helped the Broncos secure the No. 1 playoff seed. But he wasn't done.
That was supposed to be Josh Allen's year when the playoffs rolled around. With no Mahomes, Lamar Jackson, or Joe Burrow, Allen and the Buffalo Bills were supposed to romp all over the Broncos in the divisional round, and cruise to a Super Bowl berth — but that's not how it shook out.
Nix turned in a terrific performance against the Bills in the high-stakes environment of single elimination, passing for 279 yards and three touchdowns, with an interception, and rushing for 29 yards. The Broncos took the ball away from Allen five times, and ultimately won in overtime, 33-30.
That massive win over Buffalo came with a heavy price, as Nix suffered a fractured ankle on the third-to-last play of the game, ending his season. Hosting the AFC championship game, thanks to Nix's magical season, the Broncos tried to get past the New England Patriots with Jarrett Stidham under center, but he was overwhelmed by the moment, the opponent, and the weather.
In six games this season, we haven't seen the 2025 version of Nix since January 17 — or at least, not the full version. He's shown flashes, but he's looked... different.
Nix seems hesitant and anxious — like a deer caught in the headlights, at times. But he's also had signature moments, like his comeback against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 2 and Los Angeles Rams in Week 3.
Against the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday night, Nix passed for just 107 yards on 27 attempts, with his longest completion being a 16-yard check-down to RJ Harvey. But without the two touchdown drives he led in the first half, the Broncos' suffocating defense wouldn't have been able to pin its ears back and get after Sam Darnold all night.
Amid all the talk of benching Nix, few people mention how the Seahawks' defense is yet to allow a single opponent to eclipse 200 yards passing this season, or how they entered Week 6 as the NFL leader in takeaways. For that matter, I don't hear too many people pointing to the exceedingly tough schedule the Broncos have faced through the first six weeks.
The Broncos have faced the NFL's toughest schedule thus far, but they're 4-2. Every opponent the Broncos have beaten won at least 12 games and were in the playoffs last year. And each of those opponents fielded a ferocious defense.
The Chiefs are the only non-playoff team the Broncos have played this year, and a quarter of the way into the season, they've clearly reestablished themselves as one of the NFL's elite.
Perhaps Nix's ankle isn't as fully recovered as the Broncos have led us to believe. Maybe he's still feeling the psychological effects of the injury.
If so, Nix has sure done a heck of a job to overcome it and do just enough — and sometimes more than enough — to keep the Broncos on a winning track.
Bench Bo Nix? Don't make me laugh.
If you think for a second that Denver would have been able to beat the Jaguars, Rams, Chargers, or Seahawks with Stidham under center, think again. Against the NFL's cream-of-the-crop defenses, he would have folded like a lawn chair, especially after the first 15-20 scripted plays.
And that Mile High Magic that Nix is able to conjure so often? Stidham has no such wand. There would be no iconic comebacks. The Broncos would be 0-6 — maybe 1-5 — but I don't think they beat the Chargers in L.A. with Stidham at quarterback.
Meanwhile, despite his imperfections and ongoing slump, Nix has the Broncos at 4-2 and through the worst of their schedule. There's a tough game in two weeks at home against the Chiefs, but making a change at quarterback right now would only torpedo the Broncos' 2026 ambitions, and squander the benefits of what their hard-fought 4-2 start has gifted them.
The Broncos are about to go on a run. I'm not predicting an 11-game winning streak, but the schedule is about to open up in a big way.
This team may have faced the NFL's toughest schedule so far, but from here on out, the Broncos get the fourth-easiest slate of opponents, per Pro Football Focus .
Hardest Strength of Schedule this season to date    remaining Broncos       1st             29th Pats               2nd           27th Rams            3rd            13th Bills               4th… pic.twitter.com/4D9CxPovnS
Nix will get the opportunity to find his footing and break out of this slump, especially if Payton can get to the bottom of the Broncos' run-game inefficiencies . If the Broncos made a change at quarterback, they'd quickly find themselves back at .500, and then what? Go crawling back to the quarterback who won you 28 games in 40 starts over two-and-a-quarter seasons?
No. Nix is the Broncos' guy,…

title: What Broncos’ Snap Counts Revealed in OT Win Over Seahawks
full_text:
The Denver Broncos have seemingly perfected the art of winning ugly. We saw it at times last season, but it's become a regular theme in 2026.
A win is a win, though. And in the NFL, nobody should apologize for victory.
The Broncos defeated the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday night 17-14 in an overtime thriller. One of the most impressive aspects of Denver's fourth win of the season was the way its defense overcame the injuries to several key players to terrorize Sam Darnold all night long and pick him off twice.
Bo Nix and the Broncos' offensive line did not miss a snap, playing 60 snaps against the Seahawks. Beyond the starting five, depth lineman Alex Palczewski saw the field for just one snap.
As for everybody else, that's why we're here. Let's examine the Broncos' snap counts for what gleanings they can offer.
Dobbins carried the ball 17 times for 41 yards and a touchdown, but Seattle made him fight and scrape for every inch, as evidencd by his 2.2 yards-per-carry metric. He did have one really nice 16-yard run that helped set up the Broncos' second touchdown.
RJ Harvey had six carries for 25 yards and a touchdown, while also catching three passes on four targets for a team-high 31 receiving yards. Dobbins also caught three balls on three targets, but for just five yards.
Badie only received one touch before injurying his thumb, but it was a crucial six-yard gain on 4th-&-3 that extended the Broncos' first touchdown drive. Prentice saw a handful of snaps, but no touches.
The Broncos' receivers ran a lot of yards for very little production. Too many wasted routes as Nix's slump continues, but Sutton led the way in snap share, with Waddle right behind him.
Waddle led the team with seven targets, but he only caught four for 24 yards. He was open often, but Nix either didn't see him or was hesitant to push the ball. Probably both.
The Broncos may be 4-2 , but you have to wonder how Nix's slump is affecting the attitude of Waddle and Sutton. These are high-profile receivers who are barely touching the ball, despite running a high volume of routes.
Sutton only had two catches on three targets for 19 yards, but he drew a pass-interference penalty that set the Broncos up on the one-yard line. Franklin was only targeted once, catching it for two yards, while Mims earned four targets, including one deep pass that Nix put on the money.
It looked like Mims was interfered with but no flag was thrown. Humphrey did not touch the ball.
For the first time in a few weeks, Engram was not the Broncos' top snap-getter at tight end. Trautman beat him out by two, but Engram was targeted twice by nice, catching them both for 13 yards.
Trautman and Adkins were mostly blockers in their snaps, and neither did a good job against that tough Seahawks front seven.
The Broncos' D-line was relentless on Thursday night. Allen led in snap share, but Roach finished with the most quarterback pressures (six).
Uwazurike had a good game, too, pressuring Darnold four times, while D.J. Jones notched three pressures. Sai'vion Jones had two pressures and a hit on Darnold, while also getting his big mits up to bat down a pass.
Allen finished with a half-sack on four pressures.
Although he only finished with a half-sack — split with Allen — this was one of Bonitto's best pass-rushing games as a pro. His spin move was devastating, and he was a constant thorn in Darnold's side.
Hats off to Robinson, Elliss, and Tillman, too, as they all made an impact against Seattle. Robinson led the way with six pressures and a sack, but Elliss was able to finally notch his first QB takedown of the season, finishing with six pressures himself before suffering an ankle injury near the end of regulation.
Jonathon Cooper is headed back from the commissioner's exempt list, but this rush linebacker room is in the zone right now. The Broncos will be in a quandary when it comes to deciding who to sit on game day.
Singleton turned in one of his best games as a Bronco . He was one of three Broncos defenders who played 100% of snaps, and he finished with 13 tackles and three pressures, while allowing only two completions for 11 yards in coverage.
Strnad played well, too, finishing with four tackles and a half-sack. He wasn't targeted in coverage.
Barron played 100% of snaps and while he gave up nine receptions for 121 yards in coverage, he was targeted 12 times and had to cover Jaxon Smith-Njigba on five of them. It was a tough assignment, but Barron played physical, sticky coverage, and on most of the completions he allowed, he was right there to either get a hand on the ball or make the immediate tackle, but he did give up a long of 42 yards. Again, though, his coverage was tight.
Abrams-Draine answered the bell, though he too was targeted in the double digits. On 14 targets, he allowed eight completions for 94 yards, but he made Darnold pay late in the fourth quarter, undercutting a route to pick him off. Abrams-Draine's tackling left much to be desired.
McMillian was magnificent. He gave up three completions on six targets for just 16 yards, but had five solo tackles and a sack. His interception in overtime helped Denver seal the win.
Moss started the game, but only played 20 snaps. He should be back for Week 7, though I doubt Patrick Surtain II joins him.
With Talanoa Hufanga out, the Broncos relied on Jones and he answered the bell, finishing with eight tackles. He was targeted once, a completion that went for just one yard.
Rapp was elevated from the practice squad into the starting lineup, just as I suspected with Hufanga out. Technically, Key got the start, but he quickly took a back seat to Rapp, who played well in coverage and against the run in his first game as a Bronco.
Rapp finished with six tackles and was only targeted once, allowing a completion for 11 yards. It was good to have his experience on the back end of the defense because it helped prevent and deter some big plays.
Key also played well as the third safety and big nickel, finishing with three tackles. He gave up completions on both of his targets (for just nine yards), but was good in coverage. The Broncos could get by with this safety trio for some time if they had to.

title: Detroit Lions Are Small Betting Favorite Against Packers in Week 7
full_text:
The Detroit Lions will finally begin division play in Week 7 at Ford Field.
After a Week 6 bye, Dan Campbell's squad have opened as a three-point betting favorite against the Green Bay Packers, according to DraftKings sports book .
Detroit's division rival is arriving with a record of 4-2 and having defeated the Dallas Cowboys, 23-13, on Sunday Night Football.
Despite a solid performance against the Arizona Cardinals, the former NFL tight end expressed last week the coaching staff was planning to evaluate all three phases, to clean up the mistakes that will be costly, if they continue the remainder of the season.
"I think it's important we look at the whole thing. We played much better. It's one of our best games. It was our best game this year. But to say that, 'Well, there we are, we've arrived,' that would not be wise. So no, my plan is to look at all of them," said Campbell. "Like I told those guys, I don't need the numbers. I don't need the, 'Well, here's where we're at at third down percentage.' I don't need all that. I know what that is. I need to know schematically, what can we improve on? What are some things that defenses are offering like they've got a tendency on us that we need to adjust."
Another aspect the coaching staff is looking for is identifying the players they can trust in critical moments of games.
"What players are really making big plays for us across the board in critical moments? We need to know who those are. We've got a pretty good idea of who they are for us," said Campbell. "But there's some guys that may pop a little bit like, 'Okay, we need to use this guy a little bit more. This is somebody we can really count on.' And then, 'Hey, this guy's really good until you get in critical moments. And then we get in critical moments and this guy's killing us.' Well, we need to keep him out of critical moments. It's little stuff like that and it makes a difference.
"So, those are the things I want to look at, and we're going to look at it in totality," Campbell added further. "We've got a pretty good idea. I mean, we just went through the four weeks of things that weren't so good. But we're going into the bye on a positive note, and we've got things to clean up. And I mentioned this last night, that's a step in the right direction. But to think that's going to be good enough for Green Bay, it's not. We still need to clean up more than, we need to clean up a lot more than that, and we can, and we will.”
Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change.

title: Detroit Lions Face Returning RB, Will Avoid Micah Parsons
full_text:
Coming off the bye, the Detroit Lions will be tested right away against one of their fiercest rivals: the Green Bay Packers . The Packers, led by eighth-year head coach Matt LaFleur, are winners of two in a row (at time of this publication).
And they'll be equipped with their star running back , Josh Jacobs, for the first time this season.
Jacobs has been on the commissioner exempt list since Aug. 30, following the filing of misdemeanor battery and criminal property damage charges against him in May.
The seventh-year back is set to be removed from the list Monday, allowing him to practice and play against Detroit next week. Yet, the NFL's investigation into Jacobs remains ongoing, leaving open the possibility that he could still be suspended and miss additional games this season.
Jacobs should provide a significant boost to the Packers’ ground game , which has averaged a measly 3.1 yards a carry heading into Green Bay's primetime affair with Dallas in Week 6. That average, by the way, is the second-worst mark among all 32 NFL franchises.
Jacobs, meanwhile, averaged 4.0 yards per carry, and amassed 929 yards and 13 touchdowns on the ground in his second season with the Packers in 2025. He was also productive in his two games against the Lions a season ago, notably rushing for 83 yards on 17 carries in a Week 13 win against Dan Campbell's squad.
Unquestionably, Jacobs is an integral member of LaFleur's offensive attack, and he's likely to provide plenty of fits next Sunday to Detroit's pedestrian run defense.
While Green Bay will be getting Jacobs back, it will not have superstar EDGE Micah Parsons at its disposal for its Week 7 tilt at Ford Field.
Parsons, who has been on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list since the end of the exhibition season, is still in the process of working his way back from a torn ACL and meniscus injury he suffered last December. And he has still yet to be cleared to return to practice, meaning he will remain sidelined a week from now against the Lions.
Kickoff for the Packers’ Week 7 contest in Detroit is scheduled for next Sunday at 4:25 p.m. EST.

title: Lions Roundtable: Reasons for Hope, Fear After 3-2 Start
full_text:
The Detroit Lions On SI staff examines the 3-2 start to the 2026 NFL season.
Christian Booher: I think the Lions avoided a worst-case scenario with their win over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 5, and as a result there is some positive momentum surrounding them heading into the bye week. Anything less than a 3-2 start would've been tough to overcome, especially with the start that the rest of the division has had in 2026.
The Lions need to play well in their next two games in order to have a chance to win the division, with wins over both the Packers and Vikings looking necessary to keep pace. However, at the very least this looks like a team that should be in contention for a wild card spot in the postseason.
Vito Chirco: I think they're a pretty talented offensive team, but a flawed team nonetheless, particularly on the defensive side of the ball. Also, based on the first five weeks of the season, I just don't believe they're a Super Bowl-caliber squad. They might be a playoff-caliber one capable of winning nine-10 games. However, I don't see this present iteration of the Lions making a Super Bowl run in 2026.
Booher : The offense is clearly the biggest strength, however there are layers to the answer. Entering the season, there was no question that the Lions have one of the best collection of skill players in the league. However, their revamped offensive line has outperformed expectations and deserves some credit for how they've started the year as well. The addition of Juice Scruggs has been a good one, while Christian Mahogany and Tate Ratledge have both taken steps forward in their respective careers.
Chirco : The team's biggest strength, by far, is its offense. Detroit, spearheaded by quarterback Jared Goff and running back Jahmyr Gibbs, has proven time and time again this season that it's capable of being a prolific offensive attack. Goff has been one of the best passers in all of football so far this season, and Gibbs has been one of the league's very best runners. The offense is the real deal, and it could very well carry the Lions to a 10-win campaign in 2026.
Booher : I think the defense can get there. There's no doubt that the start to the season has been less than ideal, and that coordinator Kelvin Sheppard is deserving of the criticism that has been sent his way early in the year. However, they could get it back on track moving forward.
These two upcoming divisional games will be very telling about the team's trajectory. Brian Branch's impending return should be a big boost, while the pass-rush leading the NFL in sacks is also a positive development. The defense deserves the criticism that they've received, but there is hope that they can right the ship.
Chirco : I think so if Brian Branch comes back and is his Pro Bowl-caliber self. However, if he returns and no longer is an impact safety, the Lions’ defense will be in a world of trouble and will likely fail to be serviceable the remainder of the season.
Booher : Jacobs does appear to be getting activated off of the Commissioner's Exempt list heading into the Week 7 matchup. However, I think the fact that he's been sidelined up to this point will have some sort of impact on his performance in the Lions' matchup with the Packers.
Jacobs isn't a rookie, and so he likely won't need much time to acclimate. He should be able to perform well right away, but I think there will also be some rust that he'll have to work through. He certainly is a threat that the Lions will have to be ready for, but I think his workload may be lighter in his first game back.
Chirco : Sure. Jacobs is the real deal and a top-tier running back when fully healthy. So, he certainly has the potential to wreak havoc against the Lions’ league-average run defense next Sunday.
Booher : I think the MVP of the offense up to this point has been Goff. Both players have legitimate arguments for the honor, and the team would be much worse without them if one were to go down. However, I give the honor to Goff because he has been spectacular in terms of what his role is within the offense. He hasn't turned the ball over once, has 12 passing touchdowns and is one of the most productive passers in the league up to this point. Gibbs has been elite as well, and this isn't a wide margin in my eyes between the two players.
Chirco : As much as Jahmyr Gibbs has grabbed all the headlines, I believe it is Jared Goff since he is the straw that stirs the drink for the Lions’ offense. Goff has been “Mr. Efficient” thus far, playing turnover-free football through the first five weeks of the season. It's why I'd give him the slightest of edges over Gibbs for Lions MVP through the first quarter of the season.

title: Exploring Pros, Cons of Lions Claiming LB Aiden Fisher
full_text:
The Detroit Lions enter Week 6 on a bye week, fresh off of the momentum from a 45-21 win over the Arizona Cardinals. However, it came with a cost, as three Lions found themselves on injured reserve, including LB Devin White.
White was a summer addition to the Lions, getting picked up after injuries decimated the room in training camp, including hampering fourth-round selection Jimmy Rolder’s development.
On Saturday, a possible name that could replace White became available in recently waived seventh-round selection Aidan Fisher. Fisher was a productive linebacker that followed head coach Curt Cignetti to Indiana to win a National Championship.
Fisher was viewed as a strong player that trended in the right direction to become a draftable piece during his time in college, but his weakness was in the passing game.
During the pre-draft cycle, multiple outlets, including Lions On SI , had projected Fisher to Motown as a piece to round out the linebacker room. During his final three seasons, Fisher recorded 118-, 108-, and 97-tackle seasons, with the last two being against Big Ten competition. That included 22 tackles for loss, 7.5 sacks, and he also added three interceptions.
The Virginia native was a two-time first team All-American, but his lack of athleticism and pass coverage ability made him wait until the final 15 selections of the 2026 NFL Draft to hear his name called.
He was able to make the Texans' roster out of training camp, but was waived on Saturday with injured linebacker Henry To'oto'o returning to the active roster.
The Lions are in an interesting spot, and a waiver claim is a valid option. Devin White was a proven force when blitzing, and Fisher’s senior year saw 4.5 sacks with the Hoosiers. White also has had some criticism against the pass.
The Lions will likely evaluate internal options, weighing the pros and cons when compared to practice squad member Joe Bachie . Bachie spent a few games active with Motown to start 2026, but was released and added to the practice squad.
Based on his previous production at the collegiate level, it is worth the relatively low risk for the Lions to add Fisher. If he does not pan out, the Lions have the option to let Fisher walk and replace him with White when the former first-round selection is back to full health.
That said, it is unlikely that Detroit will get the chance to claim Fisher, as they currently sit in the mid-20s for waiver order

title: Detroit Lions DE Fined After Cardinals Game
full_text:
Detroit Lions defensive end DJ Wonnum finds himself lighter in the wallet, after he was fined for a hip drop tackle against the Arizona Cardinals.
He was docked $12,611 for the infraction early in the second quarter. If he incurs two more fines of the same variety, he would be subjected to a one-game suspension.
Dan Campbell indicated earlier this week the coaching staff has noticed just how much Wonnum has fit in throughout his first campaign in Motown.
"We notice him in this building. We know exactly what he is, and he’s playing at a high level. I thought he really bounced back from last week in Carolina and played really well in the run and certainly the pass game. He’s creating issues opposite of Hutch," said Campbell. "And man, he keeps doing that, with the firepower we have on that D-line, and you become very dangerous."
Detroit's defense was stifling all afternoon, causing Cardinals tight end Trey McBride to be frustrated.
Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard was praised by the Cardinals for his defensive strategy , which did not allow the Cardinal's offensive weapons to create many explosive plays.
Brissett expressed to local reporters this week he could not force the football into tight windows, due to the Lions bracketing and double-teaming McBride and wideout Michael Wilson.
"Yeah, it was about the double-team stuff. I had to bring the tablet over, and I'm like, 'Look, bro, I don't know what you want. I can't force that in and put the team in jeopardy.' He understands that," said Brissett. "It's the competitor in him."
Cardinals offensive coordinator Nathaniel Hackett called Sheppard's plan unique and fascinating.
“That was pretty unique. I’ve been doing this a while, and it’s funny, the closest thing I ever saw was, we were playing the Ravens with Davante Adams," said Hackett. "And I think there were, like, two to three guys on him the whole time. We were working on all these things we thought were going to happen, but they said, ‘nope, we’re going to take him away.’ But yeah, it was fascinating .”
Lions cornerback Roger McCreary indicated getting back to playing more man-to-man coverage suited the team, as that has become part of their identity.
“These past couple weeks, it felt like we got away from that man coverage. Like, that’s our identity. We like to get greedy," said McCreary. "And I felt like Shep said, 'Forget it. That’s what we’re going to do. That’s our course.' So, that’s exactly what we did today. Get in their faces, play man.”

title: What Lions Week 5 Win Changed about Trade Deadline Plans
full_text:
Although the Detroit Lions enter their Week 5 bye above .500 (3-2), it's no secret they have a variety of needs headed into the NFL trade deadline November 10.
Now it just comes down to which ones Brad Holmes & Co. will fill with less than a month to go until the deadline.
Despite the need for potentially a backup running back and a No. 3 receiver, Detroit's biggest flaws still lie on the defensive side of the ball. Most notably, Dan Campbell's squad remains thin in the secondary: both at cornerback and safety.
While the return of Brian Branch will provide an immediate boost to the defensive backs group, the organization is still in need of a No. 1-caliber cornerback and arguably another safety to pair with the Pro Bowler.
In a perfect world, D.J. Reed would be reliable enough to be the team's No. 1 corner while Kerby Joseph would be on the mend and ready to return to his pre-injury All-Pro form. However, if anything has been proven this year, it's the fact that the Lions can't rely on either of those things to be the case.
While Reed has shown flashes of being a top-tier cover corner, he's not consistently productive enough to be depended upon for No. 1 corner-type production on a weekly basis. It's why even after missing out on Joey Porter Jr., Holmes & Co. should continue to be in the market for a high-level cover corner. And if the front office fails to land one prior to the deadline, it'd be a big misfire.
Then, when it comes to Joseph, Detroit can ill-afford to count on him to be his All-Pro-caliber self again upon his return to action. He reportedly might have a degenerative knee issue that hinders his production level the remainder of his career. Subsequently, the Lions can hardly rely upon Joseph for high-level production in 2026.
And on top of that, there's no definitive timetable for his return. It furthers the reason why the Lions must also make a concerted effort to add a safety to pair with Branch prior to the deadline.
So, even after an improved performance from Kelvin Sheppard's side of the ball against the Cardinals, defense remains Detroit's biggest issue. Consequently, the onus is on Holmes and the front office to upgrade the secondary in the weeks ahead. And if they fail to do so, the Lions could end up on the outside looking in when it comes to the playoff picture this season.

title: Lions Star WR Has Harsh Words About His Game Against Cardinals
full_text:
Last week, the Detroit Lions dismantled the Arizona Cardinals heading into their bye week, scoring on seven straight drives to win 45-21. The Lions overcame a slow start to breeze by Arizona, with former Cardinal offensive coordinator Drew Petzing flexing his muscle in the same role with Motown.
The Lions saw their entire offense execute, with Jahmyr Gibbs recording over 200 yards from scrimmage, Jared Goff having an efficient outing, Sam LaPorta and Jameson Williams combining for three touchdowns, and Amon-Ra St. Brown recording 69 yards.
For the perennial Pro Bowl threat , however, he was harsh about his performance. The USC product had two fumbles on the game, including a punt return after he got called into action after Tom Kennedy’s season-ending MCL tear.
St. Brown was proud of the team, but bashed his own game on his St. Brown Podcast . He expressed gratitude for his teammates for picking him up in the let down of a game for the receiver, in his personal opinion.
“I felt like I had a (expletive) game, if I am being honest” the former Lions’ fourth-round pick said. “Like, one of my worst games I’ve ever had in Detroit. I just feel like it just wasn’t my best stuff. But, we got a lot of great players on our team that picked me up. That’s what good teams do. Sometimes players or good players don’t play their best, but you got other players to pick them up. I think a lot of my teammates did that last game. I’m fortunate enough to be on a team like this that has a lot of good players that can do that for me. I mean, I can’t imagine being on different teams that can’t, that don’t have the type of weapons and type of leaders that we have. Like I said, I’m fortunate, I’m blessed. Big win for us, I’m excited to be going into the bye week with that win."
The slow start was another one of the primary concerns for the All-Pro receiver.
“Offense, we started out slow. I think we had three three-and-outs is what I counted. I was on the sideline like ‘no way we just had three three-and-outs,’” St. Brown revealed. “I’m like, damn.’ But defense, I mean, they played amazing. To have them do what they did for us, they got us started. As an offense, when you can’t get things going, you’re just hoping that the defense holds strong, you get another chance, another crack at it to make a play and put some points on the board. The defense did that, they got a lot of stops on third down.”
St. Brown further harped on the slow starts . While it did not cost them against Arizona, it did cost the Lions in week two, where they found themselves down three scores to Buffalo.
“We started off slow, we can’t have that. To be where we really want to be, we got to be able to start fast and then finish strong,” the longtime Lions player said, punching his hand. “Everything between, you want to play well, but starting fast is very important and ending the half strong and finishing the game strong. If we can correct that, we will be great.”

title: 5 Players Detroit Lions Must Scout in College Football Week 7
full_text:
This week, the Detroit Lions fans get a week of stress-free, guilt-free football . The Lions get the early bye week for the season and a chance to activate Brian Branch, alongside filling two more roster holes after placing three players on injured reserve.
On Saturday, Week 7 for the college football season will be underway. The midpoint of the season has passed as teams make their bid to be among the participants in the last 12-team playoff .
The Lions have seen some holes on defense exposed recently, and here are five players they must scout.
Smith was a projected first-round offensive tackle that elected to return to college for one last season. After protecting Fernando Mendoza on his Heisman campaign, Smith now anchors blindside protection for Josh Hoover. The Hoosiers face their steepest test yet, with Ohio State heading to town.
The reigning Big Ten Lineman of the Year has allowed one sack on the season, but rates among the top percentile for run blocking and gap scheme blocking. His pass-block grade is respectable, although not in the same echelon it was in last season.
That said, Smith is still viewed as one of, if not the best offensive tackle, that will be on the board in about six months time.
The Hoosiers host the Buckeyes at noon EST.
On the opposite side of Smith will be Jackson Jr., another slightly surprising return to college. Jackson was part of eight sacks for the Buckeyes last season, and PFF credits him with three sacks and an additional 12 hurries through the first half of the regular season.
The EDGE rusher currently projects in the second round, and would be an intriguing option if the Lions cannot re-sign D.J. Wonnum after the season. However, Jackson much more closely projects to what Al-Quadin Muhaamad was with Motown, as a pass-rush specialist.
Jackson’s run-stuff ability ranks in the bottom ten percentile, while his pass rush win rate in within the 80th percentile. In easier terms, Jackson has impressed as a pass-rusher, but underwhelmed against the run.
He is currently a projected second-rounder, per PFF. As mentioned above, his matchup with Smith begins at noon EST.
Tengesdal enters his senior campaign with over 1,100 career snaps and only one allowed sack. He was the top returning Power Four run blocker to begin the year.
His playstyle is best described as a mauler, and will be one of the top options when the NFL Draft is rating interior players. His senior campaign got off to a rocky start, with his first sack allowed and a rough outing in pass protection. That said, physicality and his grip in the pass protection game are not going to be questions come draft time. Tengesdal is the real deal.
His Bearcats travel to West Virginia, kicking off at noon EST.
Any time a player draws comparisons to Kyle Hamilton, that draws attention. Satuala is drawing those comparisons in coverage and his violence as a tackler.
While his testing at the NFL Combine will not be spectacular for foot speed and movement, his tape tells another tale. His imposing size (6-foot-4) and wingspan make him a dangerous player to target. When the pass is in the air, his background as the former top recruit from Utah show, with the old wide receiver coming out to haul in the ball.
To further sell the Cougar, he has solid special teams tape. Expect him to translate well there.
The Cougars face off with Notre Dame on Saturday night, kicking off at 7:30 p.m. EST.
It feels weird marking the Pac-12 as “Group of Six,” but welcome to college football in 2026. Borjon brings the length that no coach can develop, as he towers over defenders at 6-foot-9. His tape provides plenty of up and down moments, with middle of the pack grades on almost any metric.
However, the project player has experience at both tackle positions already, and has seen an uptick in play by switching to left tackle this season with the Aztecs. He has allowed one sack this season, which is an improvement. Against Fresno State, Borjon has to stay penalty free, as the massive lineman has been whistled for seven in six games.
That alone draws concerns. With the ending of the Giovanni Manu experiment in sight, perhaps the 2026 NFL Draft is not the time to start a new experiment with Borjon.
For those wanting to watch Borjon, the Aztecs kick off at 10:30 p.m. EST against Fresno State. Get that coffee ready.

title: Former Lions Punter Kasey Redfern Dies at 35 After Long Cancer Battle
full_text:
After a long cancer battle, former Detroit Lions punter Kasey Redfern has died at the age of 35.
According to his wife, Lauryl Redfern, he battled central nervous system lymphoma since 2023. Redfern played in Motown for just one season, back in 2017.
"He fought an incredible fight," Lauryl explained recently to the California Post. "He smiled the whole way through, never questioned why and always knew God had a purpose for this, having great hope that his miracle would be healing on Earth.”
Redfern played collegiately at Wofford (2010-2013) before embarking on a six-year NFL journey. He went undrafted in 2014, but landed with the Jacksonville Jaguars.
Besides the Lions, he had stops with the Jaguars, Chargers, Panthers, Browns, Cowboys and Falcons before his career ended in 2019.
In late September, the 35-year-old entered hospice care. The impact of treatment had started to take its toll on his mind and body.
Additional Detroit Lions NFL Insider Analysis: One Advanced Metric Showcases Importance of Safety Brian Branch to Kelvin Sheppard's Defense
“His poor brain has had all it can take treatment wise so we want to make sure that he can be as comfortable as possible. As our NP pointed out this will also help me be able to love on him more/better and not have to do all of the caretaking as well," his wife shared on social media. "It’s been a really hard few weeks with this extreme decline. He’s still home and able to be home and could still have a lot more time with us, but we just can’t give him anymore treatmen t and unfortunately this decline is irreversible except by another miracle from the Lord which we are still of course praying for.
“We know that healing will take place regardless of the outcome, but if he makes it to Heaven soon, he will have it better than the rest of us and for that all I can do is be thankful and joyful and filled with peace (and a lot of jealousy) that He will be WHOLE and in glory with our Savior, the best place we could ask to be.”

title: Packers Report Card: Gold-Star Performance Highlights Grades vs. Cowboys
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The grades are in after the Green Bay Packers defeated the Dallas Cowboys 23-13 on Sunday night, and the highest marks were attached to the defense.
One year after giving up 40 points to the Cowboys, they held them to seven points before a garbage-time touchdown got them into double-digits.
The task in front of them was not a small one. The Cowboys have largely the same cast of characters. Dak Prescott is still their quarterback. George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb were healthy and on the field.
It didn’t matter. The Packers never allowed Prescott to get comfortable.
“Rush and coverage, baby,” safety Xavier McKinney said. He was right. When defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon was not dialing up blitzes, Green Bay had Prescott guessing on what coverage they were playing.
They get the highest mark in our weekly report card following the team’s third consecutive victory.
Jordan Love was three plays away from throwing four touchdown passes and topping 350 passing yards. That was not to be as the Packers’ struggles with drops reared their ugly head again.
Matthew Golden and Christian Watson dropped one touchdown apiece. Golden had another that could be called a drop or a pass breakup by Joey Porter Jr. Tucker Kraft continued to struggle with one drop and another play that could have been a reception but he did not drag his foot at the sideline.
Love, despite what the box score numbers say, was excellent save for two plays. He had one interception that he threw to linebacker Dee Winters on a telegraphed pass to Golden. He almost threw another interception that turned into an instant-replay debacle before ultimately being ruled an incompletion.
He did all that despite having little protection, zero run game and receivers that continued to let him down throughout the night.
Is it perfect? No, but the Packers’ quarterback has played very well the last two weeks.
The group in front of him left a little to be desired. Dallas’ pass rush has been largely ineffective this season, ranking 29th in sack percentage. Love was sacked three times and hit on eight occasions, according to the official stats. He was pressured on 40 percent of his dropbacks, according to Pro Football Focus. Rashan Gary had 10 pressures.
The guard combination of Laken Tomlinson and Travis Glover struggled for the first time since becoming starters against Tampa Bay earlier in the month.
With four full weeks of practice under his belt, will next week be the time for Kevin Zeitler to make his debut at right guard? That remains to be seen, but this group was not as good on Sunday as it had been. The line will face better defenses during this next stretch of games, starting with a date next week with the Lions led by the mighty Aidan Hutchinson.
If there is a way to sum up the Packers’ run game to start this season, it came on their first possession of the game.
Dallas was the 32nd-ranked defense against the run coming into play. The Packers’ first three runs had a long gain of 0 yards. Yes, 0. MarShawn Lloyd continues to try to bounce runs outside that are designed to stay between the tackles. Pierre Strong and Kaleb Johnson don’t offer much juice in the run game, either, though Strong wound up getting most of the run and made some things happen as a receiver.
Josh Jacobs is expected to return to practice on Wednesday, but will he have any room to roam if he plays on Sunday at Detroit?
In the battle of the very stoppable force against a movable object, the movable object looked like the Steel Curtain from the 1970s.
The Packers had 40 rushing yards in the first half on 15 carries, with 14 of those yards coming from Jordan Love. Lloyd, the team’s starting running back, had minus-2 yards on three carries.
The atrocity of the run game cannot be understated. The failure falls on the offensive line and the guys being asked to carry the ball.
Perhaps inserting Kevin Zeitler into the lineup with Jacobs will give them a boost next week against Detroit.
Take a bow, Jonathan Gannon.
Last season, the Packers’ defense had no answers for Dak Prescott and his group of receivers. Those same players were on the field on Sunday night. The Cowboys even added CeeDee Lamb, who missed last year’s matchup. Prescott rang up 319 passing yards and three touchdowns in a 40-40 tie, with George Pickens catching eight passes for 134 yards and two touchdowns.
Sunday night? Not even close.
In 54 pass attempts, Prescott threw for 258 yards. His only touchdown pass came after the game had largely been decided. He was only sacked once but under duress most of the night, which led to two interceptions and a third wiped away by a questionable roughing-the-passer penalty.
Pickens had six catches on 11 targets for 73 yards. Lamb had nine catches on 18 targets for 70 yards.
“Did they score?” cornerback Keisean Nixon asked.
The answer was no. The Packers held one of the top receiver duos in football out of the end zone with a cornerback group that entered the season shrouded in questions.
The difference in play style from 2025 to 2026 is prevalent. The Packers are not willing to just wait around for one of their defensive linemen to make plays. Gannon is more than willing to force the issue.
He forced the issue on Sunday, and the Packers’ defense is rolling ahead of another big test next week against the Lions.
“Yeah, I thought JG was aggressive, getting pressure on the quarterback,” coach Matt LaFleur said. “It’s hard to throw when you’ve got stuff in your face, and I thought the coverage was outstanding. Our guys challenged them. They did a great job.”
Evan Williams and Brandon Cisse had interceptions, and Carrington Valentine had a pick that was eliminated by Lukas Van Ness’s dubious roughing penalty. Javon Bullard broke up three passes, including one on fourth down.
“I was really happy just overall with our whole defensive performance, especially against that offense,” LaFleur said. “If you told me going into this game that you’re going to score 23 points, I was like, ‘Ah, we need to score 30-plus.’ But our defense, they did their job. They got one (touchdown) late in the game and I thought for the entire game our defense really balled out.”
The run game was not much of a factor for Dallas. It wants to throw the ball, first and foremost. With the Packers leading by two scores for most of the game after opening up a 10-0 lead, the run game became even more of an afterthought.
Overall, the Cowboys ran for 48 yards on 15 carries. Their longest run was 8 yards.
Not bad for a group that was shorthanded on the defensive line and is still working on replacing linebacker Edgerrin Cooper.
Green Bay has been excellent against the run each of the last two weeks but will face a well-rested Jahmyr Gibbs next week as the Lions are coming off a bye. Will they hold him to 48 yards rushing on 15 carries? Probably not, but a similar effort is going to be needed.
How was Trey Smack going to rebound after missing three kicks last week? That was a big storyline coming into a game in which it felt like points were going to be precious to each team with a shootout in the forecast.
A shootout did not break out, but the Packers’ rookie kicker was clean. He made both extra points and three field goals for a perfect night at the office. His last field goal all but iced the game in the fourth quarter.
Coleman Owen, who was elevated from the practice squad , returned punts in place of Skyy Moore and had a 16-yard-return. J. Michael Sturdivant looked comfortable returning kickoffs, as well. Daniel Whelan averaged 50.3 yards per punt. Ultimately the special teams did not make any egregious mistakes. A clean game was a welcome sight after last week’s debacle.
Forget about Matt LaFleur and Cam Achord for a minute. LaFleur had his team ready, and it built on last week’s win over the Bears in a spot that could have been prime for a letdown. LaFleur gets credit for that. Achord’s special teams were fine.
The star of the show, however, was defensive…

title: With 4-2 Record, How Have Packers Gone From Staggering to Streaking?
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Twenty-four days earlier, the Green Bay Packers were embarrassed in front of a national television audience and booed off the field in a blowout loss to the Atlanta Falcons.
The vultures were circling coach Matt LaFleur’s team after a 1-2 start. They seemed like a team ready to sink under the weight of their fatal flaws, undisciplined play and numerous injuries. They couldn’t run the ball, couldn’t protect the passer and couldn’t get out of their own way.
Incredibly, with their 23-13 victory over the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday night, the Packers have won three consecutive games. They still are a team with fatal flaws, and they certainly haven’t gotten any healthier. They can’t run the ball, they struggle to protect the passer and they can’t get out of their own way at times on either side of the ball.
And yet, the Packers have the fourth-longest winning streak in the NFL.
LaFleur wasn’t proud of the way his team played but he is proud of its mental toughness.
“I think it feels pretty good right now. But once tonight’s over, you watch the tape, you learn from it, you move onto the next,” LaFleur said. “It’s not like our schedule is going to get any easier here. So, it truly is a week-to-week league, and you’ve got to take it one game at a time – really, one day at a time. You’ve got to put in the work, first and foremost. And I love that locker room, I love those guys, they come to battle, they come to work, got a great attitude.”
The victory over Dallas serves as a decent summary for the season.
The rushing attack produced a woeful 57 yards on 26 carries. That’s 2.2 yards per carry. That’s pretty terrible. And yet, when you limit it to the running backs, 20 handoffs were turned into 36 yards. That’s 1.8 yards per carry. You could do better by face-planting.
“We got to find a way to get this run game going because it’s too inconsistent,” LaFleur said.
Later, he added: “We got to keep hammering it because it is critical in today’s football to be able to run the football at a decent level.”
Jordan Love according to the official stats was sacked three times and hit on five other occasions. According to PFF’s early grading, he was pressured on 40 percent of his dropbacks and threw the third-most under-pressure passes in Week 6.
“The goal is to not get hit,” Love said. “The O-line, that is their job, and they take pride in that. And I think we’ll look at what we can continue to clean up. But for me, that’s my job. I’ve got to be able to stand in there.”
The Packers were flagged 11 times for 96 yards. There were three penalties for roughing the passer and two for taunting.
“You can only control how you respond to all that stuff and we’ve got to do a better job of making sure, whether we feel it was justified or not, it doesn’t matter,” LaFleur said. “You got to control your emotions to the best of your ability, and you’ve got to move on and play the next play and go beat him between the whistles.”
The dynamic duo of Christian Watson and Matthew Golden made some big-time plays but also looked like they had traded their receiver gloves for oven mitts at times. Drops have been a problem all season, with Love victimized by a league-high 14 through the first five games. Watson and Love each flubbed touchdown passes against Dallas.
Nonetheless, with no rushing attack, no discipline and shoddy execution, the Packers won with relative ease. They led 17-0 at halftime and more or less cruised over the finish line.
The Packers are 4-2 and in fifth place in the NFC. It’s an unthinkable achievement, really, given how they looked like an understaffed and underfunded semipro team for the first quarter of the season.
“We’ve had some ups and downs, obviously, but most teams do in the National Football League, and it’s truly how you respond to the adversity and if you can face it head on,” LaFleur said. “One thing I love about those guys, even through it all, there’s been any finger pointing.
“Everybody’s looking inward and trying to look at what they can improve upon as an individual, because we know that’s going to help the collective. That’s the way it needs to be, and those guys are selfless guys. Certainly, we’ve got some guys that aren’t playing that probably are deserving of playing. But they just keep coming to work with a great attitude and keep battling, and that’s the mark of a good team.”
For all the warts, they found a way.
Offensively, the Packers – the worst third-down team in the league through five games – went 11-of-18 against Dallas.
“Definitely feels good to get rolling with some wins,” Love said. “That’s what we talk about as a team. The mindset is take it one week at a time. We’ve got to stack wins. Obviously, a little adversity early on in the season with a couple of losses, but it’s all about how you respond, and I think we’re responding well right now.
“It definitely feels good, but we’ve just got to keep building upon it, keep stacking, keep taking it one week at a time.”
Defensively, Jonathan Gannon put together a winning game plan and the players executed it to perfection. Cornerbacks Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse won their matchup against Cowboys receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. With some late-game fluff, they caught 15-of-29 targets for 143 yards.
“I think we’re right where we need to be,” Nixon said. “We got them losses out of the way, and I think it’s full throttle nowadays. We’ve just got to keep stacking. One-week-at-a-time mentality.”
The Packers are going to have to play better, to state the obvious. And quickly.
The Packers will play next week at the Lions, who are 3-2 and coming off their bye. Then, they will host the NFC South-leading Panthers, who are 3-2. After that, it’s a road trip to New England to face the defending AFC-champion Panthers, who are 4-2 with three consecutive wins. Finally, in the last game before the bye, the Packers will host the undefeated Vikings.
At some point, their fatal flaws will be just that. Fatal. But they are 4-2 and will be getting Josh Jacobs and Micah Parsons back at some point.
“That’s life in this league, right? Everybody’s going to have some flaws and you just got to find a way to go 1-0 every week,” LaFleur said. “I think the process is a big part of that in terms of what you’re doing from Monday to Saturday.
“I know we’re all judged on that 3-hour window of what the final product is, but I’m a big believer in the process. You’ve got to have a routine and you’ve got to come in with the right mindset and put in the work, because there’s no hiding from it.”
It wasn’t perfect on the field, though the final score showed another win. It wasn’t perfect in LaFleur’s postgame news conference, either, as he almost fumbled his closing thoughts on the final question.
“Proud of our guys. I think they do sh … stuff the right way. I almost slipped there,” he said with a laugh. “They do things the right way and I feel fortunate to be around a group of men like that that are willing to uphold a standard and do things the right way.”
