title: Winners and Losers: Jonathan Gannon Leads Packers’ Victory Over Cowboys
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers entered their Week 6 matchup on Sunday Night Football against the Dallas Cowboys in a situation that could swing their season.
A win would give them a three-game winning streak and helped build on last week’s win over the Chicago Bears. A 4-2 record in their first six games, considering how the season started, could not be considered anything other than a significant achievement for the team.
A loss would drop them to 3-3 with a date against a Detroit Lions team that will be well rested off their bye week.
They started with a bang, riding a 17-0 lead to a 23-13 victory. There was a lot of meat left on the bone for the offense, but the defense was the star of this show. They lead off our list of winners and losers.
Evan Williams said earlier in the week that he was licking his chops facing an offense like Dallas, which wants to put the ball in the air as much as it can.
Williams was the first of two Packers defensive backs to get an interception in the first half. More on that in a little bit, as Williams was in perfect position to make the play.
Evan Williams dropped from the line of scrimmage into a deep quarter — a ton of ground to cover — and still got into position for the INT. Dak Prescott never saw the rotation coming. Brilliant angle here. pic.twitter.com/Z2bMHBG6rp https://t.co/z8hoqXSDfa
Williams made plays at multiple levels of the defense on Sunday night. In the third quarter, he was sent on a blitz that got immediate pressure, forcing Prescott to get rid of the ball early. The pass fell incomplete and the Cowboys had to punt.
The Packers’ defense has not had its top two players for most of the season, and it appears that Williams has been weaponized by his defensive coordinator.
Jonathan Gannon may not have been the most popular choice to be the Packers’ defensive coordinator. It appeared that the most popular choice would have been former Wisconsin Badger Jim Leonhard, who ultimately landed with the Buffalo Bills.
Gannon was dealt a bad hand to start the season as his best player, Micah Parsons was out for the start of the season thanks to an ACL injury he suffered before Gannon was in town.
Just three games and one half into Gannon’s tenure, he lost his second best player when Edgerrin Cooper went down for the year with an achilles injury.
Gannon has simply soldiered on and helped captain Green Bay’s defense that has given up 20 points, which in the last two weeks against two powerful offenses
A year ago, the same Dallas offense with largely the same cast of characters scored 40 on the Packers.
They scored seven while the game was in the balance.
He weaponizes his best players. He keeps opposing quarterbacks guessing. We often talk about play sequencing for an offensive play caller, but Green Bay’s first takeaway of the night was the result of Gannon sequencing plays early in the game.
Gannon was not waiting around to allow Dak Prescott to find a rhythm. He was sending pressure early and often at Dallas’ quarterback.
With the Packers’ defense facing a third down following a Jordan Love interception nursing a seven point lead, Gannon tricked Prescott. He showed pressure with Evan Williams, but Williams dropped at the last second. Prescott never saw him as he fired the ball toward the end zone, and Williams had an interception.
Gannon, unlike some of his predecessors, does not wait around hoping for his front four to win. If they’re not getting pressure, he’s going to send more guys to try and make the quarterback uncomfortable.
Whenever the Cowboys had a chance to snatch some momentum, the Packers’ defense had an answer. More importantly, Gannon had an answer.
One of Jordan Love’s strengths is his ability to keep an even keel even as everything else around him continues to unravel.
Limited protection? That’s fine. No run game? No big deal. Receivers dropping passes? Love keeps putting the ball where it needs to be.
Love had one touchdown pass in the first three quarters of play, but easily could have had four. Matthew Golden dropped two. Christian Watson dropped one. Love’s game on Sunday was a case where the final stat line is not going to show how well he played.
Jordan Love Just Threw It Right Over The Cowboys Defender’s Head. What An Amazing Throw From The Packers Quarterback. Unreal. 🔥 pic.twitter.com/2WxMKSDWcx
Save for one poor decision on an interception that he threw to Dee Winters, Love was excellent on a night where his team needed him to be. If he can get a little bit of help from his supporting cast, the Packers’ offense could be really dangerous down the stretch.
Yes, it was a gift, but sometimes gifts are what it takes when you play cornerback. With the Cowboys’ offense driving and threatening to cut into Green Bay’s 10-0 lead, Dak Prescott tried to find his top target, CeeDee Lamb.
Lamb fell out of his break on his route and Prescott hit Cisse right in the numbers.
Charles Woodson used to always say that if a cornerback catches the passes that are thrown to him, he’ll lead the league.
Cisse may not lead the league, but he’ll never forget his first career interception.
Matthew Golden was so close to having a first half for the ages. He caught a touchdown pass on Green Bay’s first series of the game to open the scoring. He also converted a key third down on Green Bay’s final possession of the first half which led to a touchdown to give the Packers a 17-0 lead.
That was the good news. The bad news was the rest of the first half.
Golden was two plays away from having three touchdowns in the first half, and well over 100 yards receiving. Two separate passes from Jordan Love hit Golden in the hands, but he was unable to corral either of them.
He was also flagged for taunting on the first drive of the game. Quibble with whether the flag was weak or not, but it did happen.
His first target in the second half also resulted in a drop. It was a poor throw, but both hands touched the ball on the play.
Maybe it was the bright lights of Sunday Night Football. Maybe it was the prospect of playing the team from his home state.
Either way, the drops are uncharacteristic from Golden, but those are the types of plays that separate a good receiver from a great one.
Dennis-Sutton had a gift of a sack when he came free on a rush at Dak Prescott in the first half, but left his feet, allowing Prescott to escape.
Later in the game, he gave the Cowboys a gift of his own. Prescott threw the ball out of bounds on third-and-6 with mere seconds remaining in the third quarter. The Packers thought they were off the field, but Dennis-Sutton had extra things to say to Tyler Guyton, which resulted in a taunting penalty.
The taunting penalty was part of an offsetting foul thanks to a holding call against Dallas, but it gave the Cowboys a mulligan. They would convert on a completion to George Pickens.
Javon Bullard deflects the 4th down pass away! DALvsGB on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/yAXwn9jtgN
Matt LaFleur was livid with Dennis-Sutton, as he was immediately pulled off the field following the play.
The Cowboys’ drive that should have ended in a punt, resulted in a failed fourth down thanks to Javon Bullard’s heroics.  Still, it’s a play that should not have happened at all. It’s a play that will hurt them against the league’s better teams.
The idea coming into the offseason was that the Packers’ passing game was going to be better because it had fewer bodies to take away targets from the likes of Matthew Golden, Christian Watson, Jayden Reed, and Tucker Kraft.
The Packers were almost stretched to their limit in the first half. Tucker Kraft caught a pass on the sideline before taking a seat there. Kraft did not return for the rest of the first half, before making his return after halftime.
The point is more in what could have happened had Kraft not been able to return to the game. The Packers’ quartet of pass catchers would have been down to just a duo with Golden and Watson the only healthy…

title: Streaking Packers Start Fast, Earn Mistake-Filled Win Over Cowboys
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Was the Green Bay Packers’ blowout victory over the Chicago Bears last week real or was it a byproduct of circumstances, including facing a backup quarterback?
The Packers kicked themselves in the shins repeatedly but outclassed the Dallas Cowboys 23-13 on Sunday night at Lambeau Field. It was Green Bay’s third consecutive win. After a sputtering start to the season, it is 4-2 headed into next week’s game at the Detroit Lions.
The running game was horrendous. The pass protection was faulty. They dropped touchdown passes. They hit double-digits on penalties.
None of if mattered, though, as Jonathan Gannon’s defense was dominant.
This wasn’t against Tyson Bagent, Rome Odunze and Luther Burden, as was the case last week. It was against Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.
Not until the final drive of the night, when the Cowboys (2-4) scored a meaningless touchdown, did Prescott get past 200 passing yards. At the 2-minute warning, Lamb and Pickens combined for 12 catches out of 26 targets for 108 yards.
Jordan Love was 23-of-41 passing for 276 yards with one touchdown and his first-ever interception on a Sunday night start. He would have had about 340 yards and three touchdowns if not for dropped touchdown passes by Matthew Golden and Christian Watson. Golden, though, caught six passes for 104 yards and the opening touchdown as Green Bay rolled to a 17-0 halftime lead.
With the Packers leading 23-7, the Cowboys embarked on the most tedious drive imaginable. On third-and-20, Ty’Ron Hopper was flagged for illegal contact to give the Cowboys a first down.
Next, Carrington Valentine – who had just entered the game after Brandon Cisse sustained a stinger – intercepted Dak Prescott but Lukas Van Ness was flagged for roughing the passer for shoving Prescott.
After the Cowboys converted on fourth-and-5, Karl Brooks was flagged for roughing the passer.
Finally, the Packers made a play that held up. Van Ness sacked Prescott on first down to set the stage for fourth-and-11, when Zaire Franklin and Van Ness converged on Prescott, who flung a pass toward the goalposts, where there were no Cowboys receivers located.
That gave Green Bay the ball with 5 minutes to go and essentially ended the game. With 4 minutes to go following a first-down conversion by Tucker Kraft, a “Let’s Go Brewers!” chant rang out; it was shut down by public-address announcer Bill Jartz, who told the fans it wasn’t the right time.
With the Vikings and Lions having their byes and the Packers winning their third in a row, here are the NFC North standings through Week 6:
The Cowboys pulled within 17-7 to start the second half but Jordan Love had the response.
First, Love on fourth-and-3 found Tucker Kraft in the flat for a tackle-breaking gain of 14. One play later, Love bought time to his left – left tackle Jordan Morgan pancaked his defender – and unleashed a missile to Christian Watson for what should have been a 26-yard touchdown. The reliable Watson, who is having a second-to-none season , dropped the pass in the end zone.
Trey Smack, who missed three kicks last week, booted a 44-yard field goal to make it 20-7 with 5:02 left in the third quarter.
The Packers forced a punt, with Evan Williams coming free on a blitz to force an incompletion. However, Green Bay started at the 6 and couldn’t move the ball, with former Packers Pro Bowler Kenny Clark smoking center Sean Rhyan for a third-down sack.
The Packers appeared to get off the field but blew that opportunity when, on third-and-6, Dani Dennis-Sutton was flagged for taunting on an incomplete pass. The Cowboys were flagged for holding, meaning there were offsetting penalties. Given a reprieve, Prescott hit George Pickens for 7 and a first down on the final play of the third quarter.
Moments later, the Cowboys faced a third-and-2. Isaiah McDuffie was unblocked on a blitz and forced an incompletion. On fourth down, Prescott booted to his left and tried to hit CeeDee Lamb at the sideline, but Javon Bullard made a leaping breakup to give the Packers the ball at Dallas’ 49.
The Packers turned that into a 29-yard field goal. Love connected with Golden for 20 yards before getting hit into the middle of next week by Caleb Downs and Golden again for 12 yards on third-and-5 before getting hit by Rashan Gary. That made it 23-7 with 10:06 remaining.
At that point, Dallas’ feeble defense, which ranked at or near the bottom of the league in practically every category, including sacks, had three sacks, seven tackles for losses and eight quarterback hits in a step-backward performance by the line.
Green Bay led 17-0 at halftime. Even with some dropped passes, no running game whatsoever and a feeble first-down attack, it was total domination.
The Packers forced a punt to start the game, then marched 90 yards for a touchdown. Love was 6-of-8 passing for 109 yards – yes, 109 yards on a 90-yard scoring drive – because of two penalties for 20 yards and two rushing plays that lost 5 yards. After a pair of third-and-13 conversions, Love hit Matthew Golden on third-and-6 for the score.
After Green Bay forced a three-and-out punt, a key moment followed. After Love was sacked on first down, he threw an out to Golden. Linebacker Dee Winters saw it coming, jumped the route and made a tumbling interception. Winters got up, ran through a couple would-be tacklers and scored on a 43-yard pick-six.
A replay review, though, showed Golden touched Winters down at the 43. It was maybe the biggest tackle of the game. The Cowboys drove into the red zone but Prescott was picked off near the goal line by Evan Williams.
The Packers turned the turnover into a chip-shot field goal to lead 10-0. Golden dropped a 43-yard touchdown pass, but the Packers moved it to second-and-goal at the 1. However, Pierre Strong was stuffed on a run and Tucker Kraft couldn’t get his shoulders upfield on a catch in the flat.
After Brandon Cisse’s first career interception, the Packers extended their lead to 17-0 just before halftime. Bo Melton drew a 37-yard penalty for interference and Golden had a 21-yard catch to set up Love’s 1-yard sneak.
The Packers, the worst third-down offense in the league, went 9-of-10 in the first half. It was a remarkable achievement, considering Green Bay averaged less than 1.5 yards per play on first down.

title: Studs and Duds With Packers Routing Cowboys 17-0 at Halftime
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Could the Green Bay Packers build upon last week’s blowout win over the Chicago Bears by doing it again against the Dallas Cowboys? Or was it merely the fool’s gold that tends to sparkle against a backup quarterback?
Through the first 30 minutes, the Packers’ rout of the Bears was no fluke. With Jordan Love contributing 190 passing yards and one touchdown and 14 rushing yards and another touchdown, Green Bay is clobbering the Cowboys 17-0.
The Packers are 9-of-10 on third down. They entered the game ranked last in the NFL with a 27.6 percent conversion rate while Dallas’ defense was last with an opponent conversion rate of 52.6 percent.
Here are some first-half studs and duds.
On the opening touchdown drive, Jordan Love was 6-of-8 for 109 yards. That’s only possible in Canada, but the Packers were guilty of 20 yards worth of penalties and a pair of negative-yardage runs to help Love eclipse 100 yards on a 90-yard touchdown drive.
Love completed a pair of third-and-13s before hitting Matthew Golden for a 9-yard touchdown on third-and-6.
It was a strong start for Matthew Golden – literally and figuratively. On the opening drive, he beat Shavon Revel deep for 37 yards to the 9. Golden was flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct for flexing in front of Revel; whether he said something, only the officials know. So, that moved the ball back to the 24. Another penalty moved it back to the 29. But the Packers scored, anyway, when Golden beat Ameer Speed on a post for a 9-yard touchdown.
AGENT 0 📺: NBC pic.twitter.com/g9gZwas6JN
Midway through the second quarter, Jordan Love threw one of his majestic deep balls. It should have been a 43-yard touchdown but Golden, who was 2 yards in front of Ameer Speed, dropped the pass.  It was a four-point play, as the Packers settled for a field goal.
Late in the first half, Golden almost made an incredible, twisting touchdown catch but couldn’t hang onto the ball while falling to the turf. The first few notes of "Bang on the Drum" were played and some fireworks were set off.
He made up for it a moment later with a leaping, 21-yard catch on an extended play to give Green Bay a first-and-goal at the 2. On the next play, Golden drew a pass-interference flag on DaRon Bland. Love scored on a sneak on the next play to make it 17-0 with 23 seconds left in the half.
On the second play of the second quarter, Zaire Franklin blitzed up the middle and clobbered Dak Prescott. The floating pass was almost intercepted by Brandon Cisse and Prescott was slow to get up.
On the next play, with the Cowboys facing third-and-8 from Green Bay’s 17, Dak Prescott had a solid pocket as he muscled one over the middle to CeeDee Lamb. Lamb had position on Xavier McKinney at the goal line, but maybe it was all a trap as Evan Williams jumped in front of the pass for the interception.
EVAN. WILLIAMS. 📺: NBC pic.twitter.com/H2dBumCPkg
“For sure. For sure. You got to attack these opportunities,” Williams said this week of the challenge of facing the high-powered Cowboys. “If you’re hesitant in any facet, that’s when you get exploited as a defense. When you’re unsure or questionable about what you’re going to do, that’s when explosives start to show up and things can go downhill in a hurry.
“As a back end, you’re licking your chops for opportunities like this when you know the ball’s going to be in the air, and it’s up to you to stop it. That’s what we look forward to on any Sunday. It’s our job to shut down receivers like this, and when you get those opportunities, can’t shy away from it.”
As we wrote before the game , this was the classic case of the stoppable force squaring off against the movable object. The Packers entered the game ranked 32nd with 60.4 rushing yards per game and 31st with 3.05 yards per carry. The Cowboys were 32nd with 168.4 rushing yards allowed per game and 29th with 5.10 yards allowed per carry.
Green Bay’s running game was horrendous. Nine handoffs to running backs gained 11 yards. Even Jordan Love’s 13-yard scramble didn’t put much lipstick on the pig.
The Packers’ best running back? Until Josh Jacobs returns, it’s probably Pierre Strong. On the opening possession, Jordan Love didn’t have any options on third-and-13, so he checked it down to Strong, who broke Ameer Speed’s tackle and gained 14 yards. Later, after Evan Williams’ interception, Love on third-and-8 checked it down to Strong again. He split two defenders for a gain of 10 and another first down. Those plays led to both of their first-half scores for a 10-0 lead.
The Packers entered the game ranked 17th with 5.42 yards per first-down play. It certainly wasn’t because of the running game, which was last in the NFL with 2.47 yards per carry – 0.36 yards worse than No. 31 Las Vegas and 0.89 yards worse than No. 30 Miami.
During the first half, Green Bay ran the ball eight times or 7 yards – the last of those was Jordan Love’s 1-yard quarterback sneak – and attempted seven passes that gained 11 yards.
The Cowboys have one of the best passing attacks in the league with Dak Prescott throwing to CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Prescott finished the half 11-of-15 passing for 86 yards and two interceptions. Lamb caught 2-of-6 passes for 22 yards and Pickens caught his only target for 16.

title: Who Is Packers Returner Coleman Owen, Who Replaced Skyy Moore, Matthew Golden?
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – With Skyy Moore going on injured reserve, who would return punts for the Green Bay Packers against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday night?
Would it be Matthew Golden, who replaced Moore in that role against Chicago and had a 17-yard return? Or would they find someone else so Golden could focus on playing offense?
That answer became apparent. Usually when punter Daniel Whelan goes through his pregame routine, a member of the equipment staff catches the punts. On Sunday, it was receiver Coleman Owen.
Coleman Owen? Who’s Coleman Owen?
In the wake of Jayden Reed’s season-ending injury, the Packers signed Owen to the practice squad on Sept. 2 9. He had a superb senior season at Ohio in 2024 but went undrafted. He signed with the Indianapolis Colts and spent the season on their practice squad. He played in two games with a 28.2-yard average on six kickoff returns and 2 yards on one punt return. He did not catch any passes.
At Ohio in 2024, he caught 78 passes for 1,245 yards and eight touchdowns. He also averaged 7.8 yards per punt return with a 61-yard touchdown. He spent his first five collegiate seasons at Northern Arizona. He averaged 11.8 yards per punt return with an 85-yard touchdown and 24.5 yards per kickoff return.
Coleman Owen is fielding punts from Daniel Whelan. pic.twitter.com/zkZFU3zYcJ
According to Pro Football Focus, he had two career muffed punts – in 2021 and 2023 at Northern Arizona – on a combined 35 punt returns and 53 fair catches.
Owen is the quintessential slot receiver. He’s a bit short (5-foot-10 1/8) and not super-fast (4.53 in the 40) but has excellent short-area quickness for the make-you-miss skill needed to gain yards after the catch.
Coleman Owen is a WR prospect in the 2025 draft class. He scored a 7.32 RAS out of a possible 10.00. This ranked 1025 out of 3815 WR from 1987 to 2025. https://t.co/cPAlSyRLui pic.twitter.com/b7koHDSDJW
“I felt good,” Owen told KPRC-TV in Houston in April 2025 . “It was really fun to go out there and do it after so much training and preparation. They’re getting a guy who knows how to come in and work hard. Being a former walk-on at my last school, I know how it feels to come in and put my head down and work and contribute any way I can. That’s the kind of guy I am.”
Because he slid under the recruiting radars, he thought lacrosse might be his sport.
Owen didn’t think he’d play college football. Rather, he thought his college sport might be lacrosse.
“Didn't really have an opportunity to go anywhere,” he said after Ohio’s pro day . “Very thankful that the Northern Arizona coaches came in last second, offered me a walk-on spot there. So, I walked on there, earned a scholarship, made some of my best friends, my fiancé at that school, just fell in love with that place.
“I'm so thankful that those coaches walked into my high school coach's office at the end of my senior year, and gave me a chance to play this game, because it's brought me a lot of friends and great times. It's unbelievable.”
The decision to take Golden off punt returns was probably by necessity given his enormous importance to the offense.
“We’ll kind of work through that through the course of the week,” coach Matt LaFleur said this week. “Certainly MG’s value, he’s so valuable as a wide receiver for us, but it could be a week-to-week thing with that.”
Special teams coordinator Cam Achord minimized the risk of Golden.
“If you’re blocking well and the guy’s going to run and get tackled – offensively he’s going to get tackled too,” Achord said on Tuesday. “It’s the big collisions you want to avoid. We show up a little bit more on the kickoff, kickoff return game. You know, it’s a lot less space with those plays. You know a lot more bodies, so you get a lot more big, high contact plays than you do.
“Actually, it’s a lot more one-on-one tackles in the punting game. So I think there’s probably, there’s more injuries on the returners in the kickoff return than there is on punt, punt return. And you can always fair catch the ball, right? So, you can limit the hits by just fair catching, if you really want to.”
The team worked “multiple” players in the return role this week, Achord said.
“I think you just work through everything and who all the options are,” Achord said. “We work multiple guys at practice for that reason throughout the week and once we sit down and talk about as a staff, like what’s the best situation for the team to make sure we’re getting the ball back, getting the offense in a good field position situation, whatever we go with, I’m going to be happy with for sure.”

title: Packers-Cowboys Inactives: Most of Last Two Free-Agent Classes Are Out
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers signed four players in unrestricted free agency. Three of them will not play on Sunday night against the Dallas Cowboys.
With the Packers having only 50 players on the 53-man roster and with two elevations from the practice squad on Saturday, they only had to name four players inactive. The inactives are cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring) and offensive linemen Aaron Banks, Jager Burton and Donovan Jennings.
Banks will miss a fourth consecutive game due to knee and toe injuries. Through six games, he has played only 22 snaps.
The Packers ruled out four players on Friday’s injury report. Three of them – Hargrave (Achilles), defensive tackle Jonathan Ford (calf) and receiver Skyy Moore (ankle) – were placed on injured reserve on Saturday. The fourth player was St-Juste.
In free agency this offseason, general manager Brian Gutekunst signed four players.
Defensive tackle Javon Hargrave signed a two-year, $23 million contract after being released by the Vikings. He suffered a torn Achilles during the final moments of last week’s win against the Bears. It was his second season-ending injury in three years. In four games, he had six tackles but led the position group with six pressures.
Cornerback Benjamin St-Juste, who was excellent in part-time duty for the Chargers last season, signed a two-year, $9.8 million contract in free agency. He challenged for a starting job during training camp, has played only one snap on defense and 59 snaps on defense in four games.
Receiver Skyy Moore, who had a sensational season as a punt and kickoff returner after being traded to the 49ers last year, signed a one-year, $2.5 million contract in free agency to help fix the special teams. He was off to a strong start in that regard but suffered a high-ankle sprain early in the game against Chicago.
The fourth and final player signed was quarterback Tyrod Taylor, who the Packers will hope to God won’t have to play a meaningful snap this season.
Starting linebacker DeMarvion Overshown is the big name on Dallas’ inactives list. He will miss a fifth consecutive game with a hamstring injury. Cornerback Cobie Durant, who started the first two games, also is out with a hamstring.
Cornerback Joey Porter, who was acquired a few weeks ago, was questionable with an ankle injury but will start.
The @dallascowboys inactives against Green Bay: #0 DeMarvion Overshown (LB) #2 Cobie Durant (CB) #11 Alijah Clark (S) #31 Emari Demercado (RB) #41 James Houston (OLB) #67 Drew Shelton (T) #80 Camden Brown (WR)
The big news for Green Bay is that cornerback Brandon Cisse is active. He was added to the injury report on Friday as questionable with a hip injury. That it didn’t elevate rookie Domani Jackson, however, was a pretty good sign that Cisse would be fine for the game.
The next men up are Carrington Valentine and Kamal Hadden.
Receiver Savion Williams, who missed the first five games while on injured reserve, will make his season debut.
The Packers on Saturday elevated receiver Coleman Owen and edge player Arron Mosby from the practice squad. This will be Owen’s NFL debut; Mosby has been a valuable player on special teams.
While the 2026 free-agent class was the theme at the start of the story, the Packers signed two players to big contracts in 2025. One of them was Banks, who pocketed a four-year, $77 million contract. He practiced all week but is out again, which means Laken Tomlinson will make his third start at left guard. The other is cornerback Nate Hobbs, who signed a four-year, $48 million contract but was released in the offseason after an injury-plagued first season.
The Packers are 2-0 with Tomlinson starting, though the run game remains the worst in the league by a significant margin.
“We just got to keep hammering the details, being keyed into the details,” Tomlinson said. “The guys have done such a good job of doing all the little things and extra things and just to get out there and practice and stuff and get it on film. And now we just got to make that next step every week, every day, really. So guys are bought in, man, and we’re going to get there.”

title: Predictions: Will Primetime Packers Beat Cowboys, Extend Winning Streak?
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers crushed the Chicago Bears last week. Ultimately, though, what does the 31-7 victory mean in the grand scheme of things?
Was Green Bay’s solid-gold performance a sign of things to come after four lackluster performances? Or was it fool’s gold, a combination of a revenge game and facing a backup quarterback leading to a mirage performance?
We will get some answers when the Packers host the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday night. Who will win? Here are our weekly predictions.
The Packers were great against the Bears but, really, what does it mean?
Their victory came against mistake-prone Tyson Bagent. The quarterback opponent on Sunday night will be against Dak Prescott, who is one of the best in the business.
Bagent threw passes to Rome Odunze and Luther Burden, a decent duo. Prescott will be throwing passes to CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, perhaps the best duo in the league.
The Bears were destroyed by Jordan Love’s barrage of deep passes. Dallas’ pass defense has been terrible but premier cornerback Joey Porter will be in the starting lineup. The presence of Porter could allow the Cowboys to limit, say, Matthew Golden and then put two defensive backs on Christian Watson.
So, while last week’s win over the Bears was a potential season-changing verdict, this week’s game against the Cowboys might be the real litmus test of their playoff-worthiness. Good teams turn one good performance into another. Mediocre teams follow up good performances with duds.
“You’ve got to keep stacking,” quarterback Jordan Love said. “We talk about it in the locker room all the time and team meetings, you have a game like that, you’ve got to be able to follow it up with another great performance. That’s the mindset heading into this week. We’ve got to be able to stack wins and get rolling as an offense and as a team.
“Just comes back to it’s a new week. You’ve got to learn from the mistakes, learn from the good things that happened last week, and move on. Flush it, put all the focus on Dallas this week and understand that they’re going to be a hungry team coming in here.”
I’m tempted to pick Dallas. All along, I’ve wondered how the Packers will be able to win games like this one or next week at Detroit. Good pass defenses have a winning combination of rush and coverage. The Packers don’t have either. Their pass rush isn’t good enough to impact the quarterback on a consistent basis and their cornerbacks aren’t good enough to slow down elite receivers.
In last year’s tie, the Cowboys scored 40 points. Dallas didn’t have receiver CeeDee Lamb on the field. Green Bay did have Micah Parsons. On Sunday night, Prescott will be throwing passes to Lamb and George Pickens without having to worry about Parsons.
Turning to this season, the Packers were crushed on a Thursday night by the Falcons but rebounded during the mini-bye to beat the Buccaneers and Bears. The Cowboys were crushed by the Buccaneers last Thursday night but had the mini-bye to find some answers.
On paper, Green Bay’s defense is good. It’s ranked eighth in yards allowed per game, fifth in yards allowed per play, sixth in yards allowed per passing plays, first in interception percentage and eighth in sack percentage.
However, that success has come against a string of mediocre (or worse) quarterbacks, with the best of the bunch probably being Michael Penix. There is nothing mediocre about Prescott and his receivers.
On the other hand, Dallas’ defense is downright horrible. It ranks 32nd in yards allowed per play, 29th in yards allowed per rush and 30th in yards allowed per pass. It’s 32nd in interceptions, 29th in sack percentage, 32nd on third down and 24th in the red zone.
So, if the question is how the Packers can slow down Prescott and his receivers, the bigger question for the Cowboys is whether they can slow down Love and his receivers.
Added together, Love and Prescott will have big games. At times, they will look downright unstoppable. But Green Bay’s defense has made some big plays this season while Dallas’ defense has made almost none. On a night in which it might take only one game-changing play by the defense, the Packers seem more likely to make it.
Prediction: Packers 31, Cowboys 27.
Points, points, and more points. Dallas’ defense is terrible and does not match up well at all with the Packers’ trio of pass catchers. The Packers should be able to move the football almost at will. Jordan Love is excellent on Sunday Night Football and should know that his team needs a big performance to stave off a potential letdown after last week’s big win over the Bears.
The Packers are also facing a real quarterback for the first time this season. Dak Prescott should be able to navigate Green Bay’s defense without Micah Parsons chasing him, with his talented receivers doing some damage against Green Bay’s banged-up cornerbacks.
Ultimately, it will be a case of who gets the ball last. In this case, Love does, and Trey Smack will drill a game-winning field goal as time expires to lift the Packers to 4-2.
Prediction: Packers 37, Cowboys 34.

title: Three Reasons Why Packers Will Lose Shootout Against Cowboys
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers could score a lot of points on Sunday night against the Dallas Cowboys. The Packers’ offense got rolling against Chicago, and Dallas’ defense is one of the worst in the NFL.
On the other hand – well, let’s just roll into the three reasons why the Packers will lose to the Cowboys.
Remember last year’s 40-40 tie? What will these teams do for an encore?
(The over/under of 53.5 points is the highest on the board at FanDuel Sportsbook , by the way.)
The Packers are going to score points against the Cowboys’ porous defense. The same probably will be true for Dallas’ offense against Green Bay’s defense.
All along, the biggest question about Green Bay’s defense without Micah Parsons is how it would contend with a real quarterback throwing the ball to real receivers. Minnesota’s Kyler Murray is mediocre. The Jets’ Geno Smith is nearing the end of his career. Atlanta’s Michael Penix is a work in progress. The Buccaneers started an undrafted rookie backup. The Bears started a backup.
Dak Prescott is an elite quarterback.
The Packers’ starting cornerbacks, Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse, have played winning football overall for five games. But this will be their biggest challenge.
The Vikings’ Justin Jefferson scored two touchdowns. The Falcons’ Drake London had 194 receiving yards. The Cowboys have a premier receiving tandem with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Lamb had three consecutive games of 110-plus yards in Weeks 2, 3 and 4. In Week 5, it was Pickens’ turn with nine catches for 130 yards.
“If they see one-on-one, Dak has no hesitation of going up and just letting them try to make a play,” safety Evan Williams said. “So, I feel like for the back end, especially from the safety perspective, it puts a lot more importance and pressure on disguise, trying to show them something else, so he doesn’t know he has one-on-one on the outside before the ball’s snapped. CeeDee had, what, 20 receptions when Houston was playing two-high safety and showing it for most of the game and just made it easy.”
A good defense has a combination of pressure and coverage. While the Packers are eighth in sack percentage, applying anything resembling consistent pressure has been a problem. The Packers are only 29th in pass-rush win rate, according to ESPN. While it’s true that defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon can create pressure, doing so would put his cornerbacks at risk.
Remember, Prescott (without Lamb) shredded the Packers (with Parsons) last season.
With a clean pocket this season, Prescott’s passer rating is 116.6. There might be a lot of clean pockets without Parsons.
“You play this game, and you wanted to play in the NFL as a kid to play against the best,” Prescott told reporters this week. “That’s what this league is about and that’s what everybody wants. So, it’s what makes it fun. Obviously, wishing him all the best getting healthy. Caught up with him a lot this off season here in Dallas while he was rehabbing. He knows I support him in that.
“At the end of the day, it’s just the Cowboys versus the Packers. This isn’t me vs. Micah or the Cowboys vs. Micah. It’s about us going in and getting a win.”
Dallas’ defense is terrible. One reason is the Micah Parsons trade, with the Packers sending three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Kenny Clark to Dallas. A second reason is this offseason’s trade of Rashan Gary to Dallas.
Clark has four solo tackles, zero sacks and zero tackles for losses. Gary has 10 solo tackles, one sack and one tackle for loss, though he ranks 10th among edge rushers in pass-rush win rate.
If there ever was a game for one or both players to change a game, this would be it.
“It’s their first getting to play the team that they were here for so long, so you’ll get nothing but their best,” quarterback Jordan Love said. “I was with RG and Kenny for a long time and I’ve got a lot of respect and love for those guys. Great players, great people, so I know we’ll get their best and it’ll be cool to see them.”
Dallas’ pass defense has been shredded this season. Whichever team wins the matchup between Green Bay’s blockers and the former Green Bay tandem of Gary and Clark might win the game.
“I think it starts up front for sure,” Clark told reporters this week . “We've got to get after the passer, stop the run. They haven't been running the ball well this year. That's the No. 1 key, stopping the run. And when we get in pass-rush situations, getting hits on the quarterback, getting sacks on the quarterback.”
Last week against Chicago, Jordan Love ran the Packers’ version of the Air Raid. One big play after another led to a blowout win.
While first-year Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker is under fire for a unit that ranks 25th in points allowed, 31st in total defense and last in opponent passer rating, he’s not an idiot. The Cowboys no doubt would prefer the Packers move the ball down the field in small chunks rather than allowing Christian Watson and Matthew Golden to pile up 266 yards on 12 catches.
“Well, it’s just dependent upon who we’re playing and where we think we can take advantage,” Packers coach Matt LaFleur said of the adjustment. “The one thing I would tell you, if teams are going to play soft shell, certainly you have some beaters for those type of coverages.
“But I think at the same time, if they’re going to sit off and have a light box, you better be able to run the ball, and that’s what we haven’t done well enough up to this point in terms of run efficiency. We’ve been able to rip off some explosive runs, but the efficiency in the running game isn’t where it needs to be right now.”
He’s obviously right. Shell defense means two deep safeties rather than one deep safety and one safety near the line of scrimmage. With fewer defenders to account for in the box, it’s an invitation to run the ball.
The Packers, of course, have the worst rushing attack in the NFL. So, can the Packers run the ball at a winning level? Or can Jordan Love move the ball with the short- and intermediate-range passing game on a blustery Sunday?
“It’s a good question. We’ll see,” Love said of how defenses will adjust in light of the Chicago game. “I think, obviously, there’s two-high shell, stuff like that, but that’s not always the answer. So, we’ll see. You never know what you’re going to get until, obviously, you get into gameday, get into the feel for what their game plan is for that week. So, we’ll see, but I think, obviously, you go back to shell but I think a couple of those plays we hit were in shell.”
If the Packers have to go the extra mile, can they put up enough points to win? The Packers enter the game ranked 32nd on third down and 24th in the red zone. Even last week, they were just 4-of-12 on third down, and they haven’t had a game of better than 40 percent. So, for all the fireworks from last week, the Packers have a major problem that hasn’t been addressed.
“We’ve talked about how inconsistent we’ve been as an offense and a lot of areas that we weren’t playing up to our standard, stuff that we need to clean up,” Love said. “It hasn’t been great all-around so, definitely, when you have a game like Sunday where you put up points, make some big explosive plays and it feels good.
“In a game like that, when you leave the game feeling the way we did, it builds confidence. It’s stuff that can drive you into that next week feeling good. Now it’s how do we follow that performance up with another good one Sunday.”

title: Three Reasons Why Packers Will Beat Cowboys for Third Consecutive Win
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Can you imagine Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love throwing a touchdown pass and yelling toward the suite Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones is watching the game from and yelling, “I own you.”
No, of course you can’t. But the Packers have owned the Cowboys. Including Love’s lights-out performance at Dallas in the 2023 playoffs, Green Bay is 10-1-1 in the last dozen meetings headed into Sunday night’s game at Lambeau Field.
Here are three reasons why the Packers will continue their dominance.
Jordan Love is the GOAT of Sunday Night Football . He’s 4-0-1 as a starter and has been a dominant player in all five games.
Love has started twice against Dallas – the aforementioned playoff game and last year’s 40-40 tie. In those games, he completed 73.4 percent of his passes for 609 yards with six touchdowns and zero interceptions. His 134.2 passer rating is the highest for any quarterback that has thrown at least 50 passes against Dallas.
There is no reason to believe Love won’t destroy Dallas again.
The Cowboys have given up a league-worst 120.5 passer rating. On the road, that swells 132.4. The Cowboys are allowing 8.11 yards per passing attempt (30th), have only five sacks (30th) and have not intercepted a pass.
The lack of pass rush for the Cowboys could be a big deal, because Love is a cold-blooded killer when he has time. His clean-pocket passer rating this season is 112.8 with nine touchdowns and one interception, according to Pro Football Focus. He’s completed 69.6 percent of his passes from a clean pocket compared to 41.7 percent when pressured.
“We’ve been a lot more firm in pass pro, cleaning up some of that stuff, cleaning up who we’re going to on some of the blitzes, things like that,” Love said on Wednesday of the last two games, when Laken Tomlinson and Travis Glover were the starting guards.
“I think guys have been a lot more focused in their technique and things like that, and it’s definitely made a difference. I felt very clean in the pocket, had time to throw, get through my reads. It’s one of those things where you look at it week to week and see what we can do better and what we can clean up. But I think definitely the last two games have been some pretty good pockets.”
From Dallas’ perspective, the trade for cornerback Joey Porter Jr. should help – he was inactive for last week’s upset loss to Tampa Bay due to illness – but will be in the starting lineup. A fired-up Rashan Gary could be a bigger factor than he has been for the Cowboys.
Still, the numbers suggest that Love should be able to build on his beatdown of the Bears last week, when he had as many completions of 20-plus yards (six) as he had incompletions.
Last week , we chose the Packers’ worst-in-the-league running game as a reason why they would beat the Bears. And, sure enough, the Packers’ first-half running game was good enough to fuel all the bombs that Jordan Love dropped on the Bears.
On Sunday night, this will be the all-time case of the stoppable force against the movable object. The Packers still have the worst rushing attack in the league. Their 60.4 rushing yards per game is 18.6 yards worse than any other team. Their 3.05-yard average is 0.06 yards better than only the Raiders.
But Dallas’ run defense is just as bad. The Cowboys rank 32nd with 168.4 rushing yards allowed per game – about 12 yards worse than any other team – and 29th with 5.10 yards allowed per carry. They’ve allowed 165 rushing yards in four of five games, including 241 yards last week against Tampa Bay.
The Cowboys traded for defensive tackles Kenny Clark and Quinnen Williams, but they haven’t exactly been forces against the run. Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown will be out of the lineup again.
“Sometimes what happens is you get into a season and you’re so worried about the opponent,” embattled Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker said this week. “You got to worry about yourself and what you’re doing entirely. There have been a lot of self-inflicted wounds these first five games by us, things that are fully under our control.”
You don’t need to run the football to have success in the play-action game. But it doesn’t hurt. If the Packers can get the running game going to at least a functional level, Jordan Love will have chances to strike down the field again.
Jordan Love on play action this season (QB rank), per @NextGenStats : 467 pass yards (2nd) 5 pass TD (T-2nd) 154.9 passer rating (1st) 11.7 pass yds/attempt (2nd) 77.5 completion pct (3rd) 60.4 team rush YPG (last)
As for the Packers’ lead running back, MarShawn Lloyd, he joked that he’s seen the highlight of him running over Bears cornerback Jaylon Johnson for a touchdown a “million times.” It was a great play that was good for his confidence and perhaps a sign that Green Bay’s horrendous running game can at least be mediocre.
“Each week I feel like there’s something I’ve worked on that I’m getting better at,” said Lloyd, who is averaging only 2.8 yards per carry. “Now it’s just learning the game more, being around it, being out there more. The more opportunities I get, the more opportunities I’m able to get better and learn from my mistakes. Now I just need to keep growing.”
The Cowboys have a league-worst two takeaways and are the only team in the NFL without an interception.
The Packers won the turnover battle last week against Chicago 5-0. Under coach Matt LaFleur, the Packers are 45-6 in games without a giveaway. They are 16-1 in their last 17 zero-giveaway games; the exception was last year’s clear-the-benches lost at Minnesota.
It was the perfect way for the Packers to extend their winning streak to nine consecutive games in the month of October. During that span, they are fourth in points scored (27.7 per game) and fourth in points against (10.5).
Under LaFleur, they are 21-8 in October.
“Just taking it one day at a time, one game at a time. That’s the mindset,” he said. “Just putting in the work, trying to get a little bit better each and every practice. I really like what we’ve been doing from a practice standpoint, a little more one-on-one, ones versus ones and obviously you’ve still got to supplement that with some of the carded periods to make sure you’re getting the right looks. But that has been a big emphasis for us.”

title: Texans' Biggest Winners and Losers From Overseas Win vs. Jaguars
full_text:
The Houston Texans were able to find their way to a pivotal Week 6 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars in London at Wembley Stadium , 34-31.
And in the midst of the Texans' second-straight win within their past two, there were a select few names that wound up standing out a bit more than the rest for one reason or another.
There were also some from Houston's side of things that might've not seen this game go the way they might've liked–– even if it might've resulted in a winning effort against a division rival.
With that in mind, let's sort through some of the Texans' biggest winners and losers from their Week 6 win in London against the Jaguars:
It was another impressive week for C.J. Stroud in what's been a really strong start to his fourth year as a pro. While he did end up logging his first interception of the season thanks to a heroic play by Jaguars star Travis Hunter, he certainly made up for that error en route to a 34-point performance from this Texans' offense. He completed over 66% of his passes, threw a total of three touchdown passes, and has now really started to help this offense build some much-needed momentum compared to the first few weeks of the new season.
Stroud did a very good job of spreading the love around to several different pass-catchers on the offensive side of the ball–– even his new addition, Marvin Harrison Jr. ––but it only feels right to shine the biggest spotlight on Jaylin Noel. Noel not only led the Texans in total receiving yards for the day with 107 on just three receptions, but he also marked down Houston's longest play of the day with his 50-yard touchdown catch. It's those explosives that'll continue to force this coaching staff to keep their second-year wideout on the field.
After a long five-week wait, Texans ball-hawking safety Calen Bullock finally hauled in his first interception of the season thanks to a takeaway on Trevor Lawrence in the middle of the first half. And there was even an opportunity for Bullock to land a second takeaway on the Jaguars' final offensive drive of the game. Still, a wildly successful performance for the Texans' Pro Bowl safety.
For as much criticism that the Texans' offense and their play-calling have gotten for the past several weeks, even dating back to last season, offensive coordinator Nick Caley certainly called one of his better games since arriving in Houston . The Texans' passing offense looked much more effective, the run game finally was able to show some signs of life (more on that later), and the team was able to score 30-plus points because of it. The hope remains that Houston can continue to keep building on that offensive success moving forward.
Not exactly the greatest showing for Texans veteran safety Reed Blankenship, who saw some of his similar errors seen from the first few weeks rear their ugly head once again: blown coverages, missed tackles, even being a key component allowing Bhayshul Tuten to score one of his two total touchdowns on the day. Blankenship also wound up leaving the game in the first half with an apparent head injury. We'll learn more about his status over the course of next week, but if he does miss any time, M.J. Stewart could be in line for a bigger role.
Montgomery somehow finds his way onto the losers’ list here without even traveling with the team to London. Why? Because this running game managed to look miles better without the presence of Montgomery in the running back rotation. Woody Marks led the way in the backfield with 15 carries for 56 yards, practice squad elevation Jawhar Jordan chipped in for six carries, 43 yards, and a touchdown, and now forces you to wonder: just how does Montgomery factor into this backfield moving forward?

title: 3 Texans Takeaways From Nail-Biting Win vs. Jaguars in London
full_text:
The Houston Texans pulled out a pivotal, last-second victory in their trip overseas to London for Week 6, as a game-winning 49-yard field goal from Ka'imi Fairbairn would push the Texans over their division rival Jacksonville Jaguars , 34-31, for their second win in a row.
And this game that now lifts this team to 2-4 on the year was a much-needed confidence builder for the Texans.
The offense started to click a whole lot better than we've seen in recent weeks, they're one step closer to getting back in the race to win the AFC South, and just one week away from their bye, Houston can head into that break with a really nice sense of momentum compared to where they stood this time two weeks ago.
Let's break down three of the biggest takeaways from the Texans' Week 6 international victory over the Jaguars:
Sure, C.J. Stroud did throw his first interception of the season, thanks to an impressive play on the ball from Travis Hunter. And that play was almost a game-changing shift for the Jaguars had they converted on their last offensive possession.
But outside of that one blip on the radar, the Texans quarterback had yet another impressive day for what's been a strong start to his 2026 campaign: completing 24 of his 34 throws for 312 yards and three touchdowns; two of those going to tight end Foster Moreau.
Foster Moreau is left wide open and the @HoustonTexans are on the board. HOUvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/oPPabnAEam
Stroud was also able to get his brand new target Marvin Harrison Jr. involved for a nice debut with Houston as well, peppering him with four targets for three receptions and 34 yards. He was one of eight pass-catcher that the Texans' signal caller targeted multiple times throughout the day.
So Stroud was mostly composed, was able to spread the ball around well, and helped lead the way for the Texans' highest-scoring performance of the season so far. It's games like these that'll only help Stroud's value for his next contract, that he now feels overwhelmingly deserving of this offseason.
For as encouraging of a win that the Texans claimed here in London, it wasn't a performance without its errors along the way. And of any problem to emphasize from Houston's victory, it was certainly how their defense looked.
Granted, the Texans were dealing with injuries in the form of Jalen Pitre , and in certain pockets of the day, were without either Azeez Al-Shaair or Reed Blakenship. But even when factoring in those absences, there's little excuse for Houston to allow 30-plus points for now the second time this season.
The pass-rush was virtually non-existent, the Jaguars' run game popped, linebackers continuously left space open in the middle of the field in the passing game, and there were several moments across the day where tackling was a major issue in all three phases.
Bhayshul Tuten weaves his way in for the touchdown and the @Jaguars are on the board HOUvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/oBswI5s9Mr
Of course, all hope isn't lost for the Texans' defense moving forward. We know the type of elite talent this group has, and when they're firing on all cylinders, there can be fireworks on that side of the ball. This weekend wasn't quite that type of day for Houston, though.
A poised end to the game it was for Ka'imi Fairbairn, who came up for a game-winning 49-yard field goal at the end, making for his 10th lead-changing field goal in the fourth quarter/overtime of his career.
Really, Fairbairn's impact and consistency for the Texans on a weekly basis can't be understated. This now makes for his fourth-straight week of going perfect on each of his field goal and extra point attempts; a perfect 12/12 on field goals––three of those coming from 50 yards or further––along with a 9/9 clip on extra points.
TEXANS WIN IT IN LONDON. Ka'imi Fairbairn nails the 49-yard field goal! pic.twitter.com/8nColRjoiY
And his final 49-yard field goal kick of the day? That's certainly his most important and most clutch of the season so far. So hats off to Fairbairn for helping the Texans get over the edge in this one, because Houston might not be at 2-4 without him.

title: Texans Lead Jaguars 17-14 at Halftime: Studs & Duds From First Half
full_text:
The Houston Texans have wrapped up their first half action over in London against the Jacksonville Jaguars , where they currently lead the way, 17-14 heading into the third quarter.
Let's do a swift breakdown of the Texans' first half of action by sorting through a batch of four studs and three duds that have taken them to a three-point edge heading into the third quarter.
It's been a strong start to the day for Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud as he's continued a pretty impressive beginning to his season. He's completed 66.6% of his passes, has remained decisive with the football, and continued to limit turnovers, and got two nice touchdown scores to Foster Moreau in the first half. Hard to be anything short of impressed here.
What a fiery start it was to the first quarter for Henry To'oTo'o, who made his first appearance back on the Texans' defense since being activated from injured reserve . So far, he's logged four total tackles, one tackle for loss, and a pass break-up. Considering Azeez Al-Shaair went to the locker room in the first half to be evaluated for a concussion, his responsibilities will be further heightened in the second.
It took the Texans' ball-hawking safety six weeks before he was able to finally land his first forced turnover of the season, but he finally managed to make it happen here thanks to an interception on Trevor Lawrence in the red zone. And that pick was quite the momentum shifter. Without it, the Texans could easily be down two scores entering the half. But they've now got a bit more optimism to bank on.
You can't talk about the Texans' first half without mentioning veteran tight end Foster Moreau. He's hauled in not one, but two touchdowns in the red zone––with the second of those happening in the final moments of the second half to take Houston into the second half with some really positive mojo.
The last time these two teams faced off against one another in Week 10 of the 2025 season, it was a game dictated by the Texans' power off the edge. However, this game has been quite the opposite thus far. The Jaguars have allowed zero sacks on Lawrence through the first half, and it's a large part of why their offense has been able to consistently move the chains from the jump.
Harrison Jr. did make a nice play in the second half on his first target of the game, where Stroud found him for a 14-yard in-route that eventually led to putting three points on the board. Since that play, though, he's remained a bit of a non-factor. Harrison Jr. got zero snaps throughout the entire first quarter, and has two targets as a whole. A little head-scratching, to say the least .
This hasn't been the best showing for the Texans' offseason addition Reed Blankenship. He had a blown coverage on the first defensive play of the game, and added on top of that error with a missed tackle on Bhayshul Tuten's second touchdown of the half. Something to monitor on Blankenship, though: he did leave the game in the second quarter via cart with an apparent injury. If he doesn't return, expect M.J. Stewart to be the one filling his role at strong safety.

title: Texans Announce Inactive List vs. Jaguars With One Big Surprise
full_text:
The Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars have revealed their list of inactives right ahead of their Week 6 action in London .
And for the Texans in particular, they've ruled out a select seven players for their international action. One of those names not suiting up for Houston is also a bit more of a surprise than the others.
Let's break everything down for both the Texans and the Jaguars with kickoff right around the corner.
S Jalen Pitre RB David Montgomery DE Sabastian Harsh OG Febechi Nwaiwu OT Braden Smith OT Nate Thomas TE Marlin Klein
The Texans will be without some key players this weekend–– with two starters in Jalen Pitre and David Montgomery being the biggest names among Houston's absences.
The good news for the Texans is that both Pitre (shoulder) and Montgomery (groin) are considered week-to-week with their respective injuries. So there's a chance that one or both are able to return in Week 7 against the New York Giants. For this one, though, both opted to stay at home for the team's trip overseas.
Perhaps the biggest surprise among all of the Texans' inactives is their offensive tackle Braden Smith, who was finally elevated from injured reserve this week after missing the first five games on the schedule with a foot injury.
Even as Smith is now off the injury report, though, he won't be making his debut with Houston just yet. Whether it be because the Texans don't feel he's ready to suit up for an in-game appearance, or for another reason, he'll have to wait until that Giants matchup for his next opportunity.
Without Smith, Trent Brown will continue to start as the Texans' right tackle opposite of Aireontae Ersery, likely with Blake Fisher operating as the backup swing tackle.
Beyond those absences, the Texans will continue to do without a couple of their draft picks from this offseason in offensive guard Febechi Nwaiwu, along with their second-round tight end, Marlin Klein . This now marks Klein's third-straight healthy scratch.
CB Montaric Brown WR CJ Williams S Jalen Huskey CB Jaylon Jones LS Ross Matiscik DE Wesley Williams DT Albert Regis

Against a challenging matchup like the Texans' defensive line, though, the Jaguars offensive line won't have anything coming their way throughout the contest.
Kickoff between the Texans and Jaguars lands at 8:30 a.m. CT in Wembley Stadium, where the Texans will hope to keep their momentum flowing from last week with a second straight win.

title: 3 Bold Texans Predictions Ahead of London Showdown vs. Jaguars
full_text:
The Houston Texans' Week 6 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars is right around the corner, marking the first of two meetings for these AFC South rivals for their 2026 campaign.
And for any divisional contest, there's due to be some surprises in store. Especially in the case of this particular game between the Texans and Jaguars that'll take place across the pond in London ––marking the first time Houston has taken a trip overseas in 2019.
We've seen some crazy international games around the NFL this season. This one could be no different. And with that in mind, it feels only right to outline a few bold predictions on how wild things could get between these two talented rosters this weekend.
So, let's break down a batch of three bold predictions for how the Texans' Week 6 overseas action could go:
The last time these two teams faced off against one another, it came in Week 10 of the 2025 season when Danielle Hunter exploded for a career game : he had five total tackles, 3.5 sacks, and forced a fumble en route to one of the Texans' most exciting wins of last year.
Expecting those same numbers in this game less than a year later would certainly be a steep bar for Hunter to hit. He's only recorded 3.5 sacks one other time throughout his 12-year NFL career. But there is a good chance the Texans' veteran edge rusher can still have a pretty productive day if not to those same heights.
The Jaguars will be without Anton Harrison, their primary left tackle, who would be assigned to Hunter for most of the day. Instead, those starting duties will be in the hands of backup Walker Little, who was also starting on the outside of Jacksonville's line in the Texans' Week 10 victory from last year.
So you can connect the dots pretty easily on how Hunter could find his way to another strong performance this weekend. Three-plus sacks would be a steep projection, but two feels wildly possible.
One impressive piece of C.J. Stroud's strong start to his fourth season has been how well he's taken care of the football. He did have two fumbles in his first game of the year against the Buffalo Bills , though he hasn't thrown a single interception in each of the five games he and the Texans have played.
But it feels like if there was a game for Stroud to see that streak end, this matchup in London would be the one to do it. Not only are international games like this known to be on the sloppier side, but this Jaguars defense is a forced to be reckoned with.
Only two teams in the NFL entered Week 6 having more interceptions than the Jaguars: that's the Green Bay Packers and the reigning world champion Seattle Seahawks. Not many have been better equipped with ball-hawks than Jacksonville.
If Stroud's no-interception streak finally came to a close in this one, what a ride it's been.
Maybe it's a little too bullish to expect Marvin Harrison Jr. can hit paydirt this early into his Texans tenure . DeMeco Ryans has already made it clear earlier in the week that while their new wide receiver will be active and on the field for Week 6 in London, it might not result in him getting a super heavy share of the offensive snaps.
But even if Harrison Jr. isn't on the field for more than 20 or so snaps, it's hard to imagine the Texans won't try to get him involved early for the plays he is on the field for.
He can build early rapport with his college quarterback, C.J. Stroud , get his feet wet with the plays he's studied in practice this week, while also taking the attention away from Nico Collins, who's had a pretty strong last three games he's been healthy for.
Scoring a touchdown in game number one with Houston is a great way to start off in his new situation on a high note. And if this game turns out to be a success for Harrison Jr., that's a pretty stellar sign for what's ahead as he'll only get more and more involved as the season progresses.

title: Texans Announce Multiple Roster Moves Before Week 6 vs. Jaguars
full_text:
The Houston Texans have made a handful of roster moves right on the cusp of their Week 6 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars .
In all, the Texans have elevated a pair of names from the practice squad, cut a couple of players from the back-end of their depth chart, as well as activate one key name that's been left on injured reserve from the past four weeks.
Let's break down everything the Texans did to tweak their roster before their London battle against their AFC South rival, the Jaguars:
It's another week of the Texans opting to elevate Bryce Hall onto their gameday roster. Hall was elevated for Houston's Week 5 matchup against the Tennessee Titans, where he played in seven total special teams snaps, recording one solo tackle. This means the Texans have used two of their practice squad elevations on Hall through just six weeks of the regular season. Houston has just one more elevation at their disposal for Hall until they'll be forced to bring him onto a traditional 53-man roster spot.
Third-year running back Jawhar Jordan will be making his first regular-season appearance for the Texans this season as a practice squad elevation. The decision likely comes due to the absence of David Montgomery in Houston's backfield, who suffered a groin injury in Week 5 vs. the Titans. Jordan was in a relatively similar situation late last season as a practice squad elevation. He was activated in Week 15 vs. the Arizona Cardinals when this backfield was short-handed, putting together 15 carries for 101 total yards. Perhaps this one offers another breakout opportunity for him.
The Texans' final selection of the 2026 NFL Draft at pick 243 in the seventh round, Fisher has been cut from Houston's 53-man roster after having been active in three of the team's first five regular-season games. Fisher was brought into Week 1 as a part of the Texans' 53-man roster cut, and would hang onto his spot for the first five weeks as a depth piece that helped contribute in the midst of some injuries to the linebacker position. Now that said unit is much healthier, Houston has let go of their seventh-round rookie.
Another piece of the Texans' defense that was brought onto the 53-man roster from Week 1, undrafted defensive back Collin Wright was a standout in training camp and preseason back in August , yet wasn't able to keep up that momentum much in the regular season. In his time with the Texans, Wright played just 11 special teams snaps, all coming against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 4.
The Texans will finally be getting back their starting weak-side linebacker, Henry To’oTo’o, in Week 5, after he had missed the last four weeks of the season with a shoulder injury suffered in Houston's season opener against the Buffalo Bills. To'oTo'o has been a weekly starter for the Texans' front seven across the past two seasons, combining for 200 total tackles, seven passes defended and four sacks since 2024.

title: Texans Brushing Aside One Concern About Marvin Harrison Jr.'s Game
full_text:
The Houston Texans made a bit of a bold swing around this time last week when they made a move for wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals; a deal that led to them giving up a second and seventh-round pick in exchange for the No. 4 selection in the 2024 NFL Draft.
Harrison Jr., while one of the more promising incoming wide receiver prospects in recent memory, hasn't quite caught onto the potential he was advertised to have. His rookie year was encouraging as he recorded over 800 receiving yards, but since then, his stock has seemingly gone anywhere but up.
And one of the concerns that many have pointed out surrounding Harrison Jr. and his declining play is his lackluster effort shown up from his last couple of years in Arizona.
Whether it be not fully running routes when not targeted , being a poor blocker, or another reason, it's led to conversation of whether or not Harrison Jr.'s really playing with the highest intensity and effort that he did during college, or even during his first year pro.
Yet, based on some recent intel, no matter what that effort has looked like in Arizona, the Texans seem to have no concerns about that aspect of his game moving forward.
The Athletic 's Jonathan Jones had a recent report describing that not only are the Texans aware of Harrison Jr.'s widely discussed effort––or lack thereof––but that aspect of his game has seemingly not come with him to Houston.
"The Texans are aware of what Harrison's tape in Arizona looked like. And though he's been with the team for less than a week, there have been no signs within the organization that the lack of effort seen on tape has traveled with him to Houston," Jones wrote.
"We're hoping that because of the dynamic with his college quarterback and a change of scenery, it will unlock him,' one team source says."
That heightened confidence in Harrison Jr.'s determination hasn't just been made clear from anonymous sources either.
Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans spoke about his new receiver and how he was adjusting to Houston's offense earlier in the week, where a lack of effort didn't seem to be showing whatsoever.
"Getting a player caught up, it isn't hard when the player is attentive and he's locked in on getting the details down. So Marvin's first night here, he was with our assistant wide receiver coach, Coach Tiquan [Underwood], and they were grinding," Ryans said of how Harrison Jr. is adjusting.
Harrison Jr. himself isn't oblivious to the noise either. Those qualms about his motor were addressed during his opening presser after his first practice with the Texans this Wednesday, and he didn't seem too concerned.
"I mean, everybody has their own opinions," Harrison Jr. said. "That's really the best way I can put that. Everybody has their own opinions and what they're going to gather from information. I know who I am as a player. I know who I am as a person. However people want to label me or think of me, that's their opinion."
#Texans WR Marvin Harrison Jr.  on viral clips citing apparent his lack of effort on routes pic.twitter.com/xY1Kf1Vn5D
At least right off the bat in Week 6 against the Jacksonville Jaguars, Harrison Jr.'s involvement in the Texans offense could be a bit limited .
After all, he's had less than a week to adjust to his new team with a whole new system and set of plays, likely only putting him on the field for a select number of snaps this weekend.
However, as Harrison Jr. gets more time with a new, refreshing situation in Houston, and back catching passes from his old college quarterback, perhaps it's a combination of factors that can help the No. 4 pick find more success than he did in a dysfunctional Cardinals organization.
And with those changes in mind, perhaps any narratives surrounding Harrison Jr.'s effort from the past two years can see a big shift as well, and thus give this trade a good chance of becoming a home run for the Texans when all is said and done.

title: These 3 Texans Matchups Could Decide Their Week 6 Game vs. Jaguars
full_text:
The Houston Texans' Week 6 contest against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London is right around the corner.
And it's undoubtedly a massive game for the Texans to take on. Already in a 1-4 hole on the season and down three games in the AFC South to this Jaguars team, claiming a victory here would make for a huge boost in both confidence and momentum after a rocky start to the 2026 campaign.
However, for the Texans to win their Week 6 test against Jacksonville , there's a select few matchups they'll have to take advantage of for that 2-4 record to become a reality.
Let's break down three of those key matchups for the Texans that'll be worth keeping an eye on across Sunday's game, and could be the difference between a win and a loss:
The Jaguars will be forced to play this one against the Texans without their usual starting left tackle, Anton Harrison, who's just been placed on injured reserve following the knee injury he suffered last weekend against the Philadelphia Eagles.
That means two things. For one, Walker Little is due to start as the Jaguars' left tackle; an experienced backup with starting experience for Jacksonville, but not quite the talent that Harrison is.
Secondly, though, the road for Danielle Hunter to have a big day against the Jaguars defense might be a little bit easier going against a backup like Little as opposed to a more consistent starter in Harrison.
It was just last season these two faced off in Week 10 when Hunter had a career-day logging 3.5 sacks, paired with Little also starting upfront in that matchup. Perhaps the stage could be set for a similar performance, which would be a big boost to their chances of landing win number two on the year.
Since Nico Collins has returned to the Texans' lineup from his hamstring strain suffered earlier in the season, he's been all that Houston's offense has needed to get back on track from a rocky start.
But in this game, the Texans will have a bit of a challenge in terms of what the Jaguars' secondary brings to the table––specifically with second-year defensive back Travis Hunter, who's been more involved and more comfortable as a full-time contributor on the defense as a boundary corner.
If Collins can continue to be a strong No. 1 option for Stroud and overcome what'll be his toughest individual matchup of his 2026 campaign so far, the road to victory becomes a whole lot easier to imagine. But doing so might be a bit easier said than done.
It was tough to pick out just one of the Jaguars' top-tier defensive ends as the guy to watch in this game. So we'll just highlight both as names to keep a close eye on–– particularly as it relates to getting pressure on Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud.
The Texans' pass protection has been relatively stable through the past couple of weeks. Stroud has been taken down for two sacks a piece in both Weeks 4 and 5, and in the process, he's performed at about as good a level as we've seen throughout his career despite a 1-4 record.
However, the Jaguars' talent off the edge might be the toughest task the Texans' offensive line has seen so far this year. Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker have combined for 3.5 sacks on the year, and Jacksonville hasn't lost a game so far this year when at least one of them records 0.5 sacks in a day.
So for this scoring attack to remain consistent from start to finish, it'll rely on not only Aireontae Ersery and Trent Brown to continue holding their own in pass protection, but also for Stroud to remain composed and keep up the strong start to the season he's seen thus far.

title: Predicting Marvin Harrison Jr.’s Stat Line in Texans Debut vs. Jaguars
full_text:
The Houston Texans will be getting their first look at Marvin Harrison Jr. in their Week 6 trip to London against the Jacksonville Jaguars .
Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed earlier this week that Harrison Jr. would be making the trip overseas for this week's matchup, and would be due to play a certain number of snaps.
But how Harrison Jr.'s first game against the Jaguars could fare has the chance to go a few different directions. After all, it's a very quick turnaround for any player to make when being traded and dropped onto a new team in a week's span, and could lead to his performance in Week 6 being a bit more limited compared to how things might look a little later into the season.
So how might Harrison Jr.'s stat line look by the end of Week 6's matchup over the pond? Let's simply predict how the Texans' newest receiver could do in his official debut, and break down just how limited he could be in the offensive game plan.
DeMeco Ryans emphasized earlier this week that Harrison Jr. would be involved in the Texans' offense as soon as this weekend. However, he also made sure to note that he won't be expected to play a super high number of snaps .
"Don't expect him to come out and play all 60 snaps in the game," Ryans said on Wednesday. "But we'll make sure he gets what he needs, and make sure he's confident in what we're asking him to do."
So just how many snaps could Harrison Jr. play? One outcome that could make sense is simply putting him in the role that now-former Texans wideout Jared Wayne had been in for the first few weeks.
Jared Wayne and Marvin Harrison Jr. are vastly different talents, let's be clear. However, they are similarly big-bodied, outside receivers who can line up as a Z in several plays and situations, pairing pretty nicely next to the existing talent Houston has around the field at the position.
Last week, Wayne saw a little over 30% of the snaps on offense. He went without any offensive stats being recorded throughout, but he did see as high as seven targets back in Week 2 against the Cincinnati Bengals .
Imagine Harrison Jr. simply slotting into those same snaps; likely with a bit more involvement in terms of being targeted or being a first read, but maybe not on the field for an excessive amount until he's able to get a few more weeks of practice and overall reps under his belt.
A 30% snap share would likely be around the 15 to 20-snap mark. But in those limited looks, it feels likely that the Texans will involve him on a fair share of those plays––in this case, perhaps for four targets––to build up his confidence and rediscover some chemistry with his college quarterback, C.J. Stroud .
And in a best-case scenario for the Texans, maybe Harrison Jr. is able to haul in his second touchdown of the season so far. If Houston is within striking distance for a score, and there's an ideal situation for Harrison Jr. to fill into, why not start off the tenure with his new team on a good note?
So in all, a 3-43-1 stat line feels like a modest projection for Harrison Jr. in game one. It'd be a nice start for what hopes to be a long tenure in Houston, wouldn't overwhelm him with a ton of involvement, while also being paired with a ton of room to grow moving forward.
