title: Good, Not So Good From Jaguars' London Loss to Texans: Defense Lets C.J. Stroud Thrive
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars will be entering the bye week with a loss.
The Jaguars saw their three-game winning streak come to an end in Week 6, the result of a 34-31 loss to the Houston Texans in London off a walk-off field goal by their AFC South rivals. So, what were the highs and the lows of the game and what do they mean? We break it down in this week's good and not so good.
It was always clear that Travis Hunter was going to be a critical part of the Jaguars' success, and he once again proved to be worth the cost to land him. Hunter didn't have a perfect day, giving up a few catches and a few penalties, but his fourth-quarter two-way impact alone makes this a strong day for the former No. 2 pick. Had the Jaguars won that game, the big story would be about how Hunter had a generational two-way performance.
Hunter was tied for second in catches and third in receiving yards Sunday with four catches for 59 yards and a touchdown, easily his best day on offense this year. He had a 19-yard catch to set up an early Tuten touchdown and then caught three passes for 40 yards and a touchdown at the start of the fourth quarter to make it a three-point game. Add in his interception in the end -zone a few minutes later, and Sunday was a massive step in the right direction for Hunter.
Travis Hunter is the first player since Brian Dawkins in 2002 to record an INT and score a scrimmage TD in the same game 😤 https://t.co/hsOJwLOIgY pic.twitter.com/HfMwC0Q6G9
While the Texans' defense hasn't been as stellar this season as everyone predicted, they are still a stout unit that has not allowed too many passers to have big days. No quarterback had thrown more than three touchdowns against the Texans this year, while Lawrence went 24-of-41 for 306 yards, four touchdowns and one interception. Lawrence is the first quarterback to throw four touchdowns against the Texans since Sam Darnold did it in Week 3 of the 2024 season with the Minnesota Vikings ... 756 days ago. He and Darnold are the only quarterbacks to do it during the DeMeco Ryans era.
Lawrence's red-zone pick was obviously a bad play, but Lawrence is not within the top-10 reasons the Jaguars lost this game. Lawrence nearly had the Jaguars complete a stellar comeback after the Texans went up two scores, and this was a strong game for his continued momentum. Lawrence is improving week in and week out, and this week was no different.
The Jaguars had a little thunder and lightning going on in the running back room on Sunday. Bhayshul Tuten had his first-ever two-touchdown game with two touchdown catches, catching four passes for 39 yards. He was not quite as good on the ground, but the Jaguars were still able to establish the run whenever they needed to with Chris Rodriguez toting the rock 11 times for 55 yards. It is the first time this season Rodriguez has led the Jaguars in rushing, and he certainly set a physical tone.
The Jaguars are at their best on offense when they are balanced and able to keep defenses on their heels in terms of the run/pass guessing game. When both running backs are making plays like they did on Sunday, it opens up a lot of things for Liam Coen on the play-call sheet, and should make the Jaguars an even better team as the season goes on.
I have other thoughts on the Jaguars' 60-yard field goal by Cam Little with 1:55 left in the game, but first ... what a kick by Little. Making big kick after big kick, both in terms of distances and the moments in which he makes them, has made Little one of the best kickers in the NFL. He has always been talented, and now he is starting to become more consistent each week, giving the Jaguars a true special teams weapon.
Liam Coen is one of the best head coaches in the NFL, but he also has had a few game management blunders in the last few weeks. I understood why he punted the ball on an early fourth-down, but the three points he didn't take in the first-half came back to bite him. There is a time and place to go for it on fourth down, and I am not sure the Jaguars' passing game had yet gotten into a groove at that point to justify turning down likely three points.
Then there was the Little field goal at the end of the game. That entire process felt off to me, and here is why: just because Little can make the field goal, doesn't mean the Jaguars should kick it. It felt, to me, like the decision to have Little kick it was more so a show of confidence in the defense to get a stop than it felt like Coen playing for overtime. The issue is that just because the defense had been really good in the previous five games doesn't mean they had it today.
The odds of the Jaguars winning that game with a turnover on downs was zero. The odds of winning it after Little's kick weren't much higher. The only way for the Jaguars to win that game would have been to go for it. Add in not running the ball on any of the six plays the Jaguars ran that drive, and it was some odd game management.
It feels like you can't point the finger for the Jaguars' defensive issues at any one person or position group, which seems concerning. The Jaguars were giving up explosive plays and having coverage busts from the first drives of the game, and it felt like the entire secondary turn different turns making mistakes in coverage, and the linebackers were not much better.
The Jaguars' pass-rush did not seem to sniff Stroud, even when they blitzed. The Jaguars had two quarterback hits and no sacks in a game that felt a lot like the Denver game. The turf wasn't good for pass-rushers, of course, but that doesn't change the fact that the Jaguars got nothing from the unit when they needed them most.
The Jaguars can't blame the refs for all of their penalty woes. The Jaguars have made several penalties on their own entirely that are nobody's fault but their own. But with that in mind, there were several woeful calls that went one way and directly impacted ghe game, leading arguably to a 14-point swing. Had officials swallowed their whistles a few times, this games goes much, much differently. The calls did not seem to even be close, either, especially the Brenton Strange holding call that took a Bhayshul Tuten touchdown off the board.
#Jaguars RB Bhayshul Tuten just lost a TD because the refs called Brenton Strange for holding on a play he didn't hold. 🤦‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/BwsmqHsEtO
The NFL's officials have been judged and challenged more at the start of this season than any other in recent memory, and it isn't hard to see why with weeks like the Jaguars have had. The Jaguars get in their own way enough, it hardly helps for the officials to get in their way with a number of phantom calls at significant moments.
The Jaguars have been their own worst enemy several times throughout their 4-2 start, but they have managed to hide the issue with wins. That didn't happen on Sunday, though, with the Jaguars once again getting in their own way countless times. From the red-zone pick to the too many players on the field penalty to a host of other mistakes, the Jaguars once again made things harder on themselves than they had to at any point.
For the Jaguars to win big games, they will have to clean up the small mistakes that keep coming up in the big moments. It is because of those mistakes that they are 4-2 instead of 5-1 and even 6-0. The Jaguars knew they would have to play a clean game to get a tough AFC South win on the road in London, but they got anything but.

title: 8 Instant Observations From Jaguars' Shootout Loss to Texans: Travis Hunter's Day Wasted
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars got into a shootout on Sunday, and they came out with a loss.
The Jaguars lost 34-31 to the Houston Texans in Week 6 after a 49-yard field goal from Texans kicker Ka'imi Fairbairn as time expired, and the Jaguars have now dropped down to 4-2. So, what did we see from the Jaguars in the close loss? We break it down below.
The Jaguars had their worst defensive performance of the year on Sunday, and it came at the worst time. It might be time to consider whether the Jaguars simply have issues with Nick Caley and his scheme considering the Jaguars have now allowed big offensive days from the Texans' offense in back-to-back games, including one time to Davis Mills. I saw this coming in a sense considering I predicted a shootout , but it didn't happen exactly how I thought it would.
The Texans had much more rushing success against the Jaguars than I expected them to have in really any scenario. The passing game is ultimately what killed the Jaguars since C.J. Stroud went 24-of-32 for 312  yards and three touchdowns, but the Jaguars also gave up a 25-yard rushing touchdown and allowed the Texans to rush 25 times for 114 yards with a 4.6 average. The Jaguars can't afford to allow explosive plays at a high clip and not shut-down the run.
The Jaguars have had some slow starts in recent weeks, and it has been self-inflicted nearly every time. Houston has a good defense, but the Jaguars moved the ball to start the game ... until they started dropping it. The Jaguars' second play from scrimmage was snapped at the Texans' 46 thanks a to a 24-yard catch by Brenton Strange on the first play, but the Jaguars then saw Brian Thomas Jr. drop an easy 2nd-and-7 target that would have been a clear first down in field goal territory. The Jaguars would end up punting.
Then on the second drive, the Jaguars were able to use the field position game to start the ball at their own 45 and move it to the a 2nd-and-3 from the Texans' 37. What should have been an easy conversion was instead followed by three consecutive incompletions to Parker Washington, with at least one drop and one other rep that was iffy. Lawrence then nearly threw an incompletion on fourth-down, turning the ball over and setting the Texans up with a short field.
Then there was the Tuten touchdown. The Jaguars had a great drive set up by the running game that saw Bhayshul Tuten score from three yards out before Brenton Strange was hit with a holding call, negating the score and giving the Jaguars 2nd-and-Goal from the 13. It wasn't a good call, but it was another example of the Jaguars' offense going backward as a result of penalties. Then Lawrence threw an interception to end the drive and take away points.
I do not think there is reason to fault Liam Coen much with not taking the points a week ago against the Eagles. Coen went for it on fourth-down twice near the goal-line last week instead of kicking field goals and got zero points out of it, but that had a lot more to do with the Jaguars not having a long-snapper than anything else. With that said, Coen had a long-snapper this time and still opted to go for it on fourth-down instead of getting three points from Cam Little, and it ended up costing the Jaguars.
Facing 4th-and-3 from the Texans' 37, Coen opted for a pass play instead of the field goal and saw the play result in an incompletion. Five plays later, the Texans finished a touchdown drive that saw them start with the ball on their own 38, giving them a 7-0 lead directly because of Coen's decision. There are of course times when it makes sense to for it, but early in a divisonal game should have been a field goal and an early 3-0 lead.
The Jaguars were feeing good on the heels of Tuten's second touchdown. The Texans had just 48 seconds with the ball before halftime, and it felt like the Jaguars were about to enter halftime with a much-needed lead. The Texans quickly ruined those good feelings with a bomb from C.J. Stroud to Jaylin Noel for 50 yards to put the ball on the Jaguars' 13, putting the Texans in the red-zone and easy field goal range. Giving up three points there isn't ideal, but you can live with a 14-3 halftime lead.
Then after a Texans false start made it 1st-and-15 from the Jaguars' 18, Travis Hunter was hit with a defensive pass-interference call against Nico Collins that felt as inexcusable as the holding call on Strange earlier. A few plays later, Stroud dropped a perfect pass to Foster Moreau to give the Texans a 17-14 lead. The Jaguars were the ones who let Stroud get it to their front door, and they have nobody but themselves to blame. Speaking of ...
The Jaguars have had a lot of costly penalties this season, taking touchdowns and interceptions off the board and really keeping the Jaguars from being at their best. But the worst penalty of the 2026 season pretty easily was the 12 men on the field penalty thrown on the Jaguars on the first drive of the second-half. The Jaguars' defense held the Texas to a 3-and-out and had them setting up to punt on 4th-and-1 but ... Travis Hunter just never got off the field. He did, eventually, but it was too late and gave Houston a first-down.
Jacksonville's defense then continued to get shredded against Stroud and the Texans' passing game, with Stroud finishing off the half's opening drive with a 13-yard pass to Noel to give him his third touchdown of the game. That was a seven-point penalty by Hunter, and it happened on a play that was completely and utterly preventable.
One would think that, if the Jaguars really wanted to trade Brian Thomas Jr., they would have no issue doing so. He is clearly set to be the most valuable wide receiver that teams are set to call about with Marvin Harrison Jr. off the market, and the fact that Harrison went for such a solid package of draft picks should only make things easier for the Jaguars. With that in mind, it is tough to say that the recent performances from Thomas are alarming enough that they could start to tank his trade value.
The Jaguars saw Thomas have some serious issues in previous weeks, such as multiple drops against the Denver Broncos in Week 2. In the four games since then, Thomas has caught three passes for 25 yards and a touchdown on eight targets. He saw two targets in the first-half on Sunday, but both hit his hands in critical moments and ended up on the ground. He did not log a second-half snap after that, and it is time to wonder if they are better off benching him to preserve his trade value.
Nate Boerkircher is not going to have many games where he is just racking up the catches and is toasting secondaries, at least not as a rookie. That is not his game, and it is not the role the Jaguars need him to play this year. For the role the Jaguars need him for and drafted him for, he has done his job very well. It culminated in his first-career touchdown on a one-yard pass from Trevor Lawrence that was simply a grown-man play.
Nate Boerkircher with the INSANE one-handed touchdown catch! HOUvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/oBhAyPowx9
That play, of course, has plenty of people reminding those around the NFL that the Jaguars were absolutely killed for the Boerkircher pick. It is a reminder that draft discourse a lot of times is, well, just that. Nothing really matters until the games have been played and, so far, Boerkircher has been a good pick for the Jaguars.
What a special player that Travis Hunter is. He has already made several spectacular plays for the Jaguars this season that have put his skill set on display for all to see. Most of that has come on defense, but on Sunday Hunter got in on the offense too. He had a 19-yard catch in the first-half to set the Jaguars up for a touchdown, but he did much more than that at the start of the fourth-quarter with three catches for 40 yards and a seven-yard touchdown to make it a 31-28 game and give him his second-career touchdown.
On the next drive, Houston drove the ball…

title: Jaguars' Inactives for Texans Bout Include 1 Rookie Being Placed on Backburner
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars have released their official inactives list for Sunday's battle with the Houston Texans, including one notable rookie.
The Jaguars announced the following players will be inactive for their Week 6 AFC South tilt with the Texans: cornerback Montaric Brown, wide receiver CJ Williams, safety Jalen Huskey, cornerback Jaylon Jones, long snapper Ross Matiscik, defensive end Wesley Williams, and defensive tackle Albert Regis.
The Jaguars have more than a few rookies inactive once again this week with CJ Williams inactive every week but Week 1, Regis inactive last week, and Wesley Williams inactive every game this season. But the true notable name here is Huskey, who had been inactive for the first month of the season before getting his first action last week against the Philadelphia Eagles.
Huskey, of course, was largely active because safeties Caleb Ransaw (placed on injured reserve) and Eric Murray missed the Eagles game. Murray is officially back in the lineup for the Jaguars against his former team on Sunday, though, which naturally moves Huskey a spot down the depth chart. But Huskey now does not even get a game day nod, with the Jaguars making the No. 100 pick a healthy scratch in favor of safety Kaevon Merriweather, who was previously on the team's practice squad.
The fact that the Jaguars have had safeties miss several games over the last two weeks but have been unwilling to put Huskey on the field indicates that this is a complete and total red-shirt season for him. He was always expected to be depth at best as a rookie considering the other safeties in the room, but injuries at the position led to the assumption that he'd see some real snaps.
That didn't happen last week against the Eagles, with Rayuan Lane getting the start next to Antonio Johnson and Merriweather serving as the team's No. 3 safety. Huskey did not log a defensive snap and played a handful of special teams snaps. A week later, with Ransaw still out, Huskey is now inactive. Huskey is a selection for the future, and he now seems like someone to watch in 2027.
Three of the Jaguars' first five draft picks are healthy scratches in third-rounders Huskey and Regis and fourth-rounder Williams, with the draft picks that are set to play instead being second-rounder Nate Boerkircher, third-round guard Emmanuel Pregnon, fifth-round tight end Tanner Koziol, and sixth-round wide receiver Josh Cameron.
The Jaguars will be without Brown for the second time in three weeks at cornerback, which means they are set to lean on Travis Hunter, Jourdan Lewis and Jarrian Jones. Brown is out with a hamstring injury that limited him to six snaps last week against the Eagles.

title: 3 Reasons the Jaguars Will Beat the Texans in Week 6
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars just have a few more hours to wait.
The Jaguars are set to clash with the Houston Texans in London in Week 6 in a critical early-season AFC South battle, a matchup that has been anticipated since the Jaguars' loss to London in Week 10 last season.
We have discussed the hurdles and challenges the Jaguars have to clea r ahead of the Texans matchup. Now, we will discuss why the Jaguars will topple their AFC South rival and leave London with their third fourth win in a row.
While the Texans have a talented quarterback in their own right in C.J. Stroud, the Jaguars have the quarterback advantage once again entering Sunday. Trevor Lawrence is, for my money, playing the best football of his career this season. His decision-making and accuracy are improved from even last year's hot streak when he was an MVP finalist, and he is making a few jaw-dropping touchdowns every single game.
With the way Lawrence is playing right now, I do not think even the talented Texans' defense is going to derail him. 4-of-5 foes the Jaguars have played this season have a defense that ranks in the top-half of the league in EPA/Play, which means he has played some solid units this year and has still impressed weekly. Lawrence will be the difference-maker for the Jaguars entering the first battle with the Texans in 2026.
I think the Jaguars will have their focus right entering the week. The Jaguars are a team that has taken on the personality of head coach Liam Coen and, more often than not, the Jaguars have entered each week ready to play. The Jaguars have rarely been out-coached or out-hustled, which goes a long way in rivalry games that are already about to go down to the wire to begin with. Add in the natural stakes of a battle with the Texans, and I think the Jaguars will have the right mindset to not disappoint.
Now, one could use this argument every week to try to project the Jaguars to go 17-0 and win every single game ... but the difference is these are the Texans. The Jaguars clearly firmly remember last year's failure in Houston. They also clearly know that, above all else, the Texans are the team in the AFC South that has constantly been linked to the race for first-place alongside Jacksonville. This is a big game and big moment for the franchise, and I do not believe they will fail to meet it.
The Jaguars do a great job every single week of making teams one-dimensional, and the last two weeks alone have seen it happen in a big way as the Jaguars have held both foes to just 17 points. Against the Cincinnati Bengals and Philadelphia Eagles, the Jaguars saw 28 rushes and 94 passes. Those carries went for just 37 yards, an average of 1.32 yards. Teams have barely tried to run the ball on the Jaguars lately, instead turning to the passing game in a big way.
With the Texans' running game in complete shambles, the Jaguars should have little issue putting this game completely in C.J. Stroud's hands. Stroud has played well this season, but the Texans do not want to turn this game intro a dropback-heavy affair with the state of their offensive line, but that is exactly where this seems headed.

title: 3 Biggest Jaguars Concerns Entering Texans Bout: The Will Anderson Problem
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars need no explanation when it comes to the Houston Texans and what kind of challenge they pose.
The Texans and Jaguars have close battles year in and year out, and this year is slated to be no different. Even with Houston sitting three games behind the Jaguars in the AFC South at 1-4, the Jaguars can not afford to overlook their biggest rival in the division as they open their slate of AFC South games in Week 6 in London.
So, what are the biggest reasons for concern the Jaguars should have entering their Week 6 battle with the Texans? We break it down below.
Well, this one is clear. Not only do the Jaguars have to face All-World defensive end Will Anderson Jr. and the NFL's best No. 2 edge rusher Danielle Hunter on Sunday, but they have to do it without left tackle Anton Harrison, who is normally at his very best against the Texans. Anderson is the leading candidate in the NFL right now for Defensive Player of the Year, and the Jaguars will have to ensure somehow that Anderson doesn't make the Jaguars the next offense to fall victim to his pass-rush ability.
The Jaguars have a lot of trust in Walker Little, and they will of course ensure they utilize chips and moving pockets to help the pass-protection. But this is the same plan most teams have for Anderson, and it hasn't made him any less productive. Anderson is playing like the best pass-rusher in football right now, and he currently stands as the biggest hurdle in the Jaguars' way in Week 6. If the Jaguars are going to win this game, it will have to be by finding a way to slow Anderson down, even for just a bit.
The Jaguars' defense has perhaps its biggest challenge of the season thus far on hand with CJ Stroud in Week 6. Stroud has arguably played the best football of his career in 2026, and it has let him not making many mistakes at all with the ball. A big reason for this is due to his effectiveness in the quick game, where his processing and decisiveness have stood out in a big way throughout the season.
According to NextGenStats, "Stroud has completed 81.7% of his quick throws (under 2.5 seconds) this season, the highest rate among qualified passers. Stroud has averaged 8.4 yards per attempt on quick throws this season, the fourth-most, and has produced an explosive play on 16.9% of them, the third-highest rate." The entire weakness of the Jaguars' scheme and defensive approach is centered around their willingness to allow quick passes, which might play exactly into the Texans' hands.
The Jaguars simply have not been able to slow down Nico Collins over the last several years. Collins is one of the best receivers in football and routinely makes even the best defenses look silly for attempting to stop him, but he has produced gaudy numbers over the Jaguars for years that reflect just how big of a challenge he is, and this year's matchup is no different.
The Jaguars do have their cornerbacks playing good football in Travis Hunter and Jarrian Jones, but they have not faced a test like Collins since those limited snaps against Ja'Marr Chase two weeks ago. If Hunter and Jones allow one too many big plays to Collins, it could make all of the difference in what is bound to be a tight game in the fourth quarter. The Jaguars will need the duo's best performances of the season on Sunday.

title: 3 Jaguars X-Factors vs. the Texans in Week 5: Bhayshul Tuten Can Be the Difference
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- For the Jacksonville Jaguars to continue to stack up the wins during their AFC South race, it will take quite the effort in Week 6.
The Jaguars are set to clash with the Houston Texans in London on Sunday, and it will take high-level efforts from more than a few players to give the Jaguars the edge over their bitter rivals.
So, which Jaguars could prove to be difference-makers once the ball is kicked off in London? We break it down below.
A lot of the talk this week has been around the Jaguars' offensive tackles and their matchups with Texans star pass-rushers Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter, and for obvious reasons. But I think the Jaguars' lineman who could prove to perhaps be even more vital to the Jaguars' ability to pick up the win is right guard Ezra Cleveland, and there are a few different reasons why he could prove to be so vital along with the rest of the Jaguars' interior offensive line.
The Texans have sent four or fewer pass rushers on 78.5% of opponent dropbacks this season, the third-highest rate in the NFL, and have recorded 14 sacks with four or fewer rushers, the most. This means they are set to rely on their front four to get pressure, starting with Anderson and Hunter. But the Jaguars can offer chip help for those two and move the pocket away from them. They can't do the same for the interior, with Cleveland and the rest of the Jaguars' interior linemen set to face Sheldon Rankins (2 sacks, 10.3% pressure rate) and Logan Hall (1 sack, 11.4%). These are two quality rushers, and it will be up to Cleveland to make sure they do not wreck the game.
The Texans are a physical defense that doesn't just play that way in the front-seven. They are going to challenge wide receivers at the line of scrimmage, during the route, and at the catch-point, and it will take a physical brand of football for the Jaguars' pass-catchers to produce. The Texans' secondary has given up a lot of explosive plays, but this doesn't mean they are about to play a soft game that allows the Jaguars to just find space in the backend.
That is why the Jaguars will need Jakobi Meyers in a big way. Derek Stingley Jr. will likely be on Brian Thomas Jr., while the Texans have a terrific plan for stopping tight ends each week. This leaves Parker Washington in the slot and Meyers on the outside. I think the Texans put a good bit of resources into stopping Washington, which leads to the Jaguars placing a clear emphasis on Meyers winning his one-on-ones on the outside. Meyers is as tough and physical of a receiver as they come, and his ability to match the Texans' energy will be key.
We are going with an offensive player for the third time, but for good reason. If the Jaguars are going to beat the Texans, they can not afford to continue to let themselves get into second- and third-and-longs like they have in recent weeks. That is just asking for Anderson and Hunter to wreck the Jaguars' passing game, and the key to slowing them down might come down to Tuten above all else at the end of the day.
"Not a world you want to live in by any means. It puts a lot more pressure on the O-line, puts a lot more pressure on the quarterback, and especially against this defense, we cannot live in that world," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Friday about early-down success. "You just look at teams that have had success against Houston, specifically, have been at least on schedule and second-and-seven we can live with. Second-and-10, too often, not a lot of fun.”
The Jaguars have shown an increased confidence in Tuten each week, and now it will be largely up to him and the Jaguars' running game to ensure Trevor Lawrence and the passing attack can be effective. If Tuten can't get going, it might end being a long day.

title: Patrick Mahomes Explains Chiefs’ Inconsistent Offensive Execution in Win Over Chargers
full_text:
The Chiefs were in command for the entirety of their 22-6 win over the Chargers tonight, but Patrick Mahomes would be the first person to tell you Kansas City left some points on the board.
It wasn't exactly a vintage outing by the superstar quarterback's standards, as Mahomes didn't throw a touchdown for the first time this season and tossed a red-zone interception in the second quarter. The Chargers' anemic offense couldn't capitalize on the miscue, but Mahomes knows that won't always be the case against better opponents. The three-time Super Bowl MVP took responsibility for the interception during his postgame press conference and explained what he saw before the throw. It was an awkward in-between decision, as he was partially trying to throw the ball away while also giving his intended target, Andrew Armstrong, a chance to make a play.
"It happened faster than I expected it, so instead of just staying with it and throwing it to the end zone, I tried scrambling and did what you're not supposed to do. I was trying to throw it away but trying to give him a chance..You just can't do that, especially with how our defense was playing," Mahomes said.
Cam Hart picks off Mahomes in the end zone ‼️ LACvsKC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/zWLXiWFXZb
There were also a handful of stalled possessions, including a goal-line sequence where KC ran Kenneth Walker up the middle four straight times and came away empty-handed. The Chiefs also had multiple drives fizzle out after halftime, making execution a major talking point for Mahomes after the game.
"Missing the field goal and stuff like that, you got to execute at a higher level in the second half like we did in the first half," Mahomes stated. "That's stuff we have got to continue to work... For me, it's just about how can we be consistent for an entire game and not have those droughts, a quarter here and there where we're not playing to our standard." When asked what the offense needs to clean up to become more consistent, Mahomes pointed to the little things and specifically mentioned the fourth-and-one stop. It marked the third consecutive week Kansas City was stuffed on fourth-and-short with Walker pounding it up the gut.
"Little things here and there," he continued. If one guy makes a mistake in a moment and that just ruins the drive. Obviously, you want to be able to punch it in on that fourth-and-one at the goal line. That's a big one."
Still, Mahomes isn't going to dwell on a few missed chances after a 16-point victory. He reflected on his devastating injury last season and the grueling recovery from a torn ACL , explaining how the experience has changed his perspective and allowed him to enjoy playing football even more.
"Last year, to me, put football in perspective," Mahomes said. "We have played in so many Super Bowls, and especially those last few, we didn't play our best football in the regular season and just turned it on in the playoffs. Even last year, when stuff wasn't going right, I thought we were going to figure it out. Having to go through that rehab process and not play football, it's really made me enjoy the process of it. I try to have fun out there and enjoy the wins, because you never know when it's going to be your last one."
The Chiefs will head to Seattle next Sunday night for a much tougher test against a top-ranked Seahawks defense. That matchup should provide a better gauge of where Kansas City's offense stands, especially after Mahomes and Eric Bieniemy spend the upcoming week identifying the little things that need to be cleaned up.

title: Andy Reid Drops Chiefs Injury Updates on Jaylon Moore, Travis Kelce After Week 6 Win
full_text:
Despite being shorthanded, the Kansas City Chiefs found multiple ways to take down the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday and came away with a 22-6 victory that didn't feel as dominant as it truly was at times. The club did see some players go down with injuries in Week 6, although most of them escaped the outing without anything too significant.
The offensive side of the ball, in particular, was already missing talent and dealt with additional adversity throughout the afternoon and into the evening. Speaking to the media after the final whistle, head coach Andy Reid provided his usual injury roundup.
The only injury that forced someone out of the game long-term was to right tackle Jaylon Moore. Reid confirmed it's a concussion for his first-string lineman, also dishing out context for tight end Travis Kelce, wide receiver Jalen Royals and left guard Kingsley Suamataia.
"As far as the injuries go, Jaylon Moore has a concussion," Reid said. "That's the one that probably stands out the most there. Kelce tweaked his ankle there; he continued to play. He might be a little sore tomorrow, but he did a nice job tonight. The rest of that, everybody worked. Royals went to be checked for a concussion, but he was good there. And then Kingsley, he got kicked in the calf, but he should be OK."
The Moore news shouldn't come as too much of a surprise. Kansas City acknowledged via social media that he was in concussion protocol during the game, then downgraded him to out less than an hour later. At the time of his departure, according to Pro Football Focus , he'd played 31 snaps and been credited with a pair of pressures and one quarterback hit.
In Moore's place, Joshua Ezeudu finished out the game. Ezeudu, a former New York Giants draft pick, primarily had experience playing on the left side of the offensive line but held his own given the circumstances. The 27-year-old was acquired via trade prior to August's mandatory roster cutdown deadline.
Kelce, the biggest name who got dinged on Sunday for KC, sustained an ankle injury in the first quarter when his foot bent at an awkward angle on a tackle. He received an initial sideline examination and tape job with his shoe off before coming back into the game, then getting his foot/ankle spatted and finishing the tilt. Kelce split time with fellow tight end Noah Gray; each pass catcher had 53 receiving yards.
Suamataia appeared to be in severe pain and discomfort in the second half of Sunday's win, but he ultimately returned to the contest and finished with PFF 's highest preliminary pass block grade for anyone on the roster.
For a team that was down left tackle Josh Simmons ( back ) and wideout Rashee Rice ( hamstring ) before kickoff even happened, this is far from the worst case for the Chiefs. Moore's progress in return-to-play protocol will be worth monitoring this week.

title: 10 Instant Observations From the Chiefs’ Commanding Week 6 Victory Over Chargers
full_text:
It wasn't particularly pretty by either team, but the Kansas City Chiefs emerged victorious tonight in a 22-6 triumph over the winless Los Angeles Chargers . Despite special teams miscues and multiple turnovers, KC pulled away late as its defense clamped down. The Chiefs picked up right where they left off from their bye week and now sit atop the AFC West with a 1.5-game lead over the second-place Broncos. Here are 10 instant observations we gathered from the win.
This was a trivial moment in what was otherwise an impressive win, but the Chiefs have now been stuffed on fourth-and-short in three straight weeks with a Kenneth Walker run up the middle. It happened on a fourth-and-one opportunity against the Dolphins, again on the opening drive against the Raiders when Kansas City turned it over on downs, and once more today when the Chargers stopped Walker at the goal line in the third quarter.
Walker mentioned earlier this week that he and the coordinators were looking to correct this issue, but it nearly proved costly again. There has to be more creativity in those situations than simply handing it off to Walker and hoping the offensive line can create enough separation.
There was once a point in the AFC West where it looked like Justin Herbert would be a fierce competitor to Mahomes for years to come. We can safely say those days are no more. The seventh-year signal-caller was dreadful in this showing, tossing his eighth interception of the campaign and completing just 59.5% of his passes. He was bailed out by having a pick called back due to a penalty, only to throw another one a few plays later.
Herbert finished the afternoon with 204 passing yards, no touchdowns, and a turnover. The Chargers' anemic offensive attack looks beyond the point of repair, and it's honestly quite disheartening to see how quickly Herbert has fallen from a once-promising quarterback.
Cornerback Nohl Williams was solid through the first four games, but he took his play to another level in this one. It was easily his best performance of the season and one of the strongest showings we've seen from the second-year corner. Williams finished with three solo tackles, two pass deflections, a tackle for loss, and two huge open-field stops. Despite briefly exiting the game with an injury during the opening defensive series, he'd return and put together a standout performance as the best player in Kansas City's secondary.
Tight end Travis Kelce stepped off the field to have his ankle worked on multiple times throughout the contest. That's the product of being 37 years old and lugging 250 pounds around on your lower body.
Kelce still looks as elite as ever when he's out in open space, but an ankle injury for someone his stature is worrisome. Even after his first catch of the afternoon in the second quarter, he exited the game for one play and was slow to get up.
Travis Kelce is having his ankle worked on. pic.twitter.com/IFQ9nsp2dG
His target share had significantly dipped in the two weeks before the bye — two and four, respectively — and clearly can't be relied upon as often as he once was. Other contributors must take on more responsibility, especially if Rashee Rice's absence extends beyond this week.
While the Chargers' struggles didn't allow this to matter, Mahomes had an uncharacteristically bad interception on the goal line when the Chiefs were winning 9-3 in the second quarter. Theoretically, it could have turned the tide if Los Angeles responded with a touchdown and retook the lead.
Cam Hart picks off Mahomes in the end zone ‼️ LACvsKC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/zWLXiWFXZb
He was trying to throw it away to the back of the end zone but didn't get enough air under it, and the ball fell right into Cam Hart's hands. Those kinds of blunders aren't expected from Mahomes. It was only his third pick of the year, but history would suggest he'll clean those things up heading into the next matchup.
Trying to stay as neutral as possible here, Nikko Remigio's days as the punt returner simply have to be numbered. He had a horrendous fumble on a punt return that gave the Chargers the ball near midfield in a two-score game. He had a rare invalid fair-catch signal penalty on a punt return two weeks ago and somehow found a way to make another head-scratching mistake today. At this point, it's tough to justify holding a roster spot for a special teams "guru" when guys like Brashard Smith have been far more effective in the return game this season.
The sales pitch for Nikko Remigio is that he’s trustworthy. If he’s gonna do this, what use is he?
As people online have pointed out, Remigio's entire selling point is supposed to be his reliability. If that has gone out the window, what exactly is he bringing to the table over other deserving roster candidates?
This would've been higher on the list had it resulted in points, but we witnessed one of the worst roughing calls in recent history today. Ashton Gillotte was inexplicably flagged to wipe away a Chiefs interception despite hardly making any contact with Herbert. You make the call yourself:
Roughing the passer for barely touching the quarterback. This took away a #Chiefs INT. pic.twitter.com/KxdolOrGZx
Luckily, the Chiefs were able to snag another pick off LA's mistake-prone quarterback later in the drive, but in what world is this a penalty? Gillotte clearly does his best to minimize the contact and keep Herbert out of harm's way. If a gentle bear hug is roughing the passer, the NFL might as well turn into a flag football league.
In a matchup where Xavier Worthy had to step up in the absence of Rice and Tyquan Thornton, he did just that. The speedster out of Texas followed up his best showing of the year with a seven-catch, 73-yard outing.
Worthy's best moment came at the end of the first half when he took a ball up the sideline for 19 yards to put KC in field goal range, allowing Harrison Butker to drill a 50-yarder right before the clock expired. He looks a lot more explosive than he did during the opening weeks when he was struggling , and he should continue to be a key weapon in a Chiefs offense that lacks playmakers outside of Walker.
Cue the Kenneth Walker music, because there's no way we could write one of these 10 observations articles without giving him his flowers. His dream inaugural season in Kansas City continued with two more scores on the ground today and 139 yards from scrimmage.
Walker was the first Chiefs player to find paydirt this afternoon with a 33-yard burst up the middle on a third-and-one opportunity in the opening quarter. He's now up to 665 rushing yards and eight total touchdowns on the year, keeping him on pace to make a run at AFC Offensive Player of the Year in his first year with the red and gold.
KENNETH WALKER III DOES IT AGAIN LACvsKC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/bo0Vpy9A29
The best thing to come from today is that the Chiefs' defensive line can finally exhale after snapping its ugly three-game stretch without getting to the quarterback. Ashton Gillotte broke through in the third quarter, recording KC's first sack in more than 15 quarters of football. Earlier in the second quarter, the broadcast panned to defensive line coach Joe Cullen getting into it with Chris Jones on the sideline. Jones apparently took the message to heart, because he got into the sack column for the first time this year, splitting a takedown with rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods. George Karlaftis also got his first of the year as well.
CBS broadcast shows the discussion between #Chiefs DL coach Joe Cullen and Chris Jones. pic.twitter.com/z8NB0VnS4U
This had been a weekly talking point for a while, so perhaps the Chiefs can finally put it in the rearview mirror and get back to making opposing quarterbacks uncomfortable.

title: Complete Chiefs Inactives for Week 6 vs. Chargers: Rashee Rice and More Headline List
full_text:
After some down time to rest up for the grueling months of the season, the Kansas City Chiefs hit the ground running this week and are fresh off a bye. Week 6 sees them host the Los Angeles Chargers in a Sunday afternoon clash between AFC West rivals, presenting plenty to look out for in the late window.
It's a battle of the winless versus the undefeated this weekend, but rest assured knowing both of these sides will fight hard in an effort to secure a victory. Neither team rolls into this one with a clean bill of health, which very well could factor into how Week 6 unfolds.
With that in mind, here's who's inactive for Kansas City and Los Angeles in Sunday's matchup.
Here are the Chiefs’ inactives for today’s game against the Chargers: WR Rashee Rice TE Jared Wiley QB Garrett Nussmeier DB Jadon Canady DE Jack Pyburn OT Diego Pounds OT Josh Simmons
In advance of Sunday, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid revealed that wide receiver Rashee Rice and left tackle Josh Simmons would be missing the game. Rice continues to work his way back from a hamstring injury suffered in Week 4 against the Las Vegas Raiders, and Simmons has been nursing a back injury for around two months.
The latter made his return to the practice field this week; Rice didn't work at all on Wednesday, Thursday or Friday. The Kansas City offense will be shorthanded, meaning Los Angeles might be in for a heavy diet of running back Kenneth Walker III on the ground and tight end Travis Kelce through the air.
On Saturday, the Chiefs elevated a pair of wide receivers , Andrew Armstrong and Justin Watson. The two practices squad players joined a group that otherwise contains names like Xavier Worthy, Jalen Royals, Cyrus Allen and more. Both Armstrong and Watson are active for game day — Watson will soon make his return to the field for Kansas City after winning a pair of Super Bowls with them in his first stint.
There aren't many real surprises on the Kansas City inactives list for Week 6.
inactives for week 6 at KC Derwin James Jr. Tre’ Harris Rodney Shelley Donte Jackson Bud Dupree Kayode Awosika Joe Alt

title: Chiefs Stats and Milestones for Week 6 vs. Chargers: Mahomes and Kelce Duo Shines
full_text:
When the Kansas City Chiefs take the field against the Los Angeles Chargers this afternoon, the ultimate goal is to simply escape with a victory . Multiple subplots are worth keeping an eye on, however, especially with the home crowd cheering the team on.
Kansas City has four players who can rise up the ranks of either the franchise or the NFL at large. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes, tight end Travis Kelce, defensive tackle Chris Jones and linebacker Nick Bolton make up Sunday's list.
Let's take a look at the most intriguing stats and milestones to monitor for the Chiefs in Week 6 of the regular season , courtesy of the club's game notes.
This season has seen Mahomes return to form in multiple regards, as he's producing numbers closer to earlier in his Chiefs tenure after a few down years by his standards. The two-time MVP has at least two passing touchdowns in each game this campaign, and a big-time performance in Week 6 could underscore just how amazing his career's been thus far.
With three-plus passing touchdowns on Sunday versus Los Angeles, Mahomes would break a tie with Pro Football Hall of Famers Peyton Manning (Indianapolis Colts and Denver Broncos) and Dan Marino (Miami Dolphins) for the most games of that nature all-time in a player's first 10 seasons. No. 15 is currently at 48 such contests, with his most recent one being Week 2 against Indy.
A couple of months ago, Kelce made it clear that he felt year 14 could still see him find new ways to improve . From both a statistical standpoint and the eye test, that's been the case four games into the 2026-27 season. The 37-year-old is averaging 15.4 yards per catch with a 68.2% success rate and looks quicker both in-route and after the catch, stepping up as a top option on offense once again.
On Sunday, Kelce has multiple benchmarks within reach.
The first one is definitely the loftiest of bars. Kelce needs three catches of 25 or more yards to pass former New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers great Rob Gronkowski for the most ever by a tight end. Secondly, it'd take seven receptions to pass Hall of Fame wideout Marvin Harrison for the third-most catches ever by a player in his first 14 seasons. Lastly, just one catch would extend Kelce's ongoing streak to 196 consecutive games with a grab — the longest active span in football.
It's been a quiet season for seven-time Pro Bowler and three-time First-Team All-Pro Jones, as he's registered 11 tackles and a couple of pass breakups with no sacks in the first month of the season. He's doing so while logging just 191 snaps, though, which adds up to his lowest percentage (70%) since 2021. Advanced outlets don't reflect him being the downright elite pass rusher he typically is, as Pro Football Focus credits him with 11 pressures and nine hurries on 132 opportunities.
Still, Jones is always one good matchup away from breaking out in a big way. Considering he's going against a depleted Chargers offensive line in Week 6, perhaps this is the spot. With a pair of sacks, the CEO of "Sack Nation" would enter a tie with former outside linebacker Tamba Hali for the second most by a Chief in franchise history.
Sitting at 87.5 for yet another week, it feels like merely a matter of time for Jones.
Folks can argue about the value of tackles all they want, but they can't deny that Bolton provides them in bunches . The sixth-year man has gone into the triple digits on four separate occasions in his career, and he's tracking to do so once again if he stays healthy in 2026. Bolton's averaging 11 tackles per game across his last three outings — getting 10 or more would be huge in Week 6.
Bolton is currently tied with fan favorite and longtime Chiefs star 'backer Derrick Johnson for the most games with 10-plus tackles in a Kansas City career. The former Missouri standout is already up to 25 of those performances before even turning 27, which is impressive no matter how you slice it. Can the 2021 second-round pick make some splash plays against a division rival? If so, Johnson could be looking up at him on the all-time Chiefs standings.

title: Chiefs' Alohi Gilman Ready for Revenge Against Chargers? Not So Fast
full_text:
Sunday isn't a standard low-stakes game for the Kansas City Chiefs despite their opponent still having yet to win this season. It's an AFC West clash between first and last place in the division, and there's no love lost with the Los Angeles Chargers.
The bad blood between both sides goes back decades; an underwhelming season on LA's side isn't going to change that. Longtime Chiefs like quarterback Patrick Mahomes, tight end Travis Kelce and defensive tackle Chris Jones have ample experience setting out for contests like this with one goal on their mind: dominate.
What about someone who's been on both sides of the coin? Safety Alohi Gilman, who came into the NFL as a member of the Chargers, is set on securing the win but isn't necessarily feeling like he needs to prove anything.
"It'll be, for sure, a unique feeling," Gilman said. "Was drafted there sixth round and was there for five-and-a-half, six years. A lot of really good relationships there that I had and still have, a lot of the core guys that I was there with. So that's always special to see — not special — a unique experience. I look forward to playing against them. Just focused on here, and being together with these guys has been great. Just focused on that and whatever we've got to do."
As a defensive back pickup out of Navy and Notre Dame, Gilman spent his first five-plus seasons in Los Angeles. As a member of the Chargers, he tracked up 252 tackles, 21 pass breakups, five interceptions, four forced fumbles and four fumble recoveries spanning 73 regular-season games. Just over a year ago to the day, however, the organization traded him to the Baltimore Ravens in exchange for pass rusher Odafe Oweh.
The rest is history, as Gilman made plays for a struggling Ravens club down the stretch and latched on with the Chiefs as a free agent this past spring. The club has yet to get optimal value out of that signing, yet Gilman's blend of experience and playmaking figures to show up throughout this season.
Gilman and linebacker Drue Tranquill were both longtime Chargers, although Tranquill was already in Kansas City by the time current head coach Jim Harbaugh came to town. Both players witnessed firsthand how talented quarterback Justin Herbert is, though, and Gilman describes the looming matchup with the multi-time Pro Bowler as a "fun experience" on deck.
There's ample incentive for the Chiefs to want to crush the opposition this weekend, especially with the Chargers having ripped off back-to-back wins in the series. Even if LA doesn't factor into the postseason race in a couple of months, divisional wins play a role in seeding math for when a team like Kansas City hopes to be held in high regard.
With just hours remaining until Gilman goes head-to-head with former trusted coworkers like Herbert, Harbaugh and company, it's nothing but respect... until opening kickoff.
"Harbaugh's a great coach," Gilman said. "Obviously a lot of experience. A very genuine and unique individual, so you respect coaches like that. I've had a great relationship with him, I still have a great relationship with him. I wish him the best."

title: Chiefs vs. Chargers: NFL Week 6 Preview, Score Predictions
full_text:
For the third time in five games to begin the 2026-27 season, the Kansas City Chiefs will square off against an opponent from their own division. Coming out of the bye, it's the Los Angeles Chargers who stroll into Arrowhead Stadium to face Andy Reid's group.
With Kansas City looking to maintain an undefeated record and Los Angeles' season hanging on by the thinnest of threads, many would assume that this has the makings of a blowout. Given how close these rivals usually play each other, though, is there the possibility of a more competitive Sunday showdown?
How might today's game unfold? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 6 of the regular season.
Joshua Brisco: Undefeated vs. winless doesn’t really mean all that much to me once game day actually arrives. The Chiefs are coming off a bye, but they're still dealing with an array of impactful injuries . The Chargers are limping toward their week off, but it’s a divisional game. I don't expect the Chargers to magically find offensive success against the Chiefs, yet I could easily see this game being uglier than Chiefs fans would like.
Jordan Foote: Kansas City is well rested for Week 6, and Reid's track record after a bye speaks for itself. Not only that, but the Chargers are struggling in two of the game's three phases (offense and special teams) and are extremely banged up to boot. This team is undoubtedly more talented than its record shows , which is why I'm calling for an ugly one-score game, but the hosts should be able to overcome their own injuries and rise to 5-0 on the still-young season.
If the Chiefs lose this one, they have only themselves to blame. There's ample room for a hint of a nail-biter, albeit not an embarrassing loss to a floundering foe.
Joshua Schulman: An undefeated Chiefs squad taking on a winless Chargers team feels like the biggest trap game of all time, but it’s hard to fathom just how bad Justin Herbert and Mike McDaniel's unit has been. While they’ve been trending up in recent weeks, poor late-game execution and costly turnovers have sunk their chances.
Coming off a bye, I think the old “rest vs. rust” debate will play out for the Chiefs offense, and Patrick Mahomes may need some time to connect with his new targets now that Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton won’t be suiting up. However, they should come alive in the second half, and the defense will do enough to keep it close the first few quarters.
Tyler Brown: Early in the week, this one felt closer than the records suggest. Chiefs-Chargers games have a history of being tight regardless of the circumstances, and that reputation is hard to shake. The longer the week went on, though, the harder it became to make a case for Los Angeles.
This Chargers team is much closer to the Miami Dolphins the Chiefs dispatched 24-10 in Week 3 than they are to any legitimate AFC West contender.
The injury report alone, with Joe Alt, Rashawn Slater, and Derwin James all out, makes this a mismatch. Add in the 0-5 record and four rookie offensive linemen protecting Herbert, and the case for a competitive game falls apart.
The sack drought ends Sunday. Herbert has been sacked 30 times in 11 career games against Kansas City, and he's never faced this Chiefs defensive line with this little protection. Three to four sacks feels conservative, and one or two turnovers wouldn't be surprising.
Walker should have another big day on the ground, and tight end Travis Kelce will get going without  James lurking in the middle of the field. The young receivers will have a chance to build some chemistry with Mahomes in a low-stakes environment.

title: Chiefs Confidence Meter: How I Feel About the Team Against Chargers in Week 6
full_text:
With a perfect 4-0 record intact and a bye in the books, the Kansas City Chiefs will soon be back in action. On Sunday, they host the visiting Los Angeles Chargers in yet another bout between two bitter AFC West rivals.
To say it's been a slow start for Los Angeles would be a massive understatement. Jim Harbaugh's crew is struggling to generate any sort of momentum after hiring new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, and veteran quarterback Justin Herbert is playing some of his worst football.
Still, it's the NFL, and even this 0-5 team can't be overlooked. Andy Reid's group is well aware of that entering a new week of play.
Let's break down how both sides match up and put a bow on this Week 6 preview with a confidence meter rating on a scale ranging from 1-10.
Before the bye, Kansas City had established itself as one of the best rushing team in the sport. Running back Kenneth Walker III's 87 attempts for 537 yards and four touchdowns put him on the map as a premier threat, and he figures to be a significant part of the game plan once again.
On Sunday, Walker faces a middling Chargers rush defense that ranks 14th in EPA per carry (-0.119, via RBSDM ) and 18th in success rate. Stacking the defensive formation may not do anything to slow the standout halfback, as he's racked up 7.31 yards per tote with eight or more players in the box. Given the absences of wide receivers Rashee Rice ( hamstring ) and Tyquan Thornton ( ankle ), it makes sense for KC to try LA on the ground.
Regarding the passing attack, the aforementioned injuries and the continued inactivity of left tackle Josh Simmons could make quarterback Patrick Mahomes' life more difficult. Coming out of the bye, the Chiefs have football's third-highest share of passes behind or at the line of scrimmage (32.0%, courtesy of TruMedia ) and average 1.6 yards behind the sticks when throwing.
Los Angeles' pass defense is respectable, albeit somewhat untested (fourth-lowest pass rate over expected, per Jefe's Handiwork ). Coordinator Chris O'Leary's unit surrenders the ninth-lowest dropback EPA/play mark at 0.006 and owns the 11th-ranked pressure rate at 38.9%. This certainly doesn't feel like the week Kansas City unleashes a full-fledged aerial assault.
It's worth noting that safety Derwin James, whom many in Los Angeles circles have dubbed the "Travis Kelce stopper" over the years, is missing this one due to a hamstring injury. Elsewhere on defense, cornerback Donte Jackson (hamstring) is out and the trio of linebacker Bud Dupree (neck), linebacker Daiyan Henley (knee) and defensive end Dalvin Tomlinson (hamstring) is questionable.
This can't be what the Chargers had in mind when they ushered in the McDaniel era. Prior to the start of Sunday's play, this is an offense that produces fewer points per drive (1.4) than all but one team and gains fewer yards (24.4) on a per-possession basis than all but three.
An inability to run the football is a major part of those struggles. Despite that, via nfelo , Los Angeles still passes at the lowest rate over expected (-11.6%). This Harbaugh-influenced team runs, runs and runs again, yet it's 28th in rush EPA/play. Second-year halfback Omarion Hampton has yet to realize his potential.
Speaking of wasted upside, this is the first time in Herbert's career he's been this glaring of a problem for such an extended stretch. He enters Week 6 ranked 29th out of 30 qualified signal-callers in adjusted EPA/play (-0.117) and, according to Pro Football Focus , his 13 turnover-worthy plays lead the pack in the worst of ways.
The two-time Pro Bowler has completed a career-low 59.4% of his passes with 5.0 adjusted yards per attempt, another personal worst. In fairness to him, his pass catchers are nothing to write home about and roll into the weekend banged up. Wideout Tre Harris — stop me if you're heard this before — has a hamstring injury and is out.
Could this finally be the week the Kansas City pass rush gets going? The Chargers being without tackle Joe Alt (neck) certainly helps that prospect. Los Angeles sits in just the 10th percentile with the fourth-highest pressure rate (43.8), also allowing a sack at the NFL's second-highest clip (10.6%).
Keep an eye out for defensive tackle Chris Jones and defensive ends George Karlaftis and R Mason Thomas. This could also be a spot for former Chargers linebacker Drue Tranquill to keep turning in productive snaps and maybe send a message to his old team.
Ryan Ficken enters his fifth year as the Chargers' special teams coordinator, and he drew praise from Chiefs STC Dave Toub earlier in the week. The data tells a different story. PFF grades Los Angeles' group as 13th-best with a 77.3 mark after it was 29th in 2025, 15th in 2024 and first in 2023. There's some variance for you.
Expanding the advanced metrics, TruMedia ranks LA 31st in special teams EPA at -20.68 through five games. That includes being in the sixth percentile in penalty EPA (-5.18), kicking EPA (-16.84), kickoffs returned (66.7%) and yards per punt return (3.8). This is a side of the ball that could clearly use some work over the course of the season.
In more traditional methods of measurement, the Chargers are dead last in average starting field position on defense and third-worst on offense. How previous drives end has plenty to do with where the ensuing ones begin, though, so take it with a grain of salt.
Let's get this out of the way: Los Angeles' season is probably a cooked product at this point barring the team going on a downright miraculous run and making a full recovery starting this weekend. The Chiefs have a markedly better offense, and their Sunday foes are floundering in many regards while also having an injury report longer than CVS receipts.
With that said, it's a divisional contest against a team that typically plays Kansas City tough. Reid's team is far from 100% healthy in its own right, and the jury is still out on Steve Spagnuolo's defense just a bit — particularly with the pass rush and safety collective . The Chiefs aren't out of the woods, even at home facing an inferior squad.
But at the end of the day, the only real route Los Angeles has to pull off an upset is Herbert suddenly snapping out of his funk, putting his Superman cape on and willing his team to victory. There's no evidence of that happening anytime soon.
Unless the Chiefs simply don't show up, they're in a favorable spot.

title: Shorthanded Chiefs Elevate Pair of Wide Receivers for Week 6 Game vs. Chargers
full_text:
Despite just having a week to rest up, the Kansas City Chiefs come out of the bye still lacking a bit in the health category. The wide receiver room is ravaged by injuries , necessitating an adjustment or two prior to Week 6's contest against the Los Angeles Chargers.
The answers from head coach Andy Reid, general manager Brett Veach and company are in-house for now. Per Matt Derrick of Chiefs Digest on Saturday afternoon, Kansas City has elevated wide receivers Andrew Armstrong and Justin Watson from the practice squad.
Chiefs have elevated receivers Andrew Armstrong and Justin Watson from the practice squad for Sunday’s game against the Chargers.
During the regular season, practice squad players are allowed to be promoted via standard elevation three times. Once that limit is reached, said player reverts to the practice squad and can't rejoin the team unless signed directly to the 53-man roster. For the postseason, the allotted elevation number resets.
Considering wideout Tyquan Thornton is on the injured reserve list with a significant ankle injury and Rashee Rice is sitting this weekend out as he continues to recover from a Week 4 exit ( hamstring ), temporarily replacing them makes ample sense. Without any activations, it would've left Xavier Worthy, Jalen Royals, Cyrus Allen and company to pick up the pieces.
Armstrong, a former Detroit Lions pickup, latched on with Kansas City on a futures contract in January. The 25-year-old starred during the preseason this August, hauling in seven passes for 85 yards and recording five first downs. He has yet to appear in a regular-season game, so Week 6 could be his official NFL debut.
Watson, who's already won two Super Bowls as a Chief, reunited with the team earlier this week after it was reported that KC had interest in him . He last played with the Houston Texans a season ago, logging three catches for 30 yards in three games. His career Chiefs stats include 119 targets, 64 receptions, 1,064 yards and seven touchdowns — not including the playoffs.
Speaking to the media on Monday, Reid gushed over Watson's versatility and understanding of the offense. He hinted at the 30-year-old veteran being able to catch up quickly and potentially be available for the weekend.
"He was a good player for us when he was here," Reid said. "He obviously can run fast, and he's got great size. He's willing to do everything, he knows the offense. He's a smart kid. We felt like he could come back in as needed and contribute, step in and go. With just a slight review, he should be fine and good to go."
It remains to be seen how Kansas City will divvy up its wideout snaps on Sunday against a rival club, but there will now be options either way.

title: Jim Harbaugh Post-Game Quote Spells Doom for Mike McDaniel Following Chargers Loss
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers dropped to 0-6 after losing a clunker to the Kansas City Chiefs. The battle in Kansas City was clearly the Chargers final stand of the 2026 season but their injury-ravaged and ineffective offense could not put anything together and scored only six points.
The offense has been the Chargers' Achilles heel this season. Their defense has performed well and kept games close and have provided opportunities to the offense to attempt to mount a comeback.
Franchise quarterback Justin Hebert has not looked like himself. He has been making shocking mistakes, looked unsure of footwork and saw a massive spike in turnover-worthy plays compared to his career average.
The offense has been bad. The offense has been the worst in the NFL. New offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel was the most sought-after offensive mind in the past offseason and the excitement surrounding the pairing of he and Justin Herbert permeated throughout the media all offseason. It has been an absolute failure and the clock has been ticking on McDaniel needing to find an answer.
Following the Chargers loss, head coach Jim Harbaugh was asked by a reporter at the post-game press conference if Mike McDaniel would still be calling plays going forward and for the first time, the possibility of change was firmly acknowledged when Harbaugh responded with "We're going to look at everything."
Seeing the frustration that this just isn't working is a new turn for Harbaugh. "We have to look at everything guys," Harbaugh says, "Especially offensively, we aren't scoring enough points." Regarding McDaniel still calling plays: "We're gonna look at everything." 👀 pic.twitter.com/CYgEbU75Ft
The Chargers offense isn't just bad, they look lost. Procedural penalties have plagued the players from every position group from receivers not knowing motions or linemen committing false starts. The chaos has likely lead to most of the injuries along the offensive line from simply falling over and into each other.
To put into perspective how bad the Chargers offense has been in 2026, Shawn Syed of Sumer Sports ran the numbers from the past decade and the Chargers have the sixth-worst offense on an EPA basis.
The Chargers offense has -98 Total EPA through 6 weeks That is the 6th lowest for any team through 6 weeks since 2016, per @SumerSports
To continue the conversation on offensive EPA, the Chargers, fighting for their season against the Kansas City Chiefs, gave their worst offensive performance of the season and have landed at the bottom of multiple offensive categories. Sheil Kapadia of the Ringer, posted on X to highlight how bad today's offensive performance and described it as hitting rock bottom.
Today had to be rock bottom for the Chargers (I think). Their worst offensive performance of the season, based on EPA per drive. Their offense ranks 32nd overall. It's their worst offense through 6 weeks this century.
Jim Harbaugh mentioned that the Chargers are not scoring enough points. The Chargers have currently scored the third least amount of points in the NFL, ahead of only the Miami Dolphins and the Tennessee Titans. The joining of McDaniel, Harbaugh and Herbert was once the most excited development and hire of the offseason around the NFL, it may be nearing it's end six weeks into their first season together.

title: Ranking Chargers Who Should Be Fired, Scapegoated After Falling to 0-6
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers have officially hit rock bottom after falling to 0-6 following their latest loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. What was supposed to be another competitive season under Jim Harbaugh has instead turned into an absolute nightmare.
The team has clearly struggled to generate offense , finish drives and find any consistency.
At this point, the blame cannot fall entirely on the players.
With the Chargers searching for answers, the inevitable may happen soon. Here are my rankings for the Chargers coaching staff and who is on the hot seat.
McDaniel was brought in to help maximize Justin Herbert and give the Chargers offense a more dynamic identity. He was the biggest news in the offseason for them. Instead, the unit has struggled to produce the kind of results expected from a team with a quarterback of Herbert’s ability.
Effective offenses must capitalize on opportunities created by the defense. They must minimize turnovers as well. Which the Bolts aren't doing, and it shows. If those problems were fixed even in the lightest way, they would be doing much better.
McDaniel deserves time to establish his system, particularly with injuries affecting the available personnel. However, they cannot afford to keep making excuses for an offense that consistently fails to deliver. If his play-calling and adjustments do not improve, he should be among the first assistants considered for a coaching change.
When a team starts 0-6, the head coach has to be the first person under the microscope. Harbaugh arrived with a reputation for building disciplined, physical football teams capable of competing against anybody.
Harbaugh is responsible for the overall direction of the franchise, including how his assistants prepare their units and how the team responds when adversity strikes. Six consecutive defeats demand a much bigger conversation about the coaching staff’s effectiveness.
Harbaugh does not necessarily need to be fired immediately, but he cannot be protected from criticism simply because of his previous accomplishments. If the team continues to look unprepared and undisciplined, his seat should become increasingly uncomfortable.
The offensive line deserves special attention because Herbert’s effectiveness depends heavily on the protection and blocking in front of him. Barry joined the Chargers in 2026 after coaching Miami’s offensive line, bringing experience from a unit that had previously helped produce a productive offense.
Not every protection problem falls on the position coach. Injuries, personnel limitations and individual execution also matters. Having four rookies on the starting line is definitely not ideal.  Nevertheless, Barry must find ways to improve communication, assignment discipline and overall consistency. If the offensive line remains a weakness, the entire offense will continue paying the price.
The Chargers cannot afford to waste favorable field position or make mistakes in an area that should help keep games competitive.
The team’s latest defeat was not solely a special-teams failure, and its kicking production was responsible for all six of its points. That distinction matters when evaluating accountability.
Ficken should remain under evaluation, although he is not the primary coaching concern based on the team’s overall struggles.
O’Leary returned to the Bolts as defensive coordinator, and the current losing streak raises questions about whether his unit can consistently execute the game plan. In his defense, his unit has been the only bright spot for this team.
O’Leary should be evaluated on how well his players respond during the coming weeks. If the defense continues struggling to get off the field and prevent opponents from controlling games, Harbaugh may need to consider whether a different defensive approach is necessary.
Though, O’leary is probably the coach who has the safest job so far.

title: Chargers Offense the Walking Dead Against the Chiefs, Season Officially Slips Away
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers traveled to Kansas City to take on the Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium. The hostile environment is a challenging place to play, those challenges are elevated with a injury ravaged roster, a misfiring offense with four rookies on the offensive line and special teams unit consistently losing the field position battle.
The Chargers prepared to make their final stand of the 2026 season against their division rivals. They carried an 0-5 record into Kansas City and their season was barely on life support. There was hope for some reinforcements with the return of wide receivers Ladd McConkey, Quinton Johnston and the activation of  receiver Keandre Lambert-Smith.
Ladd McConkey exited the game promptly with a concussion after being tackled and unfortunately his head bounced hard off the surface as he went down. The rest of the offense struggled to find any rhythm in the first half. The drives were highlighted by short runs, batted passes and failed screens.
Quarterback Justin Herbert had another tipped pass interception that was luckily called back for roughing the passer call. Although he promptly threw another inexcusable interception a short time later. The pass went right to a defender on one of Herbert's now signature frustrated throws when nothing is working.
Los Angeles was trying to find any positive offense. They used one of the signature counters for Mike McDaniel's offense and most of the Shanahan tree when defenses start attacking and applying pressure through the B-gaps by using the screen game to keep the defense off balance and force the defenders into conflict.
The Chargers tried multiple screens from different formations and to different targets, none of them worked. The Chiefs took most of them away or were prepared to rally to make the tackle for minimal gains.
Finally, searching for anything, Justin Herbert uncorked a bomb on a scramble to Quinton Johnston that went to the one -yard line for a 57-yard reception. The explosive play was quickly nullified by a holding penalty from center Jake Slaughter on first-and-goal from the one-yard line that sent the Chargers back to the eleven and they were unable to advance.
Justin Hebert rifled a tight window throw to tight end Oronde Gadsden in the endzone and the ball went directly through his hands and the Chargers were forced to kick a field goal. Nothing working is the title of the Chargers offensive results. The quick passing game consistently was batted down, receivers weren't open or passes fell off receivers fingertips.
The Chargers finally had some mild success and in the fourth quarter, they found themselves with a chance following multiple defensive stops punctuated by a missed Harrison Butker field that gave the Chargers the ball with positive field position. Facing a third and one, Herbert threw a quick pass to Keandre Lambert-Smith who picked up the first down but fumbled the ball and it was recovered by Chiefs linebacker Drue Tranquill.
The Chargers can't get out of their own way. They have been consistent at doing the little football things wrong. Ball security, penalties and situational football have all been lacking with the overall exception of the defense. Their shortcomings have kept them from playing winning football.
The offense is the worst in the NFL and they are now 0-6 heading into their bye week. The organization has several massive decisions to make now that the Chargers' final stand to find hope for 2026 has failed.

title: Chargers' Ladd McConkey Suffers New Injury vs. Chiefs, Quickly Ruled Out
full_text:
A tough go for Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Ladd McConkey continued during Sunday's game against the Kansas City Chiefs.
In the first half with the Chargers losing 9-3 to the Chiefs, McConkey suffered a concussion, with the team quickly declaring him out for the game.
Before his exit, McConkey caught his lone target for 17 yards from Justin Herbert. At the time, he was one of just four Chargers targets with a single reception while Herbert had a 4-of-9 line with an interception in a game that threatened to drop Los Angeles to 0-6 on the season.
The Chargers have a bye week after the game in Kansas City so, generally speaking, McConkey should be on track to return for Week 8 against the Los Angeles Rams on November 1 if all goes well.
That said, McConkey was a question mark to even play on Sunday against the Chiefs. He’s battled a variety of different injuries this season and, prior to Sunday, had only played in four games while taking just 54 percent of the offense’s snaps.
McConkey tried to gut through this game on the road, but the Chargers star now has a new injury to come back from while Herbert’s offense attempts to get moving with wideouts Quentin Johnston and rookie Brenen Thompson.
