title: NFL Trade Rumors Before Chargers vs. Chiefs Update Jim Harbaugh, Justin Herbert Status
full_text:
Earlier this week, we painted the Los Angeles Chargers as a delusional franchise based on NFL trade rumors around Jim Harbaugh’s club.
Those 0-5 Chargers, after all, weren’t expected to be sellers at the upcoming NFL trade deadline. But falling to 0-6 would put the Chargers in a point of no return that would change things, right?
Before the Chargers visited the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 6 at Arrowhead Stadium, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport went live and updated the situation.
“Still plenty of confidence in coach Jim Harbaugh,” Rapoport said. “Still plenty of confidence in offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel…They are not acting like a team that’s going to sell. So yes, teams have been calling about Khalil Mack and several other players. Is Justin Herbert available? No. The answer is no. The Chargers believe the answers are in the building."
For now, this isn’t too shocking. Disappointing for fans, surely. But not shocking.
The Chargers aren’t going to risk mutiny in the locker room by waving the white flag publicly or to reporters in Week 6. Looking at the schedule, though, the Week 7 bye was always the point to circle in red.
If the Chargers were ever going to reverse course on a major overarching plan, it was always going to gain traction in Week 7 during the bye. If they walk into that at 0-6, it’s not hard to see how this public tune might change.
Considering the Chargers play the Rams, Texans and Ravens through Week 10, they could be looking at 0-9. But the bye is when things would likely really change.
And change feels like a must and inevitable. To outsiders, it certainly feels like Harbaugh’s message and style is failing. It certainly looks like McDaniel’s offense is too complex. And it certainly looks like general manager Joe Hortiz’s compensatory-pick, money-saving ways are backfiring with a staggeringly poor roster.
In fact, this is one of those long-term critical points for a franchise. No 0-5 team has made the playoffs. If the Chargers start winning now, but miss the playoffs, it would give the team an excuse to run everything back. If they keep losing, they could be forced out of this lull and into change, for better or worse.
The Chargers won’t ever admit to it, of course. But trading off the likes of Khalil Mack and others while revamping the strategy during the bye remains the obvious outcome if they lose in Kansas City.

title: Point of No Return: Why Week 6 at Arrowhead is the 2026 Chargers' Last Stand
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are dragging a makeshift offensive line to Missouri on top of a roster suffering multiple starters on injured reserve, the injury list is even worse . LA is 0-5 and have been fighting hard in every game this season but without results for their efforts.
At 0-5, the Chargers have very little hope of turning their season around at this point. But, the AFC has been rather weak to start the season and although the Chargers' season is on life support, they still have a tiny chance.
Los Angeles' injury-ravaged offense will attempt to find more rhythm against the undeafeated Chiefs who are coming off of a bye week. Kansas City's defensive coordinator Steve Spagnola is a master at timing up blitzes and despite the rookie-heavy offensive line playing well against the Broncos , we can expect him to mercilessly attack Justin Herbert and the offensive line.
The Chargers' running back room has been healthy and rather productive when compared to the whole offense. Anticipating a blitz-heavy afternoon against a young offensive line, the Chargers will likely lean on the run game and hope to establish some success to open up play action. The running back room is healthy and Los Angeles has two blocking tight ends paired with an additional fullback hybrid in Scott Matlock, if for no other reason, the offense should run through the healthiest units.
The Chargers' wide receiver corps should theoretically get a boost this week with Ladd McConkey, Quinton Johnston and Keandre Lambert-Smith all returning to the field. The trouble is, despite none of them carrying an injury designation into the game, how healthy are they really? At this point of the season, with a bye week on the way, this is an all hands on deck scenario, this is the Chargers final stand.
There is no precedent for a team starting 0-5 and making the playoffs, the 1992 Chargers are the only team to have started 0-4 and gone on to make the playoffs. The odds of making the playoffs at this point are almost non-existent. If there is any hope, even for a positive season, the turnaround has to happen against the Chiefs, before the bye.
The looming decisions around the organization are likely tied to the results of week six. According to NFL insider Tom Pelissero, the Chargers have pushed back against trade talks so far. It is always suspicious when NFL insiders are discussing front office details and the timing does nothing to calm the questions.
The Chargers have rejected trade calls, believing they’re close to turning things around after an 0-5 start and making no plans to hold a fire sale. That and much more in the Week 6 Insider Notebook at The Sweep: https://t.co/hVvUAJEl9r pic.twitter.com/4LDRFcJ4WB
Whether the Chargers are genuinely not interested in discussing trades, at least for now or if this is intentionally placed information to serve as a message to the team before their battle in Kansas City remains unimportant. The bottom line is, the bye week is likely a point where big organizational decisions will have to be made.
Los Angeles needs a win or those trade calls may finally be answered. The trade deadline this year is just after week nine, if they enter their bye week in week seven at 0-6, the Chargers' front office can no longer be delusional.

title: Fantasy Football Start or Sit: Shy Away From Chargers' Playmakers in Week 6
full_text:
The Chargers have a tough test waiting for them in Week 6, and fantasy managers have some decisions to make before Sunday’s divisional matchup.
Injuries on both sides could change how this game plays out, especially with several important offensive and defensive players unavailable.
Not every big name deserves an automatic spot in your lineup, and sometimes the best fantasy decision comes down to which players are in the best position to succeed.
Ladd McConkey is a player I would feel comfortable keeping in my lineup this week. The second-year receiver has the route-running ability to create separation against quality coverage, and he gives Justin Herbert an option who can contribute without needing a deep ball every time.
Tre’ Harris being ruled out makes the receiving situation worth watching. His absence leaves the Bolts without one of their leading producers, potentially opening the door for McConkey to see additional opportunities.
There is always some risk when facing a divisional opponent, but McConkey’s ability to make plays in the short and intermediate areas gives him a path to fantasy production. I would trust his skill set rather than overthink the matchup.
This is probably the toughest name on the list to bench, but fantasy managers should pay attention to what has happened through the first five weeks.
Herbert has thrown for 937 yards and five touchdowns, numbers that have not translated into the type of production fantasy managers typically want from their starting quarterback. The protection in front of him has also been a major concern, and things do not get easier with Joe Alt and Kayode Awosika ruled out.
Kansas City’s pass rush has shown that it can create problems for opposing quarterbacks. If Herbert is forced to get rid of the ball quickly or spends too much time under pressure, it could limit his opportunities for explosive plays.
I am not saying Herbert cannot have a good afternoon. He has the arm talent to change a game in a matter of minutes. However, fantasy managers with a reliable alternative should seriously consider their options before committing to him this week.
Quentin Johnston has an opportunity to contribute with Harris unavailable, but I would be careful about assuming that automatically makes him a dependable fantasy starter. Johnston has the physical tools to make difficult catches and stretch the field. The problem is that his value can depend on whether he receives enough targets and converts them into meaningful gains. A couple of catches might be useful for the Chargers without doing much for fantasy managers.
There is a reasonable argument for using Johnston as a flex option, especially in deeper leagues. However, I would prefer a receiver with a more established role if I needed a dependable floor. The matchup also comes with questions about how consistently Herbert will have time to throw. Johnston could absolutely make a big play, but I would rather avoid relying on that possibility when setting my lineup.
I would look elsewhere for a fantasy defense this week if another reasonable option is available.
The Chargers are missing several important pieces, including James and Jackson, and those absences could make it harder to limit Kansas City’s passing game. Even if the defensive front creates some pressure, Mahomes has the ability to escape trouble.

title: Khalil Mack Contract Rumors Make Things Interesting for Chargers at Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers should do right by Khalil Mack with a trade .
At this point, things are so off the rails for Jim Harbaugh’s Chargers, no matter what the NFL trade rumors say about their status as sellers, that most fans would agree that it’s only right to ship Mack away and give him a shot at a championship with another team.
Mack has still looked fantastic this year amid the chaos of an 0-5 team that looks arguably the worst club outright. It’s not like there’s a silver lining that perhaps next things would be better if Mack comes back yet again, considering this sort of flop demands major changes to the coaching staff, if not front office, too.
Until this point, though, there was a whispered thought that Mack’s contract would prevent the Chargers from doing a deal.
And that’s just not the case.
Details have usually been scarce about Mack’s recent contracts with the Chargers. He kept re-upping annually at one year and $18 million, but little pesky details like no-trade clauses never really went public.
Until now, courtesy of The Athletic’s Noah Furtado : “Mack does not have a no-trade clause in his one-year, $18 million deal, The Athletic learned, despite multiple reports in recent weeks stating he does.”
So, that’s one little hurdle the Chargers won’t have to worry about. And there wasn’t a major concern that the organization would betray Mack and ship him to another dumpster fire like the 0-5 Tennessee Titans. But the lack of a no-trade clause gives the Chargers leverage if they decide to move him and, say, choose one much higher offer from a team over another.
There’s really no sense in hanging on at this point. The Chargers already tied their long-term future on the edge to first-round pick Akheem Mesidor and Tuli Tuipulotu, who needs a contract extension.
Sure, it stinks, but the Chargers shipping away Mack and fans getting to see him at least contend for a title would be a small victory. A reunion with the Chicago Bears is obviously the most popular idea right now. That’s just where this season has landed and, if nothing else, there won’t be any contract details in the way of a trade happening soon.

title: NFL Trade Rumors Paint Chargers as Delusional
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers should very obviously be sellers at the NFL trade deadline.
The Chargers might fire Mike McDaniel while attempting to turn things around, it seems. But Khalil Mack and other trade candidates make sense as names to consider moving with the season at 0-5.
It only looks like it will get worse from here. The only thing standing between the Chargers and 0-6 is a date with the Kansas City Chiefs in Arrowhead Stadium. Exiting the bye, games against the Los Angeles Rams, Houston Texans and Baltimore Ravens give them a serious shot at 0-9 before they play the 2-3 New York Jets in Week 11. By then, anything is possible.
But new NFL trade rumors? They paint the Chargers as straight-up delusional about their situation.
The only reports that should be breaking about the Chargers anytime soon are just which players they might shop before a rebuild.
Alas, Tom Pelissero wrote on his Substack that Chargers general manager Joe Hortiz is shooting down teams that call him.
Pelissero went as far as writing that “the Chargers are holding out hope that they’re close to turning things around” and that they aren’t ready “to give up and go into fire sale mode.”
Maybe this is the Chargers just saying and doing the right things in October to keep things from erupting in the building. But there’s no turning around an 0-5 start. It’s not even a down year for the AFC West, with every non-Chargers team sporting at worst a 3-2 mark, which belongs to the usually-lowly Las Vegas Raiders.
If the hope is that this stuff leaking publicly helps the Chargers get some leverage in trade calls over the next few weeks, that’s delusional too. It’s very obvious what’s happening in Los Angeles, and teams aren’t going to pay lucrative prices for any of the Chargers’ trade pieces.
There’s a small outside chance the Chargers feel this way because they’re thinking beyond this year. Maybe there’s hope inside the building that Mike McDaniel just needs another year to really get things going and that Jim Harbaugh isn’t going anywhere. But looking this bad out of the gates and more unacceptable injury waves across the roster point to big institutional changes, even if nobody in the national scene wants to point it out right now.
This stance will undoubtedly change as losses keep happening, but for now, the Chargers get to enjoy weird coverage like this that paints them as lost off the field as they are on it.

title: Rams Winners and Losers: Sean McVay, Matthew Stafford Among Biggest Disappointments
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams lost to the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6, 18-16. It was arguably one of the most disappointing losses of the Sean McVay era . The Rams had a chance to start a winning streak, but instead found themselves in last place in the NFC West. Let’s take a look at this week’s winners and losers.
It’s more than fair to say that Matthew Stafford hasn’t played well this season. Stafford didn’t hit 100 yards passing until the fourth quarter. Early in the third quarter, he overthrew Puka Nacua on what would have likely been a touchdown. Some regression from Stafford was expected, but not many expected this much.
Whenever the Rams’ coaching staff and front office talk about Kyren Williams, it’s always how he is the epitome of what it means to be a ‘Ram’. Following Sunday’s game, Williams was asked why the offense lacks energy and responded, “Probably because I’m not out there.” It’s a dig at his role in the offense and at Blake Corum as a player. For a team that’s supposed to embody a “we not me” mindset, that wasn’t it.
Kyren Williams when asked why he thought the Rams couldn't sustain the energy drive to drive, via @sarahbarshop : "Can’t tell you, bro. Probably because I’m not out there." pic.twitter.com/vcUKP054mT
On the first possession, Lake intercepted Jacoby Brissett. It was Lake’s second interception of the season and should have set the tone for the game. IInstead, the offense had to settle for a field goal and wasn’t able to build off of that momentum.
It feels like McVay has been in the “losers” section of this list too often this season. McVay was a big reason for the loss last week after he got conservative. The Rams’ head coach was also responsible for the team’s travel plans to Australia. On Sunday, McVay called a fullback dive on 4th-and-1 to Davis Allen. McVay is one of the biggest issues on the Rams right now.
For a moment, it looked as if the Rams had solved their kicking woes. Blake Grupe made a 44-yard field goal right through the middle to give the Rams a 3-0 lead. On the ensuing kickoff, Grupe got hurt trying to make a tackle. The injury will likely put Grupe on injured reserve, and the Rams will be right back where they were last week, looking for a kicker.
One of the few bright spots on defense was edge rusher Byron Young. Young was credited with five impact plays via Sumer Sports and an 11.1 percent pressure rate. In the first half alone, Young had three pressures. When Myles Garrett returns, it should open things up for Young even more.
For the most part, Josh Wallace played well. However, he once again was on the wrong end of a controversial call at the end of the game . Wallace got called for unnecessary roughness, adding 15 yards to a 21-yard reception. The penalty essentially put the Cardinals in field goal range on one play.
What must be going through Aaron Donald’s head right now? Donald thought he was joining a Rams team that would be competing for a Super Bowl. Instead, they are 2-4 and find themselves in the middle of an identity crisis. He came out of retirement for this? The Rams were 3-6 in 2023 before turning things around and making the playoffs in what was Donald’s final season. Maybe they’ll turn it around once Garrett returns. However, right now, it doesn’t look great.

title: Sean McVay's Questionable Fourth-Down Play Call Haunts Rams in Loss to Cardinals
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams lost on Sunday to the 1-4 Arizona Cardinals , 18-16. Once again, it was head coach Sean McVay who played a large role in the team’s loss. The McVay-led Rams offense scored only 16 points against a Cardinals defense that entered Week 6 ranked No. 32 in scoring defense and No. 29 in EPA per play.
It was a perplexing performance as McVay was outcoached by Cardinals defensive coordinator Nick Rallis for much of the game. The offense didn’t start finding a rhythm until the fourth quarter and didn’t score a second touchdown until 47 seconds remained in the game.
Following a long Cardinals scoring drive in the second half, the Rams faced fourth-and-1 needing points. Going for it was the right decision from McVay, and it’s no surprise that decision was made.
However, the play call didn’t make sense. Williams has been good in short-yardage situations in the past. Additionally, the Rams have gone to Puka Nacua in those situations before on a jet sweep. McVay did neither of those things. Needing one yard, McVay called a fullback dive to the tight end Davis Allen. Allen was stopped short and the Rams turned the ball over on downs.
Cardinals defense comes up with the stop on 4th and 1! AZvsLAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/kieCYIdECf
Back in Week 1, the Rams faced a 4th-and-1 at the goal line and came up short on a quarterback sneak.Later that week, I argued here that McVay should implement a tush-push-style package with a tight end. Running with a tight end in that situation isn’t a bad idea. A fullback dive, however, is confusing.
Allen had never taken a handoff in his four-year NFL career. Additionally, he didn’t have a single rushing attempt in four years at Clemson. Running with Allen in that spot with other options available didn’t make sense. The Rams have Williams, Nacua, and Stafford and McVay opted to run with his tight end.
The play wasn’t blocked well as Colby Parkinson dove inside, leaving Mack Wilson available to tackle Allen. Still, a dive play to the Rams’ TE4 isn’t the play call that McVay should be going with in that situation.
Later in the game, the Rams went for it on fourth down again. After 4th-and-3 turned into 4th-and-8 because of a penalty, McVay called a screen to Williams that fell incomplete. Williams may have had space to get the first down, but the Cardinals sniffed out the screen.
Pass is incomplete and the Cardinals force a turnover on downs 👀 AZvsLAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/u0bfxJgdFJ
It wasn’t a good day for the offense as they went 4-for-12 on conversion downs. The offense was held to 16 points against a Cardinals defense that hasn’t played well this season.
McVay has played a role in each of the Rams’ losses this season, and it’s hard to say that he wasn’t outcoached again on Sunday. The fourth-down play call to Allen was a clear example of that.

title: Rams on Wrong End of Another Controversial Call in Week 6 Loss to Cardinals
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams were once again on the wrong end of a controversial call at the end of their Week 6 loss to the Arizona Cardinals . After the Rams took the lead, the Cardinals took over at their own 35-yard line with 47 seconds left, needing a field goal to win.
Quarterback Jacoby Brissett completed a pass over the middle to wide receiver Jalen Brooks, who was hit by Josh Wallace. Brooks’ head made slight contact with Wallace’s shoulder. What would have been a 21-yard gain that left the Cardinals outside of field goal range instead put them well within Chad Ryland’s range.
On the broadcast, color analyst Greg Olsen asked rules analyst Mike Pereira what he thought of the call. “It didn't look to me like there was forcible contact at all, was there?” asked Olsen. “My first thought was, this is one that replay could take off if there was no contact,” Pereira responded. “There is contact, but is it enough contact? To me, that's one that does not need to be called.”
UNREAL PERSONAL FOUL WHAT DO YOU WANT HIM TO DO??? pic.twitter.com/L4XLXmZw0W
It was the second time this season that Wallace has been on the wrong end of a controversial call. Back in Week 3, Wallace was called for defensive pass interference on a play in which he intercepted Bo Nix in the fourth quarter.
According to Rule 12, Section 2, Article 9 of the NFL rulebook, there is unnecessary roughness if a player initiates unnecessary contact against a player who is in a defenseless position. Prohibited contact against a player who is in a defenseless position includes lowering the head and making forcible contact with any part of the helmet against any part of the defenseless player’s body.
The NFL rulebook also states in Rule 7, Section 2 that if a defender has already committed himself and the contact is unavoidable, it is not a foul unless the defender makes forcible contact into the head or neck area of the runner with the helmet, shoulder, or forearm, or commits some other act that is unnecessary roughness.
Put skirts on em Jimmy pic.twitter.com/uV2PqhMvub
With this penalty in particular, the gray area comes into play with the “forcible contact” terminology.It’s hard to say that Wallace’s contact was forcible, as it looked to be more incidental. There’s not much more that Wallace could have done in that situation to avoid the contact.
While this call didn’t necessarily give the Cardinals the win, it certainly put them in a position to win the game.  It’s also worth noting that the Rams were also offside on the play. However, without the unnecessary roughness penalty, the Cardinals would have had the ball at the Rams’ 44-yard line with 41 seconds left. That’s still a 62-yard field goal. It would have forced the Cardinals to be more aggressive than they were on their final three plays.
The Rams had only two penalties entering the fourth quarter but committed three more in the final period, including the unnecessary roughness penalty. Timely penalties and mistakes have cost the Rams throughout the year, and this is just another example.

title: Rams Hit Rock Bottom in Stunning Loss to Cardinals as Season Spirals
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams have officially hit rock bottom six weeks into the 2026 season. Entering Week 6, the Rams needed a win to get back to .500. With the 1-4 Arizona Cardinals on the schedule, it seemed to be a ‘sure thing’. Instead, without allowing a touchdown, the Rams lost, 18-16.
For much of the afternoon, the Rams looked uninspired and lacked any sort of energy. While they took the lead with 47 seconds left, the Cardinals kicked a game-winning field goal, their sixth of the day, to win as time expired.
There’s no doubt that the Rams have been inconsistent to start the season. They lacked energy in Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers and couldn’t finish against the Denver Broncos. The Rams were lucky to get out of Philadelphia with a win, scoring 10 points in the final seven minutes. It was special teams that cost them against the Buffalo Bills last week.
Head coach Sean McVay spoke last week about not letting the Bills beat them twice. However, the Rams’ offense made a Cardinals defense that ranked 29th in EPA per play coming in look like a Vic Fangio-led Bears unit in 2018.
The Rams’ first three possessions picked up 23 yards and just one first down. Matthew Stafford didn’t surpass 100 yards passing until the fourth quarter. While the defense allowed the Cardinals to play ball control, they also kept the Rams in the game. On the first drive, Quentin Lake intercepted Jacoby Brissett. The Rams held the Cardinals to 0-for-5 in the red zone and 5-for-15 on third down. However, the Cardinals held the ball for 34:52 and their opening drive of the second half lasted 8:35.
With the score tied 9-9 at halftime, fans at SoFi Stadium could be heard booing the Rams as they walked off the field. Nobody could blame them after what they just watched. For a team that was supposed to be a Super Bowl contender, the Rams haven’t played up to those expectations more often than not. The expectation continues to be that the Rams will eventually flip a switch, but that switch hasn’t been flipped and they’re running out of time.
Following last week’s loss to the Buffalo Bills, the Rams made a change at kicker, signing Blake Grupe. The early returns on Grupe looked promising as he hit a 44-yard field goal to give the Rams the lead in the first quarter. On the ensuing kickoff, the kickoff coverage unit let Devin Duvernay through and Grupe was hurt trying to make the tackle.
Still, the offense couldn’t get out of its own way. Facing 4th-and-1 in the third quarter, McVay called a fullback dive to tight end Davis Allen. With Kyren Williams and Puka Nacua as options, McVay gave the ball to Allen, who hadn’t taken a handoff in his four-year NFL career. Earlier in the drive, Stafford overthrew a wide-open Nacua that likely would have scored.
When a 26-yard defensive pass interference penalty on Nacua put the Rams inside the red zone, Stafford fell trying to escape the pocket and fumbled, taking an 11-yard loss. On the next play, Tyler Higbee fumbled and the Cardinals recovered.
Again, it was the defense keeping the game close. The unit got another stop, but with the offense facing 4th-and-3, a false start penalty on Warren McClendon pushed the Rams back five yards. McVay then called a screen to Williams that fell incomplete.
Even when the offense finally did get it right, they still got it wrong. After Nacua had 17 catches last week, he only had three targets through the first three quarters. On the final drive, Stafford hit Nacua for a gain of 43 while evading the rush and then found him again for a gain of 16 to put the Rams in the red zone.
Two plays later, Stafford found Colby Parkinson in the flat off play-action, and Parkinson reached for the end zone. With Grupe hurt, Ethan Evans gave the Rams their first lead since the first quarter as he drilled the extra point through the uprights.
While the Rams needed to score, the clock was also a factor. Parkinson was initially called short, which may have actually worked in the Rams’ favor to take more time off the clock. However, the touchdown gave the Cardinals 47 seconds. On the first play, Brissett found Jalen Brooks for a gain of 21, and a 15-yard unnecessary roughness penalty put the Cardinals in field goal range. With his sixth field goal of the day, Chad Ryland sealed the Rams’ fate as time expired, dropping Los Angeles to 2-4.
It’s long overdue, but this Rams team needs to take a long look in the mirror. Throughout the McVay era, beating the Cardinals was as ‘sure’ as it gets. This was supposed to be a ‘get-right’ game and the start of a run going into the bye. The Rams entered this week with the easiest schedule in the NFL over the next five games. Instead, they lost 18-16 to a Cardinals team that had essentially waived the white flag on the season.
A Rams team led by Sean McVay lost despite not allowing a touchdown on defense. The 1-4 Cardinals team beat the Rams at home in a must-win game. The Rams entered Sunday with a chance to improve to 1-1 in the NFC West and overtake the Seattle Seahawks. Instead, they are 0-2 in the division and will fall to last place.
It’s fair to point to injuries to Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie. Those were the two stars the Rams traded for to get over the hump.Garrett has been on injured reserve since Week 2 and McDuffie was out on Sunday. However, injuries or not, this is not where this team should be. Two of their biggest problems right now are Matthew Stafford and Sean McVay, but those two are also the solutions.
The Rams have come a long way from being a superteam and Super Bowl contenders. They are now in last place in the NFC West, and a loss to the Cardinals puts them at rock bottom. The question now is whether it’s too late to climb out.

title: Rams Sunday Morning Notebook: Alaric Jackson Fallout, Myles Garrett Warning, Fan in Need Gets Special Surprise
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to take on the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6 as they look to get back to .500 following Monday night's loss to the Buffalo Bills. While the focus has largely been on getting back in the win column, a few other stories have flown under the radar.
Alaric Jackson wasn't the only player disciplined following Monday's game. Myles Garrett avoided a fine from the league, and the Rams stepped up to help a fan in need. .
Let’s dive into this week’s Sunday morning notebook.
Following Monday night’s game between the Rams and Bills, left tackle Alaric Jackson was seen throwing a punch at edge rusher Bradley Chubb. Jackson was initially suspended for two games by the NFL before that was reduced to one game following an appeal.
While there isn’t an excuse for Jackson acting the way that he did, Chubb may not have been completely innocent in the matter. According to Chubb, he told Jackson, “‘We’re gonna see y’all’s ass again. And when we see you again, all that chipping ain’t gonna save you. That TE and guard are not going to save you.”
A punch from Jackson was still certainly an overreaction. He still should have walked away. However, according to Tom Pelissero, Chubb was fined $14,329. The fact that Jackson’s suspension was reduced to one game and Chubb was fined would imply that the Rams’ left tackle didn’t act unprovoked.
The NFL fined Bradley Chubb $14,329 for taunting. Alaric Jackson’s suspension was reduced to one game on appeal, costing him a game check worth close to $1 million. https://t.co/YrGh5E2QxF
Last week, Rams edge rusher Myles Garrett hung out on the sideline for the first time this season. During previous home games, Garrett had been up in a box to watch the game, but against the Bills, Garrett was on the sideline. Instead of wearing team-issued gear, Garrett was seen in a Jordan Jumpman tracksuit.
Typically, this would have been something that Garrett would have been fined for by the league. With that said, after some of the criticism that the league has taken early in the season over how they’ve handled fines, Garrett only got a warning. According to The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones, the Rams heard from the league office about it, and the expectation is for Garrett to blend in on the sideline Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals.
Earlier this week, a fire occurred at the Portico apartments in Fullerton, California. When the fire happened, a man, Mark Viegas, went into the building to check things before getting stuck on his balcony. In order to escape the fire, Viegas tossed his dog down to police officers below “like Matthew Stafford to Puka Nacua,” he would say later.
Viegas is a big Rams fan, and his dog that was saved is named “Rammy.”. He also has a tattoo of a Rams helmet on his arm and his son is named Luca Ramsey. Viegas lost all his Rams gear and memorabilia in the fire.
KTLA’s Chip Yost reported on the story and KTLA’s Samantha Cortese helped get the story to the Rams. After seeing what happened, the Rams reached out and are hosting Mark and his family at the game this weekend, with some surprises in the works. The story is a reminder of how football can do good things off the field as well.
This Rams fan lost everything in a fire. He threw his dog (Rammy) out a window, got his son (Luca Ramsey) to safety, and still has a great attitude. @ChipYost with a must-watch story and, as promised, we are asking @RamsNFL to help him out! pic.twitter.com/87hIUS6lwq

title: Rams vs. Cardinals Week 6: Who Has the Advantage at Every Position?
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams enter Week 6 needing a win after their disappointing loss on Monday Night Football to the Buffalo Bills. A game against the Arizona Cardinals might be exactly what the doctor ordered. The Rams get a chance to earn their first division win of the season. A win over the Cardinals will put them over the Seahawks and into second place in the NFC West.
Let's take a position-by-position look at how the Rams and Cardinals compare heading into Sunday's game and which team has the advantage at each spot.
There isn’t a competition when it comes to Matthew Stafford and Jacoby Brissett. Stafford is very clearly the better quarterback. Given how Stafford has played at times this year, the statistical comparison may be closer than it should be. Still, Stafford ranks 11th in EPA per pass while Brissett ranks 17th. Stafford is still one of the better quarterbacks in the NFL. If Stafford throws for 300 yards on Sunday, it would mark his fifth consecutive 300-yard passing game. That would set a new career-long streak and the second-longest in franchise history. That would set a new career-long streak and the second-longest in franchise history. Advantage: Rams
At some point, Jeremiyah Love may end up better than Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. However, Love will be out on Sunday , and the Cardinals haven’t provided him with the offensive infrastructure to succeed. The Rams will face Tyler Allgeier instead on Sunday, and they will have a huge advantage here. Advantage: Rams
Even before Marvin Harrison Jr. was traded, the Rams likely would have had the advantage at wide receiver. Following the trade, the discrepancy is even more clear. Michael Wilson is a solid player, but the player behind him is Kendrick Bourne. Puka Nacua and Davante Adams have the clear edge. Advantage: Rams
The Rams may have better depth at tight end, but Trey McBride is one of the best players in the NFL. He’s the player that the Cardinals’ offense runs through. Again, the Rams may have better depth with players like Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen, but the Cardinals get the advantage with McBride’s upside. Advantage: Cardinals
Heading into Sunday’s game against the Cardinals, the Rams will be without their starting left tackle in Alaric Jackson as he serves a suspension. That loss will be big, but the Cardinals are already without their starting left tackle as Paris Johnson is on injured reserve. They also just put their starting left guard, Isaiah Adams, on injured reserve. Even without Jackson, the Rams are better on the offensive line. Advantage: Rams
There is no doubt that the Cardinals have some young talent on the defensive line. Walter Nolen is a promising player, and both Josh Sweat and Baron Browning can get after the quarterback. However, the Cardinals rank 27th in pressure rate. The Rams are deep on the defensive line and have one of the best overall units in the NFL. Advantage: Rams
The Rams aren’t better at the linebacker position than many teams in the NFL. With that said, the Cardinals may actually be one of those few teams. Nate Landman forced his first fumble since Week 11 of last year, and Omar Speights has been solid against the run. Advantage: Rams
Again, the Cardinals have talent in the secondary. Max Melton is a good cornerback and Budda Baker can still play. Unfortunately, they just don’t have depth. Trent McDuffie showed up on Friday’s injury report, but the Rams have better cornerbacks and are deeper at safety. The Rams rank No. 1 in EPA allowed to tight ends this year, and the safeties are a big reason for that. Advantage: Rams
The Rams have the worst special teams unit through five games in the history of the NFL. Until they can prove otherwise, every team will have an advantage here. Advantage: Cardinals
There’s a lot to like about Mike LaFleur as a potential head coach, but he’s just not there yet. Even with his faults this season, Sean McVay is still one of the best coaches in the NFL. Nate Scheelhaase is a better offensive coordinator than Nathaniel Hackett, and Chris Shula is better than Nick Rallis, who may not last the season. Advantage: Rams

title: Rams' Sean McVay Opens Up About Facing Former Assistant Mike LaFleur
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to take on the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday . While it’s another game between two division rivals, it’s also the first meeting between Sean McVay and Mike LaFleur. LaFleur was on McVay’s coaching staff for three seasons from 2023 to 2025 and was hired as the head coach of the Cardinals this past offseason.
“Mike and I talk a lot. I haven't talked to him yet this week just because it's been busier than normal, but I will talk to him at some point,” said McVay. “I love Mike and it's about the Rams versus the Cardinals. We're going to try to get after him as good as we can this week, but there's a lot of good tape. He's done a great job there.”
Going up against a former assistant is nothing new for McVay. Since becoming a head coach himself in 2017, teams have typically pulled from his staff to try and recreate what he’s done. Over the past nine years, McVay has helped develop seven head coaches.
McVay is 5-8 against his former assistants, but five of those losses have come against Matt LaFleur, Mike’s brother. LaFleur was the Rams’ offensive coordinator in 2017 before leaving to be the offensive coordinator with the Tennessee Titans where he was able to call plays. Matt LaFleur was then hired as the head coach of the Green Bay Packers.
The LaFleur brothers and McVay have a long history. Matt LaFleur was on Kyle Shanahan’s offensive staff with the Houston Texans back in 2008. When Shanahan was hired as the offensive coordinator with Washington, LaFleur was the quarterbacks coach and McVay was hired as an offensive assistant. McVay and LaFleur became close in Washington. That’s also when McVay and Mike LaFleur met. Mike LaFleur would fly out to Washington after he graduated and sit in film rooms.
Before hiring Mike LaFleur, McVay had struggled to retain offensive coordinators for more than two seasons. Matt LaFleur left after his first season, and then Kevin O’Connell only lasted two years before he was hired away.After Liam Coen left following the 2022 season, McVay hired Mike LaFleur. With that comes some familiarity, but it isn’t something that McVay is concerned about going into Sunday’s game.
“Not so much because this has been very normal, if you will. Going against a lot of coaches that have done a great job for us,” McVay said. “Now, if we were an operation where you're stopped at the line of scrimmage and you're communicating code words like what we did earlier when we first got here, that would be a different deal because the defense can hear it and be able to react…He knows exactly what we've been trying to do, but there are always new iterations.”
While the Rams won a Super Bowl with O’Connell, an argument can be made that Mike LaFleur was the most successful offensive coordinator under McVay. The Rams made the playoffs in all three years and had the No. 1 offense in 2025 and also had a top-10 offense in 2023. LaFleur also played a key role in reshaping the Rams’ run game to be more multiple.
However, the biggest beneficiary of LaFleur’s presence may have been Matthew Stafford. Last season, Stafford won MVP for the first time in his career . From 2023-2025, Stafford ranked sixth in EPA per pass. To start the 2026 season, Stafford has ranked 11th.
“I think he's a fantastic coach. I have a great relationship with him,” said Stafford. “A ton of respect for Mike, what he's meant in my career and being a part of the staff here when I was playing. I have a ton of trust that he'll get that thing going over there pretty darn quick. Fired up to go play against him and see him.”
While Stafford is looking forward to facing his former offensive coordinator, LaFleur will now have the challenge of trying to stop the quarterback he spent three seasons working alongside. That respect goes both ways, as the new Cardinals head coach was equally complimentary of his former quarterback this week.
“His process is the most consistent I've ever been around in my life,” LaFleur said. “Ultimate professional, better person, obviously MVP/Hall of Fame quarterback, and I look forward to going against that challenge. When I took this, I told him how grateful I am for him. But at the same time, when it's time to go on Sunday, let's go. And I'm excited to watch our guys go compete."
McVay has become accustomed to seeing former assistants find success elsewhere, and LaFleur is the latest on that list . However, Week 6 is about much more than McVay going up against a former assistant. The Rams are 2-3 and trying to avoid falling further behind in the NFC West. Both sides know each other well, but that familiarity won't make Sunday's matchup any less important.

title: Trent McDuffie's Late Addition to Rams Injury Report Raises Concern Ahead of Week 6 vs. Cardinals
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams should be as healthy as they've been all season as they enter Week 6 . Only two players will enter Sunday’s game with an injury designation. Safety Kam Curl is officially listed as questionable as he was downgraded from being limited to a non-participant on Friday. Additionally, cornerback Trent McDuffie was a late addition to the injury report and is listed as questionable with a groin injury.
Despite McDuffie not participating in practice on Friday, the Rams don’t seem too concerned about his status going forward.
“Trent felt a little something in his groin so we're going to be smart with him,” said head coach Sean McVay. “He'll be listed as questionable, but he has the right mindset and mentality and we'll just see where we're at with that.”
McVay noted that the Rams were simply being smart with McDuffie and that it was just some soreness from the game that he felt ahead of practice.
After being a non-participant in practice on Wednesday and Thursday, tight end Davis Allen was limited on Friday. McVay noted that Allen was trending in the right direction, and the lack of a game designation would seem to imply that he will be available to play. Despite Curl not participating on Friday, McVay also said that he felt good about him.
Much like every team in the NFL at this point in the season, the Rams have their bumps and bruises, but for the most part are pretty healthy. The Rams could get another boost in the coming weeks as Myles Garrett works his way back from injury .
The Rams did not open Garrett’s practice window this week, but it could be something they look to do following Sunday’s game against the Cardinals.
“We've just taken it a week at a time so whenever we connect on Monday, I'll have that answer for you,” said McVay. “He has a good look in his eye and he's making good progress so we'll see.”
On the Cardinals' side, they’ll be without rookie running back Jeremiyah Love, which will be a hit to their offense and overall explosiveness. Love did not practice with an ankle injury all week and will be officially listed as out.
The Cardinals will also be without safeties Wydett Williams and Andrew Wingard. Additionally, safety Kitan Crawford (ankle), safety Budda Baker (rest), linebacker Zaven Collins (hip), and punter Blake Gilikin (back) will all be listed as questionable.
Over the last few weeks, the Rams have dealt with their share of injuries. However, they are finally starting to get healthy at the right time. For now, the Rams will have most of their key contributors available against the Cardinals as they look to get back on track.

title: Rams Midweek Report: Favorable Schedule Ahead, Myles Garrett Update, Sean McVay Concerns
full_text:
As the Los Angeles Rams sit at 2-3, it’s easy to be down on them after their loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football. It wasn’t just that the Rams lost, but how they lost that was so deflating. The Rams should have won, but it was special teams that cost them once again .
Given the issues on special teams, it’s hard to put a lot of faith in this team. They continuously invent new ways to lose. For the first time this season, the Rams are no longer Super Bowl favorites as that belongs to the San Francisco 49ers.
At the same time, if the Rams can figure it out, there is the potential for them to go on a serious run. Here is their schedule before the bye week in Week 11:
The combined record for those teams is 6-18-1. That’s the lowest strength of schedule over the next five games in the NFL.It’s important not to look too far ahead in the NFL, but those are five very winnable games. The Rams could easily go into their bye week with a 7-3 record. At that point, the Rams may only be one or two games back in the NFC West behind the 49ers.
Future Strength of Schedule (Next 5)
A 7-3 record isn’t guaranteed. The Rams still need to go out and take care of business. However, they are past the grueling opening stretch of their schedule. They are also set to get healthier as Myles Garrett gets closer to his return and they should get Terrance Ferguson back in three weeks.
The next game that the Rams will have to be concerned about is Week 13 against the Kansas City Chiefs. Even then, that’s a winnable game and the Rams are at home. Let’s say the 49ers lose to the Seahawks in Week 12 as well as one more game.That would set up a Week 14 matchup between the 9-3 Rams and the 10-2 49ers. A win there would put the Rams back on top in the NFC West.
The Rams might NEVER LOSE another game this season 😲 @heykayadams pic.twitter.com/yk5VMwL0Sq
That doesn’t mean that it isn’t still a long shot. There’s a reason the Rams have only a 14 percent chance of winning the NFC West right now. However, a lot can change in two months, especially as the Rams get Garrett back and they hopefully start to find their stride.
As the weeks have gone on, there has been growing anticipation for when Myles Garrett will make his return to the Rams. Over the past several weeks, I’ve been writing that Week 7 was the most realistic. While the team was optimistic that he could be back on Sunday, Week 7 was the more realistic timeline with Week 8 being a worst-case scenario. NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport confirmed that this week.
“My understanding was it was a six-week recovery from a knee surgery. He had the knee surgery on the Monday after Week 1, so Week 7 should be around when he’s ready, which could mean practicing this week and then playing next week. We’re getting to the window.”
. @RapSheet shares an update on Myles Garrett's knee injury and when he will return to play 👀⬇️ (via @RichEisenShow ) pic.twitter.com/u5pLuhvURk
McVay has already said that the team wouldn’t be opening Garrett’s window this week. The Rams’ head coach was asked about it on Tuesday and said, “We will not. Not this week.” Right now, as long as things go well, Garrett could make his return when the Rams play the Raiders next week.
Following Monday night’s loss to the Buffalo Bills, left tackle Alaric Jackson was caught on camera throwing a punch at edge rusher Bradley Chubb. It adds to the growing list of off-field issues from Jackson. On Tuesday, the NFL announced that Jackson would be suspended without pay for two games for an act of unsportsmanlike conduct.
WOAH... Alaric Jackson punched Bradley Chubb after the game finished 😳 pic.twitter.com/377C2MNuBX
However, watching the video, it can be seen that Chubb potentially makes contact with Jackson first. Now, to be clear, that doesn’t give Jackson the right to react in the way that he did. With that said, Jackson appealed the two-game suspension and won. His suspension was officially reduced down to one game. Jackson will be eligible to return next week against the Las Vegas Raiders.
That will be good news for the Rams. On Sunday, they go against a Cardinals defense that has struggled to generate pressure. However, the Raiders will present more of a challenge with Maxx Crosby. They’ll appreciate having Jackson back for that game.
Through five weeks, some have wanted the Rams to make a change at their special teams coordinator spot. While there’s no doubt that the Rams need more production out of their special teams unit, making a change at the coordinator spot after just five games likely wouldn’t fix anything. The issues run far deeper than the coordinator or even the kicker for that matter.
“I have a lot of confidence in Bubba Ventrone,” said McVay on Tuesday. “There are no changes that are going to be made there. We're going to keep working. This isn't the first time that we've had adversity and the first time that we've had some different things that I have to do a better job of.”
In a matter of three weeks, the Rams have made changes at both the returner and kicker positions, cutting Xavier Smith and moving on from Harrison Mevis. Given what Ventrone has said about Ethan Evans, it’s fair to assume he’s on a short leash as well. These are changes that should have been made in the offseason, but the Rams are working on it now.
Earlier this week, I wrote about how McVay has played a larger role in the Rams being 2-3 than some would like to believe. With that said, something seems off about McVay this year. When the Rams returned home from Australia, an episode of 60 Minutes aired. In the episode, McVay appeared to be on edge because of a "bad practice." In the episode, McVay appeared to be on edge because of ‘bad practice’.
“I feel bad that you guys are doing this incredible story and you know, and I'm not in a good place right now. I'm not happy with how practice went,” Los Angeles Rams Coach Sean McVay tells 60 Minutes. https://t.co/MCHgGz2psB pic.twitter.com/r2k0pogPRq
After the loss to the Denver Broncos, McVay spoke to the media for two minutes before ducking out of the press conference. The Athletic’s Mike Sando noted in a recent column that, “Some who know McVay suspected from afar that something has been bothering him this season. They thought he seemed too cranky over traveling around the world for the opener in Australia.”
You can go all the way back to the draft, when McVay didn’t seem pleased after the Rams invested a first-round pick in a new quarterback. When McVay and Snead addressed the media following the Simpson pick, McVay almost seemed mad.
I’m not sure what it is specifically and it would be unfair to speculate. Still, McVay seems to be more on edge than he has in recent years.
As expected, the defense is getting a lot of criticism for its performance on Monday night against the Bills. Josh Allen and James Cook combined for 232 yards rushing. It was almost reminiscent of the Divisional Round playoff loss to the Philadelphia Eagles two years ago.
However, I do think they were better than the numbers would suggest. On Monday night, 73.7 percent of Josh Allen’s passing attempts were considered “short”. Allen’s 12 completions were his fewest in a game that he’s started since Week 5 of 2024. In the fourth quarter, Allen had an average depth of target of 5.3 yards. Without Allen’s 44-yard arm punt in the second quarter, Allen would have had an average depth of target of 5.47 yards for the game.
Shannon Sharpe says why are the  LA Rams paying Trent McDuffie $33 million and Jaylen Watson $20 million if they can’t cover Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir pic.twitter.com/eCTSRnOLZa
This is a secondary that is very difficult to throw on. Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson combined to allow zero receptions and zero yards while recording an interception and two pass breakups. There’s no doubt that the Rams need to do better when it comes to tackling at the second and third levels. That’s where the Bills really exploited them.
Sometimes it's easy to forget that…

title: Rams vs. Cardinals Week 6 Prediction: Preview, Matchups, and Players to Watch
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams enter Week 6 sitting at 2-3 ahead of a game against the Arizona Cardinals. A game against the Cardinals might be exactly what the doctor ordered after the Rams lost in overtime on Monday night to the Buffalo Bills.
While the Rams enter at 2-3 and need a win, the Cardinals are in a much different spot. The Cardinals just traded away one of their more talented wide receivers in Marvin Harrison Jr. After beating the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 1, they have lost four straight.
The Cardinals have typically provided the Rams a ‘get right’ opportunity in past seasons. After losing two straight last year, the Rams beat the Cardinals in Week 18 before going into the playoffs. It was what the Rams needed to feel good heading into the postseason. Following the loss to the Bills, the Rams need that more than ever.
Heading into Sunday, the Rams will be without left tackle Alaric Jackson as he serves a suspension from the NFL following an incident after the Bills’ game. That will leave the Rams with David Quessenberry at left tackle. The last time the Rams were without Jackson against the Cardinals, they lost, 41-10, and Dennis Gardeck had three sacks. The Cardinals have generated pressure on just 30.3 percent of dropbacks this season, which is the second-lowest rate in the NFL.
The Rams will likely help Quessenberry as much as they can with a tight end and try to slow down Sweat. However, Sweat still has the ability to blow up a gameplan if he can get to the quarterback, and Sunday provides an opportunity. If the Rams are going to beat the Cardinals, they need to protect Stafford, and that starts with slowing down Sweat.
It’s very possible that the Cardinals are short-handed going into Sunday. Harrison Jr. didn’t play a big role in the offense but was still talented. First-round pick and running back Jeremiyah Love could miss the game with an ankle injury. Without Harrison and Love, it’s been difficult for the Cardinals to generate explosives. Sunday should be an opportunity for the defense to get back on track.
One of the few options that the Cardinals will have available to them in the passing game is tight end Trey McBride. McBride has 19 receptions for 139 yards against linebackers this season, which is the most in the NFL. The Cardinals will likely look to get McBride matched up on Nate Landman. Meanwhile, the Rams will look to use Lake on McBride. Rams defensive backs have allowed the fewest receptions and yards to tight ends in 2026.
This is the first time that McVay will be going up against Mike LaFleur after he left to be the head coach of the Cardinals. McVay is 5-8 all-time against his former coordinators, but five of those losses are against Matt LaFleur. Unfortunately for Mike LaFleur, his roster may not be talented enough to win on Sunday.
With three receptions in Week 6, Nacua can surpass Michael Thomas for the most receptions by a player in his first 50 games in NFL history. If he gets 100 yards, he’ll have the third-most games with at least 100 yards by a player in his first four seasons. Nacua had 17 receptions last week and has 100 yards in each of his last two games. There’s a good chance that he hits both milestones.
The Rams will have a new kicker on Sunday against the Cardinals. It’s unlikely that Sunday’s game comes down to a last-second kick like last week, but it’s certainly something to keep an eye on. Blake Grupe will make his Rams debut, and it will be interesting to see how much the Rams test him, if at all.
Last season, Blake Corum had the first 100-yard game of his career as the Rams beat the Cardinals, 45-17. Corum rushed 12 times for 128 yards and had two touchdowns. Corum hasn’t been as involved in recent weeks, but I believe that changes on Sunday.I’m predicting Corum will display some of the explosiveness he showed in the early weeks of the season and have a big game.
Technically, Donald got his first sack on Josh Allen last week. However, it was called back because of a penalty in the secondary. Donald has been quiet this season and hasn’t shown up often on the stat sheet. The Cardinals just placed guard Isaiah Adams on injured reserve. That could open things up for Donald to finally get to the quarterback.
Through the first five weeks, the Rams h ave had a special teams mistake of some sort in every game . Those mistakes reached a breaking point against the Bills as the Rams lost because of a blocked field goal. With so much focus on special teams, that unit will have a lot of pressure to perform. For the first time this season, I think we get a clean game out of that unit.
McVay said it best on Monday night when he emphasized that the Rams can’t let the Bills beat them twice. A game against the Cardinals should allow the Rams to get past that, move on, and feel good about themselves going forward. While the Cardinals have been feisty at times, they simply don’t have the playmakers or depth. The only way the Rams lose this game is if they beat themselves with turnovers and special teams mistakes. Prediction: Rams 34, Cardinals 17

title: Grading Every Raiders' Position Group Following Loss vs. Bills
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders have lost three straight games. Las Vegas faced the Buffalo Bills at home on Sunday and lost to one of the league's best teams for a third consecutive week. The three teams the Raiders have lost to have a combined record of 14-3 after Week 5.
Conversely, the three teams the Raiders have beaten have a combined record of 2-15. Las Vegas' Week 6 loss only confirms they are somewhere in the middle of the two, and are likely not as bad as they looked against the New England Patriots in Week 5.
Below are the grades for every Raiders' position group based on Sunday's outing.
The Bills' defense intercepted Kirk Cousins' pass that was essentially thrown into double coverage. Then, the Bills' offense started their next drive at the Raiders' 32-yard line and scored a touchdown a few plays later. With the Raiders already down by three points, that swung the game.
Las Vegas' offense continues to stall out for long stretches, especially in the third quarter. This area specifically is where Cousins' familiarity with Klint Kubiak and Andrew Janocko should kick in more.
Scoring a flurry of points late after falling behind by double digits, in large part because of the offense's inability to score points for three and a half quarters, is fool's gold, not sustainable, and does not equate to wins, but it does make the game look closer than it may have actually been.
Still, Cousins is the best quarterback Las Vegas has had in years.
The Raiders must keep mixing up the run calls, concepts, and designs. Ashton Jeanty continues to make an impact through the air and on the ground, but the Raiders need more from him, Las Vegas' other running backs, and the offensive line.
Connor Heyward played well.
The unit looked better with Jalen Nailor on the field.
Las Vegas' pass blocking was solid, for the most part, but the running lanes are simply not there.
Las Vegas' tight ends continued to make their case as the league's best group. Michael Mayer registered seven catches for 95 yards. Brock Bowers finished with four catches for 70 yards. Both continue to give glimpses of what's possible when the Raiders add more pass-catchers.
Las Vegas' defensive line generated more pressure on Josh Allen than they did against Drake Maye last week. However, the unit also failed to bring Allen down several times when it could have, which led to extended plays against a shaky defensive backfield.
The Raiders' struggle to stop the run is also largely attributed to the defensive line.
Las Vegas' cornerbacks have struggled as expected through the first part of the season. With Las Vegas' primary focus on defense this week likely being eliminating big plays, their cornerbacks did about as well as they could.
Las Vegas' defense is still a work in progress, but the past three weeks have been valuable for the Raiders' young defensive backfield.
With Las Vegas' defensive backfield shutting down big downfield passes, Nakobe Dean's presence was felt once again. Quay Walker had a solid performance overall, but the Raiders are still learning how to use him.
Las Vegas' inability to consistently stop the run with primarily their defensive line is often leaving Walker between a rock and a hard place.
The Raiders' defense gave up big plays through the air against the Kansas City Chiefs and the Patriots. Several of those big plays came against the safeties. The Raiders largely eliminated big plays against the Bills, which gave them a chance down the stretch.
Long term, Las Vegas needs additional help at safety and cornerback.
AJ Cole averaged 55 yards per punt against the Bills.
After missing his first field goal of the season in Week 5, Gay registered another clean day of work. The veteran made all three field goal attempts and all three extra point attempts. Gay has been automatic.
Even his lone miss of the season hit the goal post in somewhat windy conditions.
After fumbling the ball in Weeks 4 and 5, Las Vegas simply getting through their kick return with possession is a win. However, as they move forward with their rebuild, finding dynamic returners could help expedite the process.
It is much easier to find two or three returners who can flip the field, if not score while returning kickoffs, than it is to revamp the rest of the roster.
The Raiders did not log a punt return against the Bills . Through the season's first six games, Las Vegas has averaged just over 14 punt return yards per game. Overall, the Raiders' punt return unit has been nearly nonexistent.
Yet this may reflect the state of punt returns across today's league, rather than an issue unique to the Raiders.
Ezekiel is a former Sports Editor from the Western Herald and former Atlanta Falcons beat writer.

title: 3 Overreactions to Raiders Competitive Loss vs. Bills
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders were once the talk of the town in the NFL three weeks ago. However, early-season success can be a tease, as the Raiders lost their third straight game to the Buffalo Bills, 33-30.
Once again, the Raiders fell behind late despite leading in periods and staying in phase with the Bills throughout the contest. It is becoming clear that even with the loss, Las Vegas is establishing a competitive culture that could be beneficial long-term. Nonetheless, losing three games in a row is tough sledding, as I share my biggest overreactions to Sunday's back-and-forth showdown in the desert.
It's clear that Ashton Jeanty is still hurt, and his efficiency is average at best. He continues to drop passes despite creating separation out of the backfield, and doesn't seem to be confident in his ability to jump into adjacent gaps and find creases to run through for big plays.
The one player who does is rookie running back Mike Washington Jr., and he might be the Raiders' best chance at a successful run game in the short term as Jeanty heals. It is important to note that the latter should still be in the long-term plans, but the Raiders need more consistency, and Washington has provided that, rushing for nearly five yards per carry. It should be considered this week as Las Vegas hosts the flailing Los Angeles Rams.
Once again, the Raiders' linebackers were making plays as former Georgia teammates Quay Walker and Nakobe Dean were impactful all game long. However, I thought Dean was the best player on defense, not named Maxx Crosby, tallying 12 tackles and a tackle for loss as he flew all over the field to make stops in the run game.
For the first time in his career, Dean is healthy, and the Raiders are reaping the benefits. Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard needs his MIKE linebacker at all times, who is consistently showing up this season.
Losing three consecutive games is not fun. Raider Nation has seen a lot of those streaks in recent years, but this year feels different because of how competitive the team has been in these types of games, coming close to taking down both Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen on their home turf. As the teams remaining on the Raiders' schedule begin to shape themselves, the future looks brighter.
Depending on how you may feel about the Raiders, there is a clear path to eight wins this season, but nothing more. This team has too many flaws to overcome if it wants to come close to a winning campaign. However, a five-game increase in win totals would be a fantastic year for the rebuilding Raiders.
Jared Feinberg, a native of western North Carolina, has written about NFL football for nearly a decade. He has contributed to several national outlets and is now part of our On SI team as an NFL team reporter. Jared graduated from UNC Asheville with a bachelor's degree in mass communications and later pursued his master's degree at UNC Charlotte. You can follow Jared Feinberg on Twitter at @JRodNFLDraft

title: Raiders vs. Bills: Winners & Losers From Las Vegas
full_text:
LAS VEGAS, Nev.—For the second time in three weeks, the Raiders faced a Super Bowl favorite team at Allegiant Stadium, and for the second time in three weeks, the team overachieved, despite a roster level far inferior to the team they were facing; they had no one to blame for the loss but themselves.
The Raiders (3-3) fell 33-30 to the Buffalo Bills (5-1), and despite a valiant performance in the midst of a Raiders rebuilding season, they beat themselves.
Everything we told you had to happen for the Raiders to win did, except the score.
I told you they had to score 30 points; they did.
I told you they had to hold Josh Allen to less than 50 yards rushing; they did: one.
I also told you that for them to win, they were not good enough to beat the Bills and themselves; I was right about that.
The Raiders are watching film together today, licking their wounds from a series of self-inflicted wounds that cost them the upset.
The NFL is not a league of moral victories. Klint Kubiak shone last week, and he made it clear after the game what he thinks of moral victories.
"I just want to say very disappointed. Very disappointed that we didn't get it done today. Credit to Buffalo; they played a great game. As a team, we did not close the game, and there's plenty of improvement. But we are not satisfied with any moral victories, and we're a 3-3 football team with everything ahead of us.”
While we agree there are no moral victories in the NFL, there are tremendous efforts and signs of progress for a rebuilding team, like last night.
So, as always, I present this week’s winners and losers.
The Raiders were embarrassed last week in New England. I told you all week I didn’t expect the Raiders to win, but I also didn’t expect them to be embarrassed. They weren’t tonight. I told Kubiak there are no moral victories in the NFL, but I asked if he could appreciate how they responded. The level-headed first-year head coach could, and did.
"Yeah, that's the expectation. We have really talented players and that was the expectation to bounce back. That's the type of football that we need to play, but we got to do it for four quarters. We've got to get the ball in the red zone. We're 2-for-5 in the red zone, and that's unacceptable. And that starts with me."
QB Kirk Cousins isn’t willing to rest on the team overachieving and being 3-3 right now.
“But it's a week-to-week league, and so you just feel like no matter what has happened, what has transpired, 0-6, 6-0, or somewhere in between, you've got to come back and do it again. And your next opponent doesn't really care what happened the previous six weeks. So, they are each their own stages. You get to the end of 17 and you settle them up, but they really are their own stages, and we've got to treat it that way and be absolute pros each time we step between the white lines."
In fact, the red zone issues Kubiak referred to were big in Cousins' mind as well. They should have been on everyone's mind, since that inefficiency cost the Raiders the win with that one stat. Cousins addressed it.
"Those are the things we'll be talking about tomorrow, and then honestly the other several possessions run together right now. But anytime you leave points on the board in the red zone, it's hard."
The Raiders threw for 313 yards but ran for only 65. Despite the horrific imbalance, Kubiak found a reason to be encouraged.
"Yeah, honestly, I am encouraged that I thought the run game was better. Has not been good enough. At the end of the game, once a game like that, you've got to play to your strengths. So, that was what we did."
He added about the leading rusher Mike Washington Jr., "Yeah, he gave us a spark. He did some good stuff. He's been practicing well, had some good runs for us, and between him and Dylan [Laube] and Ashton [Jeanty], we're going to play all those guys."
After starting the first three games of the season with very few penalties, the last three games have been epidemic, including seven against the Bills, which were devastating. Kubiak shouldered all the blame.
"Yeah, I got to go look at everyone individually, but seven penalties is seven too many."
The worst was the third (and only one today) false start by center Tyler Linderbaum. Something that sparked the head man's ire.
"It's happened three times, and it's killing us, absolutely killing us, and I have not fixed it. So, shame on me. It's on me to get it fixed."
The Raiders had all the momentum after tying the game at the end of the first half. After getting the ball to start the second half, they had a chance to really take off. Instead, they came out flat and fell on their face. Something Kubiak identified and was less than appreciative of.
"I'm really upset with how we're starting the third quarter. Go three and out. That's disappointing. Every game has adversity. The game's not over in the third quarter when you go three and out, but it really kills more than that."
Cousins chimed in on the third quarter woes as well.
"That was another one of those moments where I don't know what's going on. The refs are just suddenly walking the ball further and further down the field, and I'm getting the next play call, and I'm like, 'Okay, I know it's going to be first and 10, much closer than I thought it was going to be,' but I don't have time or energy to ask, 'Why is that?' So, I don't know what happened. I just know we got much better field position, and that was really all I had time to think about."
Cousins had one bad play, an interception, but considering he was 23-for-41 for the aforementioned 313 yards with two touchdowns, Kubiak was thrilled with his QB.
"Gritty, gutty, just the same guy you guys have seen all season. He's playing superb football right now."
Kubiak wasted no time talking about what his team needs to learn.
QB Kirk Cousins agrees with his head coach and friend.
"Yeah, there's no doubt that, that's what it is. We got to find ways to close. You got to find the inches in the fourth quarter. You can't go out in second to last possession and have three incompletions. You can't in the third quarter throw an interception that gives them a short field and they get a touchdown off of it. You can't go two for five in the red zone.”
A frustrated Cousins wasn’t done.
“You know third and goal, we got to come away with those four point plays and get the touchdown, not the kick in the field goal. Those are all the plays throughout the game that you look back on and you say, it didn't give us a chance to win. And it's just about making plays. You got to make plays and be smart and manage the game well. And if you do that, you'd like to think that you give yourself a chance to close it out in the fourth quarter."
Cousins has seen a lot in his career and is the unquestioned leader of the offense. He talked about how the Raiders can snap the losing streak.
"All I know to do is go back to work to have candid conversations on Monday that make us better as a football team. To have your process, your habits that get you ready to play well, and then to go through that process to not change anything when you're winning, to not change too much when you're losing."
"I think the only part you change is when you go back and see where we got to be better, and you emphasize that during the week. But we just got to go back to work and just put the work in and expect that if you do that, that the breaks will fly your way."
Cousins and Tucker’s chemistry is growing. Each week, Cousins is learning to trust him to get the football, and the Michigan State Spartan praised his wide receiver.
"I mean, it was a great catch by him on the first one. Great design by our coaches to get him in that position where he's open like that. The second one, he just can roll. I played with DeSean Jackson, I play with Aldrick Robinson, so I played with 4.2 guys; he can roll. And I came off the field, I said, 'I think he's faster than I realize he is.'”

title: Raider Nation Hopeful After Week 6 Defeat Against Bills
