title: Vikings Week 6: 3 Most Important Things to Watch for During Minnesota's Bye This Weekend
full_text:
The bye week is always a bittersweet event for any NFL fan.
While Vikings fans won’t be able to watch their team try to keep their unbeaten streak alive this weekend, the time off will let the team work through a growing list of offensive injuries. It also allows all of us to plop down on the couch with a bag of chips, a bowl of Top the Tater and a beverage of choice for a relatively stress-free Sunday of football.
Still, fans of the Purple and Gold have a few key storylines to keep an eye on this weekend. Here are three things to watch for in Week 6 with the Vikings on break.
The Vikings are one of two NFC North teams with an early Week 6 bye this season, as the Lions are also off for the week. That leaves the Bears and Packers as your two divisional rivals to rage-watch this weekend.
Luckily, they just played each other last week, so you won’t have to awkwardly root for one of them to win.
The Bears travel to Atlanta on Sunday to face a feisty Falcons squad . Atlanta should have Michael Penix Jr. back at quarterback barring any setbacks, after leaving last week’s game with a rib injury. The Packers will then host a desperate 2-3 Cowboys team at Lambeau for Sunday Night Football.
Needless to say, Vikings fans should have clear rooting interests in both games, as Minnesota can gain even more separation early in the divisional race. A loss would put both teams at an even 3-3 on the season.
After five weeks, only three undefeated teams remain in the NFL. The Vikings and 49ers are both 5-0, while the Chiefs come off a Week 5 bye at 4-0. No one gets a prize for being the last unbeaten team, but bragging rights and some playoff implications are on the line.
The Chiefs will host the winless Chargers at Arrowhead Sunday afternoon in a game they’ll be heavily favored to win. With this being an all-AFC matchup, the Vikings get no real benefit from the Chiefs taking their first loss of the season. Even so, Minnesota fans should root for an upset if they want to stand alone atop the mountain of unbeatens.
The 49ers' matchup against the Commanders, on the other hand, actually carries some weight.
It may seem ridiculous to discuss potential playoff tiebreakers before we’re even through October, but every game matters if Minnesota and San Francisco are battling for the NFC’s top seed throughout the season (h/t: ESPN's Adam Schefter).
Five weeks in: pic.twitter.com/KAhZ7tdjj3
The two NFC powerhouses will meet in Mexico City on Nov. 22, and any buffer Minnesota can build before then will be a major advantage. A Commanders victory at Levi’s Stadium would be a great first step.
With the Vikings pushing for a deep playoff run and the Nov. 10 trade deadline approaching quickly , it’s worth keeping an eye on teams that could be potential sellers. The Chargers, Titans and Dolphins are the obvious candidates, as none of them have even won a game so far in 2026. Miami is on their bye this week, but L.A.'s matchup against Kansas City and Tennessee’s trip to Indianapolis are worth monitoring for potential trade targets.
Chargers' pass rusher Khalil Mack is one name to watch as the Vikings' defense may look to add more weapons to its already aggressive arsenal (h/t: ESPN 's Adam Schefter).
After two trades last week, here are more names to monitor ahead of next month’s #NFL trade deadline. pic.twitter.com/i9XdEC0oPQ
The Eagles are also a fascinating team to watch as their season appears to be spiraling quickly. A fourth consecutive loss to the Panthers could prompt general manager Howie Roseman to make some dramatic roster decisions.

title: Just-Released WR Should Have Vikings' Attention as Depth Remains an Issue
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings remain undefeated as their bye week continues , but that doesn't mean they should be satisfied with their performance so far.
Although the Purple and Gold's special teams and defensive units are among the NFL's best, the Vikings' offense hasn't been firing on all cylinders this season. Sure, things were slowly improving heading into the bye, but there's still plenty of room for improvement—especially at wide receiver.
Outside of Justin Jefferson, who's been his usual dynamic self, Minnesota's wideout situation has been a bit of a mess over the past five games. Jordan Addison was picking up steam but hasn't played since Week 4 due to a hamstring injury. The Jauan Jennings signing has been a colossal bust so far ; Tai Felton has been invisible more often than not, and Myles Price has been too, who fumbled against the Saints last week.
Clearly, the Vikings need some WR help, and while general manager Nolan Teasley could look to the trade market, he should be interested in a newly available name that just hit the market.
The Vikings recently added Odell Beckham Jr. to their practice squad, and now they can sign another ex-Giant. On Friday morning, the Colts announced they've released veteran WR Darius Slayton , who signed with Indianapolis last month, two weeks after New York released him .
We have released WR Darius Slayton.
With their top wideout, Alec Pierce, dealing with a foot injury, the Colts brought Slayton in for help. The 29-year-old playmaker, however, didn't suit up for any games and was scratched in Week 5 due to a knee injury.
Assuming that the knee issue isn't severe, though, the Vikings should at least kick the tires to see if Slayton is open to joining Murray's arsenal.
Drafted 171st overall in 2019, Slayton was a reliable weapon throughout his seven years with the Giants. He was often available (missing 11 regular-season games) and productive, hitting the 700-yard mark four times while averaging 651.3 receiving yards over his last four seasons. A large part of that success stems from his blazing speed, with a 4.39-second 40-yard dash time .
For what it's worth, Jefferson and tight end T.J. Hockenson are the only Vikings on pace to surpass 700 receiving yards this season.
It's been a few years since Slayton achieved that feat, but that doesn't mean he can't help the Vikings.
He just recorded 37 catches for 538 receiving yards and a touchdown in 14 games, averaging 14.5 yards per catch, only slightly below his career average (15.0). Slayton's four penalties last season might raise some concerns, but hopefully it's something that head coach Kevin O'Connell can iron out of his game.
Slayton's reputation as a decent human being is another reason why the Vikings should want him in the locker room. He won the 2025 Alan Page Community Award for his community work in the New York area, and that's a big deal since the award is considered "the NFLPA’s highest honor." More leadership like that is never a bad thing.
It also wouldn't hurt to inject another veteran face into the practice squad after signing Beckham.
Dillon Bell and Michael Briscoe have potential, but they're both undrafted rookies whom the Vikings might not be ready to throw into the fire yet. Second-year WR Jeshaun Jones made his first-career catch (h/t Minnesota Vikings UK) against the Saints in Week 5, but even then, he played more special teams snaps (11) than offense (six).
First career catch for Jeshaun Jones 🙌 📺 Watch live on @nflondazn 🎧 Listen live on @talkSPORT pic.twitter.com/novGysE5yv
Slayton likely won't be a significant upgrade over the current taxi-squad options, but his experience stemming from 106 career games (78 starts) can't be understated. The Vikings would be better off throwing him into a high-stakes late-season game than an unproven undrafted rookie, who might not be ready for that kind of pressure.
Injuries around the NFL will keep piling up with each passing week, meaning teams will only get more desperate to sign a veteran WR like Slayton. If the Vikings are wise, they'll use their available time during the bye week to contact the just-released playmaker, potentially taking the first of several steps toward addressing their receiver-related depth concerns.

title: Aaron Jones' Role Must Change Significantly After Vikings' Bye
full_text:
Aaron Jones Sr. has been an absolute workhorse for the Minnesota Vikings this season. Through the first five weeks of the season, the veteran running back has played 73 percent of the team's offensive snaps despite being 31 years old and having an extensive injury history.
Jones was forced to carry the team on the ground when Jordan Mason needed surgery on his thumb and was placed on injured reserve. The Vikings' backup running back is eligible to return in Week 7, and having him back should make things a lot easier on Jones.
In Week 5 against the New Orleans Saints, Jones played 87% of Minnesota's offensive snaps. Although he turned that into 25 carries for 113 yards and a touchdown, plus three catches for four yards, the Purple and Gold cannot afford to continue working him to this extent.
Mason will be in line to handle a healthy amount of work, but the Vikings will not phase Jones out of the offense completely. Relying on a one-two punch of the running back duo will yield the best results in future weeks.
It is a shame that rookie running back Demond Claiborne and veteran backup DeeJay Dallas couldn't pitch in more while Mason was out, but Minnesota was fortunate that Jones was able to do so much while his backup got healthy.
To put things in perspective, Claiborne has participated in 7% of the Vikings' offensive snaps this season, while Dallas has been on the field for 12%. It is even worse when looking at only the Saints game, where Dallas played five offensive snaps and Claiborne played four.
Minnesota can't afford to have Mason miss any more time, and Jones has been too valuable to risk by playing the ridiculous number of snaps he's had recently. Although Claiborne and Dallas can't be trusted to give the running back duo some relief, Jones and Mason need to lean on each other to provide rest during the remaining weeks of the 2026 NFL season.
It wouldn't be entirely shocking if Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley explored free agency and the trade market to try to get a running back to help Jones and Mason. Unless head coach Kevin O'Connell feels comfortable with the current positional depth chart, there needs to be some change made to keep the top two contributors healthy and available.
Expect Minnesota to do what they can to cut Jones' offensive snaps starting in Week 7. Although he did an admirable job while Mason was out, the Vikings can't afford to continue working him the way they have over the last few weeks.

title: 3 Vikings Firmly on Thin Ice During the Week 6 Bye (Josh Metellus Is Becoming an Issue)
full_text:
The Week 6 bye couldn't have come sooner for a Vikings team dealing with a long list of injuries. Despite those ailments, the Purple and Gold are 5-0 and sitting atop the NFC North as they reach the second half of their bye week.
Although the Vikings are undefeated, there are still issues to be addressed . While some players are thriving this season, others are struggling to make a positive impact when on the field.
Some of the Vikings' players are on thin ice after multiple weeks of ineffectiveness. The clock is ticking on them to find their role on the team. If they can't, they may end up losing snaps or even their job on the team
Minnesota's big free-agent wide receiver signing this offseason has been a flop this season. In the team's first five games, Jauan Jennings has played 201 offensive snaps and has only caught two of the five passes thrown his way for nine yards. Not exactly worth the $8 million cash he's earning this season, per Spotrac.
There are already rumblings that Jennings could potentially be on the trade block since he has struggled to contribute to the Vikings' passing attack this year. Minnesota would be silly not to listen to offers to try to recoup an asset before the trade deadline. Needless to say, don't be surprised if he's traded, assuming that he remains on thin ice.
The Vikings prepared to limit the defensive snaps of veteran safety Harrison Smith by drafting Miami defensive back Jakobe Thomas in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft and signing undrafted free agent Jacob Thomas out of James Madison.
While both those rookies are growing and developing, Minnesota has played Josh Metellus on every defensive snap this season. In 295 defensive snaps and four special teams snaps, he has earned a putrid Pro Football Focus grade of 40.2 , ranking him 90th out of 96 qualifying safeties this year.
Metellus has played well in previous seasons, but hasn't found his footing in 2026. Minnesota will be patient with the versatile defender because they know he can rise above the recent struggles, but until one of the Thomas rookies is ready for a bigger role, he will need to be a workhorse .
Sometimes the hype around a player gets so out of hand that they can't possibly live up to the expectations. The Vikings brought back Aaron Jones Sr. on a reworked deal and have Jordan Mason returning to injured reserve after the bye
The Vikings drafted Demond Claiborne in the sixth round of the 2026 NFL Draft to hopefully become a contributor for Minnesota. Instead, Claiborne and DeeJay Dallas have been unable to share the burden of rushing the ball with Jones.
Claiborne isn't in danger of losing his job, but his ineffectiveness could lead the Vikings to look for a more reliable third option in the backfield . So far, he has run the ball six times for 13 yards and caught two passes for eight yards while only playing 18 offensive snaps.

title: 4 Winners, 2 Losers in Patriots' Hard-Fought Win vs. Jets
full_text:
It was far from pretty, but the New England Patriots won their third-consecutive game on Sunday in their 26-19 slugfest against the New York Jets.
While the Patriots ultimately took him the win in a one-possession game, the team had plenty of ups and downs throughout the way
Here are the biggest winners, and losers, from the Patriots' win over the Jets.
Henry has re-emerged as a top receiving threat for the Patriots' offense in recent weeks. The veteran has out-performed his best performance from the first three weeks of the season in each of the past three weeks.
On Sunday, the 31-year-old caught four of his five targets, plus tallied 48 yards and scored New England's final touchdown of the day.
"Yeah, it was fun," Henry said after the win. "It was cool to go out there and hit some adversity, bounce back, get some adversity and bounce back. It's hard to win in this league. Their defense was throwing a lot at us. We were able to respond, and our defense came up with some big stops there and some timely drops. It was a lot of fun."
In Brown's second game as a Patriot--and first since being activated from injured reserve --he struggled substantially. The former Philadelphia Eagle hauled in just three of his 10 targets and went for 27 yards. Mixed in were a handful of drops, plus a mishandled onside kick (which New England was fortunate to recover).
A.J. Brown dropped every one of these footballs today pic.twitter.com/WYzCY0YSBF
"I think he could've probably made a few more plays, come down with a few more plays," Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said. "He's been out for a while. I know that he wanted to do well for his football team, and unfortunately it wasn't his best effort. I know that he knows that, and we have all the confidence in the world in A.J. just to be able to finish those plays."
Byard made his way to New England after a First-team All-Pro season in 2025. The veteran's performance on Sunday served as a reminder of why he deserved that nod.
One of the Patriots' defensive captains, Byard tallied seven total tackles and combined for a run stuff with Gabe Jacas in the team's win over the Jets. Plus, the 33-year-old flew across the field for a pass breakup which saved a potential touchdown.
"I think for us as a defense, we feel like we are a dominant defense and wanted to be able to put on a dominant performance," Byard said. "It just didn't feel like that. Now, obviously we're going to watch the film and find things to correct, which I'm sure there's a lot out there, but it's a lot of good too."
For the first time of his career, Drake Maye has thrown three or more touchdown passes in three consecutive games. While the rest of the 24-year-old's final stat line may not jump off the page (18/32 passing, 235 yards), those numbers were also signifcantly deflated due to dropped passes.
Ultimately, New England's young quarterback has been back in MVP form the past three weeks.
"I think Drake Maye continues to stay very even-keeled," Vrabel said. "I think that he probably is much more mature than I probably think in my head, just being 24. But I think that he is very even-keeled."
Credit where credit is due: there is no world where Henderson should have been healthy enough to play on Sunday. The 23-year-old suffered a high-ankle sprain a gainst the Las Vegas Raiders last week, an injury that oftentimes lands players on injured reserve.
Henderson had just eight touches on Sunday, which went for 40 total yards. More important, however, was his fumble in the third quarter to set up New York inside of New England's 40-yard line. Fortunately for the Patriots, they held the Jets to just a field goal. However, a touchdown would have tied the game up for New York.
After the Patriots' 24-21 preseason win over the Eagles on Aug. 22, Vrabel gave a blunt assessment of his team's depth.
"I do not think we have a very deep team," he said. "So I think we have to make sure that we are preparing our football team and that we are doing everything that we can to keep our best players available"
Since then, New England has dealt with a plethora of injuries. A week ago, the Patriots had just three active cornerbacks against the Raiders. This Sunday, the team was down to its final offensive lineman after a slurry of players went down.
Yet, the back-end of the Patriots roster stepped up. New England did not allow a single sack to a New York squad which had been tied for the fourth-most in the NFL. Plus, between the three reserve linemen who saw action on Sunday ( Caleb Lomu , Matt Pryor , Walter Rouse ), none allowed a pressure.
"Just try to get the guys ready," Vrabel said when asked about his team's depth. "I think that that's something that we targeted. We knew that it was probably unique to add 10 players at the end of training camp that were new, and there was going to be some growing pains getting those guys ready...But then certainly I enjoy watching those guys go out and take advantage of their opportunity."
But New England's offensive lineman were far from the only ones who stepped up against New York.
The Patriots' third-string running back, Corey Kiner, played a substantial role in clinching the win. The 24-year-old had eight carries on New England's final full drive of the game, which took over six minutes off of the clock. The former Arizona Cardinal finished the afternoon with 11 carries for 57 yards, plus he took the second half's opening kickoff return 31 yards.
"It feels great," Kiner said about his performance. "To be in that position in the game, to see the smiles on my teammates' faces and my coaches' faces, that they can trust me. It felt great, all the hard work we have been putting in as a team and personally, it just feels great."
New England's depth contributions didn't solely come on the offensive side of the ball, however. Patriots backup cornerback Charles Woods also got in on the action, forcing Jets quarterback Geno Smith to throw his first interception of the season.
"It was a phenomenal play," Byard recalled. "He turned into a receiver basically."
While the Patriots' depth had plenty of struggles throughout the preseason, it has quickly turned into one of the strengths of this team.

title: Unsung Patriots CB Comes Up Big With First Career Interception
full_text:
FOXBORO — Charles Woods said postgame that he doesn't like playing defense. He wishes he could play wide receiver.
"I still think I'm a receiver at heart," he told reporters in front of his locker postgame.
The problem is, he plays cornerback for the New England Patriots , and has been asked to step up in a larger role after a number of players at his position have gotten banged up. So Woods remains at cornerback.
He made one of the biggest plays in the Patriots' 26-19 win over the New York Jets on Sunday, nabbing his first NFL interception off of Geno Smith — who to that point, had not thrown one all season.
"Just doing what I was called on that play to do, staying high," Woods said. "I just had good eyes. I really didn't think Geno was gonna throw it, but he threw it up, (I) made the speed turn and made the play."
That pick helped stunt a Jets drive that could have potentially cut into the Patriots' 10-point lead. Instead, it gave the ball back to the Patriots offense that found the end zone three times in the win.
Woods, who was given a game ball by Mike Vrabel after the game, isn't known for picking passes off. In fact, that interception off of Smith was the first time he's recorded an interception since he was playing for West Virginia in the 2021 Guaranteed Rate Bowl. Since then, he's suited up for SMU before making his way to the NFL.
He didn't feel like he had a weight off his back with the interception. Woods said that he's gotten good at not forcing anything.
"Just playing a lot of football, listening to my vets, I wasn't trying to chase plays these last few weeks," Woods said. "So (I) just let it come to me and it finally came to me. It's a blessing."
And to celebrate with his teammates, that made the moment that much sweeter for the 26-year-old.
"I was really excited to just see how excited they were for me," he said with a smile. "Everybody was smiling, happy, so that really made me happy."
That interception, just the fourth all season for the Patriots, was one of the biggest moments in what became the team's third-straight win (and second-straight win at home). The Patriots have started to roll and are right in the thick of things when it comes to the AFC six weeks in.
Woods has played a big role in that. Being primarily a special teams guy a season ago, he's come along as a nice reserve player that steps up to help fill any gap s . Carlton Davis, Karon Prunty and Channing Canada all didn't play against the Jets . Christian Gonzalez has also missed time with a shoulder injury.
No matter who's injured, Woods has been able to step up — and that interception is the cherry on top.
"It was a phenomenal play. He turned into a receiver basically," safety Kevin Byard said. "For guys to come in, take advantage of opportunities, obviously with CD being down, phenomenal play by him. He's been playing good football all year. He's a starting corner in this league, so I'm just happy that, when he gets in there and plays, he's been taking advantage of the opportunity."
"He ever knows where he's going to be at, how many snaps he's going to play," defensive tackle Milton Williams said. "But in the right spot, executing when he's supposed to, and when the ball comes to you, make a play when it comes to you. I was happy for him, proud of him. And we needed it, we needed it bad. So kudos to him. I hope he enjoys himself tonight."

title: Prideful Patriots Offensive Line, Battered by Injuries, Helps Clinch Win vs. Jets
full_text:
FOXBORO — The injuries up front for the New England Patriots were already a nightmare leading into this game. That nightmare got a lot scarier on Sunday, as three of the team's starting linemen left with lower-body injuries.
And yet, the Patriots were able to grind out a 26-19 win over the New York Jets — partially because of how well their backups stepped in to replace them.
First it was Morgan Moses, the right tackle who came into the game already nursing a foot injury. He would leave the game and remain on the sideline as the second half started before departing inside once again. Then it was left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker and his hamstring. Then Ben Brown was helped off the field after suffering a knee injury.
So, just like everyone had drew it up, the Patriots leaned on some names like Caleb Lomu, Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse on what became a 13-play, 51-yard drive that ate up more than six minutes of game time. They ran the ball nine-straight times and powered their way to a victory.
"We were able to run the football. We were able to protect the quarterback. I felt like we really gained some energy, and that was impressive to go that long and get the ball down there," Mike Vrabel said postgame. "Those guys were ready for their opportunity, and it was great to see. I just, you never know what's going to happen in this league, and we talk about it all the time, preparing for the journey. When guys get their chance, they go in there and perform. I hate that we don't have the guys. I hate when guys get injured, but I also understand that on the other side of that, there's an opportunity."
"I think those are situations that we practice and thrive ourselves on," left tackle Will Campbell said. "I feel like we did that very well last year and are just continuing to try to build on that, be an area that we excel in and do a good job at."
It took a little bit of wiggling around, but the Patriots finally settled on their eventual lineup. Lomu came in at right tackle to replace Moses — who was spotted in the locker room with a boot on.
Then once Vera-Tucker went down, Pryor came in to play right guard. Brown then moved from his spot on the right side to left guard. Brown would go down, and Rouse (the converted tackle) slotted in at left guard.
It was a lot of moving pieces, but it somehow worked. The Patriots ran the ball 36 times for 148 yards and didn't allow a single sack. The effort was gutsy beyond belief.
"The mindset is next man up," Rouse told Patriots On SI postgame. "You hate to see your teammates go down. Guys who work so hard to get out there, prepare to play and then to see them go down, especially one after another. ... I can't go into the game thinking like, 'Oh, hope you're doing well. When are they coming back out?' It's now onto the next play. How are we going to win this game?"
That same mindset was echoed by Pryor, who's only been on the Patriots for a few weeks. He was mainly used on the field goal unit during his first games with the team, but now might be in line for a larger role with a Thursday Night Football game lurking.
"Obvously, we're all new," Pryor told Patriots On SI. "When you get a new offensive line in there, you kind of lack the chemistry. So obviously, some plays are going to be hit or miss every now and then, and that just comes with repitition. So once we further get to understand each other and get the reps and combinations, everything kind of mends itself."
Pryor took pride in the Patriots' back-breaking drive to ice the game. As did Campbell, who had to play next to three different left guards in one game and came into the game questionable with his own knee injury.
"Yeah, I mean, as bad as it is and as unfortunate as it is, it’s just the way this game goes," Campbell said. "Coach Vrabel talks each week about preparing as a starter. Guys never know what could happen in a game, and you have to be ready whenever you get your opportunity. I feel like some guys stepped up big for us today."
It will be tough for a Patriots offensive line, already missing Mike Onwenu, Greg Van Roten and Marcus Bryant, to go into a rowdy environment to face the Chicago Bears in four days. Tack on the mounting injuries, and it seems nearly impossible — at least right now — to field a full unit.
And yet, that's just part of the challenge the Patriots will need to face. No matter who's out there, the Patriots will try and run the ball down anyone's throats.
"(We have) a lot of pride," Rouse said of that long drive. "There's no greater joy that doing that."
Just ask the running back who did it to the Jets.
"Everybody comes to work, no matter what," Corey Kiner , who racked up a team-high 57 yards behind the makeshift line, said. "Everybody comes to work every day and that's just the mentality we have as the Patriots."

title: A.J. Brown Breaks a Patriots Record He Never Hoped to in Home Debut
full_text:
New England Patriots star wide receiver A.J. Brown played his first full game in a Patriots uniform after missing four weeks with an ankle injury. The notoriously skilled pass catcher couldn't seem to haul in the most important throws in the team's win over the New York Jets.
Brown was traded to New England in the offseason for a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick. The former Philadelphia Eagles star and Tennessee Titans star, played less than three quarters of the Patriots' season opener in Seattle.
Making his debut in Foxboro, Massachusetts, Brown's expectation as a reliable pass catcher was severely underwhelming, as the Super Bowl-winning wide receiver recorded just three catches on 10 targets for 26 yards.
According to BetMGM , four of his targets were recorded as drops, making it the most amount of times Brown's dropped a pass in one game of his eight NFL seasons. Additionally, Brown's four drops today not only set a career-high for the veteran player, but was the most drops ever recorded by a New England player.
The discomfort was seen early when Drake Maye targeted Brown on a slant route. In a pass that was thrown behind him, Brown seemed to have made an impressive catch — turning his body around and securing the ball beneath his hands. A replay review overturned the call, ruling it an incompletion.
Then, Brown streaked down the field, beating his defende r down the right sideline for what would have been at least a 38-yard reception. Maye's pass went through the hands of his receiver, seemingly touching his hands.
Another missed opportunity came in the back of the endzone, with Maye asking Brown to climb the ladder and haul in a ball placed in a spot only he could get to. Brown leaped for it, and couldn't squeeze the ball — missing his first opportunity to score a touchdown as a Patriot.
AJ Brown… pic.twitter.com/YXKfTDO0Zj
Then, on back-to-back plays, Maye went to Brown in impactful moments. First, a 3rd-and-five, where Brown dropped a pass off his chest when he created separation on a slant route. The following 4th down play, Maye went back to the 6-foot-1 target for a 12-yard out route. Though it was well defended, Brown couldn't make the contested catch.
The final indication that Brown's hands were of real concern came when the Jets attempted an onside kick to keep the game alive.
Brown was the designated recovery player on the "hands team." As he executed his assignment of falling towards the kick, the ball slipped through his hands — once more — and rolled to the next level of defense, where DeMario Douglas was able to recover it.
#Patriots WR A.J. Brown told reporters postgame that he will be better moving forward. “No excuses… Ankle or not, I should make those plays.” Brown added that he is “absolutely” ready to play Thursday night against the Bears. (via @ByMarkDaniels ) pic.twitter.com/u1spM3qLea
"I think he probably could have made a few more plays," head coach Mike Vrabel said postgame. "We have all the confidence in the world in A.J. to be able to finish those plays."
Vrabel also shared that Brown "has to make the catches" whether or not plays are being drawn up for him.
Brown and the Patriots offense will work to correct mistakes from Sunday's 26-19 victory over the Jets , as they hastily prepare to face the 4-2 Chicago Bears on Thursday night.

title: 6 Instant Takeaways from Patriots' Uneasy 26-19 Win Over Jets
full_text:
FOXBORO — The afternoon started with a loud crowd for A.J. Brown, as the New England Patriots wide received ran out of the Gillette Stadium tunnel for the first time this season. As the afternoon progressed, those cheers continued for the next few hours.
The Patriots, led by three more touchdowns from Drake Maye, used a late clock-killing drive to knock off the visiting New York Jets to the tune of a 26-19 victory in Week 6.
It wasn't as easy as some of the other wins over the Jets in years past. In fact, after two great games, the Patriots really played down to their opponent and let the Jets hang around for quite a while and deep into the fourth quarter. And yet, 17-straight points in the first half gave them a lead they would never lose.
Here's what happened, and what it means going forward:
On the opening drive, the Jets looked methodical. Geno Smith hit Mason Taylor and Garrett Wilson for first downs, and Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis ran the ball well. It was a pretty easy march down the field for New York, who eventually scored a touchdown before an OPI took it off the board.
That 13-play drive resulted in a Jason Sanders 42-yard field goal, and that's the story of how the game went. The Patriots defense continued to bend, but never seemed to break.
The Patriots would always seem to hold strong , even if the Jets would drive deep into their territory.
One big play came in the second quarter, where Robert Spillane stuffed Allen in the gap to force a turnover on downs in field goal range. The Jets also failed to convert another fourth down on a long quarterback sneak by Smith one drive later.
But in the second half, Smith connected with rookie Omar Cooper Jr. on a busted coverage (it looked like Craig Woodson was the responsible party) for a 48-yard touchdown. One Jets drive later, a sack from Elijah Ponder forced them to settle for three points instead of a game-tying touchdown.
After two-straight wins where the Patriots quarterback looked like himself , Sunday's win was just another impressive outing. The 24-year-old went 18-for-32 for 235 passing yards and three touchdowns, and all of his scoring drives came with some magic in the pocket.
His first one came just two plays into the Patriots' second drive of the game. With all the time in the world to throw, Maye led Romeo Doubs on a crosser for a 42-yard touchdown. Doubs, who dove out to secure the catch, would go to the locker room with a shoulder injury and wouldn't return after being listed as questionable.
In the second quarter with the clock winding down, Maye found a wide-open DeMario Douglas across the middle. It was the third time in the past two weeks the pair hooked up on touchdowns, and it was aided by Maye maneuvering in and around the pocket.
The Patriots would return to the end zone exactly 50 seconds into the fourth quarter. Maye connected with Hunter Henry , who was left all alone on an out route. That score helped push the lead to 10 (Andy Borregales would miss the extra point). With the touchdown, Henry would tie Russ Francis (28) for the third-most touchdowns by a Patriots tight end ever.
Maye also became the first Patriots quarterback since Tom Brady in 2014 to throw for three touchdonws in three-straight games.
It was the headlining story of the week . Brown, who caught just three passes in the season opener, was finally making his home debut with the Patriots. However, it wasn't that impressive of an output for the  star wideout.
Brown played a majority of the offensive snaps in his game action in more than a month. Early in the game, it appeared that Brown got on the board with an impressive adjustment catch across the middle. But Jets head coach Aaron Glenn challenged it after the ball appeared to wobble, and it was overturned.
Later in the second, Brown nearly picked up a major gain, but saw Maye's pass fall just off his fingertips down the sideline. He also looked like the target on a designed double pass, but was completely covered by Jets defenders.
Brown finished the game with three receptions on 10 targets for 27 yards. He could have had a touchdown to close the first half, but dropped it in the back of the end zone. He'd also drop a pair in the second half, including a heavily-contested fourth down pass.
The Patriots entered the afternoon with their starting five offensive linemen in the game. By the time the final whistle was blown, that group looked a lot different.
Morgan Moses, who started the game at right tackle and came into the game dealing with a foot injury, would leave the game with an ankle injury. He limped off the field in the first half and would be replaced by rookie Caleb Lomu .
Then at the guard position, Alijah Vera-Tucker would head to the locker room with a hamstring injury. His absence forced Matt Pryor into the game, who'd slide in at right guard. Ben Brown, who was already the third right guard to start a game this season, switched over to the left side for the remainder of the game.
Vera-Tucker and Moses would both be ruled out in the second half.
Brown would also leave the game after holding his right knee. It took a bit of time for Brown, who was in a lot of pain, to limp off to the Patriots sideline. He would be replaced by Walter Rouse.
That unit, despite the injuries and constant changes, kept Maye off the turf. They didn't allow a sack and allowed him to operate with fairly clean pockets.
Mike Vrabel spoke this week about how the Patriots have turned the ball over in every game this season, and how it's come back to bite them at times. Well, through the first 37 minutes, they were playing clean football. That is until David Bailey stripped the ball out of TreVeyon Henderson's hands in the third.
The ball popped loose and Jamien Sherwood recovered it. The Jets would use that turnover as momentum, adding three points on a 36-yard field goal.
That would be the Patriots' only giveaway of the game. But it's a major part of how the running attack has yet to string together consistent showings. Every running back on the Patriots active roster has put the ball on the ground at least once this season (Rhamondre Stevenson fumbled in Week 2, while Corey Kiner lost it one week prior).
Douglas would also fumble it away, as he tried to do too much on a 40-yard pickup in the fourth. Sherwood punched it out from behind, and the Jets would take over. That drive would also lead to a Sanders field goal to pull within a score.
Smith hadn't thrown an interception in the Jets' first five games of the season. Charles Woods, who's been in the NFL since 2024 with both the Los Angeles Rams and Patriots, didn't have an interception in his career.
Both of those things changed early in the fourth quarter.
Under pressure, Smith tried to force the ball deep on the left side to tight end Kenyon Sadiq. Woods read it perfectly for his first interception since he played for West Virginia in the 2021 Guaranteed Rate Bowl — and the Patriots' only takeaway of the game.
The Patriots iced the game with a 27-yard field goal from Borregales with 1:12 left on the clock. Sanders would tack on a 36-yard field goal to pull within a touchdown, but the Jets failed to recover the ensuing onside kick.

title: Patriots Week 6 Inactives vs. Jets: Offense Gets Boost, Defense Remains Hurt
full_text:
FOXBORO — Injuries continue to mount for the New England Patriots . Their secondary will be shorthanded for yet another week. But at the end of the day, some big names on the offensive side of the ball will be suiting up as they take on the 2-3 New York Jets.
The major storyline this week is the return of wide receiver A.J. Brown , who was activated off of injured reserve this weekend. He's in line to make his season debut against a team that's looking for their first win in Gillette Stadium since 2023.
Both sides won't be at full strength. Here are all the Patriots and Jets who won't be playing this week at Gillette Stadium:
QB Behren Morton (emergency third QB)
WR Adonai Mitchell (finger)
CB Karon Prunty (hamstring)
CB Channing Canada (hamstring)
Brown suffered a high-ankle sprain in the Patriots' Week 1 loss to the Seattle Seahawks , and has been on the sideline ever since. He returned to the practice field this week in a limited capacity, but his activation to the roster highlights that the Patriots offense has another layer of ability outside the numbers.
"I think he's stayed engaged. I think it's difficult sometimes to stay engage," Mike Vrabel said Wednesday. "I think his routine was really good, his ability to be around guys in the meetings and then also focus on his rehab. He's just treating everything as a pro, being where he's supposed to be and working hard to get back."
After ruling Carlton Davis and Karon Prunty out on Friday, the Patriots are also downgrading Channing Canada (who was questionable) to out. He missed last week with a hamstring injury, and his role on special teams has been replaced by safeties Mike Brown and Elliott Davison.
Behren Morton will dress, but will only be allowed to step on the field if Drake Maye and Tommy DeVito both get banged up. Tanner Arkin, who was active in recent weeks as the fourth tight end, won't dress.
After TreVeyon Henderson went down with a high-ankle sprain last week , it didn't seem like he'd be available for this one. But after participating in practices and moving well on the field, he's ready to go.
"Honestly, yeah. I was surprised. I felt a little bit different than what they diagnosed it as and what the MRI showed," Henderson said this week. "I'm hoping that I'm able to be out there with the guys and try to help this team continue in games."
The Jets will be without their top back, losing Breece Hall with a quad injury for the second-straight week. That means third-year back Braelon Allen will be carrying the load out of New York's backfield. They also have Kene Nwangwu and Isaiah Davis behind him.
"(He's) a big back. Usually, the first guy doesn't tackle him, doesn't bring him down," Vrabel said. "A lot of his X play runs have been after contact where somebody's like, 'Oh yeah, they've got him,' and no, they don't. So again, he breaks a lot of tackles. He runs hard. I think he's a smooth runner and doesn't look very rigid. I’ve always liked him from even coming out of college."
Campbell also got banged up last week with a knee injury that looked similar to his torn MCL suffered a season ago. He was limited in practice this week, but was cleared to play this week.
The second-year tackle has had a strong season this year protecting his quarterback's blindside and his return to the lineup will let Caleb Lomu sit instead of starting. Against the Raiders, replacing Campbell, Lomu shined. He allowed just one pressure on 47 snaps at left tackle.
It was an inspiring showing from the rookie, who'll likely slot back in as a swing tackle. But he's shown that if Campbell gets banged up again, or struggles playing on his right knee, Lomu is more than capable.
"It was awesome to see Caleb get in there. I think it was tough," Maye said. "It may be a guy over there with a couple All-Pros and talking smack. But at the same time, it's what we do. In offense, we dictate it. I feel like he owned that and did a good job of anchoring. He's athletic and he's big."
The 3-2 Patriots and 2-3 Jets will do battle for the first time this season at 1 p.m. at Gillette Stadium. It's a chance for the Patriots to string together wins, and gain some breathing room above the bottom-half of the AFC East. A few things to watch out for stat-wise: Hunter Henry is one touchdown away from tying Russ Francis (28) for third-most in franchise history, and Maye is 102 yards to become the eighth Patriots quarterback to surpass 8,000 passing yards.

title: 3 Major Storylines in Patriots Matchup vs. Jets: Key Offensive Stars Healthy
full_text:
FOXBORO — The New England Patriots have had the New York Jets' number in years past. Is 2026 going to be a similar script?
Coming off of back-to-back wins, the 3-2 Patriots have started to roll heading into the middle of October. The Jets, in their own right, are coming off a rainy win over the Cleveland Browns. This is a game that the Patriots should win.
But will they? And if so, how?
Here's a few things to watch out for when both sides take the field at 1 p.m. from Gillette Stadium:
One of the biggest storylines surrounding the Patriots this season has been their health, and how key players on both sides of the ball have gotten banged up beyond belief. But today feels like a major step in the right direction.
A.J. Brown, who missed the last four games with a high-ankle sprain, was activated to the 53-man roster Saturday, allowing him to make his home Patriots debut . That addition to a receiver room that's improved in recent weeks should make this offense a little more potent.
"I think it definitely opens up other parts of the field and other parts of the game for guys," Drake Maye said this week about Brown's role in the offense. "I think you see it in the NBA. It's probably the closest thing that I can think of. When they start doubling the best player once they get past half court, then they're just leaving a corner 3 open or leaving a guy open for a dunk. So, it's kind of like playing receiver and with a guy like that – we've got a lot of guys that have made plays now, so it's going to be tough on defenses. But I know we've got a tough challenge this week, so looking forward to it."
The Patriots are also getting two players back after missing the end of last week's win. TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) and Will Campbell (knee) both are set to play after being listed as questionable . That will help a running game that still is looking to crack through. Henderson looked good in practice after an MRI revealed a high-ankle sprain, so he could have an interesting workload depending on how he's feeling.
This is not the Geno Smith the last time the Patriots played him on the Jets. In fact, the quarterback has the chance to beat the Patriots for the third-straight season with his third different team (Seahawks 2024, Raiders 2025). He's yet to throw an interception this year, and the Patriots defense that has prided itself in taking the ball away will need to try and force some bad throws.
How can they do that? It starts with the safeties. The Patriots are going to be without corners Carlton Davis and Karon Prunty for the second-straight game, but they'll get Christian Gonzalez back. But he's not someone who'll pick it off often.
The Patriots rely on Craig Woodson — who had a game-sealing pick in Buffalo two weeks ago — and Kevin Byard, the NFL's interception leader from a week ago. The Jets won't have Breece Hall carrying the rock out of the backfield, potentially leaving them to air it out a lot.
Last week's showing for Maye was nearly perfec t. A hair under 400 total yards of offense. Five total touchdowns. A 40-point showing. It was all going perfect for the Patriots quarterback who started the year off on a bad start.
"He looked very calm. Again, when we give him clean pockets, he's very accurate down the field," Mike Vrabel said Monday on Maye's performance. "He maybe only had a few, I would say, wrong decisions or where he wanted to go with the football. Just seemed very in control, very confident. When he felt like he needed to run, he was decisive. Then we put the ball in his hands down in the red zone, and he was able to make a guy miss."
But is there anywhere that he can improve from the Raiders' win? Against this Jets defense that's fourth in the NFL in total defense and fifth in points allowed , he'll need to avoid turnovers. The Patriots have turned the ball over at least once in every game this season, and many of those have fallen on Maye's shoulders. If the Patriots want to win convincingly like last week, they'll need to keep possession.

title: Patriots Roster Moves: A.J. Brown Activated, Veteran RB Released
full_text:
Less than 24 hours until the New England Patriots play host to the rival New York Jets , they've made a slew of roster moves.
The team announced Saturday that they've activated wide receiver A.J. Brown (ankle) off of injured reserve, while also elevating safety Elliott Davison from the practice squad and releasing running back Hassan Haskins.
Here's a look at each of these moves, and what they mean heading into Week 6 tomorrow:
The high-profile offseason acquisition for the Patriots, Brown caught three passes in the season opener before suffering a high-ankle sprain early in the third quarter. Brown, who the Patriots got from the Philadelphia Eagles for a 2028 first round pick and a 2027 fifth round pick, would later be placed on IR, ruling him out for the next four games.
Since then, the Patriots have gotten inspiring outings from the other receivers on the roster. But adding Brown back into the fold will help elevate a passing attack starting to get into a rhythm.
"I think you know what he can add. He's been a player in this league," quarterback Drake Maye said Wednesday. "It's not like we haven't seen him as a player in this league, and there aren't many like him that roam around in this league. So, I'll just try to do my part to give him some chances and keep on spreading the ball around for guys that are open. We've had a lot of guys step up. So, I'm looking forward to keeping that rolling and adding another piece whenever he feels like he's ready to get out there."
Brown comes into the game with a questionable designation after being limited all week in practice. With this move, the Patriots' 53-man roster is now filled. Offensive tackle Marcus Bryant, who returned to practice this week after suffering an ankle injury in the p reseason, was not yet activated. The team has two more weeks to do so before his season ends.
Along with the Brown move, the Patriots also made some moves with their practice squad. For the second-straight week, they'll elevating young safety Davison to the game day roster. Last week against the Raiders, Davison made a tackle on special teams early in the game and added some snaps in garbage time defensively.
They also released Haskins, who signed back with the Patriots this week. The former Tennessee Titans draft pick spent the preseason in New England , but was released after two weeks of the regular season. He signed back to the practice squad as TreVeyon Henderson worked through an ankle injury he suffered a week ago.
Henderson, who's going into the game with a questionable designation, hasn't been ruled out yet. Releasing Haskins could mean the team feels comfortable about where he is physically.
They'll have one open spot on the practice squad heading into a short Week 7.

title: Patriots 'Likely' to Make Major A.J. Brown Move Ahead of Week 6
full_text:
It's not official yet, but the New England Patriots could be getting a major piece of their offense back this week.
According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the Patriots "will likely" activate wide receiver A.J. Brown from injured reserve to play this week against the New York Jets. The star wideout, who suffered a high-ankle sprain in Week 1, returned to practice and participated in a limited capacity.
The Patriots do have an open spot on the 53-man roster, allowing Brown to be added straight to the active roster. Should the team not activate him, they'll have a 21-day window for him to return. He was listed as questionable for this week's game .
As of Friday afternoon, it was up in the air if Brown would play or not.
"We won't make that decision until tomorrow, so we'll have to see how he responds from practice today and then go from there," head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters.
The Patriots traded two draft picks (including their first rounder in 2028) for Brown's services, but haven't been able to enjoy his talents. He caught just three passes against the Seattle Seahawks in the opener, but has missed the last four games on the sideline.
Still, he's been engaged with his teammates and coaches. Brown was spotted in the locker room the past two weeks, often in cleats and chatting with Drake Maye . He's also been active on social media, cheering on his fellow wide receivers during games.
Without Brown (and Mack Hollins, who was placed on IR following the Patriots' 29-26 win over the Buffalo Bills), the Patriots had just four wideouts active — Romeo Doubs, Kyle Williams, DeMario Douglas and Efton Chism III.
"I feel like the guys did a great job. You know, last week (against the Las Vegas Raiders) was phenomenal," Brown said. "Obviously, there were still things to improve on and they would tell you that, but I think they did really well. Whenever I do decide to come back, I just want to add and continue to keep putting it out on display."
Brown will be a big jolt for a Patriots offense that's started to find its footing in recent weeks. Struggles early in the year put the team in a rut, but now they've started to open up (and it helps that Maye is playing lights out again). Now that they can add their top-tier pass catcher to that unit, the Patriots should be firing on all cylinders this week.
Vrabel said that this week of practice was good for Brown to get back into the swing of things.
"I mean, I think he looks OK," Vrabel said. "Like everybody, some good plays, some bad plays. I try to see where his conditioning level is."
The Patriots will announce any other roster moves at 4 p.m. today.

title: 4 Takeaways From Saints' 34-27 Week 6 Victory Over Giants
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints finally have something to celebrate, although Sunday's 34-27 victory over the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium was far from convincing.
After three consecutive losses, mounting criticism, and growing questions about the franchise's direction, New Orleans desperately needed a win. The Saints delivered one, overcoming a sluggish start before nearly squandering a commanding 34-10 lead in the second half.
Quarterback Tyler Shough , who completed 16 of 30 passes for 144 yards and three touchdowns, and the offense showed encouraging signs, particularly with an improved rushing attack, while the defense produced three interceptions despite struggling to contain former Saints quarterback Jameis Winston and JJ McCarthy .
The victory also provided some much-needed relief for head coach Kellen Moore , whose team entered the matchup facing increased scrutiny following public criticism from franchise legend Drew Brees and owner Gayle Benson .
However, the Saints' inability to put away the Giants after building a 24-point advantage demonstrated why significant questions remain about their consistency and ability to finish games.
Here are four instant reactions from New Orleans' much-needed victory.
The Saints always have at least one special teamer that becomes a star whether it’s Morten Andersen , Michael Lewis or Steve Gleason .
This time, it has been linebacker Isaiah Stalbird , who has been valuable on special teams all year, and he made the biggest play of the game.
Trailing 10-3 with less than a minute remaining in the first half, New Orleans looked set to enter halftime with another double-digit deficit. However, Stalbird delivered arguably the biggest play of the afternoon on special teams.
The rookie safety forced a fumble on Charlie Jones 's kickoff return, allowing tight end Oscar Delp to recover the football and give New Orleans possession deep in Giants territory.
Shough capitalized on the turnover, connecting with rookie Bryce Lance for a touchdown that tied the game at 10 with one second remaining before halftime.
The sequence completely changed the momentum.
After struggling offensively throughout much of the first half, the Saints suddenly found themselves in position to take control. New Orleans carried that momentum into the third quarter, scoring 24 additional unanswered points to build a commanding advantage.
Although Stalbird's contribution won't receive the same attention as Shough's four-touchdown performance or Martin Emerson Jr. 's two interceptions, his forced fumble was arguably the game's most important play.
After weeks of heavy criticism in regard to its horrendous rushing attack, the Saints may have figured out the formula.
New Orleans finished with a season-high 175 rushing yards, providing much-needed balance to an offense that has frequently relied on too much on Shough to generate production.
Kendre Miller led the charge with 70 yards on 20 carries, while C.J. Donaldson contributed 39 yards on six attempts. Alvin Kamara added 34 yards on seven carries, and Shough chipped in another 32 yards and a touchdown run.
The production was particularly encouraging considering New Orleans had struggled to establish a reliable ground game during its three-game losing streak.
However, the Saints still have considerable work ahead.
Miller averaged just 3.5 yards a carry, highlighting the inconsistency that continues to plague the rushing attack despite the improved overall numbers.
Another player worth monitoring is offensive lineman Jeremiah Wright , who came in for the injured Cesar Ruiz at right guard. His impact became noticeable as it was a trend that the Saints ran the ball to the right a solid amount in the second half and with success.
The Saints need their offensive front, including Wright when he is involved, to create more consistent running lanes rather than relying on individual efforts to generate positive yardage.
Sunday's performance was hardly a dominant rushing effort, but it represented a meaningful step forward for an offense desperately searching for balance.
Despite grabbing three interceptions, the Saints' secondary once struggled once again against a solid receiving corps in coverage during New York's fourth-quarter comeback.
Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely torched New Orleans’ secondary all game.
Nabers recorded 12 catches for 165 yards, while Likely had six catches for 99 yards and a touchdown.
After replacing Jameis Winston, J.J. McCarthy threw for 243 yards in just over 11 minutes, sparking three straight touchdown drives to trim a 34-10 deficit to seven points.
Still, the defense created crucial takeaways: Martin Emerson Jr. had two interceptions (one off McCarthy), Julian Blackmon picked off Winston, and the pass rush logged four sacks on Winston.
Yet, allowing 461 total yards (377 passing) highlights the already serious concerns on whether or not the secondary can slow so. Defensive coordinator Brandon Staley must fix these coverage breakdowns to prevent future collapses.
Few teams entered Week 6 under more pressure than the Saints.
Following three consecutive losses, including a disappointing 23-13 defeat against the Minnesota Vikings , New Orleans found itself under intense scrutiny from fans, former players and ownership.
Former Saints quarterback Drew Brees, who called the game for Fox and was inducted into the Saints Ring of Honor at halftime during the loss to the Vikings, criticized the team's offense and Moore's play-calling .
A few days later, Saints owner Gayle Benson publicly expressed her frustration with the team's 1-4 start during a speaking engagement at the Greater New Orleans Quarterback Club, making it clear that recent performances were unacceptable.
Benson specifically challenged the team's leadership, including Moore and general manager Mickey Loomis , to address the mistakes that had contributed to the disappointing start.
Those comments placed additional pressure on Moore, whose second season as head coach has been defined by inconsistent performances and questions about the team's direction.
Sunday's victory provided a much-needed response.
The Saints showed resilience after falling behind 10-0, capitalized on turnovers and demonstrated the offensive explosiveness that had been largely absent during their losing streak.
More importantly, they found a way to win.
Yet blowing nearly all of a 24-point fourth-quarter lead highlighted the issues behind Benson's criticism. With execution and closing troubles nearly turning a blowout into a loss, the 2-4 Saints face major questions before playing the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris. Snapping the streak offers short-term relief, but New Orleans must show real growth to make this a true turning point.

title: Postgame Live Blog: Saints Survive Late Rally from Giants to Break Losing Skid
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints survive a furious comeback from the New York Giants to pull off a much-needed 34-27 win and break a three-game losing skid.
The Saints will now travel to Paris to take on the Pittsburgh Steelers on Oct. 25.
The New Orleans Saints survive a furious comeback from the New York Giants to pull off a much-needed 34-27 win and break a three-game losing skid.
After leading 34-10 early in the fourth quarter, New Orleans nearly squandered its 24-point advantage before a final fourth-down incompletion ended New York's comeback attempt.
The Saints appeared headed toward another disappointing first half Sunday before a late rally erased a double-digit deficit against the Giants at MetLife Stadium.
SAINTS WIN! #Saints | @Gatorade pic.twitter.com/L3rLoA34Cg
Trailing 10-0 early, New Orleans mounted a crucial 10-point rally to tie 10-10 by halftime. The turnaround gave the team vital momentum as it looked to end its three-game losing slump. and a coach trying to extinguish the fire on his seat.
The Saints (1-4) struggled offensively for much of the opening half, with quarterback Tyler Shough facing consistent pressure from an aggressive Giants defense, which is ninth in the NFL in total defense. New Orleans struggled to sustain drives, while former Saints quarterback Jameis Winston helped New York build an early advantage.
Winston opened the scoring with a 17-yard touchdown pass to running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. in the first quarter. Tracy caught the pass near the line of scrimmage and capitalized on a missed tackle before reaching the end zone.
New York extended its lead to 10-0 when Dominic Zvada nailed a 34-yard field goal with ease late in the second quarter.
Meanwhile, New Orleans continued to squander scoring opportunities, including Daniel Carlson 's missed 55-yard field goal attempt earlier in the quarter.
However, the Saints finally broke through when Carlson drilled a 58-yard field goal with 1:18 remaining before halftime, cutting the deficit to 10-3.
On the ensuing kickoff, linebacker Isaiah Stalbird laid one on Giants returner Charlie Jones to force a fumble and rookie tight end Oscar Delp recovered the football to give the Saints.
A few plays later, Shough would find a wide-open Bryce Lance in the endzone on fourth-and-two, tying the game and giving Lance his first career touchdown reception.
Shough to Lance: TD Saints 🙌 #Saints | 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/bMW0CKYTSP
That led to a Saints scoring spree.
Shough connected with Alvin Kamara on a 31-yard touchdown pass to give New Orleans its first lead, 17-10. The scoring play also helped Kamara reach the historic milestone of 5,000 career receiving yards, adding to his more than 5,000 rushing yards.
AK ALL THE WAY!!! #Saints | 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/ftWZuuSHFX
Shough later scored on a 1-yard quarterback sneak before Carlson added a 51-yard field goal, extending the advantage to 27-10.
Shough Sneak ⚜️ #Saints | 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/oNfCm0szhE
New Orleans' defense continued creating opportunities, with Martin Emerson Jr. recording two interceptions and Julian Blackmon adding another.
Blackmon's interception set up Shough's 18-yard touchdown pass to Chris Olave, pushing the lead to 34-10 early in the fourth quarter.
Shough ➡️ Olave 🙌 #Saints | 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/qS5PI0R1jR
With Winston struggling, New York turned to JJ McCarthy , who immediately provided a spark.
McCarthy directed a touchdown drive capped by Tracy's 5-yard scoring run and a successful 2-point conversion. He later connected with Isaiah Likely for a 24-yard touchdown before Zvada's 41-yard field goal reduced New Orleans' lead to 34-27.
After forcing a Saints punt, McCarthy drove the Giants deep into New Orleans territory before the final fourth-down incompletion ended the comeback attempt.
Despite the fourth-quarter collapse, New Orleans produced a season-high 175 rushing yards and received its most productive touchdown performance of the season from Shough.
The victory offers some relief for second-year coach Kellen Moore after owner Gayle Benson publicly criticized the team's disappointing start .
Wild NFL games. They're always coming in different shapes and sizes. Proud of our guys to find a way to win this game. That's ultimately your No. 1 objective going on the road.
Obviously, we'll extend this road trip here shortly tonight, but proud of our guys to find a way to win.
From a medical standpoint, Cesar had a knee injury. He didn't finish. Quincy had that neck issue at the end. I think we're OK. Kool-Aid had a little bit of a migraine thing going on. Everyone else was able to play and was good to go.
Q: In hindsight, how do you feel about the decision to start pulling your starters?
A: Obviously, looking back on it, they got things going and were able to score a lot. We had to get back into that thing. It's just a couple guys who are managing some stuff, guys who are sore, and we tried to get a few guys out. Obviously, it didn't work.
Q: Was that a quick decision after the score?
A: Yeah, after the turnover. Obviously, it was a 24-point game, and we were just trying to give a couple of our guys a break. It was really Eric and Tyler. Everyone else was playing. Then we obviously had the fumble.
Q: Did Kool-Aid McKinstry's migraine develop at halftime, or when did that become an issue?
A: Just during the game. We'll work through the details of that.
Q: What changed with the running game in the second half that allowed you to have so much success?
A: I think ultimately our guys' physical play. The runners ran really hard. I thought they finished well.
Again, when you don't beat yourself with penalties and negative plays, you're able to get more rush attempts and get into the rush game and some action game off it.
I thought our guys just did a better job of playing in those mixed downs more.
Q: Did Jeremiah Wright bring something different to the running game?
A: Jeremiah, certainly. He's a really good runner — or really good blocker, excuse me. He's a physical player. We saw that through camp and all those different things, and we feel great about him.
We feel like he can go contribute and play. I thought those other guys, though, Dave, Cee's, I thought those guys did some good stuff as well.
Q: What did you like about Martin Emerson's performance?
A: Just physical football. Playing corner in this league, you've got to play physical.
I think the stat I had was two interceptions, four PBUs, seven tackles. You're just getting involved in the plays.
Just proud of him because he's had to navigate an injury, rotation, and you're trying to find your groove, so to speak. I thought he took advantage of those opportunities.
Q: Emerson had a moment on the sideline after colliding with Quincy. Was he injured?
A: He just got the wind knocked out of him. Popped back in there.
Q: There was a report before the game that Tyler Shough had two broken bones in his left hand. What can you tell us about that?
A: His hand, he's battling. Again, he's doing a great job. He's able to do everything for us.
Q: What ultimately turned the game around after falling behind 10-0 late in the first half?
A: I thought that field goal was big, and then really the special teams.
To me, all three phases at that point. That was a huge turnover, Stallberg creating that forced fumble. We're able to score right there, tie the ballgame up, and then come out of the second half and just play.
I thought a really good middle part right there. I thought it was a big, important part of this game.
Q: Was the three-running back rotation what you envisioned coming into the game?
A: Yeah, just rotate those guys. They have different roles and opportunities. Some plays are specific to players, and some are based on who's out there.
I thought they all ran hard. I thought Alvin's catch on the sideline, then to stay in bounds and get upfield, was an incredible play.

title: Saints vs. Giants: Can New Orleans Snap Its Losing Streak? Our Staff Predicts
full_text:
The pressure continues to mount on the New Orleans Saints as they head to the Meadowlands for Sunday's Week 6 showdown against the New York Giants , desperately searching for answers amid a disappointing start to the season.
Following a frustrating 23-13 loss to the Minnesota Vikings , the Saints (1-4) have dropped three consecutive games, raising questions about the team's direction under second-year head coach Kellen Moore.
The struggles have even drawn the attention of team owner Gayle Benson , who recently expressed frustration with the organization's performance and made it clear that continued losing would not be tolerated without consequences.
With expectations rising and patience wearing thin, New Orleans faces another difficult challenge against a surprising Giants team that has emerged as an early contender in the NFC East.
Here are our predictions for Sunday's game.
This is the Saints' first road game since Week 2, and it’s a strategic one at that, as the Saints will immediately fly out of New York for their game against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris next week. However, this is a critical game for coach Kellen Moore , and maybe even longtime general manager Mickey Loomis .
I don’t think Tyler Shough will have many games like he did last week in the loss to the Vikings, but he will have another matchup against a top-10 defense as the Giants are ninth in total defense. The strength of the defense is its ability to defend the pass, allowing only 199.7 yards per contest, which is good for seventh in the NFL, and have forced six interceptions, which is good for fourth.
While I think Shough will do much better, the Giants have the players needed to at least limit Shough, and New Orleans’ rushing attack is one of the NFL’s worst and will be ineffective. While the Giants have struggled to stop the run, they will have no trouble stopping the Saints.
Defensively, I think the Saints will do enough to keep the game close but not enough to win. The Giants aren’t the greatest offense in the world, but Cam Skattebo is a decent running back, while the receiving threats of Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely are going to give the Saints’ defense a heap of trouble.
I predict a one-score game in the Meadowlands with the Giants pulling it out.
Which Saints club will show in the Meadowlands today? Will it be the one from the first three weeks of the season, or the one from the last three?
We know this: those leading this organization have been put on notice by the woman that holds the checkbook. For the first time as owner of the Saints, Gayle Benson is faced with a situation that will require resolve and a possible move that will force her to make decisions that will be uncomfortable. She has put her trust and belief in those in charge. After seeing where her club has gone in the last few weeks, and the fan reaction to that direction, Mrs. Benson is having to rethink that trust.
Meanwhile, a two-week road trip followed by the Saints open/bye week may be just what the doctor ordered for Moore and his troops: a chance to regroup and rethink where things are.
Being a "glass-half-full" kinda guy, I'm getting this feeling this may be the first step to Moore, his coaches, and his players turning things around. However, don't bet the house on who I choose to win today. I've only been right once in five prognostications this year.

title: Saints vs. Giants: Three Things New Orleans Must Do to Win at the Meadowlands
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints enter Sunday's Week 6 matchup with a trip to the Meadowlands against the New York Giants looking to avoid their fourth consecutive loss, but a familiar face stands in their way and remains a fan favorite in New Orleans.
Former Saints quarterback Jameis Winston will lead the Giants against his former team as New Orleans attempts to rebound from a disappointing 23-13 loss to the Minnesota Vikings .
The Saints (1-4) have struggled to find consistency on both sides of the football, particularly offensively, where turnovers and an ineffective rushing attack have contributed to their disappointing start.
Meanwhile, the Giants (3-1-1) have emerged as one of the NFC's early surprises under first-year coach John Harbaugh , overcoming injuries and inconsistent quarterback play to remain atop the NFC East.

title: Gayle Benson Breaks Silence as Saints' 1-4 Start Puts Leadership Under Fire
full_text:
New Orleans Saints owner Gayle Benson declared the team's 1-4 start to the season was “not acceptable" on Monday, issuing a stern warning to leadership and staff as frustration mounts across the franchise and fan base.
Speaking at the Greater New Orleans Quarterback Club following Sunday's 23-13 loss to the Minnesota Vikings , Benson emphasized that accountability extends across the entire organization.
"That is not acceptable to me, and it falls short of what our fans deserve," Benson said. "I hear the frustration directed toward our team and our organization. It is not lost on me."
Benson emphasized that accountability begins with her but extends throughout the organization, specifically identifying General Manager Mickey Loomis , second-year head coach Kellen Moore , the coaching staff, and the players.
"I will not make excuses, and I will not accept this level of performance as our standard," Benson said. "I am committed to making the decisions necessary to improve this team."
While Benson did not say anything straightforward on whether organizational changes were imminent, her comments came nearly two years after she overruled Loomis and fired former coach Dennis Allen following a seven-game losing streak.
In what should have been a year of continued improvement from last season’s second-half success, along with an emerging quarterback in Tyler Shough , this year should have been full of great vibes. Instead, the Saints have been putrid throughout the first five games of the franchise's 60th anniversary season, which has featured several celebrations overshadowed by disappointing performances.
New Orleans suffered an embarrassing 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons during the 20th anniversary celebration of the historic 2006 "Domecoming" game. Six days later, the Saints lost to Minnesota during a ceremony honoring Drew Brees ' Pro Football Hall of Fame induction and his addition to the team's Ring of Honor.
At the end of both games, supporters of the Falcons and Vikings overtook the lower bowl of the stadium as “ATL” chants were heard throughout last Monday night, and “Skol” chants were also heard, but the latter were more audible because there were many Minnesota fans in attendance.
Benson referenced Brees' legacy while emphasizing the importance of restoring the standards that helped New Orleans win Super Bowl XLIV.
"It also includes a standard of preparation, discipline and accountability," Benson said. "The best way to honor that legacy is to uphold those standards today."
She also outlined the responsibilities of the organization's leadership:
"Kellen Moore and his coaches are responsible for preparing our players to perform. Mickey Loomis and our football staff are responsible for building a roster capable of sustained success. Our players are responsible for their preparation and execution. I am responsible for holding this organization accountable."
Despite her strong remarks, Benson acknowledged that public statements alone would not restore confidence in a franchise that has not reached the playoffs since 2020.
"Words will not restore our fans' confidence," Benson said. "Our performance must do that."
The Saints will attempt to end their losing streak Sunday against the New York Giants before traveling to Paris to face the Pittsburgh Steelers .
Benson concluded by reiterating her commitment to the franchise's supporters.
"We cannot change the results of our first five games. We are responsible for what we do next. I expect better. Our fans deserve better. And I am determined to see that we deliver it."
