title: Pressure Mounts on Sean Mannion as Nick Sirianni Says 'Everything's on the Table'
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA - After the Eagles’ 25-14 home loss to the Panthers dropped them to 2-4 and extended a four-game skid, the largest of the Nick Sirianni era, the head coach did what leaders often do when the offense is derailing: he spread the blame in the “ultimate team game.”
The messaging did change slightly for those paying attention, however.
“Everything’s on the table,” Sirianni said, almost ominously.
That phrasing could be foreshadowing.
The Eagles have been near the bottom of the league in points and total yards under first-year offensive coordinator and play-caller Sean Mannion . Second halves have been especially difficult. Third-down failures and stalled drives have been a recurring theme even before Jalen Hurts went down with a blood clot and Tanner McKee took over Sunday as the starter.
Injuries across the offensive line, the running back room, and the skill positions have been crippling—Lane Johnson’s retirement, the Cam Jurgens trade, and other decisions have forced a rebuild on the fly.
But four straight setbacks and an offense that has frequently looked scheme-constrained rather than scheme-empowered have turned the spotlight on the man Sirianni hired to install a more under-center, play-action, outside-zone system drawn from the Shanahan-McVay tree.
Sirianni’s postgame answers were a study in collective accountability when asked by Eagles On SI if morphing the offense around McKee has to be ramped up in future weeks.
Asked about helping the offense get going, he said they would “have to do different things,” that they would never make excuses, and that “everything’s on the table” because “to do the same thing over and over again and not get the results, that’d be foolish.”
When pressed on how much responsibility falls on Mannion specifically and his scheme, Sirianni replied that “we’ve got to be able to score more points, period,” and that “it’s not just on one coach. It’s not just one coach on an island… It’s the ultimate team game."
“We all have to do better.”
On McKee, who completed 26 of 45 for 215 yards and a touchdown to DeVonta Smith, Sirianni noted that the backup “battled,” took care of the football, and made some good throws (including a nice third-down connection to Dontayvion Wicks). The larger point, though, was the same: points were scarce, and “all of us have a lot of improving to do.”
This is not the first time Sirianni has refused to isolate Mannion.
Earlier in the season he said the coordinator would “wear a lot of this” while also stressing shared ownership. The approach is consistent with how he has framed the offense all year: identity questions remain open, growth is the priority, and public finger-pointing is limited.
It is also protective of a coach who arrived with almost no play-calling experience and whose biggest public selling points were work ethic, conviction in his system, and detail.
Conviction is now being tested in real time. Mannion has repeatedly said the staff still believes in the core structure and intends to keep leaning into it rather than overhaul it.
The early-season numbers on under-center usage and play-action success have not matched the vision that helped him land the job.
With McKee—in theory, a more traditional pocket passer—now under center for the foreseeable future while Hurts recovers, there is a narrow window in which Mannion’s preferred concepts could look more natural. The first test for those results did not provide that evidence.
In Jeffrey Lurie's organization, “everything’s on the table” is rarely just an empty message. It is usually a signal that the status quo is no longer defensible.
Whether that means more schematic adjustments, greater involvement from Sirianni in the weekly plan, personnel tweaks, better execution of what is already installed, or more drastically, a change in job descriptions, remains to be seen.
The heat on Mannion, though, is not manufactured by one press conference. It is the product of weeks of low output, visible struggles to establish an identity, and the reality that a first-year coordinator with limited experience is the face of an offense that has not yet delivered.

title: Eagles Refused to Give Tanner McKee the Support He Needed Most in Week 6 Start
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – Good friend DeVonta Smith was back for Week 6 after missing two games and was useful. Dallas Goedert is a good buddy too, and a solid security blanket, and he was both of those things. The quarterback’s best friend, however, is supposed to be a running game.
The Eagles didn’t have one in their 25-14 home loss to the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. Tanner McKee could have used his best friend. Instead, he was forced to throw the ball 45 times. In just his third career start.
It’s like the coaches just said, “Hey Tanner, go win us this game.” For all the talk about everybody playing their part, the Eagles sure put a lot on McKee’s shoulders.
OK, I get it. The Eagles running back room is a lonely place. Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley are on injured reserve. Saquon Barkley has missed the last two games with a hamstring injury. Then, as if that wasn’t bad enough, the Eagles lost Carson Steele to a shoulder injury in the first quarter.
Steele returned later. He took a couple of special teams reps but was then shut down for the second half. That left them with Dameon Pierce and Jaydon Blue, who was added to the roster on Saturday then parked on the bench when the offense took the field.
Reduced to just those two players - one, really, because there was, surprisingly, nothing in the game plan for Blue - doesn’t mean you just stop trying to run the ball, even with an offensive line that is patchwork at best.
You just don’t throw in the towel when the team on the other side of the ball brought with it the next-to-last run defense in the NFL, allowing 168 yards per game.
The Eagles couldn’t be bothered with trying to dent it. Pierce ran it 12 times for 35 yards. McKee ran once for 0 yards.
So, that’s 45 passes to 13 runs. Drunken sailors have better balance.
Nick Sirianni was asked postgame for his thoughts on the imbalance. The coach said something about being behind 19-7 and needing to play catch-up.
“We had to go fast with, I don't know, 12 minutes left or something like that,” he said. “Two possessions; you only scored seven points at that point. You gotta go fast to give yourself a chance to score, which we went down and scored, and then get it back, and that was the mode that we had success on, so we did it again.”
Never mind that on the first play of the game, McKee dropped back and was sacked for an 11-yard loss. Buried in a hole, two more pass plays were dialed up, including one on third-and-21. Neither worked, and they punted.
On their next series, the Eagles threw three more times, one of which was a 3-yard loss to Makai Lemon. That led to another punt. They threw four straight times on their third possession with enough success to at least get a first down.
They threw or tried to throw on their first 10 plays when the score was 0-0 and 3-0.
McKee was asked about playing without a quarterback’s best friend, too. He “um-ed” his way through the answer.
“I'm a quarterback,” he said, mixing in a couple of ‘ums’, “I am excited to execute the play that is called (more 'ums'). I love slinging the ball around. I know I can be better with things like that. I personally, I don't see that as a terrible thing.”
It’s not a winning formula to throw 45 times and run the ball 13 times. Not in the NFL. The best teams like balance in their offense. The Eagles do, too. They’ve shown that to be the case during the last five years when they’ve been to two Super Bowls and won a lot of games.
Sirianni relented a bit later in his answer about the imbalance.
“Obviously, right now we're not running the ball the way we want to,” he said. “You do whatever you gotta do to try to win the game. That's what that game called for. Obviously, we didn't win, but that's what that game called for, and there's circumstances that go to that.”
Barkley could be McKee's best friend, and getting him back could do wonders, but it's still not clear when that will be.

title: 5 Losers & 3 Winners After Eagles' Skid Extends to Four Games With Loss to Panthers
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. – The Tanner McKee era got off to an uneven start. The backup quarterback, pressed into action for at least the next four games after Jalen Hurts landed on injured reserve for the first time in his career with a blood clot in his calf, did some good, but mixed in just enough bad to keep the Eagles winless in their last four games after a 25-14 loss to the Panthers at Lincoln Financial Field in Week 6.
Now, 2-4, the Eagles will prepare for a visit from the Cowboys on Monday Night Football next week.
The game was there to be won, with the Panthers hurting themselves with penalties and the Eagles' defense playing well enough for as long as it could, but the offense just couldn’t quite make it happen.
They made it interesting when McKee hit DeVonta Smith with a touchdown pass (h/t NFL) from 19 yards with 10:47 to play in the fourth quarter that brought Philly to within 19-14, but the momentum left when Jake Majors's bad snap went for a 12-yard loss after the Eagles got the ball at the 48 midway through the fourth, needing a touchdown to take its first lead.
Tanner McKee throws DeVonta Smith a perfect ball for the touchdown CARvsPHI on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/6xngV0MgMW
McKee probably did enough to earn a second start – really, what other options do the Eagles have?
He sprayed the ball high and wide on many of his 45 throws, but other times, when he got the ball out quickly, he was able to find a rhythm and lead a pair of TD drives. The first ended with a two-yard touchdown run by Dameon Pierce to pull the Eagles to within 10-7, a score that stood at halftime. The other was the nice throw to Smith.
McKee was sacked three times, and while his numbers will look decent, some of it was after the Panthers went up 11 points in the final quarter. He finished 26-for-45 with 215 yards, a TD, and no interceptions.
The play-calling was suspect, however. Rather than try to run the ball early, the Eagles dialed up six straight passes, which led to three-and-outs on their first two possessions of the game. They had five of them in the game.
The Panthers (3-2) were called for 13 penalties totaling 149 yards, all in the first half, which ended in Carolina’s favor, 10-7.
Not even the addition of McKee could help the Eagles find a way to score points in both the first and third quarters. They were shut out in both quarters again and have just three points in each of them this season.
DeVonta Smith: His return was most welcome, if not nearly enough to secure a win. He was targeted 14 times and finished with seven catches for 75 yards and a TD.
Jalen Carter: The defensive tackle rarely came off the field. He had two passes batted at the line of scrimmage and three tackles while seemingly playing most of the game.
Dallas Goedert: The tight end had six catches on eight targets for 61 yards.
Jake Majors: With momentum on their side, the Eagles' center had a bad, low snap that lost 12 yards. The Eagles had just gotten a three-and-out stop and took over at the 48-yard line. The Eagles couldn’t overcome the gaffe and punted with 8:30 left.
Special teams: The Eagles had a punt partially blocked after going three-and-out after Majors’s gaffe, giving Carolina good field position. It’s the second straight week the special teams have had a breakdown. Last week it was the kickoff return with eight seconds left that led to defeat. This one allowed the Panthers to open their lead to 11 points.
Running game: Dameon Pierce had his moments. His two-yard touchdown run to cut Carolina’s lead to 10-7 in the second quarter was his first TD since Jan. 5, 2025, while with Houston. He had two in that 2024 season. Still, the Panthers’ defense was next-to-last in the league at stopping the run.
Yet the Eagles managed just 35 yards on the ground, though they rarely tried to run. Pierce had 12 runs, and McKee scrambled for another rush. Carolina entered allowing 168 per game.
Moro Ojomo: The defensive tackle was called for encroachment early in the fourth quarter with the Panthers inside the five and lining up to go for it on fourth down. It was the second time this season Ojomo had a five-yard penalty on a team lining up to go for it on fourth down. The Panthers scored two plays later to open a 19-7 lead with 13:34 to play.
Cooper DeJean: The defensive back is not having the same kind of season he did last year. He committed an illegal contact penalty that gave Carolina a third down, and his inexcusable personal foul with seven minutes to play pushed Carolina deeper into Eagles territory at the 20. Carolina put the game away from there with a touchdown with 6:32 to play.

title: 3 Free-Agent QBs Eagles Must Call Immediately After Losing Jalen Hurts to IR
full_text:
It's been a rocky start to the 2026 NFL season for the Eagles, who are now without star quarterback Jalen Hurts for at least four games. Blood clot issues led to the veteran signal-caller's placement on injured reserve earlier this week, leaving backup QB Tanner McKee as the de facto starting option against the Panthers in Week 6 and for the foreseeable future.
Without Hurts, it remains to be seen if Philadelphia's quarterback room is good enough to turn the season around.
Despite flashes of potential here and there, McKee began Week 6 with only two starts under his belt, and even though the Eagles signed Joe Milton off the Cowboys' practice squad for help this week, he still hasn't started an NFL regular-season game. The same goes for rookie QB Cole Payton, who shouldn't see the field this year unless it's an absolute emergency.
With the aforementioned trio the Eagles' only QB options behind Hurts, general manager Howie Roseman might want to look at bringing in another veteran for help. Although the pickings are somewhat slim at this stage of the season, there are at least three options for the Philly front office to consider.
What's old could become new again.
Philadelphia traded for Andy Dalton back in March to acquire some competition for McKee. The three-time Pro Bowl passer impressed the Eagles enough throughout the offseason to win the No. 2 job from McKee, but his run didn't last long. Dalton attempted one pass that resulted in an interception against the Bears in Week 3 before eventually being released by the Eagles on Oct. 9 .
But now that Hurts is sidelined, the Eagles might want to bring Dalton back. He's already received some calls from other teams since his release, according to NFL insider Mike Garafolo, who added that "Dalton is an option to return for the Eagles."
Andy Dalton is an option to return for the #Eagles . He’s had a few teams check in with him since the team released him, per sources, though there’s familiarity and a clear role in Philly for him if he decides to return. https://t.co/bNeypdIjiO
Sometimes, familiarity trumps all, and that's what Dalton has with the Eagles. He might not want to learn another new system at this stage of his career, so running things back in Philly could be the most attractive option if the Eagles join the teams already in contact with Dalton.
If the Eagles prefer an option with a championship pedigree, Jimmy Garoppolo could be an interesting possibility for Roseman & Co. to consider.
The former 2014 second-rounder has won two Super Bowls throughout his career, both coming with the Patriots. Although Garoppolo didn't play a large role in either run, you can't take that experience away from him. He's since gained plenty of in-game experience on the West Coast, going 41-21 with a 67.4% completion rate, 15,138 passing yards, 91 touchdowns to 52 interceptions and a 97.2 passer rating in 65 games with the 49ers, Raiders and Rams.
Garoppolo hasn't started a game in nearly two years, but he likely still has enough left in the tank to at least be a reliable backup. His presence could also push young guys like McKee and Milton to step it up, all while giving Payton another veteran presence he can lean on for advice.
He wouldn't be the "Jimmy G" who went 13-3 while passing for almost 4,000 yards and 27 TDs in 2019, but there's a lot worse that the Eagles can do at this point.
The remaining QB options are less than ideal, but Bailey Zappe might be the best of the bunch.
A well-traveled journeyman, Zappe has made steps in New England, Kansas City, Cleveland and New York since being drafted 137th overall in 2022. His resume is far from perfect, but he's only one game below .500 in nine career starts and has completed 62.1% of passes for 2,223 yards, 12 touchdowns and 14 interceptions. That should be enough experience that Sirianni would feel comfortable putting him in a game if needed.
Additionally, Zappe may be motivated to prove himself after being released by the Jets last month. He's only 27 years old, so better days could be ahead, and joining a winning organization like the Eagles could be what he needs to bounce back. Of course, that would be a win-win outcome for both sides, adding to why Philadelphia should give it a shot.

title: McMullen: Eagles’ 2026 Season Has Become Its Own Goodfellas-Like 'Bust-Out'
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — The cleanest analogy for the Eagles’ 2026 season is the iconic Goodfellas (1990) monologue in which Henry Hill (Ray Liotta) explains how Paulie Cicero (Paul Sorvino) bleeds a business dry once he becomes a silent partner.
“Now the guy’s got Paulie as a partner,” Hill says. “Any problems, he goes to Paulie. Trouble with the bill? He can go to Paulie. Trouble with the cops, deliveries, Tommy, he can call Paulie. But now the guy’s gotta come up with Paulie’s money every week, no matter what. Business bad? (EXPLETIVE) you, pay me. Oh, you had a fire? (EXPLETIVE) you, pay me. Place got hit by lightning, huh? (EXPLETIVE) you, pay me.”
The Nick Sirianni era’s sustained success is the original healthy business in this comparison. Reaching and then exceeding those heightened expectations is the weekly payment that now has to be made regardless of circumstance.
The “bust-out” is underway after significant adversity. The organization and the fan base have signed on as partners. There are no more free weeks in Philadelphia.
Lane Johnson retires? Three novices starting on the offensive line? Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith both out? (EXPLETIVE) you, win.
The bill is still due on game day, lightning strikes or not.
Maybe the Vatican won’t be chiming in, but the Eagles staying competitive against the Rams and Jaguars in Weeks 4 and 5—and still in position to win late in both—already qualifies as a minor miracle under the current conditions. Moral victories can't even bring temporary relief; however, never mind canceling the next installment.
The stress inside the Jefferson Health Training Complex hit a new peak this week once it became clear that Jalen Hurts could miss extended time as he landed on injured reserve with a blood clot. The organization is at its breaking point, and the next payment is due against the Panthers on Sunday.
Tanner McKee will start at quarterback. His running backs will be Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele and Jaydon Blue. Willie Lampkin and Jake Majors are expected to make their second NFL starts, while Markel Bell is on No. 3, serving as the mixture of youth and duct tape . At least Smith is expected back, which removes one hurdle, but the overall picture remains bleak.
Through it all, the refrain does not change. The context does not get a vote. The Eagles are deep enough into the Sirianni-era success cycle that the only acceptable answer to every new problem is still the same two words: win anyway.
Right now, that's still the only standard that's acceptable and it's not realistic.

title: Eagles vs. Panthers: Who Wins and Why in Week 6
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — It’s been one body blow after another for the Eagles. Perhaps it will be one too many for them to absorb, and they will be knocked out. Not just on Sunday, when the Panthers visit for a 1 p.m. ET kickoff at Lincoln Financial Field, but for the season.
The team’s injury reports this week have had the length of a CVS receipt : the starting quarterback and the three top running backs are out, the offensive line is young and inexperienced, and the safety position is in disarray thanks to injuries to Marcus Epps and Michael Carter.
That said, here are some keys to determining who wins Sunday's Eagles vs. Panthers showdown and why.
It’s not like this Carolina group is the Monsters of the Midway, ranking near the bottom in total defense at No. 29. It’s that the Eagles are starting Tanner McKee , who began the season as the third-string QB and was elevated to the No. 2 last week when Andy Dalton was released.
This will be his third career start in his fourth season and his sixth game overall. His numbers aren’t bad: five touchdowns to one interception and a 61.4% completion rate. There may be more starts ahead depending on the health of Hurts, who was ruled out on Thursday with a superficial blood clot in his calf.
Sidenote: While McKee is the Eagles’ backup, Kenny Pickett is the backup in Carolina. Pickett, of course, is a former Eagles backup QB and won a Super Bowl with them in 2024.
The former Eagles edge rusher, who played just eight games in Philly after being acquired at the trade deadline from Miami, has played 70% of the defensive snaps for his new team and has collected two sacks, one in each of his last two games.
Because Phillips lines up all over the defense, he will likely face both the Eagles’ tackles, though with this being just the third career start for rookie blocker Markel Bell, he may line up over the right tackle more often than not.
The Panthers quarterback Bryce Young is off to one of the best starts of his four-year career. He has the Panthers ranked third in the league in total offense, with a passing offense that is at the top of the NFL heap. He has completed 62% of his throws with nine touchdowns and just two interceptions.
Quinyon Mitchell will likely matchup with Young’s top target, Tetairoa McMillan, who is 10th in the league in receiving yards with 385 and three touchdowns on 26 catches.
Dameon Pierce is the Eagles' fourth-string running back and got his first game action last week, but he will get the bulk of the carries against a Panthers run defense that, statistically, is one of the worst in the league, ranked 31st. Pierce had 11 carries for just 14 yards last week.
It hasn’t happened often, but a team that plays an international game that meets a team coming off a bye week is 0-4. The Eagles, of course, played in London last week. The Panthers had the weekend off.

title: Tanner McKee's Time Is Now for Eagles After Jalen Hurts Lands On IR
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – For the first time in his seven-year NFL career, quarterback Jalen Hurts was placed on injured reserve with a superficial blood clot in his leg . The Eagles made the move on Saturday afternoon, a day before they host the Carolina Panthers in Week 6.
This is Tanner McKee’s team now.
“As a quarterback, especially as a backup quarterback, you have to be ready at a moment's notice,” said McKee. “The thing that's been nice is the way I prepare, and the way that I've been preparing is not going to change. I feel like these last few weeks of being whether it was the three, the two, the one, whatever it was the preparation's gonna be the same.”
McKee has been here for four years. He’s no stranger to playing in front of a demanding fan base or to winning games. It's a small sample size, but he's 1-1 in his two starts. He will play in his seventh NFL game and make his third career start, throwing five touchdowns and only one interception.
There’s no quarterback available in free agency, and general manager Howie Roseman isn't trading for one who can step in and start immediately in Sean Mannion’s offense, which McKee called "wordy."
McKee can do it, though. All week, his teammates have expressed confidence in his ability to get the job done.
“Great quarterback,” said rookie receiver Makai Lemon on Friday. “He's been having a good week of practice. I'm excited to get out there and I'm excited for him to get that job, that spotlight, because I feel like he's ready for it.”
“It's been smooth, man,” said DeVonta Smith, who will return to the lineup after missing the last two games with a hamstring injury. “He takes command of the offense when he gets his opportunity and things like that. He's done a great job of making sure everybody's on the same page and things, so it's smooth.”
Depending on how McKee does, he could play himself into a second contract in Philly or elsewhere. The Eagles have four games until the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
If he plays reasonably well, and his teammates rally around him, there’s a chance the Eagles could be buyers in the trade market. If the slide continues, they will try to trade some players and plan for the future.
What does the future look like?
If the Eagles miss the playoffs, will they part ways with head coach Nick Sirianni? I don’t think so.
Will they part ways with Hurts? Again, I don’t think so.
They could run this back in 2027 and see how far Sirianni and Hurts can take a healthy team with some new blood added and some of the old talent flushed out. If they don’t get to the postseason and make a run, it could make sense to start fresh in 2028 with a new coach and new quarterback.
General manager Howie Roseman has already loaded up on draft picks in ’28, with a pair of firsts and a pair of seconds. More could come depending on how the rest of the month goes and whether he trades some talent to get premium picks back in 2027 and 2028.
That’s looking too far ahead, though. In the short term, the Eagles will rely on McKee and a running back group that started the year on the practice squad. Running back Jaydon Blue took Hurts’ roster spot, and he will join a backfield of Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele. The Eagles elevated a pair of rookies from the practice squad for Sunday—outside linebacker Keyshawn James-Newby and safety Cole Wisniewski.
“He's the starter for a reason this week,” said rookie quarterback Cole Payton, who will be McKee’s backup this week. “We have a ton of faith in him and a ton of confidence in him. I've got his back, but super excited to watch him.”

title: Eagles' Linebacker Rotation Plan Set to Debut in Week 6
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA - The Eagles are expected to rotate linebackers Jihaad Campbell and Jeremiah Trotter Jr. opposite All-Pro Zack Baun on Sunday against the Carolina Panthers, something defensive coordinator Vic Fangio confirmed earlier this week.
The plan, which calls for a series-by-series split rather than situation-specific substitutions, was originally set to debut in last Sunday’s 19-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London.
It never materialized after Trotter was ejected following a scuffle on the opening kickoff. Fangio, though, rejected a broadcast report that Trotter was slated to start, calling it “an out and out lie,” while acknowledging the team intended to get him more work.
The decision stems primarily from Trotter’s performance in Week 4 against the Los Angeles Rams. Filling in for an injured Baun, who was out in the concussion protocol, the third-year linebacker recorded a career-high 15 tackles and a pass breakup in the 24-20 loss.
“Trot played good in the start that he had when Zack was out,” Fangio said. “It was close. I just think he deserves playing time.”
Fangio described Campbell’s effort in London as “OK” when asked by Eagles On SI and said he has no concerns that a reduced role could potentially derail the talented second-year player’s progress.⁠
Campbell, the Eagles’ 2025 first-round pick (No. 31 overall out of Alabama), entered the season as the full-time starter opposite Baun after Nakobe Dean left in free agency for Las Vegas.
Through five games the 22-year-old has 42 tackles, a sack, a tackle for loss, a forced fumble, and a quarterback hit. His Pro Football Focus grades have been disappointing, with stronger tackling metrics offset by struggles in coverage and mediocre instincts for the position. Lately, he's been dealing with knee and wrist injuries that may be contributing to some of the issues.
Trotter, a 2024 fifth-round selection out of Clemson and the son of Eagles Hall of Famer Jeremiah Trotter Sr., doesn’t have Campbell’s athletic gifts but seems to have a better feel for the game.
In theory, Trotter’s ability to the Mike spot, could also free up the playmaking Baun to handle the Will position, which allows a little more freedom in Fangio’s scheme.
To date, Trotter has largely been a solid special-teams contributor for Michael Clay. Trotter is looking forward to his expanded role, whatever it may look like. In the 2024 postseason, Fangio mulled a rotation with Trotter and veteran Oren Burks after did was injured.
Burks took the baton and played so well that the plan was never implemented.
“I definitely feel good, and I’m excited to go out there and get some more opportunity. I can’t wait to utilize it,” Trotter said earlier this week. “But at the same time, this is football. They’re calling my name, so I gotta go out there and do my job and perform. At the end of the day, I guess it’s nothing new. I just gotta go out there and do my job.”
Trotter pointed to his Rams performance as the moment that built trust. “Just doing my job, showing that they can trust me to go out there and be where I need to be and make the plays that I should make. I feel like they gained trust for me during that game.”
Fangio and linebackers coach Bobby King were impressed by Trotter's performance telling him that he “had a really good game, and they were super proud.”
Both players framed the competition positively. “Trot’s a good player. He’s been playing great ball too,” Campbell said. “Football is all about competition… our whole room is ready for preparation and ready for domination.”
Trotter echoed that sentiment, noting the two have pushed each other for years: “We’ve been pushing each other back and forth, just sharing knowledge, making each other better. I feel like that’s what makes great teams, when you got competition and you’re out there just pushing one another, just learning from one another. We have a really talented backer room and a really talented group in general, and we’ve got a lot of depth.”
On the validation of his patience and offseason work, Trotter said, “I definitely think that hard work definitely pays off, and I’m just starting to see the fruits of that labor. I just thank God that He’s allowing it to come into fruition, and I’m just really excited to go out there and do my part on the defense and help the team any way I can in my role.”
In general, linebacker is not a rotational role in Fangio's defense so Trotter's ascent is notable and Campbell's failure to grab the baton Burks once did is one of the more disappointing developments for the Eagles' defense early this season.

title: DeVonta Smith's Potential Return Provides Tanner McKee With Much-Needed Weapon
full_text:
When it comes to injury issues and the Philadelphia Eagles this season, the news has been overwhelmingly bad. The Eagles have had a plethora of players dealing with injuries all season , and star quarterback Jalen Hurts being suddenly sidelined indefinitely due to a superficial blood clot in his calf is just icing on the cake.
But, the Eagles finally got a bit of good news in the injury department heading into their crucial Week 6 matchup against the Carolina Panthers. After missing the past two games due to a hamstring injury, star receiver DeVonta Smith returned to practice this week and is expected to play for Philadelphia on Sunday. His return will provide backup quarterback Tanner McKee with a much-needed weapon for his third career start.
Having Smith out on the field should be a big boon for McKee, who will want as much talent as possible around him to make his job easier. Keep in mind, the Eagles will be without the top three running backs on the depth chart, including starter Saquon Barkley, leaving practice squad players Dameon Pierce	and Carson Steele as the team's top two active backs.
So, it could be tough for the offense to establish much of a rushing attack, meaning that McKee is probably going to have to air it out to keep the Eagles in the game.
Having a true No. 1 wide receiver out there in Smith will not only provide McKee with a reliable target to focus on, but it could also work to open things up for other players on the offense. Carolina's secondary will be forced to pay a lot of attention to Smith and they'll likely put their top cornerback on him.
The more attention paid to Smith, the less paid to Philadelphia's other pass-catchers like Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper and Dallas Goedert. Those guys are all capable of making plays, especially with Smith setting the tone.
Then, if the passing game gets going, perhaps that could soften things up for the ground game, as the defense wouldn't be able to pack the box as much if the Eagles are moving the ball well through the air. Everything on offense is connected, so Smith's potential return is great news for McKee.
Smith and McKee already have some chemistry together, as they've enjoyed some shared on-field success before. In fact, the first completion of McKee's professional career came on a pass to Smith during a game against the Cowboys in December of 2024.
Tanner McKee connects with DeVonta Smith for the first completion of his NFL career pic.twitter.com/WeZnUJN0Tt
The pair also connected on a nice touchdown across the middle later in that same game.
📁 Things We Love To See 📁 Tanner McKee & DeVonta Smith 📁 Touchdown vs. the Cowboys (Kelly Green) pic.twitter.com/kG2zCubj17
So, there's some familiarity there. When asked what McKee does especially well ahead of his start against Carolina, Smith pointed to McKee's ability to take command of the offense, which can often be difficult for backup QBs.
"[He] takes command of the offense," Smith said of McKee . "It's hard for a quarterback to come in who doesn't get a lot of reps and things like that to get with the starting group and just come in and take command. I think he does a great job of taking command."
The Eagles will look to McKee to take command against the Panthers on Sunday, and having his top target in Smith available should make doing so easier.

title: Injuries Taking Toll on Eagles'  RB Room, But 'New' Guys Are Excited for the Moment
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – Meet your Week 6 Eagles running backs: Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele. No preseason prognosticator could have seen this coming. But here we are— no Saquon Barkley, Tank Bigsby, or Will Shipley . Only Barkley has avoided injured reserve among the three, and he will miss his second straight game.
“That's the story of the game, unfortunately,” said Steele, two days before the Eagles host the Carolina Panthers . “It's a blessing for me to be able to play, but it's unfortunate because guys are getting hurt.”
Pierce and Steele still dress at the very back of the locker room in the area the Eagles added in the offseason. They sit with their backs to each other, separated by a wide aisle. The two played together for a couple of weeks in Kansas City with the Chiefs.
“Carson is a great guy,” said Pierce. “Great guy. Cool, down to earth, man. You would think he from Cali, that's how cool he is.”
How great can they be together in Philly? We’re about to find out.
Steele played his first 20 snaps with the Eagles last week. They all came on special teams. Earlier in the week, offensive coordinator Sean Mannion said Steele has worn a lot of hats for the Eagles in the first month of the season. He wasn’t kidding.
Steele said he has taken practice reps at tight end and lined up as a receiver. He could get some carries on Sunday and maybe even see some time at fullback, something Mannion alluded to when asked if that could happen.
Pierce went to London not expecting much playing time. He ended up with 48 snaps (77 percent) after Shipley left with a foot injury. He had 11 carries, but for just 14 yards.
“Shaking off some rust getting back acclimated to everything,” he said. “Just playing ball, getting comfortable, getting your feet back wet, man. Man, you don't forget how to ride a bike, but you can darn sure fall off of it.”
Pierce woke up on Monday feeling like he did fall of a bike.
“As soon as we landed from London, I got up like Frankenstein,” he said.
That Pierce was even able to be in London required some foresight. He had never been out of the country before, but he figured he should get a passport last year, just in case.
He looked like a breakout star in 2022 when he ran for 939 yards and four touchdowns as a rookie with the Texans. He hasn’t had a season like that since, and signed as a free agent with the Eagles. He was released after training camp but came back to work on the practice squad, hoping maybe he’d get another chance.
Now, "just in case" is here.
“That's part of working,” he said. “That's part of keeping your head down in this league, because the league can chew you up and swallow you if you let it.”

title: Mike McCarthy Nearly Cost Steelers a Win
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers continued their disappointing trend to begin the 2026 season, dropping their third straight on the road to start their first campaign under a new head coach.
The Steelers’ 0-3 record away from Acrisure Stadium can be dealt with. Lots of teams deal with this type of situation year in and year out.
But one piece of this remains unaddressed and unresolved, like a ghost in the attic that refuses to depart. Once again, a coaching blunder cost the Steelers a victory in regulation. Through the first six weeks of the season, Mike McCarthy is guiding this team to wins, but he's failing to live up to many of his training camp words.
A huge component of training camp were these supposed high-intensity moments during practice sessions. Wherever players were, when a certain signal occurred, everyone went to the main field for some type of truncated high-stress situation. Most of the focus was on two-minute drills and red zone opportunities.
The goal was to get this team ready for the adversity and tough moments an NFL game brings. McCarthy dubbed them “Franco Moments” at camp.
The Steelers had a golden opportunity to take what they focused on at camp and put it into action. With less than two minutes left in their Week 6 contest, the Steelers’ defense forced a turnover and gave the offense the ball inside the Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ 5-yard line.
The strategy is rather simple in this scenario. The goal is to run out the clock while putting up points. That usually translates into a couple of handoffs with plenty of time in between snaps.
So, what did the Steelers do? They ran a play-action pass on first down, followed that up with a handoff to Jaylen Warren for a yard, and then went back to the pass on third down. Both passing attempts were incomplete, stopping the clock each time. The Steelers ended the drive with a field goal and the lead, but it left ample time for the Bucs to get into field goal range.
Asked after the game about what his considerations were when the offense took the field for that drive, McCarthy's answer was less than illuminating.
"Absolutely. You're talking clock. The first down, it was a boot," he said. "Then the second down, the run, we caught them with 10 on the field, so you know, it was a substitution and all of those things, but definitely was aware of the clock there."
Okay, so you don't take as much time off the clock as you wanted to. That's not the end of the world. The Steelers had the chance to stonewall the Bucs before they tied the game up.
The defense failed. They gave up a big play immediately that brought the Bucs into field goal range.
But McCarthy's blunder came with how he managed the clock. With roughly 30 seconds left on the clock, the Bucs trotted their field goal unit onto the field. Instead of immediately calling timeout and stopping the clock, he allowed it to run down to 13 seconds before the officials stopped the game clock.
After the game, he chalked it up to a miscommunication between himself and the officials.
"Yeah, there was some miscommunication there," he admitted. "We were thinking right away (of calling timeout) there at 34, 35 (seconds). Then there was just some miscommunication between the referee and I. So, that's why it went down as low as it did. But, ultimately, it worked out."
Yes, it did work out for the Steelers. But only in spite of the decisions their head coach made.
The team did what McCarthy asked coming out of Week 5. The team stacked victories and improved to 4-2. They also stacked coaching blunders, which should be as concerning as the back-to-back wins.

title: Steelers WR Search Heating Up: What It Means
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are well aware of the wide receiver issue plaguing their offense right now. With Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson both on the Injured Reserve, the offense has just two reliable targets for quarterback Aaron Rodgers.
Even though the Steelers made the most of things with a gutsy win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 6, the organization knows it cannot continue with this roster of receivers for the remainder of 2026.
Apparently, the organization isn't just sulking over the issue, they are actively trying to address it. According to NFL insider Tom Pelissero, the Steelers are "calling around" to upgrade their wide receiver room. On a recent update on his Substack page, The Sweep with Tom Pelissero , general manager Omar Khan is inquiring around the league, and two names, Jalen Tolbert and KaVontae Turpin, have some immediate ties to Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy.
"Jalen Tolbert and KaVontae Turpin are the two guys with connections to Mike (McCarthy) that are on rosters now and know his offense," he wrote. "But I haven’t heard of anything on either front. I do know the Steelers have been calling around on veteran wide receivers since the injuries last week and I’d imagine that continues with two WR on IR."
Both of these names are being thrown out there because of their ties to McCarthy, and that makes sense. During his time as the head coach of the Dallas Cowboys, both Tolbert and Turpin enjoyed career-best performances.
During the 2024 season, McCarthy's final year in Dallas, Tolbert produced in an anomalistic way. Over 17 games, he hauled in 49 receptions for 610 yards and seven touchdowns.
While Turpin didn't reach the same heights as Tolbert, he still had career-high numbers under McCarthy. During that same 2024 campaign, Turpin 31 receptions for 420 yards and two scores.
It's true that both receivers put up respectable numbers under McCarthy, and expecting either veteran to come to Pittsburgh and be a decent player is reasonable. It's not a guarantee, however.
Tolbert is the perfect example. Outside of his 610-yard season in 2024, he's never exceeded 300 receiving yards in a season. Now in his fifth year in the NFL, his ceiling is concretely set as a bottom-of-the-depth-chart player.
Turpin was slightly more productive after McCarthy's departure. In 2025, he posted just under 400 receiving yards and two more touchdowns. Still, it's the same type of production that Tolbert delivered.
The problem is that it doesn't solve the issue for the Steelers. Depth is wonderful and sorely needed for this injury-riddled squad, but it doesn't solve their problems. If anything, it continues them. Both veterans are solid, unexciting options that would only add to the sea of averageness taking up the Pittsburgh depth chart.
If the Steelers are truly trying to upgrade, they have to get creative and accept that it comes with a cost. That remains unlikely to be the case, so low-priced veterans are the route they will go.
But unless the Steelers want to give up a high draft pick to make a deal, they won't be getting that number one or two receiver to strengthen the position.
That leaves players like Tolbert and Turpin. Free agents like Marquez Valdes-Scantling. That leaves practice squad players like KJ Osborn and Xavier Gipson.
The Steelers are looking for receivers, that's certainly clear. It's just a matter of where they are looking that remains to be seen.

title: 5 Winners, 3 Losers From Steelers Comeback Win Over Bucs
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers looked out of sync for most of their Week 6 matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Then the fourth quarter happened.
Down 13 points with just under 14 minutes left in the game, the Steelers fought their way back into it and even took a 19-16 lead with 1:21 left before Tampa Bay sent it into overtime.
From there, Pittsburgh drove 70 yards down the field and put seven points up on the board courtesy of Germie Bernard's first career touchdown.
The Steelers' defense turned the Buccaneers over on downs on the ensuing possession, moving them to 4-2 on the year heading into a Week 7 meeting with the New Orleans Saints in Paris.
With that, here are our winners and losers from Pittsburgh's comeback victory on the road.
After missing the Steelers' Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts with an ankle injury, Dean was a hero in his return to Tampa Bay.
Facing the team that he won a Super Bowl with and spent the first seven seasons of his career playing for, Dean picked off Jalon Daniels with just under two minutes left in the contest while it was tied up at 16-16.
That set up Pittsburgh at the Buccaneers' three-yard line, and while it didn't punch the ball into the end zone, Chris Boswell made a 20-yard field goal that put the black and gold ahead before Tampa Bay sent the game into overtime.
Dean also posted six passes defended, per ESPN .
Watt has cooled down rather significantly over the past few weeks.
After recording 4.5 sacks through Week 4, he failed to record a single stat over 51 snaps vs. Indianapolis.
Then, against the Buccaneers, Watt had just two pressures across 37 pass rushing reps (per SumerSports ). He remains an elite run defender, but the Steelers simply need far more production from him.
Ramsey showed up in a big way for a Steelers secondary that had a bounce-back performance across the board.
He was all over the field vs. Tampa Bay, recording two sacks (including one on the last play of the game) and constantly getting into the backfield against the run, as evidenced by his four tackles for loss.
Ramsey also had the second-most tackles for Pittsburgh with 10, which was one less than Payton Wilson's total.
Iheanachor, after a dominant outing against the Colts last week, had a rough showing in this one.
Per SumerSports , the first-round right tackle gave up a sack to David Walker while also allowing four total pressures.
With Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) on the reserve/injured list while Ben Skowronek (calf) was inactive for this contest, Bernard stepped up for a second-straight week.
Aaron Rodgers could've lost some faith in Bernard after running backwards on a 4th-and-3 and being short of the sticks in the first quarter despite initially having the first down, but he didn't.
Instead, Bernard logged 87 yards on 11 catches and scored what ultimately became the game-winning touchdown in overtime.
Much like Iheanachor, Fautanu had trouble holding up in pass protection.
The third-year left tackle's day looked strikingly similar to Iheanachor's from a statistical perspective too, as he also gave up four pressures and a sack to Walker (per SumerSports).
At long last, Herbig came alive as a pass rusher and notched his first two sacks of the season in this game.
The 24-year-old also had four total pressures (per SumerSports) and picked up three tackles for loss.
It took time for him to get going, but Metcalf came up clutch when Pittsburgh needed him the most.
He logged six receptions for 51 yards in the fourth quarter as the Steelers made up a 13-point difference while also hauling in a 16-yard pass on 3rd-and-13 in overtime that kept the drive alive and helped lead to Bernard's touchdown.
When it was all said and done, Metcalf closed out the day with 11 receptions (his most in a single game with Pittsburgh) for 93 yards.

title: Steelers vs. Buccaneers Takeaways: The Comeback Tells Nothing
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- Jamel Dean revenge game. That's it. The Pittsburgh Steelers defeated the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 26-19 in Week 6 in a crazy overtime game. But the final quarter-plus was what mattered in this one.
Dean intercepted Jalon Daniels with under two minutes remaining in a tied ball game. Dean, who played well all game, took the ball down to the three-yard line, setting the Steelers up for a field goal. It wasn't the end as the Buccaneers kicked their own field goal and sent the game into overtime. But Pittsburgh finished strong, scoring in OT and leaving Raymond James Stadium winners in this one.
Outside of Dean's heorics, the Steelers walk away with a 4-2 record and a season that's still very much so alive. But things weren't pretty. This game was tough to watch, and left plenty of takeaways for the black and gold.
The Steelers were not a good football team for three quarters. Truthfully, they were pitiful. Their offense wasn't awake, their quarterback was struggling, their stars were nowhere to be found and their defense was bland at best.
It was as poor of a showing as they could put on.
But the fourth quarter told a different story. Aaron Rodgers found his mojo and started moving around, DK Metcalf became the fourth quarter hero he's been on several occasions this season and the defense put pressure on Jalon Daniels.
Everything flipped, and the Steelers walked away winners. And while it wasn't pretty, it's a win. Sometimes in the NFL, that's all you can ask for.
Now, in terms of reflection, there isn't much good. Yes, a victory keeps the season moving in the right direction, but the team has some serious concerns leaving Tampa Bay.
The Steelers have the worst kick return team in the NFL, and the conversation would be much less notable if they didn't spend a fourth-round pick on a player who is putting up numbers comparable to Cordarrelle Patterson's only year in Pittsburgh.
There was a moment of life for Wetjen in the first half of this game, but it was called back by a blindside block by Cole Holcomb. Immediately afterward, things went back to their disappointing ways, and seemingly got worse as the game went on.
The special teams unit as a whole is a disaster right now. Chris Boswell is becoming a bigger concern than an asset for this team, missing another field goal against the Bucs, and the coverage teams are average at best.
None of it's good. But the thing that stands out the most is how bizarre it is to continue keeping Kaden Wetjen around, or on the game-day roster, especially when the team is banged up at wide receiver.
At this point, it doesn't make any sense to keep things the same. And starting by ending the Kaden Wetjen experiment feels like the right call.
Who knows what it is, but Aaron Rodgers looks like a completely different, and much worse, quarterback on the road compared to at home. When the Steelers are playing at Acrisure Stadium, Rodgers is sharp, dynamic, athletic at times, and makes plays.
On the road, he's almost scared. He throws off his back foot a ton, doesn't try to extend plays and hasn't been able to find consistent momentum in any of the team's three road games.
Rodgers' energy is the life and death of the Steelers' offense. When he's hot, they're moving well, making big plays and winning games. When he's not, there's no life to this group.
On the road, there hasn't been any energy in three games.
This team doesn't stand a chance without Rodgers playing well. And at 4-2, they're going to need him to find his footing on the road before this season gets out of hand.
The Steelers need Elandon Roberts, or at least need to test him out. Patrick Queen is just nowhere to be found, and when he is involved in a play, he's usually behind an offensive player, chasing someone down or just standing near the play.
It's all around bad for Queen right now.
There are a lot of players on Pittsburgh's defense who are underperforming. None seem to be as crucial and disappointing as Queen, though, and none seem to have a replacement option as good as Elandon Roberts.
Who knows if Roberts provides better play than Queen is giving the Steelers, but he's worth a shot.
Maybe a physical inside linebacker is what the Steelers need most. But even if it's not, this group can't be playing much worse, so you might as well try.
It's not too surprising that DK Metcalf has vanished from the Steelers' offense outside of the fourth quarter, but it is concerning. Metcalf has struggled all season, and it's looking more like the team needs to find other options, because him being on the field doesn't add much to this receiving core.
Metcalf finished Week 5 against the Indianapolis Colts with three receptions for 12 yards. He finished Week 6 against the Buccaneers with 11 receptions for 97 yards.
He had 12 yards coming into the fourth quarter. And while it's nice to get contributions late in the game, Pittsburgh needs three more quarters of play from their top wideout.
It's evident that Metcalf is no longer a true WR1 in the NFL, but that shouldn't mean he's no longer a contributor to an offense.
Metcalf, McCarthy, Rodgers - who knows what needs to change, but something does. The Steelers need Metcalf to get involved, and actually make plays. Otherwise, general manager Omar Khan better be on the phone looking for another wideout.

title: HC Mike McCarthy Gets Injured During Steelers Game
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers ' head coach has joined the team's list of injuries.
According to the CBS Sports broadcast of the Steelers ' Week 6 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Mike McCarthy spent the entirety of halftime in the blue medical tent.
As a result, McCarthy did not head to the locker room at all with Pittsburgh down 13-3 once the first half had concluded.
#Steelers HC Mike McCarthy is injured and spent the entire halftime in the blue medical tent. He’s still coaching now in the second half. Here’s the video: pic.twitter.com/9AKTipW7R2
It's not often that you see a head coach go down with an injury in the NFL. McCarthy likely wasn't able to make the necessary halftime adjustments while he was being checked out, meaning the rest of the Steelers' coaching staff had to pick up the slack following a disappointing start on the road for the black and gold.
McCarthy's offense has been dealing with quite a few injuries, especially at wide receiver. Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) are both on the reserve/injured list, and Ben Skowronek (calf) is inactive vs. Tampa Bay.
Now, all eyes are on McCarthy, who was seen walking around with a noticeable limp as he looks to get Pittsburgh back into the game against Jalon Daniels and company.
So far this season, Pittsburgh has struggled to get much of anything going on the road.
In its first game away from Acrisure Stadium, the Steelers fell by a score of 20-3 to the New England Patriots in Week 2 at Gillette Stadium.
Then, in a Week 4 Thursday Night Football vs. the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field, Pittsburgh lost a 27-24 nailbiter to its division rivals.
When the black and gold have suited up at home, however, it's been a completely different story. The Steelers opened the campaign with a 20-13 victory over the Atlanta Falcons, and in Week 3 they took down the Cincinnati Bengals by a score of 30-27 before taking down the Indianapolis Colts 34-22 in Week 5.
Those road struggles have popped back up thus far against the Bucs, though, continuing what's becoming a bit of a worrying trend for Pittsburgh.
The Steelers are going to have to hunker down at some point and figure out a way to show up when they're on the road, especially against opponents on the same level as them, or else they run the risk of their season falling apart.

title: Steelers CB Injured on Punt Return vs. Bucs
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers had absolutely nothing going for them during the first half against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. What was supposed to be a statement game for the team's offense and a chance to get their first road victory quickly turned into a nightmare through the first two quarters.
The rough start continued for the Steelers, as an injury to a key defender brought even more negativity to the team.
As the Buccaneers punted to end their final offensive drive of the first half, Tampa Bay's special teams had a free runner at Steelers returner Kaden Wetjen. It wasn't due to lack of coverage, however, it was because cornerback and jammer on the punt return team, Brandin Echols, was injured during the play. As the action came to a close, Echols was seen limping off the field.
After halftime ended, the Steelers ruled Echols out for the remainder of the game with a hamstring injury. ESPN's Brooke Pryor provided the update via her X account.
Steelers CB Brandin Echols (hamstring) is OUT
The Steelers had a beat up secondary entering Week 6, and this injury to Echols is only more concerning. The defense received a boost with the r eturn of veteran Jamel Dean, but Echols was a key part of the depth in Pittsburgh.
Without Echols, the defense will need even more from rookie Daylen Everette. The recent third-round pick has been pressed into more and more responsibility as the 2026 season has progressed. With the loss of Joey Porter Jr. earlier in the campaign, Everette went from reserve defensive back to first-team outside corner.
Where the Steelers will need Everette or anyone else to step up the most is on special teams. Echols plays a crucial role on the both the kicking and return units. As a jammer on the punt return, he's the primary blocker for the return man. Without him doing his job, the returner has no shot of producing a positive play.
On the punt team, Echols is usually one of the gunners. Due to his speed, he's a huge asset on the outside, tracking down the punt returner. The team is already down a Pro Bowl-caliber gunner in Ben Skowronek, who was ruled out for Week 6 earlier in the week.
This isn't even the first time Echols has been injured on a special teams snap this season. He sustained a concussion earlier in the year on a heroic play that forced a fumble and turnover for the Steelers.
The Steelers haven't had a consistent special teams performance this season. Under new special teams coordinator Danny Crossman, this group has regressed. They were far from elite in 2025, but on either side of the ball, thie Steelers' special teams are underachieving.

title: Steelers Get Starting CB Back Against Bucs
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers have been ravaged by injuries early into the 2026 season, but they received a bit of good news ahead of their Week 6 contest against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
The latest bit of news is a notable boost to the Steelers’ defense. After missing the team’s Week 5 contest with an ankle injury, Jamel Dean has been trending in the right direction. He rejoined his teammates on the practice field, albeit in a limited capacity.
That was enough, however, to get Dean back to where he and the team needed him to be active. Ahead of kick-off against the Buccaneers, Dean was ruled active for the contest, giving the Steelers their top cornerback back as they seek their first road victory of the season.
The Steelers were without Dean for one game, but his absence was felt. Dean is not only the elder statesman in the cornerback room, he’s also the leader of the depth chart. He’s a competitive defender who can play effectively in both zone and man-based coverages.
He was also quite productive in his first few weeks in a Steelers uniform. Through four games, he had 14 tackles to go alone with two forced fumbles and two passes defended. With him back on the field, the pressure is immediately lessened on players like Asante Samuel Jr. and rookie Daylen Everette.
What Dean provides, more than anything, is insight into the Buccaneers organization. A former third-round pick of the franchise in 2019, Dean’s entire career was spent in Tampa before signing with the Steelers. He won a Super Bowl with the Bucs, and he has a close relationship with many of the players and coaching staff still in Tampa.
That knowledge is vital. The little tells, the tendencies and the acquired knowledge he gained during his tenure with the Buccaneers could be the big difference between the Steelers leaving Raymond James Stadium with a win or a loss.
While it’s a tremendous boost to the defense to have Dean available, they have to proceed with some caution. Dean has been battling this ankle injury for a few weeks, and even with his return to action, it’s not clear if he is at 100% health.
That’s why the Steelers have to be cautious with Dean. The risk of aggravating this lower-body ailment is still present, and this team cannot afford to be without him long-term.
That could influence how the Steelers deploy him in his first game back. They can’t limit his snaps too much, but there may be a series or two where Samuel and Everette are the two corners on the outside.
Either way, the Steelers are pumped to have their veteran leader back in the secondary.

title: Steelers Get Good News on Pat Freiermuth for Bucs Game
full_text:
One of the Pittsburgh Steelers' top weapons in the passing game is expected to play against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 6.
Despite being deemed questionable in what was a late entry to the injury report with a calf injury, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport has reported that the Steelers are optimistic tight end Pat Freiermuth will suit up vs. Tampa Bay.
The #Steelers are optimistic that TE Pat Freiermuth, who was added to the injury report with a calf injury on Saturday, will play, sources say.
With DK Metcalf (illness) having been removed from the injury report while Rico Dowdle (toe) is also expected to be active for the first time since Week 2, Pittsburgh has finally received some positive news on the injury front as it looks to move to 4-2 on the season.
The connection between Freiermuth and Aaron Rodgers during the latter's first season as a Steeler in 2025 never seemed to fully come together.
That isn't to say Freiermuth wasn't productive, as he did finish the year with 486 yards and four touchdowns, but those numbers represeted a noticeable drop-off from the 653 yards and seven scores he posted in the 2024 campaign.
There were signs that the rapport between Rodgers and Freiermuth was growing in a new offensive system during the summer, though, and that's translated to an extent through the first five weeks of the season.
Freiermuth has posted 169 yards thus far, meaning he's on pace for rough 575 yards over 17 games, and he's also already matched his touchdown total from 2025 with four.
He's been more involved as a whole in Mike McCarthy's offense than he was in Arthur Smith's last year too, playing 69 percent of the team's snaps after being on the field for 51 percent of them in 2025 (per Pro Football Reference ).
With both Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) on the reserve/injured list while Ben Skowronek (calf) is out against the Buccaneers, Pittsburgh's wide receiver depth will be tested in a major way moving forward.
Rookie Germie Bernard is certainly capable of handling an elevated role, as evidenced by his 80-yard performance in the team's Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts, though Kaden Wetjen is the only other healthy receiver on the 53-man roster beyond him and Metcalf. Wetjen has yet to play an offensive snap in his rookie year, however.
The Steelers elevated a pair of receivers in Brandon Smith and Brandon Johnson from their practice squad ahead of their matchup with Tampa Bay. Smith logged 16 offensive snaps after coming up from the practice squad vs. the Colts, though it might be tough for the team to rely heavily on him in the passing game.
Whether it's inline or from the slot, Freiermuth can help make up for Pittsburgh's absences at receiver as a proven playmaker from the tight end position who offers a potential mismatch.
Whether it's in 11 personnel with three receivers on the field or 12 personnel, where he'd be out there at the same time as Darnell Washington, Freiermuth can move around a bit and be a top target for Rodgers who can help pick up the slack for the time being.

title: Steelers Get Offensive Boost Before Bucs Game
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers offense gets a much-needed boost as they take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 6. According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, running back Rico Dowdle is expected to return to the field for the first time since Week 2 when he suffered a toe injury.
Dowdle dislocated his toe twice in Week 2 against the New England Patriots. He has been sidelined since, returning to practice for the first time last week, but missing the game against the Indianapolis Colts. Now, with his second week of practice in the books, he's back on the field and ready to contribute.
Steelers RB Rico Dowdle (questionable, toe) is expected to play Sunday vs. Bucs, per source. Dowdle has been out since Week 2.
The Steelers could use all of the weapons they can get. Heading into the game, they're without wide receivers Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger), who are both on Injured Reserve. Ben Skowronek (calf) will miss the game, and tight end Pat Freiermuth (calf) popped up on the injury report during the team's final practice day, just 24 hours before kickoff.
The Steelers have found a superstar in Jaylen Warren since Dowdle has been off the field. Warren has taken the team and league by storm, contributing over 100 total yards in all three games since Dowdle got hurt.
He's rushed for over 100 twice, collecting 101 rushing yards, 87 receiving yards and two touchdowns against the Colts in Week 5.
Head coach Mike McCarthy made it known that even when Dowdle returns, Warren is the feature star of the offense, and they'll continue to use him as such.
"Jaylen’s our featured player right now. Let’s make sure we all recognize that. He’s hot. He’s playing great football for us,” McCarthy said. "So it’s important for us as an offense, you know, coaches and players alike, to continue to put him in position to make plays. So, that won’t change."
So, expect Dowdle to become a contributor to the offense right from the jump, but don't look for Warren's snap count to go down too much.
With injuries at wide receiver and tight end, Pittsburgh may be leaning much heavier into their two running backs for the next several weeks, giving Dowdle a good opportunity to find his footing as he returns.
But in a week when the Steelers got bad news after bad news on the offensive side of the ball, they'll head into the game with some much-needed good news in the backfield.
Dowdle finally returns for the Steelers.

title: Steelers Star T.J. Watt's DPOY Stock is Surging
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- An accidental eye gouge couldn't keep Pittsburgh Steelers superstar T.J. Watt off the field in Week 5. Indianapolis Colts tackle Jalen Travis's hands hit Watt up high above his facemask and forced him into the blue medical tent temporarily.
Watt returned in the second half of the Steelers' 34-22 victory over the Colts, but he wasn't quite right. For the first time in the 2026 regular season, Watt was kept off the score sheet after failing to record a tackle or a sack.
Still, through five games he has 13 tackles, 4.5 sacks, a forced fumble, one fumble recovery, two passes defended, an interception and a touchdown. Once again, the 32-year-old is an early-season candidate for the NFL's Defensive Player of the Year Award. But how does he stack up against the league's best so far?
Watt's right in the thick of it, which is exactly what the Steelers were expecting after a down performance in 2025. Two real candidates stand in his way as the regular season marches on.
The biggest challenger for DPOY in 2026 isn't hard to find. Houston Texans star Will Anderson Jr. is one of the richest players in the league, and he's worth every single penny and more than his organization pays him.
Through the first five games, Anderson has been a game-wrecker. He recorded 27 total tackles, 16 of those individually. He leads the league in sacks, with 7.5, one pass defended, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery.
The Texans aren't in the best shape currently, but Will Anderson Jr. certainly is.
The league is dominated by edge rushers right now, and one of the most disruptive right now is Buffalo Bills star Greg Rousseau. The 26-year-old is like a Madden video game cheat code this year, and that's a terrible thing for opposing offenses.
Rousseau is off to a torrid start, with 19 tackles in the first four games. He recorded two sacks in each of the first three games, giving him 6.0 over the first four weeks of the season in addition to three passes defended.
He's a nightmare for quarterbacks, but any ball carrier has to beware of Rousseau. He's forced three fumbles in four games, using a combination of power and technical expertise to pry the ball loose.
Behind Anderson and Rousseau, Watt has to be considered the next favorite. His Week 5 performance has him a bit behind in sack totals, but that is just a blip on the radar as the teams head into the slog of the schedule.
There are some other names to watch as well. Minnesota Vikings linebacker Dallas Turner has been elite to begin this campaign. His teammate, cornerback Byron Murphy, leads the NFL in interceptions so far. New York Jets rookie David Bailey is already crushing the competition as well with 5.0 sacks.
And right at the top of that conversation is Pittsburgh's defensive leader, T.J. Watt.

title: Seahawks See Shake Up in NFC West Standings in Week 6
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are part of a shakeup in the NFC West, even though they were sitting on the couch on Sunday watching the rest of the NFL's Week 6 action.
The Seahawks saw one of the biggest upsets of the season so far, as the Arizona Cardinals beat the Los Angeles Rams 18-16 in the only NFC West game of the day. Here's a look at the standings now after the matchup.
The Niners are the final team to suit up for Week 6 as they take on the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football. They are one of just three undefeated teams in the NFL, alongside the Kansas City Chiefs and Minnesota Vikings, who were on a bye this week.
The 49ers can extend their lead in the NFC West to three games if they find a way to beat the Commanders in the prime-time matchup.
The Seahawks have lost consecutive games for the first time since Weeks 16 and 17 of the 2024 season. The team has lost all three of their games by a combined eight points, which has sparked a lot of frustration in Seattle, especially when it comes to the offense.
Luckily for the Seahawks , they aren't the only ones struggling in the NFC West, as the Cardinals and Rams sit behind them in the standings, having only won 2 games this season.
The Cardinals have two wins this season, both on the road at SoFi Stadium. They beat the Los Angeles Chargers to open the season but then suffered a four-game losing streak, which included a Week 2 loss against the Seahawks in their home opener.
They returned to Los Angeles to face the Rams, where they pulled off an improbable victory as time expired when kicker Chad Ryland knocked down a 43-yard field goal to win the game.
Many considered the Rams to be a Super Bowl favorite going into the season, but the first six weeks of the year have been nothing short of a disappointment. Some of their losses come against strong teams, including the 49ers, Denver Broncos, and Buffalo Bills, but dropping a game at home against the Cardinals when they were favored by more than a touchdown is a big red flag.
Now they find themselves 3.5 games behind the NFC West lead and have some catching up to do in the coming weeks.

title: Seahawks Need to Target Tight End AJ Barner After Week 6 Game
full_text:
There was a lot of hope going into the 2026 NFL Season that the quarterback Sam Darnold would still play like a Pro Bowl-caliber quarterback and the Seattle Seahawks' offense would be unlocked more under new offensive coordinator Brian Fleury . Among the players that could've been given more opportunities is tight end AJ Barner.
​Instead, the offense hasn't found their rhythm, Darnold has regressed and thrown interceptions that cost three games and the running game is flat. This comes after the Seahawks had their worst offensive performances in the 17-14 overtime loss to the Denver Broncos . There are many factors to why the offense is struggling, but the inability to use Barner is showing.
​Barner is the fourth-most targeted pass-catcher through six games this season. He is behind the league's best wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, wide receiver Cooper Kupp and wide receiver Rashid Shaheed. It is clear that the Seahawks' offense revolves around the receivers going deep, far from the line of scrimmage. Barner has caught 15 receptions on 24 targets for 138 yards.
​He has 24 yards less than Shaeheed, who has been underwhelming as the Seahawks' No. 2 receiver. Kupp hasn't been the saving grace for the Seahawks' offense either, as he is well past his prime, but is serviceable enough to account for a few solid catches on good-enough separation against the younger defensive backs. Kupp and Shaheed are getting paid extensively despite their lack of production. Kupp is only one of the two who have a touchdown.
​Barmer hasn’t accounted for a touchdown this season, but that is based on how he has been utilized. Within the last few games, he has been moved from the line of scrimmage to the backfield as a fullback. This has been evident with second-string fullback Brady Russell only having six offensive snaps in the Week 5 loss to the San Francisco 49ers and two against the Broncos. Barner has filled in as more of a fullback in single tight sets, but he'll occasionally get at the line of scrimmage.
​Fleury has to make some changes to this Seahawks’ offense before they face the Kansas City Chiefs at home in Week 7. One way they can improve is by getting Barner out of the backfield as a fullback and putting him back at the line of scrimmage full-time. Barner is the only consistent pass-catching tight end for the Seahawks. He is one of the more trustworthy pass-catchers and he is a tough runner after the catch.
​Barner has only one game this season where he accounted for over 20 yards and one game where he caught more than four receptions. That was in the 33-31 Week 3 road loss to the Washington Commanders, where he made solid screen plays for 15 and 32 yards. Barner finished the game with five receptions for 69 yards. The Seahawks' offense opened up with Barner being a significant factor in the passing game.
​Fleury has a history of working with tight ends and developing into a high-caliber playmaker . It feels like he has limited his potential and the Seahawks’ potential because he is also the best blocker. While the offense should run through JSN, Fleury has to get variety, consistency and aggression with Barner being one of the top targets for Darnold.

title: Should the Seahawks Try to Right the Ship With a Big Trade?
full_text:
A couple weeks ago, I wrote a series of articles discussing possible trade targets for the Seattle Seahawks over the next month. I planned (and still plan on writing) articles this upcoming week exploring even more, as more teams make themselves firesale candidates. But before we go any further, let’s make sure that it’s even a good idea on the face of it.
First, understand that this discussion isn’t about a small trade that provides a push in the right direction in an area that looks destitute. A seventh round pick for Arnold Ebiketie, a sixth rounder for Tony Pollard , even a fifth round selection for Khalil Mack. If you can make those trades, go for it and don’t sweat it too much. The risk isn’t big enough to sweat.
But going bigger than that? In this deep, talent-rich draft class, even a fourth rounder is pretty valuable. I hesitate to offer up even that much at the moment. Obviously, you have to carefully consider a home run trade for someone like Laiatu Latu or Maxx Crosby, but I’m not even sure if I’d sign off on Bucky Irving for a late day two pick. Let’s think about this.
Let’s start here. Is a player, even a great player, or even two great players, what this team needs to fix their problems? Is their current issue one of talent? If you trade for an offensive player, remember that you will be throwing them into a situation with a struggling playcaller, flailing quarterback, weakening offensive line , and even some underachieving receivers.
There’s a real chance they show up and accomplish very little in such a circumstance. And while I won’t pretend there’s no value in improving your depth on defense to future-proof, I also have to ask, how can the defense get much better? It’s top five in almost every meaningful metric that I use, and is probably the second best in the league right now. It can’t get much better.
I can’t believe we’re here right now, but with the way things have gone through six games this season and the way things currently look, we have to accept this reality. As of this moment, there looks to be a realistic possibility of the Seahawks not making the playoffs. If that happens, their picks will be a lot higher, and any picks traded for players are more valuable.
If you trade for that player, and then don’t even make the postseason, you get bitten twice by the same decision. Sometimes, it works out, like in prior Seahawk seasons with Ernest Jones and Leonard Williams, but I think there’s a great argument for standing pat and waiting. On some level, this team needs to earn the right to take a swing at a trade.
