title: New 2027 Seahawks Mock Draft Lands Versatile Plug-and-Play Offensive Lineman
full_text:
Through the first six games of the season, the Seattle Seahawks have had more than their share of issues. While their defense has remained strong, their offense has had several problem areas cost them games.
One primary concern has been their inability to run the ball. Injuries have slowed them down, with Zach Charbonnet still out following a torn ACL suffered in January. Rookie Jadarian Price is also sidelined, leaving them with Emanuel Wilson and George Holani. They have also had issues with turnovers as Sam Darnold has seven interceptions over the past four games.
Those problems can be traced to the individual players, but they're not solely responsible. Many of the mistakes are happening due to the offensive line's inability to protect Darnold as well as their struggles in run blocking. They might be able to clean some of that up, however, by selecting Minnesota's Greg Johnson. That's exactly what they do in a recent mock draft from Pro Football Sports Network's Alec Elijah .
As Elijah says, the Seattle offense has been solely running through Jaxon Smith-Njigba, which isn't sustainable. Adding Johnson would give Darnold more time, while also helping them in the ground game as well.
"The Seattle Seahawks’ offense has run through reigning Offensive Player of the Year Jaxon Smith-Njigba this season, but keeping the passing game on schedule will require a sturdier interior offensive line. Greg Johnson is the No. 2 guard on PFN’s big board with an 85.2 prospect grade, and many evaluators view the Minnesota senior as the best interior offensive lineman in the class through the first half of the season," Elijah wrote.
"Johnson is a massive presence at 6-foot-6 and 327 pounds, playing with the heavy hands and physicality you would expect from someone his size. What separates him, though, is how smoothly he climbs to the second level and connects with linebackers in space. His ability to play both guard and center gives Seattle valuable flexibility up front, and he projects as a plug-and-play starter who can raise the floor of the entire offensive line."
Where Johnson plays would be up for discussion. Anthony Bradford had been playing well at right guard before suffering a knee and hip injury . He's scheduled for free agency and could be replaced by Beau Stephens. At center, Jalen Sundell has been the starter and has been solid, but they could stand to upgrade that position as well.

title: Proposed Seahawks-Titans Trade Could Solve Seattle's RB Concerns
full_text:
Running the ball was easy for the Seattle Seahawks in 2025. Kenneth Walker III led the way with 1,027 yards while Zach Charbonnet added 730 yards. Charbonnet was the touchdown leader on the ground with 12, while Walker added five.
During the postseason, they lost Charbonnet to a torn ACL and Walker became a huge star. He helped carry the offense and was awarded the Super Bowl MVP award before leaving in free agency. With him gone, and Charbonnet not back from his injury, running the ball has become very difficult for Seattle in 2026.
Not only are the Seahawks still waiting for Charbonnet to come back, but they also lost rookie first-round pick Jadarian Price to injury as well. That has them leaning on Emanuel Wilson and George Holani, which has been a struggle. For that reason, CBS Sports' Jared Dubin believes the Seahawks should be willing to make a move for a running back and named Tony Pollard as an option.
Dubin admits that Pollard isn't the explosive threat he once was, but he's been a consistent producer who knows how to follow his blocks. Dubin also believes Pollard could be their answer in a committee if Price misses extensive time.
"The Seahawks cannot run the ball at all, as we have seen throughout this season and that was on full display on Thursday night against the Broncos. Pollard is no great shakes, but he's got 1,000 yards in four consecutive seasons and is at least a professional runner who can get what's blocked and a bit more," Dubin wrote.
"The Seahawks should be getting Zach Charbonnet back fairly soon, but we don't know if or when Jadarian Price will return. Pollard would be an upgrade over Emanuel Wilson and/or George Holani as a complement to Charbs. It's not the sexiest deal in the world and might not even be the best possible use of resources, but the Seahawks do need help in the backfield."
Pollard is in the final year of a three-year, $21.75 million deal signed in 2024. He had 1,000 yards in each of his final two seasons with the Dallas Cowboys and did so again in each of his first two years with the Titans. This year, he's off to a slow start with 273 yards and a touchdown through five games, although he is averaging 4.0 yards per attempt.

title: Early Options at a New Starting Quarterback for Seahawks in 2027
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks have given Sam Darnold a chance to be the franchise quarterback. The 12 thought he had earned it after helping the team win a Super Bowl, but not even half a season later, all trust and hope for him are gone. Darnold has regressed significantly and can't be trusted not to turn the ball over.
Darnold's seven turnovers in the last four games are a direct reason why the Seahawks are 3-3 and looking like they will miss the playoffs. He was signed to a team-friendly deal of three years, $100 million in the 2025 offseason. The Seahawks created a potential out this upcoming offseason if they should feel the need to activate it.
There is a chance the Seahawks start over at quarterback going into next season, regardless of whether they might make the playoffs or not. General manager John Schneider and his front office staff have some good options.
​There was a time this 2026 NFL Season when the Seahawks had one of the most efficient quarterbacks and it wasn't Darnold. Through five weeks and the Thursday Night Football game, backup Drew Lock remains at the top of the league in quarterback rating at 127.3. Through most of the game versus the New England Patriots and the entire game versus the Arizona Cardinals, Lock has completed 72.9% of his passes for 422 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions.
​The Seahawks should give Lock a chance to prove to the team that he can’t put the team in danger of losing late off mistakes like Darnold. What is the worst that could happen? Lock could have a late turnover that costs the team a win, but the team already has three of those losses. Lock could be the top option moving forward if Seattle needs a new starter in 2027.
​The 2027 NFL Draft is an option that the front office should take seriously if they need a new franchise quarterback. There are seven quarterbacks in the top 25 of ESPN's Mel Kiper Jr.'s latest board. Oregon's Dante Moore, Missouri's Austin Simmons and Notre Dame's CJ Carr are players the Seahawks should be interested in the most.
​Seattle has 11 picks in the 2027 Draft , but the problem is that if they need to move up for a quarterback, teams won't be interested in one of the multiple late day two or day three picks. If the Seahawks continue to lose, they might find themselves in a favorable spot to draft a quarterback in the first round without having to trade.
​One decision the front office could make that might be less favorable than the 2027 Draft or Lock is getting a temporary option. There is less risk for players who set to be free agents at the end of the season and there aren't great players, but they are serviceable enough to not throw late interceptions. Among the options who are set to be free agents next offseason are Kirk Cousins, Marcus Mariota (who beat the Seahawks in Week 3), Kyler Murray and Mac Jones.
​The Seahawks might look at the trade market too for disgruntled quarterbacks. Some options might include Philadelphia Eagles' Jalen Hurts, Baltimore Ravens' Lamar Jackson, Cincinnati Bengals' Joe Burrow and Houston Texans' CJ Stroud. This is a risky move considering the Seahawks would have to give up a lot for these quarterbacks and pay them a lot of money. All options should be on the table if Darnold single-handedly costs more games.

title: 3 Risers and Fallers After Seahawks' Week 6 Loss vs Broncos
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks kicked off Week 6 on the road versus the Denver Broncos on a short week. Much like the Broncos, the Seahawks had the tough task of playing a game four days after another. This 17-14 overtime loss to Denver showed some real concerns for the team moving forward . Three Seahawks’ personnel should start to worry about their status on the team. There were also a couple of players who could have a bigger role on the team after Thursday’s game.
​Once again, linebacker Tyrice Knight showed why he is a quality-level starter for the Dark Side Defense. He started in place of Drake Thomas, who was out with an ankle injury. Knight accounted for eight total tackles. He was aggressive and quick to make plays against the Broncos' defense, who were trying to take advantage of the short passing game. If the Seahawks utilized a traditional 4-3 front as opposed to a 4-2-5, Knight would easily be a full-time starter.
​Both tight ends Eric Saubert and Nick Kallerup could count as one, but they are utilized differently moving forward. The Seahawks changed plans of having Brady Russell as the first-team fullback with Robbie Ouzts out for the year. AJ Barner has been taking that role, along with Saubert and Kallerup at times. Saubert had 16 offensive snaps and 20 special teams snaps while Kallerup had 10 offensive snaps and six special teams snaps.
​Wide receiver Irv Charles finally got his chance to play for the Seahawks after missing the first five games while still recovering from a torn ACL from last year with the New York Jets. Charles showed how much of a reliable player he was as a special teams player by making a big tackle in one of the 15 special teams snaps. The Seahawks like consistent and assertive special teams defenders. He might be proven to be a reliable player to trade for.
​It is time we take some serious thought about benching quarterback Sam Darnold after essentially giving the Seahawks their third loss of the season. He has lost three of the four games that he started and finished for the Seahawks. Seven interceptions in four games is an embarrassing statistic and he and the coaching staff promised the turnovers would stop. As of right now, the only reason the promise could be kept is if Darnold sits and Drew Lock starts.
​Darnold isn’t the only starter who should be worried about regressing. Right tackle Abraham Lucas should be highly concerned about one of the worst performances of the night. Between missing on blitz pickups, poorly facing the opposing edge rusher and being slow/latheratic on screen coverages, Lucas was a problem on Thursday. If he continues to play this poorly , the Seahawks might have a conversation about reducing his salary or replacing him.
​First-year offensive coordinator Brian Fleury went from being clear to being worried about his job to potentially being on the hot seat. Outside of Darnold, Fleury was the biggest reason why the Seahawks’ offense laid an egg until the final half of the fourth quarter.
Fluery continues to go with a power back in Emanuel Wilson, who is slow and has no vision and George Holani, who was awful in the one thing he was supposed to be good at: pass protection. If the Seahawks continue to struggle offensively, his first year as an offensive coordinator might be his only year.

title: The Seahawks Can Not Protect Sam Darnold
full_text:
Brian Fleury. Sam Darnold . John Schneider. Emanuel Wilson. George Holani. Rashid Shaheed. Elijah Arroyo. AJ Barner. Jadarian Price. If you want to fire off some anger and frustration at the offense of the Seattle Seahawks, there are a lot of potential targets. And after Thursday night, you can make an argument for adding the entire offensive line to the list.
I would characterize the Seattle Seahawks offensive line through six games this season as ‘inconsistent’. There have been games where it felt like the pass protection has been way ahead of the run blocking, and then games where the opposite felt accurate. Last night, it was most certainly the opposite (not that I was enamored by the run blocking either).
According to Pro Football Focus, Sam Darnold was pressured 27 times against the Denver Broncos. The six offensive linemen that currently make up Seattle’s front line (Haynes and Stephens rotate at right guard) were credited with 26 pressures allowed (multiple players can take blame for one pressure). Meaning very little was considered Sam’s fault.
Charles Cross, who has been relatively clean in pass protection this year with 7 pressures in the first 5 games, let up 4, including 2 QB hits. Abraham Lucas, admittedly already somewhat leaky this year , had one of his worst games ever with 7 pressures allowed, including 2 sacks, after 11 to start the season. Jalen Sundell threw in 4, ridiculous for a center, after 6 in prior weeks.
Grey Zabel, who seems to be in the midst of something of a sophomore slump (not that the playcalling is helping him), allowed 3, which actually isn’t a season high for him. Christian Haynes got wrecked, allowing a sack and 2 QB hits for 5 total pressures. And Beau Stephens, despite a reduced snap load, gave up 3. Everyone is to blame right now.
The problems aren’t over there. George Holani deserves a lot of criticism here. One of the reasons why you carry Holani on the roster is because of his abilities as a blocker. Supposedly, coming into the season, the team considered him their best pass protector out of the backfield. Through six games, he has been a complete disaster, and Thursday was a new low.
4 pressures on 12 reps. He’s allowed at least one pressure in every game this year, allowed three (including a sack) against the Chargers, and is currently graded at a 19.3 in pass blocking. He might be injured , but at this point Emmanuel Wilson (clean in 11 reps) and Jadarian Price (clean in 8 reps) are clearly superior options. And at that point, why even have George?
There’s a lot of stuff that needs to improve, fast, if this offense is going to right the ship. So the last thing we need is for the offensive line to become a liability. Maybe we need more max protect, but these players need to play better too. Fleury and Darnold can get it together all they want to , but if those guys can’t figure it out, you can forget about it.

title: 49ers Christian McCaffrey Plan Is Paying Off
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers are getting a more efficient version of Christian McCaffrey in 2026 than they did in 2025. His yards per attempt is up from 3.9 to 4.7, and his success rate went from below 50% to 55.6% in 2026. One of the biggest reasons the team has been able to get a more efficient version of McCaffrey is that they are using him a bit less .
McCaffrey played 80% of the offensive snaps last season. He is only playing 69% of the snaps this year. What is most important is the manner in which they are able to rest him.
The 49ers have 26 short-yardage snaps . McCaffrey has played just 16 of them. They subbed him out for two goal-line snaps as well. Beyond that, when the 49ers have a multi-score lead, they find ways to rest him.
He has played just one snap in what is deemed garbage time. So, just taking 23 snaps and giving them back to McCaffrey would have him closer to 78% of the snaps. That is back in line with what he was doing last year.
The 49ers are able to sit McCaffrey more in these scenarios because they have faith in rookie Kaelon Black. Black is not producing impressive stats. Brian Robinson averaged 23 yards per game last year, and Black is at 27 yards per game this year.
Still, the difference is efficiency. Black has a 56% success rate on his carries this year. Robinson was at 46% last year. So, he was converting the short-yardage snaps into positive plays nearly s often. It made it harder for the 49ers to lean on the depth behind McCaffrey.
It took away from the efficiency of McCaffrey because he was being asked to do the dirty work. So, even when he was converting plays, it was not pretty and not for big gains. Then, he was worn down for the chances to hit the explosive.
Now, McCaffrey still plays in the two-minute drill and long downs and distances. When they need big plays, he is there, and he is well rested. The stats of Black and McCaffrey might not be as impressive from a volume perspective this year. However,the team is going to look much more efficient, and it could give them a higher ceiling heading into the playoffs.

title: Assessing the 49ers’ Management of Christian McCaffrey’s Workload
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers’ front office has repeatedly stated this season that it wants to monitor Christian McCaffrey’s workload.
It's five games into the new season, with three tough opponents in the form of the Seattle Seahawks, the Los Angeles Rams and the Denver Broncos.
This is a perfect time to assess whether McCaffrey's workload has made him better.
McCaffrey faced the most intense workload in his career in 2025. He had a career-high 311 carries and 102 receptions throughout the season. On the one hand, it's an impressive effort, as he went through the entire season without picking up any injuries.
That said, McCaffrey’s workload was way too excessive. He recorded the second-most carries in the league, while his average dropped to 3.9 yards per carry. Although that figure is not necessarily poor, it represents a significant decline from the 5.4 yards per carry he averaged during his 2023 Offensive Player of the Year season.
But compared to 2024, winning the Comeback Player of the Year award was completely deserved.
McCaffrey has only had 61 carries across five games this season, putting him on track for around or just over 200 for the season. Let's be honest, that's a massive reduction.
Credit to the 49ers for this. After drafting Kaelon Black in the third round this season, he's done well to remain healthy and help reduce McCaffrey's output. He's averaging 3.7 yards, which is a solid return from a rookie.
In truth, it's proven so far that they've made the right call. McCaffrey has averaged 4.7 yards per carry, with 286 rushing yards and has also recorded five touchdowns.
While many of those touchdowns have come from close range, McCaffrey has shown a noticeable improvement in explosiveness compared to last season.
The 49ers have also utilized him more heavily toward the end of games, which appears to be a smart approach to managing his workload while maximizing his impact when it matters most.
He's tied sixth in the league for touchdowns and 18th overall in rushing yards. Most of his explosive performances this season have been against tougher opponents, averaging 6.8 per carry against the Rams and 6.2 yards against the Seahawks.
So he's still a massively bright spark on that offense still, but he's simply being managed properly, which the front office to their credit have done very well.

title: 49ers George Kittle Gets Involved in Trade Deadline Buzz
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers are sitting at 5-0, and there are few players available at the trade deadline that are not being connected to San Francisco. Earlier in the week, General Manager John Lynch told KNBR radio that he hears the rumors, not only from the media, but from his own players.
Lynch admitted that George Kittle asked him about the possibility of a Khalil Mack trade recently.
“We seem to be connected to everyone, and I don't know where that comes from,” laughed Lynch when asked about the Mack rumors.
Lynch went on to add that players will come up to him and ask if the rumors are true, and that is headlined by Kittle.
“Usually it's Kittle because he asks about everything, which I love,” said Lynch .
Kittle admitted that he does enjoy asking Lynch questions. While he admitted he is not typically campaigning for specific players, he did admit that he likes to joke with Lynch and try to get inside information.
“I just like to chirp him and ask what he is interested in,” said Kittle on the nature of what he asks about trades. “See if he'll give me anything.”
John Lynch said today on KNBR that George Kittle asked about the possibility of trading for Khalil Mack. Here’s George on that exchange who added that Lynch probably only really tells Trent Williams stuff pic.twitter.com/fiX5TMjaFF
Kittle added that other veterans such as Kyle Juszczyk and Trent Williams join him in asking the 49ers GM what his plans are.
“Me, Juice, Trent, we all chirp just to see if he will actually tell us anything,” added Kittle. “I think he tells Trent the most, not me.”
The 49ers locker room is clearly all in and tied to the idea that they could make a trade. Leaders in the locker room are leading the discussion of adding players, making the rumors appear even stronger.
It will be interesting what the 49ers do at the trade deadline. Receiver and edge rusher are the positions linked to them the most.
While they are thin at both positions, they also could be getting most of their depth back in the coming weeks. Mykel Williams just returned, and Nick Bosa should be back soon on the edge.
Christian Kirk is practicing, while Demarcus Robinson and Deebo Samuel should only be a few weeks away. Lastly, the team will get De’Zhaun Stribling back in a few weeks.
This could leave the interior defensive line as the most likely spot for a trade acquisition. We will see if 49ers players continue to demand a new name next week.

title: 5 Matchups 49ers Must Win Against Commanders
full_text:
When the San Francisco 49ers take on the Washington Commanders in Week 6, they will have plenty of matchups in their favor. What are the matchups they have to win to avoid the upset?
The 49ers' run defense is great from an expected points perspective , but they struggle down by down to create negative plays. The Commanders do not have a great rushing attack, but Jayden Daniels is one of the best rushing quarterbacks in the NFL.
However, the athleticism of Fred Warner should be on display against Daniels. How Warner and rookie Jaden Dugger spy and contain Daniels will determine how much Washington scores.
The Commanders' linebackers and safeties have been a weakness so far. At safety, Nick Cross has been hurt, while Quan Martin and Jeremy Reaves have struggled. At linebacker. Frankie Luvu is better as a blitzer than he is in coverage. Sonny Styles is an athletic rookie but has issues adjusting as well.
This is bad timing for Washington, because the 49ers offense runs through George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey. These two could dominate the target share.
Back in 2016, the Atlanta Falcons made a run to the Super Bowl with Kyle Shanahan calling the offense and Dan Quinn calling the defense. Since they have split paths, Shanahan is 3-1 against Quinn. However, the one loss was when Quinn was with Atlanta. The three wins were when Quinn was with the Dallas Cowboys.
Now, we will see how the two fare with Quinn back as head coach of the Commanders. Right now, Shanahan has his number.
The Commanders' biggest offensive line issues are at left guard and center. They have shuffled two options at center, and current starter Lucas Patrick is questionable to play. At left guard, Chris Paul has been a problem. The 49ers' interior defensive line is not deep, but Odighizuwa is a playmaker. He needs to dominate.
Connor Colby has played above his head through four weeks but came soaring back down to earth in Week 5. Now, he gets Daron Payne, Tim Settle, and Javon Kinlaw. Too much interior pressure could make this game closer than expected.

title: 5 Biggest Questions Facing 49ers Ahead of Week 6
full_text:
As the San Francisco 49ers get ready for a chance to go 6-0, what are some of the biggest questions on the roster entering their Week 6 matchup with the Washington Commanders.
The 49ers receiver room has been getting thin, and the team is going to be without Deebo Samuel in Week 6, making the group even thinner. With Samuel out, the team essentially shuffled Jacob Cowing, Jordan Watkins, and Brandin Cooks as the second through fourth receivers behind Mike Evans.
Can the two young names step up, or will they lean on the veteran Cooks?
When Juszczyk suffered a knee injury in Week 4, the expectation was that he would be missing a couple of weeks. However, after missing one week, he is not only at practice; he is practicing in full . The 49ers' lack of skill players is going to push the team to get Juszczyk on the field for a significant role if he is healthy. What does that look like?
Dre Greenlaw is suspended for Week 6, and Garrett Wallow is likely to miss due to an injury. The team is going to give rookie Jaden Dugger his first look as an every-down linebacker in Week 6. Dugger was supposed to be a high-ceiling project, but playing so much as a rookie has raised the floor as well. How does he look with even more put on his plate?
The 49ers eased former first-round pick Mykel Williams back into action after he tore his ACL last year. Williams played 23 snaps, which amounted to about one-third of the defensive snaps. Williams hardly rushed from the interior in his debut, which is where he was most dynamic as a rookie. Will Williams step into a bigger role, and will they use him in a more versatile manner?
Colby has been better than expected through the first four weeks. However, once he had to step up in competition against the Seahawks, he fell back to earth. Now, he gets Daron Payne of the Washington Commanders. This could end up being an issue for Colby. San Francisco’s backup, Carver Willis, is currently injured, so they have to ride with Colby.

title: 49ers QB Brock Purdy's Reaction to Potentially Historic Stat Says It All
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy has completed impressive stats since becoming the starter.
It's crazy to think that, in just his fifth season, Brock Purdy has already led San Francisco to a Super Bowl, an NFC Championship Game and a Divisional Round appearance in three of the last four years.
Having put up impressive efficiency numbers throughout his career, Purdy is on the brink of history, sitting just five pass attempts away from reaching the 1,500-pass threshold that would make him eligible to rank first all-time in passer rating.
His response upon hearing this stat line is relatively simple: "To be honest, I don't really know. Obviously, when you look at your stats, are you efficient with your completions and, I guess, not turning the ball over, throwing touchdowns, things like that. "
"I guess, yeah, your rating of course is going to be good. I guess it's, yeah, it's a good thing. But at the same time, I'm not getting done with games going, 'Alright, was my rating at least 100 and something?' I could really care less about that. It's more so, did I do my job well for my teammates? Did I compete and do everything I could to help this team win?
"I know it sounds cheesy, but that's the reality. That's what I'm thinking about and it's what matters. I guess that maybe reflects, though, playing pretty good quarterback play, so I'm not trying to act like it's nothing.
"But, it is cool. If I could answer that again too, I would say obviously it goes more into just me (laughter). I've got great coaches, a great team, dudes that help me be who I am and I'm just grateful that I get to be the quarterback for the 49ers so, yeah, it's cool."
And that's why he's deeply respected within the organization. He doesn't care about the stats. He only wants to be the best version of himself.
Purdy has made it clear in the past that his sole focus is bringing a sixth Super Bowl title back to the City by the Bay . Whether he achieves that remains to be seen, but his approach to the game is refreshing in an era where that kind of single-minded focus can feel increasingly rare.
This mentality extends further in trying to improve. He's on the cusp of something quite special, yet he doesn't care. He simply wants to win football games.

title: Brock Purdy Explains How 49ers DC Raheem Morris Helped Him Improve
full_text:
Brock Purdy has been playing extremely well this season. His performance has played a key role in the San Francisco 49ers' 5-0 start.
Purdy seems to be playing sharper and more comfortably than ever before. Part of that is the help he has, as well as the work he put in the offseason. However, there’s another factor that helped him out.
Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris is someone whom Purdy has credited with his improvement this year. Now, you may wonder how a defensive coach is helping an offensive player?
Morris isn’t working one-on-one with Purdy like quarterbacks coach Mick Lombardi is, or even Klint Kubiak and Kyle Shanahan. But what he did do was give him quality reps in training camp that forced him to elevate his game.
“A lot more man-match technique and tighter windows. It felt like everything for me had to be on time and it had to be aggressive,” Purdy said. “I don't know if there was as many layered kind of throws, just because of how they run things. Everything for me, it seemed like it was just always tight and the vision zones of dropping back and dropping it in the bucket over hook defenders and stuff like that.
“You get that every once in a while, but for the most part, man, he made me have to play aggressive. And I appreciated that, actually. I think that's translated into the season for me to throw with that, I know we've talked about this, but that aggressive mindset and everything. So, it's a big credit to Raheem.”
If it wasn’t clear before, it's definitely clear now that Morris is an upgrade over Robert Saleh . Not only has he gotten the 49ers’ secondary to raise their game — he’s gotten Purdy to as well.
It’s like the cliché saying, “iron sharpens iron.” That’s exactly what training camp was for Purdy, going up against the 49ers’ new defense under Morris. This is why he looks so sharp.
Morris’ defense forced Purdy to play at a high level. And as he said, it translated to the regular season. If you look back at reports during training camp, it was rare for Purdy to turn the ball over.
He was also cited as taking some nice shots and playing within himself. That’s exactly what he’s been doing through five games this season. Adding Mike Evans has helped Purdy out a ton.
But Morris is the one who’s had the greater impact on him.

title: One 49ers Player is Emerging as a Breakout Star
full_text:
A significant reason for the San Francisco 49ers starting the season 5-0 is because of how sweet countless players are performing.
All eyes are on Brock Purdy as arguably the 49ers' best performer, which is why he's being crowned as the MVP already. It's undeniable that Purdy is playing great.
However, there's another 49ers player who deserves recognition. This player is easily emerging as a breakout star and is the 49ers' breakout player of the year so far.
It's none other than cornerback Renardo Green. He's picking up where he left off in his promising 2024 rookie season. Last year, he fell off.
He had a handful of blown assignments that allowed an explosive play or a touchdown. Green didn't look comfortable playing for Robert Saleh.
But under Raheem Morris , he's flourishing. Green had by far his greatest performance of his career in Week 5 against the Seattle Seahawks.
He picked off Sam Darnold twice, marking his first-ever multi-interception game. His first interception was by far his most impressive, as he was defending against Jaxson Smith-Njigba.
It wasn't a tricky route run, but most defensive backs struggle to stay tight in coverage on Smith-Njigba. Green has stepped it up big-time this year, and the stats back it up.
Green has been targeted 21 times this season and allowed a 52.4% completion rate – a career low and the lowest among cornerbacks on the 49ers, per Next Gen Stats .
His five passes defended are a career high through the first five games of a season and this is the first year he has recorded multiple interceptions in a season (3).
His 23.8% ball hawk rate is the highest of his career and the highest on the team among cornerbacks, and he is the only 49er cornerback who has yet to allow a passing touchdown this season.
Call me crazy, but I'd say that is pretty darn good. Green is easily the 49ers' best defensive back this year. He's even better than Deommodore Lenoir.
Morris will get the credit for why Green is playing so well, but it's also a major credit to the work Green put in, and it all started early in the offseason.
"The way Renardo came to day one of Phase One, you could tell that he had put work in away, which prepared him so much more for the month that we got with him," Kyle Shanahan said. "He had an awesome Phase One, Two and Three... You could tell he'd been working all year and really locked in to getting better at everything."
Green is performing at a Pro Bowl level. If he keeps this up, he'll have a case to be named an All-Pro player. And to think, he was mentioned in offseason trade rumors.

title: The Most Impressive Part About the 49ers’ 5-0 Start
full_text:
Seeing the San Francisco 49ers open up the season with five straight wins is nothing short of impressive.
Now, they were expected to be a good team this season, but anytime you start off the year 5-0, especially notching a win over the Seattle Seahawks , who whooped the 49ers the last two times, it deserves applause.
It’s not just the wins that are awesome to see; it’s how the 49ers are doing. Brock Purdy is playing very sharp, along with Mike Evans , and the 49ers’ defense under Raheem Morris has been lights-out.
However, it’s not the most impressive part of their 5-0 start.
They haven’t needed to rely on Christian McCaffrey. Last year, the 49ers were McCaffrey or bust. They might as well have renamed themselves the San Francisco McCaffreys at that point.
That’s how heavy and insane his usage was, but it was also incredible, even if he wasn’t efficient. Without McCaffrey, it’s unlikely the 49ers make it to the playoffs.
Deviating from a player who’s been the star of the offense is risky and easier said than done, but the 49ers knew they couldn’t replicate his workload in 2026. Not even close to it.
During the offseason, Kyle Shanahan pointed out that the 49ers need to help him out. He’s said that before in previous offseasons, so it was tough to fully take stock of his words.
However, unlike in previous offseasons, McCaffrey wasn’t coming off unreal usage. He’s also not the same player he was in 2023 when he won the Offensive Player of the Year award.
That played a role in the running game’s ineffectiveness last year. Shanahan knows that, which led them to draft Kaelon Black. The rookie has done a solid job of filling in for McCaffrey in spurts.
But Black isn’t the only one helping McCaffrey out. Purdy is doing his part as well. Shanahan is dialing up more passing plays than in previous years.
Their passing game has been more responsible for how great their offense is clicking than the running game. They’re relying more on Purdy and his receivers than on McCaffrey.
It's a surprising yet magnificent sight to see. The best part of it all is that it preserves McCaffrey for when the 49ers need to use him heavily late in the season.
Shanahan surely has that card ready to use when the need arises. Until then, their offense is operating soundly with their newfound identity.

title: One 49ers Player is an Afterthought Despite Impressive Debut
full_text:
With injuries thinning out their wide receiver depth , the San Francisco 49ers have needed their young players to step up.
One player who did that well in Week 3 against the Arizona Cardinals was Jordan Watkins. He caught two explosive passes for 60 yards in his season debut.
He was also blocking amazingly well. That game raised Watkins' stock, and it should've earned him more playing time with the 49ers dealing with injuries.
However, Watkins has been a ghost despite his impressive debut. He hasn't registered a single catch, and that's because he isn't being targeted. Watkins is an afterthought in the 49ers' offense, but if you ask Kyle Shanahan, he doesn't think so.
“He's just gotten more opportunities since his injuries and keep doing what he's doing," Shanahan said. "Guys just run routes and sometimes the ball goes to them, sometimes it doesn't. His opportunity percentages go up with the guys that have been hurt. He was backing up Deebo last week and Mike at times. We had Cooks doing the same. But, when guys go out, you get more opportunities.”
Shanahan is correct that the ball sometimes goes to a receiver and sometimes it doesn't. The thing is, he's the head coach and the offensive play caller.
If he wants Watkins involved, it will happen. One way he can help Watkins be featured more is by having him run more routes. Against the Seattle Seahawks, Watkins only ran eight routes.
Meanwhile, Brandin Cooks, who only just arrived less than a few weeks ago, ran 12. It's clear that Watkins isn't a player that Shanahan wants to use.
In hindsight, maybe Watkins' involvement against the Cardinals was for Shanahan to see how he would respond after he approached Shanahan about playing more.
It's not like he failed that test. Otherwise, Shanahan wouldn't have spoken so highly of him. Even now, Shanahan still speaks highly of Watkins.
"We've been really happy with how he's played in these games. I think he's earned a lot of respect in these three games and with us it doesn't have to do with the stats. I know he's had two catches and stuff in his first game, and those are two really good plays, but because he hasn't had any in the other two games doesn't really mean much to us."
It seems like the only way Watkins will see opportunities with the ball again is if the 49ers are desperate at wide receiver. You'd think that would be the case now with Deebo Samuel out .
But that doesn't appear to be the case. I wouldn't bank on much involvement as a pass catcher from Watkins anytime soon, if at all, this season.

title: Aaron Rodgers Calls Out Raymond James Stadium After Beating Buccaneers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers fell to the Pittsburgh Steelers 26-19 on Sunday, moving down to 1-5 on the year. The Bucs held the edge throughout the half, but the Steelers turned it around and gave Tampa Bay another close loss, this time in overtime.
The Steelers were led by quarterback Aaron Rodgers, who will go down as one of the best to ever play the game. Rodgers has played in Raymond James Stadium a few times over the years, and while this will almost certainly be the last time, he had a parting shot for the stadium in his post-game press conference.
Rodgers may have gotten the win, but he made his displeasure known about a certain aspect of playing football in Tampa Bay.
Rodgers told Steelers media after the game that he thought the playing surface at Raymond James Stadium is one of the worst in the NFL.
"It's gotta be one of the worst surfaces in the league," Rodgers said Sunday. "We're talking about player safety. I'm very thankful to not get hurt — I've gotten hurt twice on this field, in my opinion, because of this turf. I know USF plays here, I believe. That surface, you know, I don't think it's very safe."
#Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers calls out Raymond James Stadium for being “one of the worst surfaces in the league.” pic.twitter.com/Rc2eaJOGR3
The evidence from the last NFLPA report card backs up Rodgers' claim. In the anonymous survey, the Buccaneers' field was ranked F-, tied for worst in the NFL. Five teams earned an F- — three of them were turf, and the only other grass field was, ironically, the Steelers' Acrisure Stadium.
As Rodgers mentioned, USF playing its home games at the stadium the day before probably contributes in a big way to this problem. The turf also often hosts bowl games, too, so it gets a lot of use from teams that are not the Buccaneers.
Rodgers has played on that field at Raymond James Stadium seven times against the Buccaneers. He's 3-4 after his win on Sunday, and it will likely be the last time he ever plays in the stadium.
The Bucs won't be playing on that field next Sunday, as they'll play their first NFC South rivalry game of the year when they face off against the Carolina Panthers in Charlotte.

title: The Best and Worst Position Groups in the Bucs' 26-19 Steelers Loss
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers lost another matchup, this time in overtime against the Pittsburgh Steelers. There was a lot of good and bad in this one, with certain groups doing much better than others.
Let's go over the grades for the Bucs' Week 6 loss:
It was a very rough game for Jalon Daniels. The Steelers knew how to rattle the rookie, and Daniels finished 22 of 43 passing for 164 passing yards, one touchdown and two interceptions.
Daniels also had 39 rushing yards on the day and was sacked five times. One thing that won't show up on the stat sheets is the bad missed passes late in the game to open players like Emeka Egbuka and Bucky Irving.
After a great game against the Dallas Cowboys, Bucky Irving came back to earth in this game. Irving finished with 21 touches for 49 yards and zero touchdowns.
Kenny Gainwell didn't do much better with three touches for 24 yards, and we saw no opportunities for second-year back Josh Williams.
Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin combined for 24 targets today for 11 receptions, 85 yards and a single touchdown from Egbuka.
Ted Hurst also finished with three receptions for 40 yards as well. However, there were a couple of drops in this game with Egbuka, Godwin and Tez Johnson all having at least a single drop in this game.
The Bucs offensive line continues to struggle to protect the quarterback. That's not fully their fault, as the Steelers blitzed a ton that day. However, the team was not able to run block either in this matchup.
David Walker was an absolute star in this matchup and finished with seven total tackles, two sacks, two tackles for loss and three quarterback hits.
We also saw A'Shawn Robinson get his second interception this season, which is absolutely insane. Rueben Bain Jr. got his first sack of the season and had the deflection on the pass that Robinson intercepted. Finally, you had other big contributions from guys like Yaya Diaby and Al-Quadin Muhammad.
Josiah Trotter looked good in this game, leading the defense with 12 total tackles and one pass deflection that should've been a pick-six for him.
Christian Rozeboom also had a great pass deflection in this game as well and has earned more playing time. Alex Anzalone, however, still missed multiple tackles in this game and was a bit of a liability towards the end of the game.
Zyon McCollum led the way for this group with 11 total tackles and one pass deflection. However, the star of the group was Keionte Scott, who had eight tackles, one sack, one tackle for loss and a quarterback hit.
Jacob Parrish was yet again solid with six tackles, one tackle for loss and two passes deflected.
The positive is that kicker Chase McLaughlin was awesome, making all of his kicks and keeping the Bucs alive going into overtime. The negative was that Riley Dixon was really bad in this game, and the team still needs to look at a new punter going forward. Yes, the game was windy, but it was not an issue for McLaughlin in this game, so I see it as no excuse for Dixon.

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly From Buccaneers' OT Loss to the Steelers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers came into this Week 6 matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers knowing it was one they had to have. After going 0-4 to start the season, the Bucs were desperate to win consecutive games for the first time in over a year. Doing so would be a necessity to climb back up the standings in the NFC South.
Unfortunately, despite appearing to be in full control while holding a16-3 lead in the fourth quarter, the Buccaneers managed to squander a golden opportunity to turn their season around and fell to the Steelers at home in overtime, 26-19.
Let's take a closer look at the good, the bad, and the ugly that transpired in this demoralizing loss for the Buccaneers.
A'Shawn Robinson recorded his second sack of the interception in the first half of this game, and without checking the stats, I'd be confident in suggesting he is the only 300+ pound defender in the NFL leading his team in interceptions.
Beyond his role as a hefty ballhawk, Robinson's power, aggression and relentless style of play have been a welcome addition to Bowles' defensive line. Robinson has been one of the league's most impactful interior defenders so far this year, especially against the run, and his presence was felt again on Sunday.
Both David Walker and Rueben Bain Jr. recorded sacks for the Buccaneers in this game. For Bain, it was the first of his NFL career, and in addition to coming against a future Hall of Famer in Aaron Rodgers, it should feel like a weight lifted off his shoulders as everyone expected this milestone to come much earlier in his NFL career.
First-career sack for @ruebenbainjr 😡 📺: #PITvsTB on CBS pic.twitter.com/Q2Hta1d6FN
David Walker has been a menace whenever he's on the field for the Buccaneers this season. His two sacks today increased his season total to four, which leads the Buccaneers by a healthy margin. After missing his entire rookie year because of a torn ACL, this has been Walker's true rookie season, and the impact he's made despite limited opportunities has been outstanding. He has been the Bucs' best pass rusher throughout the first 6 weeks of the season, and it hasn't been particularly close.
David Walker records his second sack of the game, dropping Aaron Rodgers for a nine-yard loss. Walker's 4.0 sacks are tied (With Curt Jarvis) for the third-most by a Buccaneer through their first six career games since at least 1982.
McLaughlin was four-for-four on his field goals in this game, and he is now a perfect 14-for-14 on the season. McLaughlin has been one of the NFL's best kickers since joining the Buccaneers, and even though many of his teammates have not met expectations this season, that does not apply to him.
McLaughlin is a real weapon in the kicking game, and it's unfortunate his consistently exceptional performance is being wasted by an otherwise inept offense.
The Buccaneers led 16-3 at the half, and Daniels looked like the player we saw in Dallas on Thursday Night Football up until that point. Unfortunately, he looked like a completely different player as the game went on.
After halftime, Daniels was 8-for-20 passing with two interceptions. Not only was he throwing the ball to the Steelers, but he wasn't anywhere close on the passes intended for his own receivers for the majority of the second half and OT, air-mailing passes and missing receivers by several feet. Daniels finished the game 22-for-43 for 164 yards through the air.
The offensive collapse by the Buccaneers was largely because of Daniels' inability to execute, but his wide receivers got absolutely bullied by the Steelers DBs for the majority of the game. Former Buccaneer Jamel Dean looked like an All-Pro, and he was all over whichever Tampa Bay receiver he was covering at the time.
As good as both Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin Jr. have been in the past, neither player is explosive enough or consistent enough when it comes to creating the separation needed to be a team's No. 1 wide receiver. Life without Mike Evans is difficult for everyone in Tampa, and the Buccaneers' current group of receivers is making that abundantly clear to anyone who hadn't yet recognized it.
It's always unfortunate to see empty seats in a stadium, but it's even worse for a home team when you see more of the opponents' colors in the crowd than your own. Because of the beautiful weather in Tampa, Raymond James Stadium is notorious for attracting visiting fans. However, when an iconic franchise like the Steelers is in town and the Bucs are struggling, the 'home field disadvantage' can become that much more of a factor.
That was certainly the case today, as a sea of yellow terrible towels dominated much of the Stadium, creating an environment that surely helped fuel Pittsburgh's fourth quarter comeback in this game.

title: Overreactions From Buccaneers' Overtime Loss to Steelers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers lost their fifth game of the season to the Pittsburgh Steelers, falling 26-19 in overtime. The Bucs go to 1-5 with the close loss, and they fall even further down the division ladder.
The Bucs started out strong with a 16-3 lead, but the momentum massively shifted in the third quarter and Tampa Bay fell behind, eventually losing in overtime to Pittsburgh. It was the first overtime game the Bucs played since 2024.
Here are our three overreactions to Tampa Bay's game:
The Bucs may have lost the game, but Tampa Bay's defense has been looking strong ever since its game against the Cleveland Browns in Week 2. And it showed up again in a big way on Sunday.
The Steelers had just 2.2 yards per attempt in the first half of this game, shutting down Aaron Rodgers completely. The team racked up multiple sacks, including from Miami rookies Rueben Bain Jr. and Keionte Scott, and they were largely able to contain the run game as well.
This Bucs team stifled Pittsburgh at every turn. While the team still needs work and they weren't challenged at all downfield, Tampa Bay's defense deserves a lot of credit on Sunday — and the last few weeks — for being a stout unit.
Unfortunately, the offense did the Bucs no favors, tiring out the defense with frequent three-and-outs. But the Bucs held the Steelers to multiple field goals on the day and did their job, which is encouraging for the team going forward.
It's been tough sledding for Buccaneers punter Riley Dixon. Heading into Week 6, Dixon ranked 33rd of 33 qualifying punters in net yards per punt (37.1).
This game against the Steelers wasn't much better. Dixon averaged just 40.8 yards per punt against the Steelers, putting the Bucs' defense in bad situations throughout the day. It's only a matter of time before it impacts Tampa Bay in a big way going forward, and it arguably did in the loss to Pittsburgh on Sunday.
The Bucs should at least take a look at what else is out there so far — and they should at most make a change going forward this season.
Feels like we say this way too often. Walker has three sacks this year with limited snap time, and he got another on Aaron Rodgers in a big way to stop what could have been a scoring drive for Pittsburgh. He got another late to force the Steelers to kick when the two-minute warning hit.
He also had a nice pressure to get Al-Quadin Muhammad a sack, and he made a tackle for loss to force a Steelers field goal on that same drive. Walker has been a disruptor every time he's been on the field, and it's about time that he gets starting reps in this offense.
So far this year, he's proven he's the best pass rusher on the team. The Bucs should realize that and give him the starting reps he deserves going forward.

title: Buccaneers Running Back Inactive vs. Steelers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers need to stack as many wins as possible to save a season already on the brink. The Bucs are 1-4 and trying to move to 2-4, but the Pittsburgh Steelers are coming to Raymond James Stadium in hopes of knocking them down to 1-5.
Tampa Bay's offense played well last Thursday in a 24-16 win over the Dallas Cowboys, and the running game particularly excelled behind the legs of Bucky Irving. Running back Kenny Gainwell plays behind Irving, but Tampa Bay will not have their RB3 against the Steelers when they play on Sunday afternoon.
Here's who's inactive vs. the Steelers in Week 6:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers will be without running back Sean Tucker for their game against the Steelers, the team announced Sunday. Tucker, who was questionable to play with a quad injury, is inactive — he did not practice Wednesday but was a limited participant on Thursday and Friday.
Week 6 inactives for the Bucs: DL DeMonte Capehart G Luke Haggard QB Baker Mayfield CB Benjamin Morrison G Billy Schrauth RB Sean Tucker S Antoine Winfield Jr.
Tucker only has eight carries for 28 yards, averaging 3.5 yards per carry. He does have a touchdown, though, and he got eight yards on a 4th & 1 carry the play prior to set that touchdown up. Offensive coordinator Zac Robinson has mentioned wanting to get him more carries, but with Tucker hurt, he'll have to wait.
In Tucker's place will be running back Josh Williams. Williams has already been elevated to the practice squad once before this in Week 1, so this is his second elevation — the team's other elevation, Easton Stick, will now have been called up three times and can no longer be called up unless he's signed to the active roster.
Cornerback Benjamin Morrison is also inactive, as he was doubtful to play with a quad injury of his own. Morrison has missed significant time this season, missing the last two games with a quad injury. Cornerback Ayden Garnes, questionable to play on Friday's injury report, will replace him.
The Bucs' rushing attack will lean on Irving and Gainwell, just as it has even with Tucker available to play. The Bucs will have to try and break through a vaunted defensive line that includes standouts like T.J. Watt, Cam Heyward and more.
The Bucs play the Steelers at 1 p.m. on Sunday at Raymond James Stadium.

title: Our Buccaneers vs. Steelers Score Predictions Are In
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are looking to get their second win in a row, and they'll get the opportunity back home when they host the Pittsburgh Steelers at 1 p.m. on Sunday.
The Bucs beat the Dallas Cowboys 24-16 last week, but now, they'll face a tougher defense and a legendary quarterback in Aaron Rodgers.
As always, our staff has made its picks for Sunday's big cross-conference matchup in Tampa Bay. Here's how we see the Bucs' game against the Steelers shaping out:
The Bucs are coming off their first win of the season, and they have an excellent chance to continue that momentum against the Steelers.
I expect the Bucs to continue being efficient on offense, so it will be up to the defense to stop Warren and not allow the playmakers for the Steelers to make big plays.
I think the Bucs do, but aren’t able to come away with a clutch play that would give them the win.
I believe this will be a low-scoring affair, as both defenses have the chance to be good. However, I give the nod to Aaron Rodgers over Jalon Daniels, who will get a start once more with Mayfield on the mend.
So far, the 2026 NFL season has been very deflating for a Buccaneers team that had plenty of optimism heading into it. But because they play in the NFC South, the Buccaneers aren’t dead yet. However, if they have any hope of turning their season around and eventually making a push for the playoffs, they need to build some momentum off their first victory of the year in Dallas last week.
Defensively, the Bucs match up pretty well with the Steelers. Tampa Bay's corners have played out of their minds this season, and this will be their easiest matchup yet. That should allow Bowles to really sell out to stop the run led by Jaylen Warren, who has developed into the Steelers’ most dynamic offensive weapon.
Jalon Daniels and Zac Robinson need to take care of the football and control the clock like they did against Dallas. If they can, the Bucs will win.
This front seven for the Steelers is going to be a lot different than what Jalon Daniels has faced this season. Zac Robinson will want to get the run game going again with Bucky Irving, but it won’t be easy with Cam Heyward and others in the middle for Pittsburgh.
I think this is a great game to take advantage of an immobile Aaron Rodgers and find multiple sacks throughout. If you can’t find sacks in this game, you’ve got issues going into the rest of the season.
I think the Bucs keep this one close against a dinged-up Steelers team but don’t pull it off in the fourth quarter.
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers got a huge win against the Dallas Cowboys 24-16 last Thursday, and now, they'll try to pick up another with quarterback Jalon Daniels under center. The good news? This offense isn't nearly as good as Dallas' offense. The bad news? The defense is much better.
The Bucs put up 24 against a paltry Dallas defense, so they should put up less against a more competent unit. T.J. Watt, with 4.5 sacks in five games, will be the best edge rusher the Bucs have faced so far this year, and he'll probably make Daniels' life hell for four quarters.
On the offensive side for the Steelers, Aaron Rodgers' quick-fire short game matches up perfectly against Bowles' defense. Jaylen Warren is arguably the most dynamic player the Bucs have faced this year since Ja'Marr Chase, and he'll give Tampa Bay's defense fits, too.
The Bucs could keep this close, but I think Pittsburgh takes it.
The Bucs got it done against Dallas, but most of our panel doesn't think they can get it done against the Steelers back at home. Will Daniels and the Bucs make it two in a row for the first time since the beginning of the 2025 season? Or will the Steelers knock the Bucs down to 1-5 on the year?

title: Steelers Cornerback Who Won Super Bowl With Buccaneers Talks Return to Tampa Bay
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are facing the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday, and when they do, they'll see two familiar faces.
One of those faces is very familiar, because he was a Buccaneer two weeks ago. Cornerback Sean Murphy-Bunting was on Tampa Bay's practice squad at the start of the season, but now he's on the Steelers' 53-man roster after Pittsburgh signed him two weeks ago.
Murphy-Bunting will reunite with the other familiar face, and that's cornerback Jamel Dean. Both of them won a Super Bowl with the Bucs in 2020, but Dean played with the Bucs until 2025. He hit free agency afterward and signed with Pittsburgh, and now, he's already making his homecoming to Tampa Bay after seven seasons with the Bucs.
Dean will have to go up against players he was teammates with just last year. This week, he's spoken on what it will mean to return to Tampa Bay — and how he's been helping the Steelers out.
Dean spoke to Penn Live reporter Nick Farabaugh about returning to Tampa Bay. Dean called it a "bittersweet moment", and he seems particularly excited to go up against his former head coach and defensive coordinator, Todd Bowles.
“It kinda feels like it’s going to be student finally going against the teacher.  I can’t wait to see how everything unravels," Dean said . "It’ll be a bittersweet moment for me. When I go into the stadium, hopefully I don’t go on autopilot and walk into their locker room.”
That's not all, though. According to ESPN reporter Brooke Pryor, Dean has also been trying to give the offense some tips on how to go up against Bowles' defense — he just doesn't think he'll be much of a help against his former head coach.
"I gave [the Steelers offense] little nuggets of what could possibly happen," Dean said . "But knowing [Bowles], he's probably planning for this right now, so won't be much use."
Dean has played good football so far this year. He's already had two forced fumbles, 14 combined tackles and he hasn't allowed a passing touchdown yet this season.
The Bucs will reunite with Dean when they play the Steelers at 1 p.m. on Sunday, but they'll hope he goes back to Pittsburgh with a loss as Tampa Bay tries to move to 2-4 on the year.

title: New Report Reveals When Baker Mayfield Could Return for Buccaneers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers will look to improve to 2-4 on the year when they face off against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday. When they do, they won't be playing their starting quarterback.
Undrafted free agent rookie has been deputizing starting quarterback Baker Mayfield for the last two games as Mayfield recovers from a dislocated thumb he suffered in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings. Daniels hasn't been bad in the role, and he's set to play another game on Sunday under center as Mayfield continues to recover.
This is Mayfield's team, though, and the team's three-year, $165 million extension of him this offseason proves it. Mayfield has been itching to get back to action ever since his injury, and one NFL insider pinpointed the exact game that could happen — and it's coming up very soon.
NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported Saturday that there's "optimism" in Tampa Bay that Mayfield could return for the team's Week 7 game against the Carolina Panthers.
Bucs QB Baker Mayfield will miss a third consecutive game since dislocating his thumb in Week 3. But there’s optimism he’ll return next week — just in time for Tampa Bay’s first division game of the season at Carolina. More in The Sweep: https://t.co/hVvUAJDNjT pic.twitter.com/HwpFcNzTQY
Mayfield tried to throw on Wednesday afternoon after Bucs practice. It's unknown how that throwing session went, but the team clearly did not think he was ready enough to get back to practice this week, so Daniels gets the start once again for Tampa Bay.
This return timeline makes sense for a lot of reasons, however. To begin, Bowles' initial assessment of Mayfield's injury was three weeks minimum — it will be past that assessment once the Bucs play the Steelers this Sunday, so Mayfield's window has opened up.
Additionally, this will be Tampa Bay's first NFC South game. The team, despite being 1-4, is one and a half games out of the NFC South lead, so it's crucial to gain some ground in that division. Tampa Bay will want its starting quarterback out there when it does, so it's understandable that Mayfield would try to get back in time for it.
Finally, Mayfield used to play for Carolina in 2022, and the experience was an overall negative one for him. He's made it very clear that he pays particular attention to revenge games on the schedule, so there's probably some extra incentive there as well.
Before he got hurt, Mayfield had thrown for 615 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions. He's struggled in a few different respects, though, as he's fumbled the ball three times this year and lost all of them. He'll look to bounce back from his recent stretch of play when he gets back under center for the Bucs.
Tampa Bay — led by Daniels — will play the Steelers on Sunday at 1 p.m. in Raymond James Stadium. But don't expect Mayfield to be away for long.

title: Former Super Bowl Champion Believes Jalon Daniels Is Bucs' Best Option at QB
full_text:
Baker Mayfield has had a rough start to the 2026 season.
Not only did Mayfield fail to lead his team to a single victory in each of his four starts this year, but his individual performance has predominantly been defined by turnovers, poor accuracy and a lack of poise in the pocket. To make matters worse, Mayfield suffered a brutal dislocation of his right thumb in the final moments of his team's home loss to the Cleveland Browns a few weeks ago, forcing him to the sidelines for an undetermined period of time.
Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels, who surprisingly beat out veteran free agent signing Jake Browning for the backup QB job in training camp, has been tasked with holding down the fort after Mayfield's injury. And that's exactly what he's done.
After a narrow defeat at the hands of the Green Bay Packers in his first NFL game, Daniels showed out in Dallas on Thursday Night Football in Week 5, leading his team to an impressive and improbable victory against one of the most prolific offenses in the NFL.
Meanwhile, although he's been very supportive of Daniels, Mayfield has been dead set on returning to the lineup as soon as possible. In fact, he recently resumed throwing in hopes of fast-tracking his path back onto the field.
But would that really be good for the team?
At least one member of the Buccaneers Super Bowl winning team in 2020 doesn't think so.
On a recent episode of his podcast hosted with Jarvis Landry, 4th and South, Fournette had quite a hot take about the Bucs' current quarterback situation.
"I think, me personally, Jalon Daniels is the perfect fit for the Bucs right now," Fournette said. "They're winning! When Baker was back there, they weren't winning nothing. So I think it was a blessing and a curse. I'm not wishing nobody gets hurt, but at the same time, he's giving them more opportunity to win."
Fournette believes that Daniels is the team's best option to win right now.
"And I'm not saying Jalon's decision-making is better than Baker," he said. "To me it's even, because Baker throws picks, he fumbles, he does a lot. But at the end of the day, what can you do for me now? They're winning. I say keep Daniels in until we figure it out. Yes, Baker's got $100 million contract, but damn that, we want to win, coach."
Lenny wants Jalon Daniels to KEEP the QB job in Tampa 😳 Jarvis isn’t buying it 👀 Jalon Daniels might be the winning fit... #4thAndSouth #GoBucs #NFL pic.twitter.com/eysRVLdDFm
Fournette is certainly entitled to his opinion. That being said, as good as Daniels looked last week against the Cowboys and as bad as Mayfield looked in the first month of the season, the Buccaneers are going to be at their best for a longer period of time with Mayfield under center.
Not only that, but there isn't a chance that the Buccaneers would even consider relegating a healthy Mayfield to the bench because of the massive contract they awarded him just over a month ago.
The Buccaneers believe in Mayfield. And with every positive performance they get out of Daniels, their belief in him will continue to increase as well. But this is Mayfield's team, and the Bucs are prepared to sink or swim with him as the captain of their ship.

title: 3 Most Dangerous Steelers Players Buccaneers Will Face
full_text:
Even though they're only 5 games into the regular season, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers have already entered 'must-win' territory. As would be the case for any team that opened the season with 4 consecutive losses.
The Bucs do have some positive momentum, though, as they're coming off an impressive victory in Dallas over the Cowboys last Thursday night. Not only did undrafted rookie QB Jalon Daniels impress in his second NFL game, but the Bucs managed to contain the Cowboys' most dangerous weapons, holding each of Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens well below their expected output and allowing the Bucs to secure a much needed victory on the road.
If the Buccaneers hope to kickstart a winning streak, they'll need to do the same against the Steelers at home and limit the damage from Pittsburgh's most dangerous players. Let's take a closer look at who those players are and how the Bucs could achieve that:
There's little doubt about which player Todd Bowles' defense should be most concerned about on Sunday.
Jaylen Warren has always had explosive ability, but he was mostly used as a change of pace back under Mike Tomlin. Now that he's finally been given the keys to the backfield, Warren has taken that opportunity and run with it... literally.
Warren currently ranks third in the NFL in total yards from scrimmage with 640 and he's undoubtedly established himself as the team's most dynamic offensive weapon. Not only is Warren averaging an impressive 5.7 yards per carry running the football, but he's also been the team's greatest weapon as he leads the team in both receptions (19) and receiving yards (230).
Warren appears to be gaining confidence as he continues to earn more touches. He had arguably his best game as a pro last week vs. Indianapolis, where he exploded for 188 yards and 1 TD.
Despite having a relatively quiet 2025 season (at least by his standards) T.J. Watt has wasted no time reminding everyone why he remains one of the NFL's truly elite edge defenders. Although his 4.5 sacks are tied for the sixth most in the league, Watt is impacting the game in other ways this year, too.
According to PFF, Watt has been the best run defender among all edge rushers so far this year with an outstanding 92.1 run defense grade. Watt has been an extremely well-rounded player in 2026, producing 13 tackles, 6 TFLs and 7 QB hits to go along with 1 forced fumble and 1 fumble recovery.  Watt also has an interception this year, which he returned 35 yards for a TD to help seal a Steelers' victory against the Falcons back in Week 1.
The point is that T.J. Watt is still a game wrecker, and the Buccaneers will need to account for his presence at all times. If not? Watt could single-handedly turn the tide in his team's favor.
Some people may roll their eyes when they see Aaron Rodgers listed as one of the Steelers' most dangerous players, but the truth is, he's still got what it takes to lead his team to victories.
Rodgers has quietly played some pretty good football over the past few weeks, as the 42-year-old has now thrown three TD passes in each of his last three games. Rodgers is currently fifth in the league with 11 TD passes this year and 11th in total passing yards with 1,234.
Although Rodgers is very much immobile at this point of his career, he's still got more than enough arm talent to make every throw on the field. He also processes the game at an elite level, which is a big reason why he's been able to find so much success this season despite a really underwhelming group of pass catchers to work with.
If the Bucs aren't strategic with the looks they give Rodgers, both in coverage and pressure packages , he will make them pay.

title: The Titans May Have Won, But Cam Ward Still Has to Improve... and He Knows It
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans picked up their first win in emphatic fashion, as they overcame a 13-point halftime deficit to beat the Indianapolis Colts 26-20.
This was the Titans’ first win over the Colts since 2022. More importantly, it finally gives Tennessee something positive to build off of. Things certainly looked bleak in the first half. The Titans seemed well on their way to a sixth straight loss after being out-gained by 168 yards over the first two quarters.
In total, Tennessee produced just 64 yards of offense and three first downs.
QB Cam Ward accounted for 37 of those yards with an ugly interception on top of it. It was the kind of half that made you wonder how much longer this was truly sustainable. Fortunately, Ward played better in the second half, albeit nothing truly noteworthy outside of a couple of nice throws to rookie WR Carnell Tate.
Going into the third quarter, the Titans had an active streak of 13 consecutive scoreless drives dating back to last week. That streak came to a screeching halt after halftime as the Titans dropped 26 points over the final two quarters.
While the major nod has to go to the defense and special teams for their second-half performances, credit has to be given to the Titans’ young signal caller for making the winning plays when they were there to be made.
After Sunday’s win, Ward talked about the importance of complementary football on a day where all three units fed off each other to complete the second-half comeback.
“I think going into the second half, we didn’t play how we wanted to offensively. We still got a lot of things to clean up offensively. But the mindset didn’t change in the locker room," said Ward.
"It was a two-possession game coming out (of the half). Defense gave us a great turnover, and we were able to capitalize on that with a field goal. We really need seven, though. But at the end of the day, I think all three phases complemented each other at the right time.”
The second-year quarterback also talked about his budding connection with Tennessee’s rookie pass catcher and how important he is to this offense.
“He’s real big (for the team). He’s a great contested catcher like you seen today. He’s good at scramble drill. But the biggest thing about him is he doesn’t show no emotion. Each and every drive, no matter what happens, he comes back, he wants the football, and he’s trying to make plays for the team.”
Tate was undoubtedly the focal point of the offense. He accounted for 68 percent of Ward’s yardage on the day, catching six balls for 70 yards, along with the first touchdown of his career:
Tate gets his first NFL TD! 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/sQ7HfdARtC
However, outside of Tate, no other pass-catcher topped 22 receiving yards, resulting in Ward totaling just 102 passing yards for the game.
That’s something that has to change for this offense to truly take off. There will be times when Tate is taken away, and somebody else will have to step up. Unfortunately, nobody has proven that they’re capable of doing that for this team just yet.
But in reality, for any of that to happen, they’ll need more efficient play out of their young quarterback going forward, which is something Ward acknowledged after the game.
“I gotta improve each and every day. There’s still a lot of stuff that we have to clean up offensively. There’s a lot of plays that we want back for sure. But at the end of the day, we’ll take an ugly win over a loss each and every week."
The Titans are taking the correct approach to a win like this. Enjoy it, but make no mistake about it, there’s still a lot of work to be done before this team reaches its full potential.
“We know [we have to be better]...'', Ward said. “we’ll enjoy this for the next couple of hours, and as we get into the building tomorrow, it’s time to reset and try to get a win next week.” The Titans face the Browns next Sunday as they try to win consecutive games for the first time since November 2022.
Shaun is a longtime Titans fan who has years of experience in the field. He missed being on the team beat, and is here to change that. He also writes scripts for EA Sports' Madden games, where fans may have heard his work.

title: Postgame Quotes That Matter from Head Coach Robert Saleh After Titans' Gritty Win Over Colts
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans have won a football game in 2026. Despite trailing 13-0 at halftime and showing no life for the first 30 minutes, the Titans put together an excellent second half and picked up a 26-20 win over the Indianapolis Colts on the road.
Everything came together for Tennessee in the final two quarters. The defense held the Colts' offense to one second-half touchdown and also forced two turnovers, the special teams blocked a punt in the fourth quarter and returned it for the go-ahead touchdown, and the offense did just enough to seal the deal.
Head coach Robert Saleh spoke to the media after his first win as Titans head coach, and here are the most notable quotes.
After starting his tenure in Tennessee 0-5 , Saleh finally captured a win as head coach of the Titans, and he admitted that it's a relief to win games in the NFL . Saleh added that Tennessee needs to get back to work as the team looks to build on the momentum gained from the comeback victory on the road.
"Winning in this league is relief," Saleh said. "We'll enjoy it for about 24 hours, but we gotta get back to work."
Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk has caught a lot of heat to start the year because of her organization's dysfunction being at an all-time high. Sunday's win over the Colts came at the perfect time for Strunk, and Saleh made sure to give her a shoutout while at the podium.
"I'm happy for Miss Amy – I apologize to her that it took a little longer than we all wanted. The players, these kids put in so much work, and this league is hard. We'd been close on a few occasions, and to knock this one out for them, I am much more excited for them than for myself," Saleh said.
Saleh acknowledged that his group, especially the defense, came out and played with a different fire in the second half. The Titans head coach credited superstar defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons for his message to the team at halftime and called Simmons the best defensive tackle in football .
"I want to give a special shoutout to Jeff Simmons, who I thought was outstanding in the locker room" Saleh said. "It made it more noticeable for me when watching and observing the team.. He's the best defensive tackle in football."
Despite facing double teams for most of the day, Simmons still tallied six tackles, two sacks, and two tackles for loss against the Colts. It's hard to argue that the franchise has seen a more dominant defensive player in the last two decades than Simmons.
The Titans will look to kick off a winning streak next week as they return home to face the Cleveland Browns. Though Tennessee still has a lot of work to do , it's nice to get their first win as October nears its end.
